Heading: Participation of armed forces in traffic management a success - Indian Express
Content:
An 11-year-old girl was allegedly raped by a youth in Sangam Vihar area on Wednesday night.

Police said the girl Ramya (name changed) was sleeping with her mother and her little sister in their house. At 10.30 pm, the accused, Amar Pal (19) went to the house with one of his friends and asked him to stand guard outside the house.

"Pal went inside and took the girl into another room, where he raped her. The girl's father came in around 10.40 pm and saw Pal's friend standing outside the house. When he questioned him, the boy fled," a senior police officer said. Alarmed, Ramya's father went inside and caught Pal red-handed in the act. He raised an alarm and his neighbours assembled and beat Pal up. He was later taken to Pul Prehladpur police post.

On Thursday morning, Ramya was taken to AIIMS, where a medical examination confirmed rape. Police arrested Amar Pal under the charges of raping a minor.

Police said Amar Pal is from Faridabad and was staying with his uncle in the area. Ramya's father runs a general store in the area.

Heading: Gang of robbers held in S Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
A year after it was initiated by Lieutenant Governor Tejendra Khanna, the "special traffic wardens" scheme that involves officers from the Army, Air Force and Navy assisting the traffic police in managing traffic on the Capital's roads, has shown positive results.

Some 303 officers from the armed forces have joined as "special traffic wardens" since the scheme was started. In the last year, they have forwarded a total of 7,301 challans to the Delhi Traffic Police for violations by people on city roads.

A "special citizen warden" as part of this scheme, Wing Commander Ajay Kumar Tyagi has contributed around 35 per cent (2,048 challans) of the total figure on his own. He regularly managed traffic in Dwarka and noted down the registration numbers of violators when on the moved in the city.

Tyagi has also involved his wife in the scheme and together they account for up to 3,000 challans out of the total figure of 7,301. Other special traffic wardens have also contributed with 400 to 1,000 challans, while others have contributed in numbers ranging from 1 to 100.

Officers from the armed forces have been managing traffic at intersections and crossings in their areas and other roads, in morning as well as evening hours. They forwarded notices to the traffic police after noting down the registration numbers of vehicles violating traffic rules. The traffic police then, in turn, sent the challans.

These challans included not wearing helmets and seat belts, zigzag driving and red light jumping. "I stand at the Dwarka intersection for two hours each in the morning and the evening everyday and ask people to obey traffic rules. I forwarded notices to the traffic police whenever I found people breaking the law and the traffic police responded and helped me a lot," Tyagi said.

He said: "I have forwarded challans and have also educated people in resettlement colonies, autorickshaw drivers and tempo drivers about traffic rules, whenever I got time from my work."

When the scheme was started, only Air Force officers joined it. But the other armed forces also agreed to join in and now there are 158 officers of the Air Force, 33 of the Navy and 105 of the Army participating in the scheme.

"Everybody has contributed. This is what we need — public participation in managing over 60 million vehicles," RK Meena, DCP (VIP Traffic), said. "This acts as a deterrent for people living around special traffic wardens. They don't violate rules themselves and tell their relatives and friends about the responsibilities of being a warden," Meena said.

In the last one year, officials said, the number of violations has come down in areas where these traffic wardens have been active. They have received prompt support from the PCR and inspectors of the traffic police. Their identities have also been kept a secret.

Officials said the scheme would continue as it has been successful and by the time the Commonwealth Games start, there will be many wardens assisting the traffic police in managing traffic in Delhi.

Apart from the special traffic wardens, "general traffic wardens" and "professional traffic wardens" also assist traffic cops. General wardens are from the public and professional wardens are people from different professions like engineers, doctors and journalists.

Heading: Woman hangs self, family alleges dowry harassment - Indian Express
Content:
South district police have busted a gang of robbers who looted passengers posing as auto-drivers at night time after taking an auto on rent for the whole night. With the arrest of three of the gang members, Noor Mohammad (20), Mohammad Yasin (18) and Danish (18), police claimed to have solved two recent robbery cases, including the robbery attempt on Zee TV employee Saurabh Mishra on October 4 near the Andrews Ganj flyover.

Officers said that one gang member, Anees, is still absconding. The gang had a unique modus operandi — they used to take an auto on rent at the rate of Rs 300 to 400 for plying the roads at night. "They would then take a passenger on rent. Another gang member, posing as a passenger, would be picked up after a while by the driver. When they reached a flyover, the robbers would threaten the victim with knives, and after robbing his belongings, they would flee the spot," said DCP HGS Dhaliwal.

One Deepak Rana was robbed in this manner of Rs 7,000, two mobile phones and two silver rings on September 27. Later, Mishra was attacked on October 4 but the robbers fled when he resisted.

"They used to target the victim near a flyover where vehicular movement merges. The robbers also changed the auto-rickshaw everyday. The actual auto drivers had no idea about the gangs' motives and were happy to earn while not working," said an officer.

Heading: He’s got the look - Indian Express
Content:
Online data lost due to virus, PT Usha among those made to wait for hours together

Hours before the kickoff of the Commonwealth Youth Games, chaos ruled at Marathon Bhavan and Baburao Sanas Ground where the accreditation process was on, giving credence to the general belief that organisers have left many things for the last minute.

Mediapersons who were informed on Friday evening by email to collect their accreditation passes the same day from the Marathon Bhavan by 3 pm reached the place to be told they should report to Sanas ground the next day. On Saturday morning technical officials from all parts of the country and mediapersons reached the ground. But they were told that nothing had been processed as all the online data had been lost due to a virus. They had to go through the process of applying for accreditation all over again, a task most had done 45 days ago.

As people began to badger the volunteers for information, the volunteers went on an hour-long flash strike, compounding matters. Among those who had to put up with inconvenience was Payoli Express P T Usha who came with her team and was upset that she had to wait from 12.30 to 5.30 pm for she could get her accreditation. "The organisers should complete all paper work and not leave it for the last minute," she said. Many technicians were also surprised that the accreditation centre was 25-odd km from the Games venue.

The technical officials of the weight-lifting association were waiting at the centre since morning. They were not issued their passes so they stormed out. Sudeep Barve, the Asian umpire for badminton, was surprised to find his name excluded from his pass. "I received a letter from the officials to make the necessary rectification and so I have come here, but have to wait interminably, to make it happen," he rued. Uday Sane, the technical official for badminton, was disappointed with the treatment meted out to the guests.

"Officials come from different parts of the country. There is no reception counter at the station. They have to find their own way to the venue. They dished out their own funds to reach the Balewadi grounds. There they found they had to first go to the Marathon Bhavan. It's all very disorganised," he said even as Raj Kumar the boxing coach echoed the opinion.

Two weightlifting officials, Ramesh K Malhotra and K Subramaniam, who are also the coaches of the Indian team and referees at the international level arrived in Pune at 8 am on Saturday.

They were made to wait at the Baburao Sanas ground till 10 am till the office opened after which they were there till 2.30 pm without anything to eat. Finally they stormed out and threatened to boycott the Games.

K Subramaniam said, "We had sent all our details for the accreditation pass to the Commonwealth Games office via email. When we arrived at the office we found they had lost all the information. When we received our passes they were without a hologram making us ineligible to enter the sports complex. On top of it the volunteers were rude. Being an international referee, I have visited many sporting events but never have I seen such chaos when it came to accreditation. I was very angry and so I went to the airport and purchased a ticket to return to Bangalore but the president of the Weightlifting Federation persuaded me to stay."

According to an organising committee official, the confusion was due to a technical problem beyond their control and that it was not the sports officials and media persons alone but also their own staff who had to go through the process of accreditation all over again and put up with the inconvenience.

It was only by late afternoon that things seemed to be under control once the volunteers returned from their protest and started attending to the long line of persons gathered there who were finally issued their passes by late evening.

Heading: Out of character - Indian Express
Content:
Himesh Reshammiya got a sexy hairstyle, shaved his chest and got into shape for Karzzz. Still, he can't seem to comprehend why a classic hero must be Adonis-like

Himesh Reshammiya knows that he can never be like Clark Gable or James Dean. He maintains that he isn't an archetypal Hindi film hero, nor can he ever be. This, despite the fact that his second film, Karzzz, is releasing on October 17 with a phenomenal 1,200 prints, there are queues of people waiting to interview him and his film's music is already a sell-out success. "The first criterion of becoming a hero is that you have to be good-looking. That, in itself, disqualifies me," he says.

We aren't going to deliberate on what he looked like earlier, but now, he's got himself a cool new hairstyle, shaved his chest hair and gotten into shape. "You have no idea how tough it has been. I had to go on a strict diet (I didn't work out at all), undergo hair transplant, wear extensions... it was crazy. And still people accuse me of trying to emulate Rishi Kapoor. He is one of the most effortlessly handsome faces of his time. However, I believe that Karzzz is a tribute to Rishi Kapoor from an ardent fan."

With Karzzz, the flashbulbs will be trained on Reshammiya, the actor. "In that sense, Karzzz is my real acting debut. My acting skills will be put to test on October 17. We're treading rather carefully. Bhushan Kumar has spent lots of money to make this film. After careful consideration, we brought the release date forward from December and work is going on at breakneck speed. We're getting ready for the verdict." It's true. Although the 35-year-old has been accepted as entertainer par excellence, he is yet to set the big screen ablaze with histrionics. "This is my attempt to win over my critics," he resolves.

In a creative outburst, he composed the music for Tandoori Nights over a meal of grilled chicken. "I was getting too frustrated controlling my diet, eating boiled, bland and grilled meals. That has found expression in Tandoori Nights. It's doing so well now."

Although Karz, the 1980 original, won Laxmikant- Pyarelal awards, Reshammiya has a feeling that his music may not quite bring home the coveted trophy. "I don't know why I am saying that. I just have a feeling. Anyway, I made Pyarelalji listen to my rendition of Ek Hasina Thi. He loved it. And FYI, I have abandoned my nasal twang in this one, I've sung it normally."

Reshammiya's date book looks quite scribbled in. "I am doing five films, and they are all in the big-budget category. Then, I'm making music for others. I intend to take it easy on films for fear of over-exposure," he says.

Clearly, Reshammiya is the most famous package to come out of Gujarat. He says, "I am a good Gujju boy at home. I refrain from talking about my family because they are media-shy. They are happy being in the background. My 10-year-old, Swayam, is my biggest fan and critic. He's going to give me feedback on Karzzz tonight. You also pray for me, okay?" Okay.

Heading: FACE TO FACE with Anjana Sukhani - Indian Express
Content:
Sharman Joshi has whooped it up in the comedy genre. He now wants to try out a variety of roles

If there is one actor who will never undermine the significance of multi-starrers, it is Sharman Joshi. After playing the role of the affable Sukhi in Rang De Basanti, and the over-ambitious Rahul in Life in a Metro, he now plays Shyam Varma, a call centre employee in Hello. Joshi who has worked with industry bigwigs right from his debut film Godmother, is gung-ho about sharing screen space with some of Bollywood's best yet again, that include Salman Khan and Katrina Kaif.

"With Hello, I have achieved two things: the opportunity to work with a bunch of talented actors and a chance to do a role based on a fictional character. Moreover, Atul (Agnihotri, the director) has taken care to see that everyone has equal screen space," he vouches.

The movie, based on Chetan Bhagat's bestseller, One Night @ the Call Centre, had the entire cast posted at a call centre for a

30-day period. "I read the book a couple of times and then got used to the workings of a call centre. To convert a 300-page book into a 30-page script is a difficult job and there are definitely going to be comparisons with the character in the book," says the 34-year-old actor, who is up for the challenge.

Although Joshi has been considered a versatile actor and a powerhouse performer, he still has to prove his mettle at the box office through a solo hit. But for this cheerful actor, it seems, personal achievement coexists with the movie's success. "All films are multi-starrers in that sense. A single person cannot make a successful film. It is the effort and hard work of many involved."

Joshi, who started off his stint almost a decade ago, comes from a family of distinguished theatre actors. "Both my father and uncle are from the theatre fraternity. And I'd happily return to my theatre roots whenever my film career ceases to satisfy me. At the moment, films are an uplifting experience and I'm totally into them." After playing Shabana Azmi's truant son in Godmother, it was an avalanche of comedies that followed. But he doesn't want to be stereotyped as a comedian. "I am not averse to comedies. Right now, my priority is a good script — it could be of any genre. You get the same offers sometimes but then you have to wait for the right time. If something that I am looking for doesn't come my way, I am okay with just chilling at home."

Clearly, Joshi's date diary looks occupied for the year. Onir's Sorry Bhai and Raqeeb are ready for release and he has begun shooting for 3 Idiots. But at the moment, it is Hello that he hopes will see huge success. "The book had more than 10 million readers. With the movie, we hope to cross that mark," he says, ambitiously.

Heading: Very filmy - Indian Express
Content:
What's on your iPod?
Nothing, because at the moment, my iPod is non-functional.

What's your DVD pick?
I just bought The Bourne Ultimatum; I'm a huge fan of Matt Damon.

Your favourite romantic scene in a movie?
I recently watched P.S.I Love You, and I think that whole movie is so romantic. The whole idea of a man who knows he's dying and wants his wife to get over him soon; I find that very touching.

Which actor would you love to go on a date with and why?
Shah Rukh Khan, because he's so witty and has an amazing sense of humour.

Which dialogue have you mouthed in front of the mirror the most?
I've watched Maine Pyar Kiya more than 45 times, and there are two-three memorable scenes in the movie which I've enacted innumerable times, especially the one where Bhagyashree goes to Salman Khan and says, "Dekho to, mere haathon ki mehendi kaisi lag rahi hai?"

Who inspired you to become an actor?
Nobody inspired me in the beginning. But once I got here, I decided to stick around. But if you ask me who is inspiring me right now, I'd say it's Priyanka Chopra and Kareena Kapoor.

The worst film you ever watched?
Jawaani Deewani. Watching that movie was such torture.

Which film you wish you could be a part of?
Zubeida. I loved that movie. If I were in love, I'd be exactly like Zubeida, where her man becomes the centre of her world.

What makes you an actor?
There's an inbuilt something that makes someone an actor. It isn't enough to want to be one. You have to have the talent as well.

Quiz: From which film is this line: Michael ko maut se dar nahi lagta, maut ko Michael se dar lagta hai. Is liye aane mein der lag rahi hai.
I don't know, but it sounds like a Mithun Chakraborty or Amitabh Bachchan movie.
(Correct answer is Majboor)

Heading: No more candle-light vigils in national capital - Indian Express
Content:
Mirror image
Imran Khan is not only following in uncle Aamir's footsteps but he also seems to have donned the same pair of shoes — the similarities just don't seem to end. The lad has been on his toes ever since the release of Kidnap. He has been travelling across the length and breadth of the country in attempt to salvage his film Kidnap. Says Dhilin Mehta, producer from Shree Ashtavinayak Cine Vision, "Imran, like Aamir, believes in doing everything with sincerity and gives his 100 per cent to whatever he does. He was very cooperative and would turn up for all promotional events on time despite his overnight rise to stardom." It won't be long before Imran's mirror has Aamir mamu staring back at him.

Diamonds and baubles
KIM Sharma says that New York is her favourite shopping destination as it houses all international brands. The actress, who's of late only visible at social dos, says that she makes frequent trips to the Big Apple and usually shops at Bloomingdales and Canal Street for clothes and Clay Pot for her sparkling diamonds. But all we wish to know, darling, is: where is all the money coming from?

South speak
ARJAN Bajwa is working hard to impress the South Indian audiences. The model-turned-actor has signed three South Indian films and is now learning martial arts. "The directors down South do not like to use body doubles — the actors are expected to do their own stunts," he explains. Bajwa will star alongside Nagarjuna, NT Ramarao's son Balakrishnan and South superstar Mohan Babu in his forthcoming projects. The actor is also learning the local languages, which seems to be the most difficult task. "Ask me to jump from a 50-storey building; I would find it easier than learning Telegu," he laughs.

Heading: Recession in the Ruffle - Indian Express
Content:
People planning candle light vigils in the national capital to highlight their cause will now have to think of another mode of protest as Delhi Police on Friday decided to prohibit processions carrying flames.

City Police Commissioner Y S Dadwal issued an order in this regard which prohibits the carrying of "torch carrying live flames or live fire candles or live fire in any form in processions, rallies and functions" in the capital.

The order comes in the backdrop of police receiving inputs that some people may indulge in activities prejudicial to the maintenance of peace in the city, a senior police official said.

"We have received information that such activities may seriously endanger life and property of the citizens and maintenance of law and order," the official said.

Those found disobeying this order shall be punishable under section 188 (disobedience to an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant) of the IPC.

The contravention of the order may lead to an imprisonment up to six months or a fine of Rs 1,000, the official said.

Heading: Gem of an Auction? - Indian Express
Content:
A clutch of new designers for the forthcoming India Fashion Week shuns the famed obsession with ornamentation

Isn't a possible recession George W Bush's problem? Should debut designers in Delhi be worrying about sliding rupee and market meltdown? But look keenly at the collections of some of the 18 first-time designers at the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week Spring-Summer 09 that begins on Wednesday, and you will find recession in the ruffles. With minimalist designs characteristic of post-war Europe and austerity associated with post-modern architecture inspiring them, a tempered palette and severe silhouettes will be out on the runway. And even when a couple of them are going retro, they are slipping into the dainty dresses of early Sixties that would look chic at a derby.

Designer duo Gaurav Jagtiani and Ritika Gupta, both 24 and the youngest on the block, have created "Definite Space" revolving around the postmodern design movement in which ornamentation is shunned. And the source of inspiration is British-Iraqi architect Zaha Hadid, who stresses on deconstructive designs. On the runway will be dresses in austere silhouettes and tempered colours. The duo have mixed whites with ivory and icy mint. "There are no prints, no embellishments, no sequins, no Swarovski-studded tunics. There will be no external influence; it is all about playing with the concept of design," says Jagtiani.

IIM graduate Anupama Dayal has since moved to the ramps, but the 34-year-old is as much bothered about market as she is about fashion. "With the slowing down of the economy, business is changing and people are increasingly designing resort dresses for the upcoming season," says Dayal, who has been on the circuit for five years, with four Paris fairs and a Lakme Fashion Week under her designer belt. She has cranked out "The Gallerina", inspired by Swedish, post-war minimalism and rustic Bengal life. The square-cut dresses in intense colours and "European sophistication" are embellished with Indian motifs, with Jamini Roy's classic, big, dark eyes and paisley prints blending impeccably on a tunic. "I have referenced Scandinavian textile companies such as Nordiska Kompaniet and the Stromma," says Dayal, whose palette ranges from faded gold to amethyst.

Even the '60s look borders on girlish prettiness, with practical trousers and chic dresses in muted colours sans indulgence. Rohit Mittal, 28, with his Audrey Hepburn-inspired collection "My Fair Lady" has a potpourri of creamy dresses paired with a dainty parasol. "The colours are mostly whites," says Mittal. While a white crepe skirt is brightened by a green, ruffled hemline, an old-fashioned, full-sleeve blouse is paired with a white sari set off by scarlet flowers and an English hat. The Delhi-based designer, says, "It's a light, summery collection meant for Sunday brunches, polo afternoons and resort wear."

Practicality bodes well for 29-year-old Ashima Singh as well. Her "Sonnets", a daywear collection for 20-somethings, includes such unembellished, non-OTT dresses as lime-green frock and a pink frilly top paired with purple trousers that gather at the knees. "The wardrobe is practical and could be easily worn as evening wear as well," says Singh, who has had a successful stint at a London fashion fair this year.

And with two fashion weeks ready to run neck-and-neck, will these sequin-less ensembles stand out? The newcomers are ready to give it a go and earn enough reputation and rupees in these Sensex-wracked times.

Heading: Stage Cause - Indian Express
Content:
Not quite. The first public auction of jewels in the country did not dazzle with its results, but more are following

At 42.02 carats, it is the world's largest Forevermark yellow diamond, estimated between Rs 2.7 crore and Rs 3.2 crore — one best friend for a man or a woman. But when the unmounted gemstone came under the hammer at the recent Saffronart Fine Jewels auction, it failed to invite a bid that touched the reserve price. The fate was shared by 74 of 130 lots that went on sale, and the closing figure stood at Rs 6.3 crore, far from the estimated Rs 22-28 crore, but that did not deter the spirit of Minal Vazirani, co-founder of the online auction house. "Keeping the current global economic conditions in mind, we did well," she said, still beaming at having organised what is arguably India's first public auction of fine jewels and watches on October 7 and 8.

With only international auction houses to look for guidance, Vazirani had formed an in-house team of experts that scouted precious jewels from the world over. Apart from the diamond, there were a natural pearl necklace with a seven-strand cascade that invited the highest bid of Rs 1 crore, a diamond necklace that sold for Rs 79.8 lakh and a diamond sarpech that went for Rs 49.8 lakh. "The auction comprised jewellery made over the past 100 years," says Vazirani.

Saffronart's results might not have dazzled, but in his Bangalore office Maher Dadha, CMD of the auction house Bid & Hammer, is busy examining the provenance of vintage jewellery. It will be part of the auction that will take place in January 2009. Unlike Vazirani, Dadha will bring to the auction, jewellery that is a minimum of 50 years old and will tap sources that have remained outside the radar of international auctioneers that are bound by trade regulations that restrict the export of heritage jewellery from India. "There is a lot of demand in India and it will not be difficult to find buyers," says Dadha.

Mumbai-based Ma Passion, meanwhile, hopes to revive the craft of gemstone carving with its October 22 auction. Curated by Nisha Jamwal, this will comprise, among others, emerald Ganesha, Krishna and Radha in blue sapphire and crystal Buddha under the Bodhi tree carved by craftsmen from Rajasthan.

Even as the country wakes up to hammer coming down on jewels, foreign shores will as usual be glitzy. At its Geneva auction next month, Sotheby's will have enough Indian jewels, while later this month Christie's will bring under the hammer, in Dubai, an early 20th century rose-cut diamond sarpech, estimated at $50,000-70,000, and two India-influenced Cartier jewels — a pendant estimated at $200,000-300,000 and a 1940s clip brooch priced at $13,000-18,000.

Heading: BJP to move common man’s court for mandate  on GUJCOC - Indian Express
Content:
Sohaila Kapur doesn't mind the trend of alternative theatre venues. "The more, the merrier," says Kapur. "As a theatre person, I know the hassles of booking premier auditoriums. Now five-star hotels are proving to be very theatre-friendly," says Kapur, whose hit comedy 45-35-55 will be staged at the Banquet Hall at the Ashok Hotel today evening. 45-35-55 is a "Hinglish" comedy about three women who have more than just generation gap between them. Two middle-aged, Punjabi sisters, played by Kapur and Smita Bharti, have to go by the will of their mother: they have to live together for a year in their mother's house before deciding to sell the property. But the sisters don't see to eye to eye and a series of misadventures follow. The entry of a young, working woman, played by Aparajita Basu, as a paying guest, adds fuel to the fire. "It is a black comedy about families," says Kapur. The play premiered at the World Theatre Festival in Lahore last year and was well received. Today's production is a benefit performance to raise money for the rehabilitation of those affected by the Kosi floods.

The play will begin at 7 pm. Contact 41688955

Heading: Repair work will stop water supply to some city areas today - Indian Express
Content:
All district units of the party to garner support through rallies, graffiti

The BJP has decided to come out on to the streets to gather support of the common man on the anti-terror GUJCOC Bill. In the coming two weeks, the ruling party has decided to cover every city, taluka and village through different programmes to build public support for GUJCOC.

Be it through press conferences or public meetings, Chief Minister Narendra Modi has not missed a single opportunity to garner support for the Bill. Now, the BJP headquarters in Ahmedabad has asked all the 25 district units to conduct some unique programmes in their respective areas from October 9 to 20 to highlight the need for GUJCOC.

BJP Ahmedabad city president Jagdish Patel said: "We are going to paint each public wall in all the 60 wards of Ahmedabad city with a theme on GUJCOC and terrorism. Each ward will see nearly 150 paintings. The painting exercise will begin from October 15."

Besides, a number of rallies, including on cycles and scooters, will also be organised, he said.

In Rajkot, an Atankwad Virodhi Rath Yatra (anti-terror rath yatra) was kicked off by the district unit on Thursday.

The rath has a tableau on the theme of GUJCOC. It will go to all the nine talukas in two days. "Villagers will be explained about GUJCOC and why it is necessary. They will be asked to sign letters addressed to the Prime Minister for the implementation of GUJCOC," said Rajkot district coordinator Chandu Singala.

In Surat city, a mock court session was organised on Wednesday. Surat BJP secretary V Kishor said, "The mock session showed how easily a terrorist can get away with severe crimes like planting bombs, in the absence of a strict law."

For Vadodara, the BJP has planned dharnas at major crossroads to attract public attention towards the Bill. "Like Ahmedabad, Vadodara is also planning to go for a wall painting programme," said BJP Vadodara co-coordinator Bharat Dangar.

Senior party leader Jayanti Barot said: "Each district has been asked to plan its own event. The aim is to reach to the common man and create awareness about anti-terror law."

Heading: Pay up within 15 days or lose property: VMC tells tax defaulters - Indian Express
Content:
There will be no water supply in some areas of the city, including Chhani, Lalbaug, Sayajigunj, and GIDC, for the next two days as the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) will repair a damaged pipeline on the National Highway 8 from Friday.

A leakage in the water pipeline was reported last week on the Gujarat State Fertilizer's and Chemicals Ltd crossroads.

"The pipeline was laid 40 years ago, and that is the major reason behind the leakage. We are scanning the line and ruptured area where the pipes are around 10 feet underground. We will try to complete the work by the evening," said V N Tailor, VMC city engineer. "The areas of rupture will be patched or the joints in the line will be repaired as per the requirement," he added.

The disconnection of supply comes at a time when the residents of Sama, Manjalpur, Jail Road and others were already facing the problem of low water pressure.

"Water supply has been a perennial problem in the area. While the duration of the supply has been reduced to just half and hour a day, the pressure of the supply has decreased," said Kruti Shah, a resident of Sama.

Not only the residents, but also those using the national highway have been experiencing problems due to water logging caused by the leakage.

Tailor further said the traffic on the highway will be diverted during the course of action. "We have spoken to the officials of the National Highway Authority of India. The traffic on this route will be diverted while the work is on," he said. Apart from Ajwa Sarovar water supply, the city heavily depends on the feeder lines connecting the French wells.

Heading: Identify yourself if you want to deposit a Rs 500 note in this bank - Indian Express
Content:
With the month-old tax collection drive of the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) yielding poor results, the civic body has issued orders to the defaulters with dues over Rs 1 lakh to pay the tax amount within a fortnight or face seizure of property.

If the defaulters with dues between Rs 50,000 and Rs 1 lakh fail to pay the pending tax before October 23, their properties will be sealed. The VMC has resorted to this as the big time defaulters owe it 20 per cent of the total amount of the pending property taxes.

Municipal Commissioner M K Das issued the order after a meeting with the concerned department and officials on Wednesday. Performance of the officials was also discussed at the meeting. A separate list of areas with a high number of defaulters has been prepared to identify the officers who are going easy on the defaulters.

"There are over 300 cases where the property tax due is over Rs 1 lakh," said Das.

According to him, the VMC expects to recover Rs 10 crore by cracking down on the big defaulters.

At present, the property tax dues for the VMC is to the tune of Rs 56 crore. The collective tax amount of these 300 cases touches Rs 10-crore mark. "The drive is on and the VMC has been seizing smaller properties now and then to recover the dues. Now, the same procedure will be followed for the big defaulters," Das added

Das went on to say that through this drive, the VMC wants to send its message loud and clear.

"The objective is to achieve the target of making big defaulters paying up the dues. The step will also send the message across that no one will be spared," he said.

Heading: Irfan Pathan’s father accused of cheating - Indian Express
Content:
Do not be surprised by the board hanging at the office of Pancham Cooperative Credit Society Limited (PCCSL) near VIP Road, asking the customers to furnish details like names, addresses and phone numbers if they want to pay their electricity bills in denominations of Rs 500.

The incident that triggered such an order was a fake note that landed at the Harni branch of Bank of Baroda (BoB). The currency, of a face value of Rs 500, was deposited in the bank as the payment of an electricity bill.

"Though we destroyed the fake note, ultimately, it was left to our cashier to make up for the loss," said Shilpa Desai, branch manager at a PCCSL branch.

"In order to do away with such anomalies, the PCCSL has decided that every customer who deposits notes of Rs 500, will have to submit his/her details, so that the bank can revert back to them if need be."

According to the law, an FIR will be lodged against any person found in possession of counterfeit currency.

However, authorities at the Harni branch of BoB have decided not to lodge any FIR as this was a genuine error, and something that happened in one in a thousand cases.

"Since the person involved in the incident is an old customer and also, that he is not aware of the source, we decided not to lodge a case," said a bank official.

"Our main aim is to destroy the fake currency so that it is not reproduced or circulated in the market," said P D Potnis, Divisional General Manger, BoB, Vadodara.

Heading: To Sir with love: college alumni to felicitate mentor - Indian Express
Content:
Mirror image
Imran Khan is not only following in uncle Aamir's footsteps but he also seems to have donned the same pair of shoes — the similarities just don't seem to end. The lad has been on his toes ever since the release of Kidnap. He has been travelling across the length and breadth of the country in attempt to salvage his film Kidnap. Says Dhilin Mehta, producer from Shree Ashtavinayak Cine Vision, "Imran, like Aamir, believes in doing everything with sincerity and gives his 100 per cent to whatever he does. He was very cooperative and would turn up for all promotional events on time despite his overnight rise to stardom." It won't be long before Imran's mirror has Aamir mamu staring back at him.

Diamonds and baubles
KIM Sharma says that New York is her favourite shopping destination as it houses all international brands. The actress, who's of late only visible at social dos, says that she makes frequent trips to the Big Apple and usually shops at Bloomingdales and Canal Street for clothes and Clay Pot for her sparkling diamonds. But all we wish to know, darling, is: where is all the money coming from?

South speak
ARJAN Bajwa is working hard to impress the South Indian audiences. The model-turned-actor has signed three South Indian films and is now learning martial arts. "The directors down South do not like to use body doubles — the actors are expected to do their own stunts," he explains. Bajwa will star alongside Nagarjuna, NT Ramarao's son Balakrishnan and South superstar Mohan Babu in his forthcoming projects. The actor is also learning the local languages, which seems to be the most difficult task. "Ask me to jump from a 50-storey building; I would find it easier than learning Telegu," he laughs.

Heading: 16 blast accused sent to one-week police remand - Indian Express
Content:
The alumni of Rajkumar College will gather at a special function on October 12 to felicitate Ayaz Khan Babi, the scion of Pajod, a principality in Junagadh.

The members of the Old Boys of Rajkumar College will come here from across the country and even abroad to personally hand over a memento to Babi, telling him how much he meant to them as a teacher.

A member of the royal family, the son of late Ranisaheba and Kumar Darbar Immamuddin Khan (Ruswa Mazlumi) of Pajod, Babi is better known as the longest serving principal of Rajkumar College — established by the royals of Saurashtra region.

Here, he spent three quarters of his life, starting as a student. Now 69, Babi joined the college as an English teacher in 1963, before becoming the housemaster and thereafter the principal. He resigned from the post in April 2008 under a cloud of controversy, following his disagreement with the trustees over the issue of management.

For his students though, it is irrelevant. Cutting across age and professions, they will congregate in Ahmedabad on Sunday to honour him.

Babi enthuses not only love but adoration from his students, who believe that there could not be better purpose of the alumni meet, first time after his resignation — to affirm their love for him.

Kumar Shah, the owner of Vadodara Samachar, a Gujarati daily based in Vadodara said: "He has gone through thick and thin in his life but has always come out smilingly. He was a prince and gave up the throne to teach. He was a mentor and an ideal father to every child in the college."

The college is one of the oldest princely schools in western India. The college had on its roll most of the royal children of the region, training them not only in academics but also extra-curricular activities.

Chandan Nath, president of the Mudra Group industries, who is co-ordinating the event, said: "He was my hockey coach. I remember him pushing us hard and leading us. I owe a lot to him for what I am today."

Another former student, Punjawala, who is now the principal of Sunshine School in Ahmedabad said: "He was my housemaster and I shared a great equation with him. He was a friend to everyone but at the same time a strict teacher too. He instilled discipline and a sense of perfection in all his students."

Now leading a quiet retired life in Rajkot, Babi is touched by his students' gesture. "I feel elated. It feels good that the students are showing appreciation for their old teacher," said Babi, looking forward to the Sunday function.

The Old Boys, meanwhile, would rather not comment on their mentor's controversial resignation, saying they just want to honour their teacher whom they love dearly. "This is an initiative by the alumni. It is a private function. The college management will not be present at the event," said Nath, adding that the alumnus official website www.rkcalumni.com will be also launched on the occasion.

Heading: Hearing in Ahmedabad blasts case to be held in-camera now - Indian Express
Content:
DCB looks to establish role of Delhi blast accused in the Ahmedabad blasts

In an in-camera proceeding, the designated Metropolitan Court hearing the Ahmedabad blasts case on Thursday remanded 16 accused, including Mufti Mohammad Abu Bashar, Sajid Mansuri and Abbas Sameja, to police custody till October 16.

The latest remand of the accused comes in the case registered under the Ramol police station in connection with the blast that took place near Hatekeshwar Circle.

In its remand application, the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) said that the custody of the accused was necessary to gather information about the planting of the bomb. The DCB is also looking to establish the role of the Delhi blasts accused in the Ahmedabad serial blasts based on the initial findings in the Delhi case.

The role of Afzal Usmani, arrested by the Mumbai police, with that of the accused is also under the scanner. The DCB has also sought remand on the ground that Usmani was present in the city on July 26, the day of the blasts and had links with the accused. The investigating agency is looking to find out more about Usmani's connection to the accused.

In line with its earlier remand applications, the DCB has also said that it needs to find out from the accused more about the various meetings of the banned SIMI held in the state.

The DCB had arrested Zahid Sheikh, Imran Sheikh, Sajid Mansuri, Iqbal Sheikh, Samsuddin Sheikh, Yunus Mansuri, Gyasuddin Ansari, Arif Kagzi and Usman Agabattiwala, along with Bashir on August 17. Abbas Sameja, Naved Kadri, Aiyaz, Saiyeed, Javed Ahmed, Salim Siphai and Ashok Kabira were arrested on September 4.

The accused were earlier sent in police custody in connection with the blasts at the Civil Hospital, Manninagar, Khadia and Naroda Gam.

Heading: Bond with the Waste: Ankleshwar plant awarded for medicine feat - Indian Express
Content:
Magsitrate's decision takes both defence and accused by surprise

Metropolitan Magistrate G M Patel's decision to turn the proceeding of the Ahmedabad blast case in-camera on Thursday surprised both defence lawyers and kin of the accused. For, it came three days before the scheduled hearing of an application filed by the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) requesting the same.

Patel's decision came at the start of a remand hearing involving 16 accused, including Mufti Mohammad Abu Bashar and Sajid Mansuri. Only advocates representing the accused, special public prosecutors and police officers were allowed to be present in the court.

Hashim Qureshi, representing six of the accused, said: "There was no need for an in-camera proceeding. This is not the trial stage of the case. Investigation is going on and no chargesheet has been filed as yet. No evidence collected in-camera at this stage can be made admissible at the trial stage. This has turned a public court into a private court."

I M Munshi, another advocate representing the accused, said: "Though the court has discretionary powers to take such a decision, there was no hurry for this. The hearing on the application was just a few days ahead. Also, nothing untoward had happened in the court to demand it. The hearings were being conducted peacefully."

Relatives of the accused see the court's decision to keep the proceedings closed against the interest of the accused.

A family member of one of the accused said, "First, the court does not allow our lawyers to meet him in the absence of police. Now, we cannot see what happens in the court."

Contrary to this, the special public prosecutors appearing in the case said the order was necessary as this is a crucial stage of investigation and also for the security of the accused as it is not possible to keep tab on all the persons coming in an open court.

The DCB had submitted an application under Section 44 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, on Wednesday, requesting in-camera proceedings in the case.

The DCB had cited security of the accused and protection of witnesses as ground for this.

Heading: Why are always we picked up for questioning? ask 2002 Panchmahals blast accused - Indian Express
Content:
The Ankleshwar plant of the German pigment company Heubach Limited has been honoured with the Indian Chemical Council's Acharya P C Ray Award by the government of Maharashtra for turning its toxic waste into medicine.

The plant has been awarded for developing indigenous technology for making pharmaceutical-grade ammonium hydroxide, which can be used as antacid. Group Captain (Retd), A G Chitre, Director of the Ankleshwar plant, who received the honour from Maharashtra Governor S C Jamir on September 7, said the treatment of the wastes started in 2000. The research and development team of 35 skilled experts realised that the storage of toxic residues will get overfilled and cause environmental damage. Now, around 1,500 metric tonnes of ammonia hydroxide is produced per year out of the 32,000 MT of sludge produced, he said.

"While producing around three tonnes of the green pigment, we are left with about 13 tonnes of the toxic sludge, which mainly comprises ammonium chloride and copper sulphate. The research and development team suggested that we could treat ammonium chloride and produce pharma-grade ammonium hydroxide," added Chitre. Of the 32,000 metric tonnes produced by the company, Chitre said that around 70-80 per cent of the sludge is treated at the plant.

On the other hand, the residual copper sulphate is used to extract copper and sold to local retailers, he said. "We have pharmaceutical companies around the country, who buy the ammonium hydroxide. It is sold as antacids, commonly suggested to patients with digestive problems. Copper is extracted and sold to local retailers, while some of it is stored," said Chitre. Since the inception of the treatment facility for the toxic sludge, the company has been able to add another Rs 6 crore per year to the company's turnover. "The Rs 6 crore is generated from treatment by default as we do not market the ammonia hydroxide, but have fixed retailers who buy it from us," he added.

Heading: Pious threads move NHRC to liberate manual scavengers - Indian Express
Content:
Six people picked up by the Ahmedabad Crime Branch for questioning in the Modasa blasts case, returned to Godhra on Thursday evening. Panchmahals Deputy Superintendent of Police, R V Asari, who is now probing the Modasa blasts along with the Ahmedabad Crime Branch, said the six persons rounded up for questioning, had come with a history. "They are the same persons who had been accused in the 2002 bombings that took place at several places in Panchmahals district. We rounded them for questioning so as to figure out where they were during the blasts," said Asari. Meanwhile, Mohammed Yousuf Giteli, one of those who were picked up by the Ahmedabad Crime Branch, told Newsline that the repeated questioning was an embarrassment for him and his family. "I am summoned whenever there is a problem in the city or the district. It makes me feel like a criminal," said Giteli, an employee of the Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited. Giteli, runs English and Gujarati medium schools.

Asari said they had instructions for picking up all the six whose role had come under the scanner in the 2002 bomb blasts case in Panchmahals.

On October 6, the Ahmedabad Crime Branch had picked up Hussain Ada, Mohammed Yousuf Giteli, Bilal Hayat, Mugni Hayat, Mobin Gora and Amir Ahmed Inderji for questioning. According to the law, an FIR will be lodged against any person found in possession of counterfeit currency.

Heading: State Cong accuses Modi of running away with Nano credit - Indian Express
Content:
After receiving rakhis, national commission sends notices to authorities in two districts

After receiving rakhis from manual scavengers with a plea to liberate them from their traditional occupation, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has issued notices to at least two district authorities of Gujarat, and sought a report on the status of manual scavenging in the state.

This comes at the back of manual scavengers sending rakhis to MLAs, district collectors and other government officials with the same plea on this year's Independence Day. Newsline had reported this on August 14.

In its September 6 notice to the district magistrates and police superintendents of Rajkot and Surendranagar, the NHRC has asked to submit a report on the issue within four weeks. It has further said that "in default, the Commission may proceed to take such action as it deems proper."

Both district collectors were, however, categorical in denying the existence of manual scavenging in their respective districts. "Our officials have visited the area from where the rakhis were sent, but there is nothing of that sort happening there," said Surendranagar Collector JD Bhad. "We have already sent our reply to the NHRC. There is no manual scavenging happening in the entire district," he added.

Rajkot Collector HS Patel said that while the practice of manually cleaning human waste is a thing of past in Gujarat, he has still sought a report from the DDO in this regard.

"Such complaints are filed by vested interests. We shall reply to the notice once we get the report from the DDO," he said.

According to the state government, at present there are nearly 60,000 sanitary workers (read manual scavengers) in Gujarat, out of which, around 12,000 were rehabilitated by 2007. The government was also pulled up by the National Commission for Safai Karmacharis in June this year for failing to protect the sanitary workers from occupational hazards, which often prove fatal.

"There is no other alternative, but to do this dirty job," said Madhu Purbiya from Vichhiya village of Jasdan taluka, Rajkot, one of the women who had sent rakhi to the NHRC. "I received a letter from the NHRC too. I still clean the open toilets manually, as there is just no other way I can earn bread for my family," she added.

"Our father passed away four years ago and we are yet to get his pension. My younger brother is studying, while I work as a casual labourer, with no fixed income," said Munna, Madhu's son.

Referring to the caste system, Manjula Pradeep, Director Navsarjan, a pan-Gujarat Dalit rights organisation, said: "While manual scavenging is intricately linked to caste based occupation, in rural areas, society does not leave any room for a person from the lowest rung of society to opt for some other occupation other than his/ her pre-determined profession."

Heading: Textile worker stabbed to death - Indian Express
Content:
The state Congress party has accused the Narendra Modi government of misrepresentation and taking the entire credit for Nano's entry into Gujarat.

State Congress party spokesman Arjun Modhwadia said: "The recent huge welcome given to Nano by the BJP and the huge incentives given to the Tatas by the state government is creating a wrong impression. It's as if the Tatas will provide the Nano free to all Gujaratis."

He said they are not against the entry of Nano into Gujarat. "We welcome the Tatas into the state, but the way Modi has presented the entire issue and taken the credit is not welcome. The state government has provided precious land of the Agriculture University to the Tatas at a negligible price," said Modhwadia.

He said the incentive given to the big industries should be given to local small and medium scale industries that are on the verge of extinction.

The saree printing industries of Jetpur, automobile and engineering industries of Rajkot, textile and diamond industries of Surat and north Gujarat should be encouraged instead of these corporate houses, he said.

These small and medium scale industries have not been given any special incentive by the state government. Even those benefits which the Congress government had earlier given to them were withdrawal by this government. Instead of giving the Tatas land near Sanand, the government should have provided them with land near some small town or city so that they could also grow, he added.

Modhwadia further said that the Opposition was not taken into confidence by the BJP when negotiations took place between the state government and Tata Motors.

He said all industries coming to the state should learn from the Tatas' bitter experience in Singur. "They should first take people into confidence before establishing their business. They should not consider only the approval of the ruling political party."

Modhwadia further said: "Earlier, the Congress brought many industries like Reliance refinery to Jamnagar and General Motors to Halol, but never took the credit or publicised them like Modi."

Heading: Diagnostic packages now in Gujarat hospital, too - Indian Express
Content:
A 19-year-old textile worker was stabbed to death in a textile firm at Moghrawadi in Udhna Magdalla Road early on Thursday morning. Police suspect internal dispute to be the cause of the murder.

Amar Hariram, hailing from Orissa, was found dead in a pool of blood at the supervisor's room of the textile unit by some labourers.

According to the police, Amar had joined the Jariwala firm just about a month ago and had settled in Surat to earn a living. He used to live alone in a room at Udhna Magadalla Road, and sent home the money he earned.

The firm's owner, Chandrakant Jariwala, lodged a case with the Umra police station.

Umra police inspector R S Patel said: "Amar was regular in his duties and had no conflict with other employees. On Wednesday night, there were 13 textile operators in the unit. On Wednesday, Amar left his machine and went to the first floor of the building where two other labourers were working. We have taken their statements."

The body has been sent to New Civil Hospital for post-mortem examination, police said.

Heading: PG students will prepare their teachers’ report card - Indian Express
Content:
The Vadilal Sarabhai General Hospital has become the first public sector hospital in Gujarat to offer total diagnostic facilities in a package form at affordable rates.

The hospital launched two packages, basic and executive, on Thursday.

Hospital Superintendent Dr M H Makwana said there would be two tariffs chargeable for diagnosis. Under the basic package, the hospital would charge Rs 450 for the check-up and the subsequent follow-up process. The executive package would entail payment of Rs 1,100 and would have a few more tests on offer, he said.

"The objective is to provide expert diagnostic facility to patients under one roof and follow-up action by senior doctors who will also offer their advice in the light of the reports," he said.

Registration will be open on all working days of the week, while the tests would be carried out on Tuesdays and Thursdays, he said. The basic package offers blood test, blood glucose, blood pressure, x- ray and cardiogram among others.

The executive package will include 2D echo cardiogram, pulmonary tests, thyroid, liver, kidney and calcium level tests, he said. The registration will be done on the first floor office of the resident medical officer.

When queried, Dr Makwana said patients are free to avail of the package and get further treatment done in other hospitals as well.

Heading: Over 300 colleges, more than 2.5 lakh students, yet only 4 hockey teams in GU! - Indian Express
Content:
Students of Gujarat-based universities might soon have the privilege of assessing the performance of their teachers; which was, of late provided only by higher institutes such as the IIMs.

Following the Chadha Pay Review Committee recommendations — endorsing the pattern of students assessing the teaching style of teachers; this evaluation might be followed in all the universities of Gujarat and India.

All India Federation of University and College Teachers' Organisation (AIFUCTO) and Gujarat State Federation of University and College Teachers Associations (GSFUCA) have given their consent to following the protocol. AIFUCTO will also organise a three-day meeting from October 17 onwards to discuss the Chadha Pay Review Committee recommendations and the multiple evaluation scheme, at its meeting in Bangalore.

Incidentally, AIFUCTO treasurer Nikhil Desai is from the Geology faculty of M S University (MSU). He said many teachers from Gujarat will be participating in the meeting.

Commenting on the aspect of students evaluating the teachers, Desai said: "I support this kind of evaluation provided it is done by post-graduate students. The general understanding is that there are more students at the under graduate level, which reduces the chances of quality. But this pattern of assessment could be followed at the PG level."

He said teachers owe a lot to society given the hefty salary they draw, but such parameters of evaluations should be set properly.

In the same vein, Prof Thomas Joseph from AIFUCTO told Newsline: "Similar recommendations were made by the Rastogi Pay Review Committee in 1996, but nothing concrete came out of it. Though we support the students' evaluation programme, there should be a plan set up by the UGC."

GSFUCA president K S Shastri made yet another point on this issue. He said: "Though, one will like to go ahead with this pattern, I will suggest that there should be some objective in devising the pattern of evaluation, the reason being that there could be biases from the teachers' side also."

Heading: Man killed over money dispute - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat University (GU) may be the biggest university in the state, but when it comes to contributing players for the hockey teams, it stands nowhere. There are over 300 GU affiliated colleges with more than 2.5 lakh students, but the number of hockey teams is just four!

This is despite the fact that every year each student pays Rs 20 to the GU and their respective colleges as gymkhana and sports fees. But if the officials are to be believed, the funds are not used suitably to revive the sport, in which India remained unbeaten at the Olympics from 1928 to 1956.

"Only the Gujarat College in Ahmedabad has a proper and good hockey ground. We will not find a hockey ground even in the GU campus that spends lakhs for uplifting and upgrading sports other than the national game," a senior official of the Sports Authority of Gujarat told Newsline.

"There are no doubts that the craze towards hockey is fading with each passing day. Also, the budget which the GU and colleges gets for the development of hockey in the state is not being utilised properly," said N J Chaniyara of the Physical Education Department, H L College of Commerce.

He added: "The authorities are not doing much to promote hockey even at the school level. Due to this, we are unable to find sportspersons who want to take up hockey as a career."

Jwalant Bhatt, senior hockey coach, Gujarat College, feels the biggest problem that the game is facing today is that most players do not have access to opportunities. "There is a need to make the players independent and self-respected," he added.

Dharmashih Desai, Secretary, Ahmedabad Zonal Local Sports Committee, said the university appoints several hockey coaches but "they are not asked to do any work."

He added: "They do everything except coaching. They are not interested and the GU is also not paying attention towards improvising the situation."

Partiv Raj, vice president of Gujarat unit of the National Students' Union of India, said that instead of spending money on the promotion of hockey, colleges spend money on fashion shows and dance shows.

"It is shameful not only for colleges, but also for GU. The future of hockey in the GU affiliated colleges is in danger," he added.

Heading: Jaipur blast accused produced before court - Indian Express
Content:
A 31-year-old man was killed by a group of six people over a property dispute in the Gota area late on Wednesday. The Sarkhej police have registered a case of murder and investigations are on to nab the accused who are at large.

The deceased has been identified as Mayurdhwajsinh Dahiya, a resident of Jivraj Park area. Dahiya had a business of weighing machines.

Dahiya's friend Dhavalgiri Goswami, who lodged the complaint, has named Prakash Bharwad, Salim Chichak, Mahesh Bharwad, Jayanti Ahir, Manav Shrimali and Dharmendra Sharma as the accused in the case. Inspector G D Trivedi, who is investigating the case, said that Sharma, a land broker and a small time builder, is the main accused. He said that Sharma had a real estate business at Hathijan village on the outskirts of Ahmedabad and had convinced Dahiya to invest in it.

"Dahiya had booked 10 flats and paid Rs 10 lakh for the same as advance to Sharma. Later, Dahiya realised that the property is disputed and a civil court had banned any construction there," Trivedi added.

Following this, Dahiya demanded his money back from Sharma. The police said that Dahiya had talked roughly to Sharma over the phone on Wednesday morning and asked him to return the amount that night.

"After dinner, Dahiya was standing at a pan shop in the Gota area with some friends when some of Sharma's men called him up and asked him to meet them to clear his due. After some time they came to the area and attacked him with a sharp-edged weapon and fled from the scene," Trivedi said.

Dahiya was first taken to the Sola Civil Hospital, where doctors referred him to the SAL Hospital. But he died on his way to the SAL Hospital, said the police.

Heading: Over 400 radio experts to chant ‘Ham sab ustaad hain’ from Oct 11 - Indian Express
Content:
Jaipur blast case accused Mehandi Hasan and Atiq-Ur-Rehman, who have been brought to the city on a transfer warrant, were produced before the designated Metropolitan Court on Thursday.

They will be produced before the court again on Friday when the initial 24 hours of their arrest by the Gujarat Police comes to an end.

The Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) has brought the two here to probe into their alleged role in the Ahmedabad serial blasts.

The Rajasthan Police had arrested the two on August 27. They are said to have harboured Sajid Mansuri, a key accused in the Ahmedabad blasts, in Jaipur during the planning of the blasts.

Heading: Terror is the leitmotif of this year’s Ramlila - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat Institute of Amateur Radio is hosting HamfestIndia to showcase innovative techniques of communication

To popularise Ham radio activities in the state, over 400 Ham Radio operators from across the country will participate in a two-day national event, HamfestIndia, from October 11.

The Gujarat Institute of Amateur Radio (GIAR) will organise the event wherein the operators will demonstrate innovative techniques of radio communication, and also present their technical papers.

Engineering students, particularly those studying communication and information technology have been invited to attend the event.

Principal Secretary (Forests) and GIAR Chairman S K Nanda said that Gujarat Assembly Speaker Ashok Bhatt will inaugurate the event, while Governor Nawal Kishore Sharma will chair the concluding ceremony the next day.

He added that there about 600 licensed Ham radio operators in the state, with the majority of them being senior government officials.

Nanda said though Ham radio activity is increasingly being taken as 'a scientific hobby' by the locals, it has emerged as 'a life-saving means' of communication during natural calamities like earthquakes, cyclones and floods.

It has helped in keeping communication lines open when other means of communications have collapsed, he said.

About 60 Ham radio sets have been installed at the city-based GIAR premises. Here, the youths have free access to use them and also learn about its technical aspects. Nanda said: "The learners are even provided with all the necessary study materials needed to become a Ham radio operator," adding that GIAR is also associated to the Gujarat State Disaster Management Authority. (GSDMA).

GIAR Joint Secretary P C Valera said about two years ago the government had directed the Revenue Department to ensure that a Ham Radio station is set up in each of the district collector's office across Gujarat.

He said while this is yet to be implemented, the European Commission has provided funds of Rs 86 lakh for the same.

Heading: LPG cylinder blast injures couple - Indian Express
Content:
The series of bomb blasts in the country in the recent past has left a deep impact on people's minds. This is apparent in the themes that are being selected for Ramlila in Vadodara.

Northern India Cultural Association, which manages the Ramlila committee in the city, has selected terrorism as the theme for this year's Ramlila to be staged during Dussehra, the last day of Navratri.

"We have selected the theme of terrorism to make people aware about the growing menace," said Shashikant Das, director of Drama Forum Club, a part of the Ramlila committee.

To lay stress on the message of communal harmony, the role of Lakshman is being played by Abid Sheikh.

"It gives me immense pleasure to play Lakshman's role. It is a very interesting experience as I am going to give a special message to people of all the communities," said Sheikh, a resident of Mirza Colony at Akota. He added: "My family has no problems. In fact, some people of my community appreciated me for playing Lakshman's role." Ramlila, with the new theme, will display how Lord Ram manages to tackle the evil called terrorism.

The 80-odd actors have been practicing for nearly a month for the Ramlila.

Heading: City celebrates Dussehra - Indian Express
Content:
A Couple sustained injuries when an LPG cylinder leakage caused a blast and fire at a bungalow in the Nava Vadaj area late on Wednesday.

Mehul Patel (32) and his wife Kinjal (30) were admitted to the Gujarat Burns Hospital for treatment.

Residents of Bungalow no. 4 of Lav-Kush Society, near Vyas Vadi, the couple had gone to watch garba. A leak in the rubber pipe allowed the gas to fill the entire house. Deputy Chief Fire Officer Rajesh Bhatt said an external spark may have caused the blast and the subsequent fire.

Ahmedabad Fire and Emergency Services (AFES) had to rush to the house to extinguish the fire.

Heading: Sangat darshan begins today, MLAs expect booty from CM - Indian Express
Content:
City celebrated the festival of Dussehra with enthusiasm and gaiety on Thursday. The festival was celebrated at more than 15 locations in the city and was attended by people from all religions. Conveying the message of good over evil, the effigies of Ravana, Meghnath and Kumbhkarana were set on fire.

At the historical Daresi ground, the effigy of Ravana was set on fire with his golden palace in Lanka. Deputy Speaker of Punjab Vidhan Sabha, Satpal Gosain pressed the button of a remote control to set the effigy on fire. The 75-feet effigy caught fire from the right side and soon the fire spread in the remaining portion.

Sumer Singh Gurjer, Deputy Commissioner Ludhiana, was the chief guest on the occasion. Senior Superintendent of Police, R K Jaiswal Ludhiana distributed the prizes to the artistes. Metal detectors were installed at entry points and police teams were deployed at various places to keep a strict vigil in the area. The ground wore a festive look with swings and stalls of food items and toys.

Shri Durga Mandir Committee Urban Estate, Dugri Road Phase-1 celebrated the festival with pomp and show. Main attractions were religious tableaus related to Ramayana, as most of the participants were children and youths.

At Bhai Randhir Singh Nagar, the Ramlila Committee organised the Dussera mela. The epic battle between Lord Rama and Ravana was also performed. Crackers were burst and dolas (big balloons carrying fire) were released in the air.

Many people were carrying children on their shoulders to show them the glimpses of burning effigies.

Shri Dushehra Committee Kitchlu Nagar, Urban Estate Phase-11, Upkar nagar, Focal Point, Agar Nagar, Jamalpur, Pakhowal Road also celebrated the festival with enthusiasm and thousands of people participated in the festival.

Heading: Playing around with monkeys? Be ready to face action - Indian Express
Content:
Project proposals worth Rs 200 crore have been sent to Badal

Stage is set for ten-day sangat darshan of Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal in Ludhiana, beginning from tomorrow.

Proposals of projects worth Rs 200 crores have been sent to Badal and MLAs are expecting handsome grants from the CM for development works in undeclared areas, slums, schools, roads and sewer system. The residents of undeclared areas, which are not notified in the municipal records, have pinned great hopes on the CM who will hold sangat darshan for 10 ten days in the city. Civic officials are busy making the last minute arrangements such as beautifying the roads and cleaning the areas where the CM will pay a visit.

On Friday, he will visit 10 wards of Dakha constituency of MLA Darshan Singh Shivalik to listen to the complaints of masses.

Shivalik told the Newsline: "My constituency has a number of wards in outer areas of the city and more than 20 colonies are not yet declared due to which corporation is not providing water and sewerage facilities in these areas."

He added, "As per the rules, the civic body can undertake projects only in the declared areas. Once we receive grants from the CM, we will be able to spend money in undeclared areas and resolve the problems of masses."

The MLA also said, "Community centres, cremation grounds, parks and various other projects are urgently required in these areas. A detailed project report has already been submitted to the CM. We need an investment of over Rs 50 crore in the projects."

Of the 10 wards in Shivalik's constituency, two belong to Congress councillors and rest to the SAD-BJP councillors. Badal will travel from Ferozepur Road to areas like Haibowal, Shimlapuri, and BRS Nagar to listen to the people's complaints.

Sangat Darshan in Harish Rai Dhanda's ward will be held on October 11. He told the Newsline: "I have submitted proposals of projects worth Rs 40 crore including upgradation of three government schools, facelift of Ambedkar Nagar, strengthening of sewer system and renovating the dairy complex."

Heading: Adhya murder: accused face charges of destroying evidence - Indian Express
Content:
Call it the impact of Monkey God Hanuman on Dusshera. Monkeys havefound some saviours in the city. Cape India, an NGO for animal welfare, has taken a strict note of a recent television advertisement of Punjab state lotteries in which monkeys are shown to be performing in public.

In a letter to principal secretary (finance) and director Punjab state lotteries, Cape India authorities said the performances of five animals— lion, tiger, panther, monkey and bear— are banned as per the notification dated October 14, 1998 issued by the Government of India.

The letter asks the director to immediately stop the telecast of the advertisement.

Cape India official D Rajasekar said: "The Centre has notified the Performing Animals (Registration) Rules, 2001 under Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, which says that any animal used for public performance has to be registered with the Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI)."

He added: "Before using any animal for a performance in any serial, feature film or advertisement, a person should first apply to the AWBI for pre-shoot permission."

After shooting, the stills and clippings of the performing animals should be submitted for post-shoot approval of the Board," Rajasekar added. Only after receipt of a No Objection Certificate from the Board, such films or serials can be telecasted, he said. Rajasekar also claimed that no such permission was sought for the present advertisement.

Cape India has asked the government to take action against the officials who had violated the rules.

Heading: Two more train robbers arrested - Indian Express
Content:
The Ludhiana police are yet to make any headway into Vinod Adhya's murder case. The police have not been able to recover neither his body nor any of his belongings in the Sidhwan canal. He was last seen with some unknown persons near the canal on August 12 evening and had gone missing since then.

A police officer said if the police had recovered even a single belonging of Adhya in the canal, it would have established that the industrialist was killed and dumped in the canal.

The police have now discontinued the search operations in the canal and are planning to register a case of destruction of evidence against the three accused- Balwinder Singh, Harminder Singh and Satnam Singh- all residents of Faridkot. A police officer said, "The chances of retrieving the body from the canal are very slim. Therefore the police have decided to lodge a case under Section 201 of the IPC."

The police said the muddy waters of Sidhwa canal posed a major obstruction in recovering the body. Superintendent of Police (City-2) Gurmeet Singh Randhawa said, "We are waiting for the canal water to recede, after which we will resume the search operations."

Heading: CMCH holds eye camp to celebrate World Sight Day - Indian Express
Content:
The General Railway Police (GRP) arrested two robbers, Jeetu and Deepu, on Thursday. They are accused of looting the passengers in the Amritsar-Saharsa Express, popularly called the Jansadharan Express, on September 24. Four mobile phones and Rs 30,000 were recovered from the accused.

Gurnam Singh, Station House Officer, GRP, said, "The duo has been sent to two-day police remand." Of the five persons suspected to have committed the train robbery, the police had already arrested Suraj and Amit, while the mastermind, Bambaiya, is still absconding.

Heading: Protest held against write-up in magazine - Indian Express
Content:
The Department of Ophthalmology, Christian Medical College and Hospital, in collaboration with Orbis International, celebrated the World Sight Day here on Thursday.

The theme for this year was 'Eyes on the future: fighting vision impairment in later life.'

A special free eye camp was organised in which 328 patients were screened and 59 were selected for free operations. Medicines were also provided free-of-cost.

The programme was inaugurated by the chief guest, Dr Abraham G. Thomas, Director, CMCH. He appreciated the efforts of the eye department in reaching out to the weaker sections of the society and providing free comprehensive eye care through the mobile eye services for the last 50 years.

The guest of honour was Dr S.K.Chopra, former professor and head of the Department of Ophthalmology, CMC & H. He elaborated various ocular conditions affecting older population. He said that 80% of people living with blindness were over 50 years of age.

Other dignitaries present on the occasion were Dr Sunil Singh, Principal, Dr Kanwal Masih, Medical Superintendent, and Dr S.M. Bhatti, Professor of Department of Ophthalmology.

Heading: Manch activists burn effigy of Amar Singh - Indian Express
Content:
Press Movement Anti-Crime and Corruption Society on Wednesday observed a "black day" by tying black bands on their arms to protest against a write up about Lord Shiva, which has appeared in a Hindi magazine.

After burning the copies of the Hindi magazine, Hemraj Jindal, president of the society, who was leading a protest rally near Sanglan Wala Shiwala, said, "The Hindi magazine has carried an article about Lord Shiva and hurt the sentiments by writing that Shivlingam is wastage of milk and water. It has also been written that in the month of "sawan," people waste thousands of litres of milk on Shivlangam and also waste a lot of money on donations to pandits." While the priest of Sanglanwala Shiwala said, "Nobody has the right to hurt the religious sentinments of Hindus. There should be strict action against the writer."

Hemraj Jindal said the society members would gherao the Chief Minister's house if no action was taken in the matter.

Heading: Dengue spreading but primary kids still wearing shorts - Indian Express
Content:
Activists of Rashtriya Hindu Manch burnt the effigy of Amar Singh, general secretary of the Samajwadi Party, for his statement on Jamia Nagar police encounter. Raising slogans against Amar Singh, O.P. Tripatthi, general secretary of the Manch, said, "Amar Singh should be hanged for making this statement, and POTA law should be implemented."

He said that by giving a hurting statement about inspector Mohan Chand Sharma, who sacrificed his life for the nation, Amar Singh was encouraging terrorists.

Appreciating inspector Mohan Chand Sharma, he said, "Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma's encounter with the terrorists unearthed a strong terrorist network, which helped in saving thousands of lives. The Central government should arrest Amar Singh after filing a case against him." The protesting members included Parveen Sehgal, Rajinder Parashar and Vipan Bhardwaj.

Heading: Diamond jewellery collection launched - Indian Express
Content:
The patients suffering from dengue are still pouring into the city hospitals and clinics. The doctors are advising residents keep their body parts covered to keep off the dengue threat. But majority of the city schools are still continuing with summer uniform for primary children.

The students of primary schools are still wearing shorts and full sleeve shirts. The parents find it risky to send their wards to school in shorts as Aedes mosquito, which spreads dengue, remains active during the day time.

Aradhana Bhanot, mother of two school-going children, said, "As dengue spreads every year, the schools should allow primary children to wear trousers of summer stuff."

The school authorities however say that they can not start winter uniform right now as weather is too hot. "The weather is also very unpredictable. In the morning, it is little cold and after some hours, it becomes too hot. If we start winter uniform, the students will have rashes by wearing woolen stuff in this weather. So we have asked the students to wear full sleeve shirts with shorts."

Dr Vandana Shahi, principal of BCM School, Dugri, said, "We have given an option to parents to send their wards in summer either in shorts or pants of summer uniform. Last year, I made it compulsory while keeping in view the dengue outbreak. But parents did not appreciate the idea saying that it was difficult for them to arrange the summer uniform trousers immediately. So I have given them option."

Meanwhile, the schools which give no such option to the parents find it unsafe to send their wards in shorts while the dengue is spreading fast.

Heading: Animal welfare our prime concern: GADVASU V-C - Indian Express
Content:
Kirtilals, Gold and Diamond Jewellery has launched its "Karuva Chauth diamond jewellery collection". The collection would be available from October 10 to 16 at its Ludhiana store.

In addition to this, Karuva Chauth double bonanza offer has also been announced where customers who purchase at Kirtilal's Ludhiana store have a chance to participate in the lucky draw contest and win Rs1 lakh worth diamond necklace. Also, Kirtilals in association with All India Gems and Jewellery Trade Federation, supported by World Gold Council, is offering Lucky Lakshmi Contest - 2008 where customers can participate in the lucky draw and can win a lot of exciting gifts like gold bars, cars and laptops.

Heading: Decks cleared for Sarangpur Education City - Indian Express
Content:
