The move comes amid concerns over the softening TV advertising market and lower ratings for Hollywood's biggest event of the year.

"The revenue from the show fuels our programs all over the world," Academy President Sid Ganis said. The academy generates more than $65 million a year in TV license fee revenue from Walt Disney Co.'s ABC television network and foreign channels.

"That's a lot of dough, and it's very important to us," Ganis said. "Since the show is a celebration of movies, why not let upcoming movies represent themselves in a way that is intelligent and smart and not offensive to anyone?"

The ban was put in place in the early 1950s, when the Academy Awards were first broadcast. At the time, the academy fretted that commercials for films during the show would be unseemly and viewers could conclude that the awards were influenced by the studios that bought the ads. In recent years, some —including ABC — have lobbied to reverse the prohibition.

"It's a perfect advertising venue for films," said George Belch, a marketing professor at San Diego State University. "The telecast delivers an audience that is very interested in movies, and that's the target audience that the studios want to reach."

Under the new rules, a studio will be allowed to buy only one 30- or 60-second spot in the show. However, a media company with multiple distribution arms could buy a commercial for each label. Ads for movies that are in contention for an award would not be permitted in the show. ABC will determine where the spots are to run.

Only newly created ads for movies will be accepted, and then only for films released the final Friday of April, or later. The Oscars will air Feb. 22.

Not lost on the academy was the success that pro football's Super Bowl has had driving up ad rates, in part by creating "event television" with splashy ads. More than a decade ago, Fox used the Super Bowl to launch a marketing campaign for its big-budget movie "Independence Day" with a catchy TV ad announcing, "This may be your last Super Bowl." In some years, there has been more buzz surrounding the innovative ads than the action on the field.

Heading: Meltdown hits G O P Congress chances - Indian Express
Content:
Two little men argue on a creaky stage, locked like electrons in orbit, while an actress wearing a powdered face and red lipstick lurks in the wings near a harried director who repeats "God willing" into a cellphone as the audience for the evening's performance gathers in the lobby, whiffs of perfume competing with the faint scent of gunpowder.

War in the streets, war in the wings; this is theatre in Baghdad. Suicide bombers explode, armoured vehicles creep down alleys, soldiers squint through barbed wire. But in the half-lighted theatre, amid worn velour seats and costume racks sparse in sequins and silk, director Haider Munathar runs through lines of a satirical comedy about nattering politicians and a lost king in a strange, violent yet hopeful country known as Iraq.

"Bring the King, Bring Him" opened a few days ago, hours after a car bomb shook the National Theater, crumpling the dressing room ceiling and bruising Zahra Beden, Munathar's wife, and another actress in the play. Munathar, who also stars as the king, worried that the attack would keep audiences away. But the crowds keep coming, braving the city's frequent explosions and horizon of curling smoke.

"We are working in an impossible situation," says Munathar, a slight man with a graying beard who moves with the mercurial trickery of a cartoon character. "But we just can't fold. We have to work. The curtain must keep going up.

"We were sold out the other night. The Iraqi people have pushed past their state of fear. Life is coming back."

Munathar says the play is the first at the National Theatre since the US-led invasion of 2003 to be performed after sunset — a time of day in the not so distant past when it was too dangerous to wander beyond one's neighborhood.

The play skewers the nation he loves. The two-act cabaret-style show, written by playwright Ali Hussein, portrays Iraqi politicians as petty, corrupt and detached from the people they govern. A scene in parliament shows legislators discussing the ozone layer, importing garlic seeds (there is no garlic in the play's Iraq) and increasing their salaries —everything but how to end bloodshed and rebuild Iraq.

"There is hope," Munathar says. We don't want people saying, 'God bless the old days.' They were the worst days and we don't want Iraqis imagining that they were better than today."

Heading: Hole in law lets Obama suck in big funds in small doses - Indian Express
Content:
The economic upheaval is threatening to topple Republican Congressional candidates, putting more Senate and House seats within Democratic reach less than a month before the elections, lawmakers and campaign strategists say.

Top campaign officials for both parties, pollsters and independent experts say the intense focus on the economic turmoil and last week's bailout vote have combined to rapidly expand a Democratic advantage in Congressional contests. Analysts now predict a Democratic surge on a scale that seemed unlikely just weeks ago, with even some Republicans in traditional strongholds fighting for their political careers, and Democratic leaders dreaming of ironclad majorities.

In North Carolina, Senator Elizabeth Dole, a former Republican presidential contender and cabinet member, is teetering. In Kentucky, the opponent of the Senate Republican leader, Mitch McConnell, has drawn even in some polls, though Republicans say they believe he will win.

Democrats say they feel confidently ahead in five Senate races where they hope to pick up Republican seats, and they believe their candidates are running competitively in seven more.

In the House, Democrats say they could capture a dozen of the 26 Republican seats left open by retirements, and challengers are closing in on Republican incumbents in Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Michigan, Nevada, New York and elsewhere.

"The last week has severely damaged Republican candidates," said Stuart Rothenberg, a nonpartisan analyst who predicts that Democrats could gain as many as six to nine Senate seats and 25 to 30 House seats. "Everything points to warning signals for Republicans."

If such projections are realised, it would push Senate Democrats tantalizingly close to the filibuster-proof 60-vote majority that has eluded Senate leaders since the late 1970s. While the environment could change again in the remaining weeks, recent polling suggests a fundamental shift, with Republicans absorbing more of the blame for the economic uncertainty.

At the same time, the political arms of Congressional Republicans are being outspent — their House organization recently borrowed $8 million — and have fewer targets, with only a handful of Democrats in Florida, Louisiana, New Hampshire, Pennsylvania, Texas and Wisconsin and in potential trouble.

Republicans are understandably nervous.

"There is no question the economic crisis, the great stimulus debate and the aftermath changed a playing field that had been improving to one that has become considerably more challenging," said Representative Tom Cole of Oklahoma, chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee.

Senator John Ensign of Nevada, chairman of the National Republican Senatorial Committee, said he was encouraging candidates to "stay positive" and "run like you are 10 points down," which in some cases they are. "You don't have to scare people this election cycle," Ensign said. "As far as our candidates, they know to take this seriously."

Strategists for both parties say Republican House and Senate candidates are being hurt by the dip in support for John McCain at the top of the ticket, frustrating Republicans who had initially viewed him as a strong asset who could appeal to independents and even moderate Democrats and protect Republicans in a tough year.

But the market volatility and perceived Democratic edge on handling the economy has evidently turned voters to Democrats, a view supported by one top adviser to Republican candidates.

"This financial crisis has provided momentum to Barack Obama and other Democrats, and their campaigns now have the wind at their backs," said the consultant, who asked not to be identified, speaking pessimistically about the Republican outlook.

Heading: Irritating, unstable Vista? There’re ways around it - Indian Express
Content:
Barack Obama's money machine is fueled by the likes of Martha Murphy, a granny who has donated 104 times for a total of $2,475.34.

Murphy has used her credit card to donate in amounts as small as $10. "It is amazing how it adds up," she said.

Obama has revolutionised campaign fundraising, employing the Internet to tap into more donors than any candidate in history. The campaign has reported $160 million in contributions from donors of $200 or less, more than a third of the $458 million raised. But as Obama sets records, his fundraising has come under scrutiny.

The Democratic candidate's donors also include "Derty Poiiuy," an individual with a scatological sense of humor who has given $950. "Mong Kong" has contributed $1,065 and lists an address in a nonexistent city. "Fornari USA" gave $800 and listed the address of an apparel store of that name near San Francisco.

The Republican National Committee filed a federal complaint this week, alleging that some of Obama's small donations are illegal because they come from foreign nationals or exceed the limit.

The contributions have also exposed a loophole in the law, which does not require disclosure of identities of donors who give $200 or less, making it impossible to determine whether they are legitimate without a federal audit.

Lawrence Norton, a former Federal Election Commission general counsel, said the law was written when "no one conceived that a candidate could raise millions" in such small amounts. "It certainly is a case where the 1970s law is not in step with current campaign fundraising practices," he said.

Exactly why a donor would use a name like Derty Poiiuy is not clear. "It's part of phenomenon that we've never seen before," FEC spokesman Bob Biersack said. People who make up names when donating to federal candidates violate laws against making false statements, but Biersack could not recall anyone being prosecuted for such a crime. "Odd names by themselves aren't enough. A lot of people have odd names," Biersack said. "I have certain sympathy for that."

Obama has returned a lot of the donations. "Every campaign faces the challenge of screening and reviewing its contributions," his spokesman Ben LaBolt said. "We have taken every step to make sure our contributions are appropriate."

Heading: Boxer shot after smoking row; killer gets 28 years - Indian Express
Content:
Consumers have had issues with Vista since its release in January 2007 - even though more than 140 million copies of the operating system have been sold so far. Taming Vista on my Intel chip-equipped Sony Vaio laptop became, after a while, a measure of maintaining patience, never mind sanity. But then, the fact is, Vista doesn't have to be as bad as the competing Apple ads say it is. Here are some ways to make your Vista experience more livable, and perhaps even more lovable.

Say farewell to the U A C

Among the features that many users found most annoying early on in Vista's life cycle was the user account control feature.

The U A C was meant to save newbie Web surfers from spyware and viruses that might otherwise install themselves on the hard drive. So, a warning box pops up on the screen every time a program or application is about to be installed: 'Windows needs your permission to continue.'

"Almost every other question I get was how to get rid of the U A C," said Karl L Gechlik, who fields such questions on his Web site, www.asktheadmin.com.

Microsoft now allows you to turn off U A C permanently if you have a newer version of Vista, or have downloaded the Service Pack 1 release. If you haven't downloaded Service Pack 1 yet, do it at www.tinyurl.com/55k8a4; the upgrade fixes a host of bugs with Vista.

Add memory

Vista is a memory hog. Microsoft says a computer running Vista needs 512 MB or more of random access memory. In the real world, a gigabyte of RAM is a more realistic minimum. Two GB is better.

Adding RAM isn't brain surgery. Nor is it outrageously expensive, but installation is best left to an expert. If you are a D I Y type, you can search Google for 'Installing more RAM'.

Give Vista a boost

With a flash memory device — a USB flash drive, CompactFlash or SD card — of at least 256 MB, you can make the PC use data faster. Plugged into a USB port or media reader, the memory device serves as an additional memory cache. (The more memory the better, up to 4 GB.) After the device is inserted, Vista asks you if you want to use it to improve performance. You can choose to allocate part of the card or drive's memory to what Microsoft calls ReadyBoost and use the remainder to store files.

Use only what you need

You may think you have only the Firefox browser running, but Vista starts a host of programs every time you start it. And they all use the computer's memory.

Go to Control Panel. Click Uninstall a Program and in the Tasks pane on the left, click Turn Windows Features On or Off. You should see a checklist of the programs. Hover the cursor over each entry and a pop-up box tries to explain what it is. Uncheck the ones you do not need. This does not remove them from your PC; it just turns them off.

Make Vista uglier

Vista makes your PC's desktop prettier, but uses a lot of memory to throw widgets on the side of the screen and make icons transparent. Go back to Control Panel, this time to Personalisation. Disable the transparency feature by removing the checkmark on Enable Transparency. Click the Performance and System Tools tab, and click Adjust Visual Effects. Click Adjust For Best Performance.

There are more ways to make Vista run faster. Microsoft has other tricks at www.tinyurl.com/5a439r.

Heading: Terror hits Pak terror-fight hub - Indian Express
Content:
A gunman was jailed for at least 28 years on Thursday for the murder of a former boxing champion who had asked a group of men to stop smoking in a bar. Kanyanta Mulenga, 23, was given a life sentence at the Old Bailey after being found guilty of killing James Oyebola, 46, in Fulham, west London, in July 2007.

This was nothing short of a brutal killing carried out for the most trivial of reasons, judge Peter Rook said, according to the Press Association.

Oyebola, who was shot in the neck and leg, died in hospital four days after the shooting when doctors switched off his life-support machine. The father of three had been asking people to stop smoking in the garden area of the bar, which counted as enclosed premises because it had a retracting roof.

Police said Mulenga and his friends sauntered away from the scene after the shooting, with one of them grabbing a bottle of vodka from the bar on their way out.

The defendant chose the cowardly option of pulling a gun on James over something as minor as smoking a cigarette, said Detective Inspector Steve Horsley, of the Metropolitan Police, who led the investigation.

Oyebola's family said the killing was pointless and had changed their lives.

"The late great Dr Martin Luther King Jr. once said 'Let no man pull you low enough to hate him'. We do not hate this young man found guilty; on the contrary we feel sorry for both him and his family," their statement said.

Oyebola won the British heavyweight title in 1994 and the bronze medal at the 1986 Commonwealth Games in Edinburgh, where he lost to Lennox Lewis in the semi-finals.

Two other men who were in the bar were cleared of murder after agreeing to give evidence for the prosecution.

Heading: In first editorial, Rane thanks Thackeray - Indian Express
Content:
Weeks after carrying out a bloody suicide bombing in the heart of Pakistan's capital, suspected militants struck again on a high security police complex here and also hit a jail van in NWFP, killing 16 and injuring ten.

The casualties were less in the police lines complex attack in Islamabad as the suicide bomber struck the Anti Terrorism Squad office when most of the security personnel were out on patrol in view of the joint session of the Parliament reviewing strategy to combat upsurge in violence.

Though initial reports had put the casualty figure at eight killed, the Islamabad Chief Commissioner Kamran Lashari later said ten people were injured. Confusion prevailed as officials did not know the whereabouts of a police commando team which had left the building minutes before the blast. But, police officials said the casualty figure was clarified when the team returned.

There was also confusion over how the attack was carried out. Some reports said a suicide bomber rammed an explosive-laden vehicle into the building, while others said a man carrying boxes of sweets came out of the car and entered the ATS office shortly before the blast occurred.

Officials said they had found a letter in Pashto at the blast site warning more such attacks would be carried out if the Pakistan Government does not stop supporting the war on terror.

In the Dir Bala area of North West Frontier Province, 16 people, including four children and four policemen, were killed and several others were injured when a roadside bomb went off while a prison van and a school bus were passing by. The van was bringing prisoners from a court to jail when it was attacked with a remote-controlled bomb, state-run PTV reported, adding a school bus passing through the area was also hit by the blast.

No group claimed responsibility for the attack.

The people in Dir district had recently formed a 'lashkar' or militia to protect themselves against the local Taliban, forcing militants to leave the area.

Meanwhile, Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Yousuf Raza Gilani condemned the attack on the ATS office. In a message, Zardari said such incidents would not deter the government's resolve to fight terrorism.

Gilani directed law enforcement agencies to further strengthen security in all important cities, particularly the federal capital, and to initiate an immediate inquiry so that the perpetrators could be brought to book.

The Islamabad Police headquarters and the National Police Academy are located within the Police Lines. The area also houses the International Islamic University, a government hospital and one of the city's largest fruit and vegetable markets.

Heading: Pak NSA likely to visit India next week - Indian Express
Content:
In the first editorial comment in Marathi daily Prahaar, which hit the stands on the Dussehra, Maharashtra Revenue Minister Narayan Rane expressed his gratitude towards Shiv Sena chief Bal Thackeray and claimed the switchover from the Sena to the Congress was his destiny.

In the signed editorial carried on the front page of his newspaper, Rane stated, "I am a politician. I had the honour of occupying several political positions over the past 40 years. I had to join the Congress after working for 39 years in the Shiv Sena. I feel it is the play of destiny in my life."

Expressing gratitude towards Thackeray for his rise from a corporator in the Sena to the chief minister of the state, Rane said, "I am indebted to him. May he live a long and healthy life." However, he has pointed out that nobody should read too much into his gesture, because he was just acknowledging favours received by him.

The expression of gratitude indicates that he does not want to lose the goodwill of Shiv Sainiks and his former mentor. Rane and MNS chief Raj Thackeray are both poaching Shiv Sainiks and no Shiv Sainik would like to hear anything against Thackeray Sr. Both Rane and Raj rebelled against Uddhav's style of functioning, but have, all along held Thackeray Sr in high reverence. Rane has also expressed gratitude towards Congress chief Sonia Gandhi for admitting him into the party, appointing him as a minister and treating him with honour.

Setting the tone for his journalistic endeavour, Rane said a newspaper was a powerful weapon of public awareness and revolution and he wanted to use it for the overall development of Maharashtra.

He clarified to his opponents that contrary to what they were thinking about his newspaper, it was not launched to attack them. He said he was capable of confronting his opponents, even without a newspaper. "My point of focus will be the farthest citizen of Maharashtra," he said, pointing out that Prahaar would work for the overall development as well as fight against injustice.

The first issue of Prahaar, however, carried a story based on sources, on how Uddhav was trying to project himself as the potential chief ministerial candidate of the Sena and, thereby, trying to stall the chances of Manohar Joshi's candidature in event of the party coming to power. The story has raised questions on the capabilities of Uddhav as a politician and administrator, stating that a person who has never won an election and who has no knowledge of administration could not become the Chief Minister.

Heading: On Kanshi Ram’s death anniversary, Maya gifts Rs 3,000-cr schemes to UP - Indian Express
Content:
Mahmud Ali Durrani, Special Advisor on National Security to Pakistan PM Yusuf Raza Gilani, is expected to visit India next week to give tangible form to the promise of "good news" on the Indo-Pak front that Asif Ali Zardari had made on his first day as Pakistan's new President.

According to sources, Durrani will be meeting his Indian counterpart M K Narayan and Foreign Secretary Shiv Shankar Menon. With security and bilateral cooperation on his agenda, a special meeting of the Joint Anti-Terror Mechanism, as decided between Zardari and Prime Minister Manmohan Singh in New York, is expected to be decided upon during Durrani's stay in New Delhi.

The derailed foreign secretary-level dialogue between the two countries is also expected to get a shot in the arm. Durrani and Menon share friendly relations since the latter was posted in Islamabad as India's High Commissioner to Pakistan in 2003.

Durrani's post is newly crafted in Pakistan's Cabinet. Apart from being National Security Advisor, he also holds additional charge of a federal minister. Before this assignment, he was appointed by Pervez Musharraf as Pakistan's Ambassador to the US. The Zardari-led PPP handpicked him for his current post because of his impressive credentials on the US, Afghanistan and India fronts.

Heading: Paswan asks Left to support demand for Prez rule in Orissa - Indian Express
Content:
If Kanshi Ram's first death anniversary last year brought 12 development projects worth Rs 3,987 crore for UP, this year the number of projects went up to 158, although the allocated funds went down to Rs 3,000 crore.

Paying floral tributes to her mentor, UP Chief Minister Mayawati said that the projects were dedicated to the memory of Kanshi Ram — the founder of BAMCEF, DS4 and the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). Mayawati also released My Struggles and the Journey of the BSP Movement, the English translation of her book Mere Sangharshmay Jeevan Evam BSP Movement ka Safarnama (Volume 3).

The projects announced on Thursday included the construction of new bridges and rural roads, widening of various existing roads, the foundation of the Dr Shakuntala Mishra Handicapped University (named after the mother of BSP general secretary Satish Chandra Mishra), the Kanshi Ram Shahri Garib Awas Yojana — a housing scheme for the poor — and a new building for Lucknow district jail. She also dedicated to people the Kanshi Ram Bahujan Nayak Park, a new Media Centre at Shashtri Bhavan (CM Office building) and a new section in the Ram Manohar Lohia Medical Institute building. Mayawati said that the works started in the memory of Kanshi Ram symbolised the state Government's continued commitment to the causes espoused by Kanshi Ram, such as the upliftment of the poor and downtrodden.

Voicing her regret that Kanshi Ram was not awarded the Bharat Ratna despite her requests and that no national period of mourning was declared on the occasion of his death anniversary, Mayawati added that the present state Government had declared his birth anniversary as a public holiday and had also created and named a new district after him.

Mayawati said that under the Kanshi Ram Shahri Garib Awas Yojana, two-room set residences would be allotted for poor people. More than one lakh houses will be constructed per year for five years in a phased manner under this scheme.

Heading: Bainsla overture to Raje, targets Cong - Indian Express
Content:
Lok Janshakti Party (LJP) chief Ram Vilas Paswan on Thursday sought the support of the Left parties for his demand for President's Rule in Orissa following continued attacks on Christians.

"The Left parties are known for their commitment to secularism. They should also come out and demand the dismissal of the communal BJD-BJP Government in Orissa. I urge them to strengthen the hands of the secular forces," he said.

At the Cabinet meeting yesterday, Paswan and RJD chief Lalu Prasad had pitched for a ban on the Bajrang Dal-VHP and pointed out that Orissa was a fit case for use of Article 356. Reiterating the demand today, he said: "I and other Cabinet colleagues will continue to fight for the demands to be accepted."

Denying that the Centre lacked the political will to ban the Bajrang Dal, Paswan said the UPA government was accumulating facts against the saffron outfit. He said that there was huge support for his demand to ban the Bajrang Dal.

"The Congress party has also favoured a ban. In fact all the parties, except the NDA, are in favour of clamping down on the Bajrang Dal," Paswan said.

On imposition of President's Rule in Orissa, Paswan admitted that the UPA Government was probably not ready to take the step, fearing it would not be ratified by Parliament. "But I feel that we should not worry about it. The situation in Orissa is going out of control and President's Rule is needed to control it," he said.

On BJP prime ministerial candidate L K Advani's statement asking why the Centre was not talking about imposing President's Rule in Assam, Paswan said: "In Orissa, the attack against Christians was state-sponsored, while in Assam private groups were engaged in violence."

Heading: Naxalites on mind, Nagpur to get forensic unit - Indian Express
Content:
In a clear indication that the Gurjjars will back the BJP in the coming Assembly elections in Rajasthan, the Gurjjar Arakshan Sangharsh Samiti (GASS), lead by Colonel Kirori Singh Bainsla, has accused the Congress of "playing politics" and creating roadblocks in the process of granting ST status to the community. Bainsla has sought the intervention of the PM and President in clearing the Bill giving 5 per cent reservation to the Gurjjars. The Bill has been pending with the Rajasthan Governor for nearly three months.

"The Bill has not been cleared because of the political reasons. This is not at all acceptable to us. We will wait for 15 days before taking a decision on our next move," Bainsla said. Accusing the Congress of influencing the Governor for political gains, he said similar Bills were promptly cleared in states like Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra.

Samiti vice-president Hari Prasad warned that the Congress party would have to pay a heavy price if the Gurjjars' demands were not met. "The Congress-appointed Governor is not clearing the Bill. The party will have to face consequences," Prasad said.

Although maintaining all along that the Gurjjar Arakshan Sangharsh Samiti is a non-political organisation, the Gurjjars made it clear that they would help the party which would ensure reservation for them.

"At present, discussions are on at various levels in Rajasthan and other parts of the country among Gurjjars. We will support whichever party gives us reservation. But I will not personally join politics," said Bainsla, adding that he had already met the Governor and requested him to give his assent to the Rajasthan SC/ST/OBC/Special Backward Category and EBC Bill.

Heading: As tourist season starts, Goa fights fresh embarrassment - Indian Express
Content:
With the Naxalite threat topping security concern for the Maharashtra Police, investigation of Naxalite related offences in the state is now slated to become less time-consuming with a state-of-the-art forensic unit being opened in Nagpur. It will deal with arms and ammunitions cases from the Vidarbha region.

While a Regional Forensic Science Laboratory already exists in Nagpur, it now has its own super speciality Ballistics Division to exclusively deal with Naxalite cases.

"Every year we receive over 250 cases of arms and ammunition from Vidharba which are solely investigated by the Mumbai lab thus far. However, with a ballistics division in Nagpur, all cases will be sent there, thus preventing the time spent in sealing the items and getting them to Mumbai," said Dr Rukmani Krishnamurthy, Director of Forensic Science Laboratories.

The Naxal-affected districts are all located in Vidarbha, and police-Naxalite clashes here have claimed several lives and led to the seizure of large hauls of sophisticated weaponry.The Nagpur lab is the first in the country to have a super specialty unit at the regional level. While the Nagpur laboratory has just one ballistics expert at present, Kirshanamurthy said it would receive more personnel after a shuffling process.

Heading: Country’s first women TV channel, in Telugu - Indian Express
Content:
On the day the first flight bringing in the foreign tourists from Moscow landed at Dabolim airport, marking the begining of the international tourist season, Goa was faced with another embarassment over the death of a 65-year-old Australian tourist at a pub in Calungute beach. John Kellie, who was assaulted in a bar, succumbed to injuries at the Goa Medical College and Hospital here.

The last tourist season was marred by the rape and murder of British teenager Scarlett Eden Keeling, who was found dead on Anjuna beach on February 18, 2008. Goa receives around four lakh foreigners every year, of which almost 42 per cent are Britons. Russians rank second contributing for nine per cent. The flight from Moscow on Thursday will be followed by many such landings.

Kellie's death comes at a time when the state, in a bid to pre-empt any untoward incident, had tightened security around the coastal belt. The police announced that they would not allow violation of laws by the shack owners. They would be held responsible for any drug peddling or consumption in the shacks, the police had warned.

But the Australian's death has shocked the state, which faced much bad publicity after Scarlett's death. Police officials enquiring the Australian's death has said that it was not a planned murder. "We are still investigating the case," said Superintendent of Police Bosco George.

Tourism officials contended that the incident should not be used to judge law and order in the state. "The state is absolutely safe and this is an isolated incident. All the measures are in place here to ensure that tourist enjoys his holiday better," said Lyndon Monteiro of the Tourism Ministry.

The police have already arrested Manak Basak (32), Jagat Pradhan (23) and Jaykrishna Das (25) under Section 302 of the IPC. The trio had reportedly assaulted Kellie after he complained about their "style of serving beer" on Wednesday morning. The Australian died at 6 pm while undergoing treatment, police said.

Heading: Cong takes Left on word for word, plans publishing house - Indian Express
Content:
The Hyderabad-based Rachana Television Private Limited launched the country's first TV channel devoted exclusively for women on Thursday.

Vanitha TV in Telugu will have all programmes related only to women including health, counselling and discussions on women empowerment and will be beamed across Andhra Pradesh on a 24x7 basis.

The Rachana TV launched by Tummala Narendra Chowdary, also has a 24-hour news channel in Telugu, NTV. It is launching Vanitha just one year after it started its operations. The new channel, which went on air at 5 pm, will be headed by well known writer Volga.

As Chief Editor, Volga believes that the channel will attempt to view the world through a woman's perspective and will not engage in "gender politics".

Heading: In a U-turn, TDP says it stands for Telangana state - Indian Express
Content:
With a majority of the state's writers and intellectuals identifying themselves with Leftist politics, the Congress in Kerala has decided to have a publication house of its own. Priyadarshini Publications, a registered charitable society, has Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee chief Ramesh Chennithala as president and a battery of leaders as members.

The Congress has long felt the need for a publication house in the state, where the CPI(M) and other Left parties have never faced any dearth of writings to drive home their political viewpoints. If the CPI(M) has Chintha Publications, the CPI has Prabhat Book House, while the RSS owns Kurukshetra Prakashan.

The Congress hopes to groom a crop of pro-party writers with the publication house, apart from winning over eminent writers who have distanced themselves from the Left. Sources in the Congress said the party would meet the initial financial requirements of the venture.

On the business front, it is confident of making the book business viable. The publication industry in Kerala registered 6 per cent growth last year, despite threats from the visual media. Some groups have diversified into real estate, professional education and allied areas.

A member of Priyadarshini Publications and the former director of the Kerala Language Institute, Dr M R Thampan, said though the thrust of the venture would be promoting new-generation writers, the first batch of books would be from established Malayalam writers such as Kakkanadan, M G S Naryanan and Kamala Surayya (Kamala Das).

"Priyadarshini Publications would have a branded distribution network across the state. Ten books would be brought out in January, marking the formal entry of the party into the book industry," said Thampan.

Priyadarshini hopes to cover the whole gamut from literature to travelogue to children's stuff. In 2009, it plans to bring out 50 titles.

"Of course, the Congress's ideology would find a place among the titles. But the party would not interfere with the selection of non-political works. Expert subject committees have been formed to select the books," Thampan said.

Heading: Chiranjeevi backs statehood - Indian Express
Content:
In a turnaround that will have major political ramifications, the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) on Thursday said that it fully supports the demand for a Telangana state. The party had previously taken a strong stand against the division of Andhra Pradesh.

Party president N Chandrababu Naidu, addressing mediapersons at TDP office, said that he had delayed taking a decision on statehood for Telangana, as it was a "sensitive issue" and because it was necessary to develop a consensus within the party and gather opinion from the people. "We are for a separate Telangana state. We are positive about it. We arrived at this decision after carefully considering the sentiments of the people of Telangana as well as others. The feelings of all Telugu-speaking people in whichever region are important to us even if it means a separate Telangana and Andhra Pradesh," he said.

The TDP's decision also clears the decks for an alliance with the Telangana Rashtra Samiti (TRS). Reportedly, talks regarding a possible alliance between the two parties are already in progress. The TRS had trucked with the Congress in the 2004 elections with an agreement that the Congress would make efforts to carve out a separate Telangana state. However, in what TRS chief K Chandrasekhara called a "betrayal", the Congress failed to make any move in that direction. The TRS broke away from the alliance and 16 of its MLAs and four MPs resigned in March this year. The party put up an unimpressive show in the July by-elections, retaining only 7 of the 16 seats it resigned.

With elections early next year, the TRS has been busy scouting for alliances and has approached the TDP while keeping its communications open with Chiranjeevi. The TDP's decision has paved the way for at least one partner for the TRS. Last week, the CPI(M) conveyed that it would tie up with the TDP for the next elections, while the CPI state committee will meet next week to take a decision on alliances.

With Chiranjeevi's party in the fray and no sign of anti-incumbency sentiments against the Congress, the TDP appears to have rethought its political strategies, resulting in its volte-face regarding Telangana. Naidu had constituted a committee gather opinions on the formation of a separate Telangana state about two months ago. The five-member committee, headed by TDP MP K Yerrannaidu, submitted its report to Naidu on Monday. "We discussed the findings of the report for nearly three days and arrived at the decision to support the Telangana cause," Yerrannaidu confirmed.

It is well known that Chandrababu Naidu had taken an oppositional stance against a separate Telangana state for more than a decade. The party chief's stand not only incensed several senior pro-Telangana party leaders but also alienated him from the TDP's rank and file. But this had not stopped Naidu from issuing show-cause notices or expelling party leaders for airing their pro-Telangana views. In the process, senior leaders like Devender Goud, who was second in command in the TDP, quit the party in June this year and then formed the Nava Telangana Praja Party. Former minister K Vidyadhar Rao was expelled from the party for his pro-Telangana statements in March. He has since joined actor-turned-politician Chiranjeevi's Praja Rajyam Party.

Heading: Hyderabad blasts: After HuJI, police now suspect IM hand - Indian Express
Content: A few hours after TDP's Chandrababu Naidu announced his party's support to the demand of separate Telangana, filmstar Chiranjeevi, president of Praja Rajyam Party, too clarified his stand. At an impromptu public address at Srikakulam on Thursday evening, Chiranjeevi said his party too would support the Telangana cause. "I respect the feelings of Telangana people and my party will do everything possible for them." Chiranjeevi had so far maintained that Telangana statehood was a very sensitive issue and any decision on it needed careful consideration. However, as news of TDP's turnaround to support separate Telangana spread, Chiranjeevi too made his stand clear.

Heading: CPM leader under party scanner for building house - Indian Express
Content:
A special investigation team of the Hyderabad Police which has been probing the blasts that occurred in the city last year suspected the Harkat-ul-Jihadi to be behind the attack. But though close to 100 persons were picked up or called for questioning, police did not make much progress.

The Hyderabad Police did arrest Majid Bilal, brother of HuJI commander Sahid Bilal, accusing him of purchasing the SIM cards which were used in the mobile phones to trigger of the blasts. However, though Majid Bilal revealed some names of accomplices including a local youth, police could not corroborate it.

The role of Raziuddin Nasir, who was arrested by Karnataka Police, was also probed, especially after he claimed in his narco analysis test that he had planted the bomb at Lumbini Park but police could not find any evidence to link him to it.

Now, 14 months after the blasts at Lumbini Park and Gokul Chat House, the Hyderabad Police are hoping to finally unravel the mystery behind the terror attack that left 36 people dead, and investigating agencies groping in the dark.

A team of Hyderabad Police left for Mumbai earlier this week to interrogate two persons who the Mumbai Police are claiming planted the bombs at the laser show theatre at Lumbini Park where 11 persons were killed and the crowded Gokul Chaat House where 25 persons were killed on August 25, 2007. According to Mumbai Police, Riyaz Bhatkal alias Roshan Khan, Anique Shafique Syed and Akbar Ismail Chaudhray planted the bombs in Hyderabad.

According to the Mumbai Police, Riyaz Bhatkal alias Roshan Khan planted the bomb at Gokul Chaat, Anique Shafique Syed placed the bomb at Lumbini Park while Akbar Ismail planted one bomb at Dilsukhnagar which did not explode. Riyaz Bhatkal is absconding but both Anique Syed and Akbar Ismail have been arrested by Mumbai Police.

"The names of these three persons never cropped up during our investigation but Mumbai Police are sure and they have prima facie evidence of their involvement in the Hyderabad blasts. Since all three are from outside the state we are looking at what kind of local support they got for planning and executing the attack," said Hyderabad Police Commissioner B Prasada Rao.

Mumbai Police Commissioner Hasan Gafoor said: "Leads and clues on these trhee were gathered based on information we were working on for several days. During investigation of recent blast cases their past record came under scrutiny. We were able to gather more information after sharing information with Delhi Police after the Delhi blasts accused were interrogated."

Heading: Bhoj varsity V-C booked for copying thesis - Indian Express
Content:
In a curious political development, a CPI(M) local committee in Ernakulam on Thursday asked the district committee to initiate action against Thripunithura area committee secretary C N Sundaram for constructing a palatial house. Sundaram is a leader of the faction led by CPI(M) state secretary Pinarayi Vijayan.

The demand has embarrassed the party leadership, which is known to have embraced a luxurious lifestyle.

Sources said Sundaram is a full-time party worker and has no known source of income. Hence, his construction of a huge house has raised suspicion. The district committee is likely to discuss the matter in the next meeting.

Three years ago, much heat had been generated with the party after Pinarayi Vijayan constructed a splendid house at his native place Pinarayi. But it was not Vijayan who faced party's wrath, but three CPI(M) activists who had gone to see their leader's house. They were ousted from the party on the ground that they had gone to see the party secretary's house without permission from the leadership.

Heading: Won’t return without adequate security, riot victims tell Gogoi - Indian Express
Content:
Madhya Pradesh Bhoj Open University Vice-Chancellor Dr Kamlakar Singh is in trouble with the police registering a case of forgery against him for plagiarising portions from the thesis of his guide.

One of the most controversial figures in the field of education in the state, the 49-year-old has been accused of reproducing two chapters in his thesis related to fertility of female albino rats from his guide Prof S C Norton's thesis.

Though the alleged plagiarism took place way back in 1986, the matter surfaced only a few years ago when Singh was associated with the Barkatullah University. Matters gathered momentum in 2005 when he was being considered as Vice-Chancellor of Bhoj University.

The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad had launched an agitation against the V-C, often knocking on the doors of the Governor and approaching courts. Two inquiry reports, including one initiated by the state Government, had found the charges against him true. Singh, however, had got a court stay in the matter for the last couple of years but the Parishad continued to press for his removal saying he was involved in other irregularities as well. After a favourable order from the High Court last week, the Parishad filed a complaint against Singh in the Bagh Sevania Police Station. Two days ago, the police asked the university for information, but failed to get it. The police then wrote to the university and questioned a few officials before registering a case on Wednesday night under Section 420 of the IPC.

Singh could not be contacted despite repeated attempts on his mobile phone and his residence number.

However, senior Parishad leader Vishnu Sharma alleged that the Governor was not acting against Singh because of his proximity to HRD Minister Arjun Singh. The Parishad sought time from Governor Balram Jakhar on Thursday but did not succeed. Sharma said the students' body would continue its agitation till the Governor sacked Singh. Though one member of the search panel had registered a note of dissent, Singh had been appointed to the V-C's post given his political connections, he added.

Heading: India’s ties with Israel its sovereign decision: Abbas - Indian Express
Content:
Panic-Stricken after the outbreak of large-scale violence that has devastated normal life in the Assam districts of Udalguri and Darrang, most of the people who have taken shelter in the 100-odd relief camps there have said they would not go back to their respective villages unless the Government arranged for inadequate security.

Inmates in all the three relief camps that Assam Chief Minister Tarun Gogoi visited on Thursday also told him that there was a genuine sense of fear and insecurity after the violence that broke out on October 3. At least 55 people have been killed so far and over one lakh rendered homeless.

Gogoi visited relief camps at Bhakatpara and Rowta Chariali in Udalguri and Besimari in Darrang. While the Bhakatpara camp comprises entirely of Bodo villagers and the Besimari relief camp had Muslim refugees, the camp at Rowta Chariali comprised of people from various ethnic groups.

The inmates also requested the Chief Minister to establish police pickets and outposts in their villages so that they could return home and resume normal life. With harvest season approaching, the villagers do not want to lose their crop during a year in which floods had already caused considerable loss.

The violence that broke out on October 3 had mostly affected a large number of villages inhabited by Bodo, Assamese and other communities, while a number of villages belonging to Muslims of migrant origin were also reduced to ashes. The Government has suspected the involvement of the outlawed National Democratic Front of Bodoland (NDFB), an armed underground group currently in a ceasefire with the Government. Opposition parties and student groups, however, have blamed fundamentalist forces for triggering off the violence.

Gogoi assured the inmates that his Government would provide full assistance for their rehabilitation including rebuilding houses that were burnt and destroyed during the clashes. The Government would also provide adequate compensation for the loss of livestock and other properties, apart from providing the people utensils, mosquito nets and clothes.

Later, reviewing the situation with senior police and civil officers in Mangaldoi, the Chief Minister stressed on the need for initiating a series of confidence-building measures. He also asked officers of both the districts to draw up an action plan for foolproof security and identify points where police outposts or pickets were required to instill a sense of security and prevent recurrence of clashes. He also asked the officers to activate village defence parties.

Heading: IIT-Delhi, IIT-Bombay in world’s top 200 institutes list - Indian Express
Content:
As Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas completed his four day visit to India on Thursday, New Delhi sought an end to the expansion of Israeli settlements in occupied Palestine.

When asked about India's growing engagement with Israel in defence, Abbas told a select group of media persons that India's relations with Israel was its 'sovereign decision'.

"We are not going to interfere and we know very well that India is supportive of the Palestinian struggle for achieving its own independence."

A joint statement by the Palestinian Authority and the Indian Government said, "India calls for an end to the expansion of Israeli settlements in occupied Palestine and for an early and significant easing of restrictions on the free movement of persons and goods within Palestine."

Abbas earlier met Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

During the visit by Abbas, seen as another in the series of engagements with the top West Asian leaders — including Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmedinejad and Syrian President Bashar Al-Assad in the recent months — bilateral talks centered around India's solidarity with the Palestinians in the their struggle.

New Delhi "reiterated its well-known support for the Palestinian cause in line with its backing of the United Nation's Security Council Resolutions 242 (1967) and 338 (1973) calling for a negotiated solution resulting in a sovereign, independent, viable and united State of Palestine living within secure and recognised borders, side by side and at peace with Israel as endorsed in the Quartet Roadmap and United Nations Security Council Resolutions 1397 and 1515." India also repeated its support for the Arab Peace Plan.

Recalling its participation in the Middle East Peace conference convened in November, 2007 at Annapolis, India expressed the hope that discussions between the Palestinian National Authority and Israel aimed at resolving all outstanding issues would be taken forward in an "expeditious and purposive manner".

Asked about his views on Israel's new leader Tzipi Livni who will replace Ehud Olmert, Abbas said he did not differentiate between the two. At a press conference an hour before his departure, Abbas said, "Until this moment we have been negotiating with Mr Olmert. During his negotiations, she attended all the meetings and she is really acquainted with the negotiation process. We cannot really compare the two — Olmert and Livni. But both belong to the same political party and they have the same political tendency."

India and Palestine also agreed to consider the formation of a joint committee to discuss bilateral economic cooperation activities.

Both countries will also work together to develop an information technology park in Palestine. The two countries will also explore ways of cooperating in the water resources sector.

Abbas also invited the President and the Prime Minister to visit Palestine.

The invitations were accepted and dates would be settled through diplomatic channels in due course, the joint statement said.

Heading: Be responsible in telecast of news, channels told - Indian Express
Content:
The only two Indian institutes that have notched a place amongst the top 200 universities ranked by the Times Higher Education-QS World University Ranking survey for 2008 are IIT-Delhi and IIT-Bombay. The institutes havebeen ranked 154 and 174 respectively in a list topped by Harvard University of US. The ranking survey was published this week.

The two institutes had been the only Indian institutes on the top 400 list put out by the survey last year. IIT-Delhi had stood at the 254th position in 2007 while IIT-Bombay was at 269. The rankings have improved this year.

While no Indian university could make a mark on the international rankings largely dominated by UK and US-based varsities, as many as nine Asian institutes are among the top 50 institutes, including three based in Hong Kong.

China has as many as five universities in the top 200, with Peking University placed at 50 and Tsinghua University at 56. Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and Seoul National University are the two new entrants into the list this year.

Harvard Universits followed by Yale, while the universities of Cambridge and Oxford in UK were placed third and fourth respectively. Britain, meanwhile, has 17 of its universities in the top 100, down from 19 last year. It has a total of 29 universities in the top 200, one less than last year.

Heading: Now, two-year-old boy falls into borewell near Agra - Indian Express
Content:
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting issued an advisory to the Indian Broadcasting Foundation (IBF) and News Broadcasters Association (NBA) to direct their member channels not to telecast any news item which may endanger the life of a person after the media showed visuals of 12-year-old balloon seller Rahul.

He had seen the bombers plating bombs at Barakhamba Road on September 13, the day serial blasts shook the capital. He had also helped the Delhi Police make sketches and had been subsequently rewarded.

The advisory has been issued on a request from the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) who had written to the ministry about its serious objection on the repeated telecast of a live interview with Rahul. The NCPCR had informed the ministry that the act was insensitive and negligent, endangering Rahul's life, with no one to protect or advise him of the serious consequences.

The NCPCR also observed that the media instead of having concern for his safety had exhibited the identity of the child to the nation. So, the ministry has issued the advisory for the media to restrain themselves in selecting content for broadcasting.

The teenage balloon seller was one of the main witnesses who had seen the bombers put a black polythene inside the dustbin just before the explosion at Connaught Place. He had informed the police that the bombers had been wearing black clothes and had left in a three-wheeler after putting the bomb. Rahul sells balloons in the Connaught Place area.

Heading: Deadline for women’s quota report extended - Indian Express
Content:
In another incident of a child being trapped in a pit, two-year-old Sonu fell into an abandoned 150-ft-deep borewell in Tohra village of Agra's Shamshabad area on Thursday morning.

While rescue operations are on, with the Army and police both sending men, Sonu was still stuck at around 70 ft inside the borewell when this report was filed 15 hours later.

Authorities are worried that water might permeate into the narrow borewell from a nearby pond.

The son of Pappu Khushwaha, a resident of the village, which is located around 26 km from Agra, Sonu was playing with friends in front of the borewell when he fell into it.

A JCB bulldozer and earthmover are being used to dig a borewell parallel to the one Sonu has fallen into, while oxygen is being administered to him though a pipe.

Efforts are being made to talk to the boy, who could initially be heard crying for his family members. However, Agra SSP Raghuveer Lal, who is present at the spot, added that Sonu hadn't made a sound after the first couple of hours.

Lal said the borewell was just one foot in diameter, too narrow for someone to go down and bring out the boy.

DM Anil Kumar has also rushed to Tohra, along with a team of doctors from S N Medical College. Several cases of children falling into uncovered borewells have been reported from different parts of the country in the recent past. The most famous incident being that of five-year-old Prince, who captured the imagination of the country in July 2006 after surviving 50 hours inside a borewell in Kurukshetra.

Heading: Ministry to bridge Dawki gap, contracts soon - Indian Express
Content:
The deadline for the Parliamentary Committee on Personnel, Grievances, Law and Justice for submitting its report on the Women's Reservation Bill has been extended to November 21, sources disclosed on Thursday.

The panel, headed by Congress Rajya Sabha member E M Sudarsana Natchiappan, is back to the drawing board after an extensive tour of the country to solicit suggestions on the bill. Explaining the reason for this delay, Natchiappan said, "It is not fair to enact a major amendment in the Constitution, which is not supported by a national consensus."

The committee, instead of broadening the mandate of the Bill, has fallen back on a safer route to provide 33 per cent reservation to women. The latest proposal under consideration of the committee is to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats by one-third of the present strength and set them aside for women. Natchiappan had asked the representatives of various parties on the panel to get back with the official position of their respective organisations and they have sought more time to do so.

The Congress, BJP, the Left parties, DMK and AIADMK want the bill passed in its present form while the Samajwadi Party, Rashtriya Janata Dal, Janata Dal (United) and PMK are opposed to the Bill.

Heading: Kandhamal rioters torch 8 houses in Boudh - Indian Express
Content:
Literally bridging a gap with neighbour Bangladesh, the Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport & Highways (MORTH) is set to award contracts for construction of a two-lane bridge over River Umngot at Dawki, the last Indian post in Meghalaya. The bridge will help shorten the distance to Bangladesh and expedite the movement of coal from Garo and Khasi hills to the neighbouring country.

Under discussion for more than a decade, the two-lane bridge will take the load off the single-lane 136-metre suspension bridge built by the British as the overland link between the provinces of East Bengal and Assam. The MORTH had invited consultancy bids for the new bridge project last year and the Detailed Project report (DPR) has since been completed.

"The Rs 20-crore bridge at Dawki will help create a viable and shorter route to Bangladesh and also link the area directly to Shillong. At present, there is no concrete bridge across the river. So, traffic from Shillong to Dawki, headed towards Bangladesh, has to take a long detour via Jowai, making it a 130-km long trip. With a permanent bridge across the river, the distance between Shillong and Dawki will be reduced to just 84 km. The link is crucial for transportation of coal and other goods, and figures high on our priority list. We hope to award contracts for the project this month itself," said a senior official.

Dawki forms a crucial part of the trade corridor between Bangladesh and the Northeastern states and is located on the Indo-Bangla Frontier at the end of NH 40. The new bridge is being planned on the 163-km road from Jorabat, near the Assam-Meghalaya border, to Tamabil in Bangladesh via Shillong on NH 40.

Several transport corridors are being planned between India and Bangladesh through this sector. The Dawki bridge in India and Jamuna bridge in Bangladesh will be crucial for better connectivity in the region. The Indian side has been trying to prevail upon Bangladesh to upgrade the Jamuna bridge as well.

Improved Indo-Bangladesh connectivity also figures prominently in the SAARC multi-modal transport study and discussions are on to create rail, road and inland corridors across the area.

Heading: Another NCM team to visit Orissa - Indian Express
Content:
Even as riot-scarred Kandhamal district is slowly heading towards normalcy, violence flared up in neighbouring Boudh district on Wednesday night when a group of tribals from Gochhapada area in Kandhamal entered Lamsaripali village under Kantamal police station area of Boudh and set fire to about eight houses. No casualties have been reported.

However, police officials claim that this incident was not an outcome of communal tensions. According to Deputy Inspector General of Police R P Koche, Kondh tribals from Kandhamal had torched the houses of Dalits because of past enmity.

Incidentally, communal clashes broke out in this area of Boudh last week when over 100 houses, mostly belonging to Pano Christians, were set on fire by tribals. The situation had been brought under control since then and no further incidents were reported until Wednesday night.

IGP Koche added that police movement to the area was affected, as the attackers had blocked roads by felling trees, but some of the arsonists have been arrested. Additional security personnel, including one company of CRPF jawans and three platoons of the Orissa State Armed Police have been deployed in the area.

Picking up the pieces

•Even as Kandhamal remains peaceful, the biggest challenge before the administration is to ensure that the people in the relief camps return home, say officials. Out of about 23,000 people who had sought refuge in the camps, around 15,000 still remain.

• The CID team probing the Laxmanananda murder has sought extension of the remand of three tribal Christians accused of being involved in the crime. The three, Duryodhan Sunamajhi, Sanatan Badamajhi and Munda Badamajhi, have admitted to their role in the murder and are disclosing the names of other conspirators, said a CID official.

• The Archbishop of Cuttack-Bhubaneswar Diocese Raphael Cheenath told The Indian Express that the nun who was allegedly raped during the Kandhamal riots is not in Delhi. He added that the 29-year-old does not want to surface anytime soon as she has lost all faith in the police.

Heading: Voice is like the most jealous woman in the world: Placido - Indian Express
Content:
As the political pitch sharpens over the continuing violence against Christians in Orissa, the National Commission for Minorities (NCM) has voiced concern over the Naveen Patnaik Government's intentions in controlling the situation.

The Commission is sending another team, the fourth to visit Orissa in the last ten months, to the violence-hit areas, especially the epicentre Kandhamal, to investigate the state government's role in preventing the attacks on Christians and providing relief to the victims.

The announcement came after a high-level NCM delegation met Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and apprised him of the situation on Wednesday.

Sources in the minority panel said that a feeling was gaining ground that the state administration did not want to control the violence, which first broke out in December last year. "It has been ten months and had they wanted to control it, they would have controlled it a long time ago," they pointed out.

Senior NCM member Harcharan Singh Josh told The Indian Express that, "if the violence against Christians can be controlled in Karnataka, why can't it be controlled in Orissa? It means that the state administration is not taking it seriously. Indirectly, they are giving freedom for violence."

Some of the NCM members also feel that there is political pressure on the Patnaik Government to go slow on taking action against outfits like the Bajrang Dal and in cases related to attacks on Christians and places of worship.

On Wednesday the NCM had demanded that investigators from outside the state be brought in to probe the cases.

NCM chairperson Mohamed Shafi Qureshi said a two-member team consisting of vice-chairperson Michael P Pinto and Harcharan Singh Josh would be visiting the state next week to see whether the assurances given by the state government have been fulfilled.

"The state Government had made certain promises to an NCM team which visited the trouble-torn areas last month regarding nabbing of culprits, rehabilitation of victims and compensation to the family of those killed and those who suffered damage to their property. We want to see whether these promises have been fulfilled," he told The Indian Express.

With the violence showing no signs of abating, sources in the Commission said it may conduct a public hearing in the affected areas next month.

Heading: YSR’s son to complete Andhra polls’ family picture - Indian Express
Content:
"We'll have to end the concert by 10 pm," says conductor Zubin Mehta, "Apparently, there is supposed to be no noise after 10 and, these days, we're classified as noise. But there is no more beautiful noise than Placido Domingo."

The renowned tenor himself demurs and adds to the joke, "We'll just have to sing faster, if we want to cover the whole programme."

Domingo is set to perform at the Brabourne Stadium, Churchgate, as part of the Mehli Mehta Centenary Concert series on October 11 and the handsome tenor, is visibly excited. "It is a great feeling to be here in Mumbai, though this is my first time in India."

Domingo, 67, speaks of his connection with the Mehta family and how honoured he is to be performing at the concert for them. "I didn't hesitate when Zubin asked me to come," he says. "Many people may have heard my records, but this is the first time people in India will be hearing me live. So I am a little nervous about it," he says with disarming modesty.

Domingo, a multiple Grammy winning singer and conductor, has even greater recognition outside of the world of opera. He is one of the famous The Three Tenors, along with Jose Carreras and Luciano Pavarotti, and has performed at several FIFA World Cups and even the recent Beijing Olympics. He has lent the drama and passion in his range to the most famous compositions by Verdi (Otello, La Traviata), Puccini (Tosca, Madama Butterfly), Wagner (Parsifal) and Tchaikovsky (Eugene Onegin), among scores of others.

Mehta is all praise for his long-time colleague and friend for his ability to juggle many roles. "Not many people are aware that Placido is not just a singer and conductor. He's also the music director and the guiding spirit of two opera companies in America. I don't know how he does it. He's also one of the few Latin singers to perform Tchaikovsky's operas in Russian, and that too very fluently."

Domingo says he finds singing to be most challenging. "When I'm conducting, I'm more relaxed because I know I have to lead everybody. But while singing I'm always trembling. The voice is like the most jealous woman in the world. You have to take care of her, pamper her. Every morning I wake up and I ask myself, is my voice still there?"

Domingo is more reticent while talking about his favourite performance to date. "It is so difficult to say. I've had close to 3,500 performances and there have been so many special evenings," he says. "Emotionally, you change over time. So what's happening today feels more special."

Heading: Govt moves away from symbolism in ads about schemes for minorities - Indian Express
Content:
Chiranjeevi has his film star brothers campaigning for him, while the TDP's Chandrababu Naidu has turned to the NTR magic by patching up with the former chief minister's family ahead of elections. Now it is the turn of Chief Minister Y S Rajasekhara Reddy to fall back on family. YSR's industrialist son Jaganmohan is set to to join his father and contest the next Lok Sabha elections from their native district Cuddapah.

His uncle Y S Vivekananda Reddy is currently the MP from the Congress from the constituency but is expected to vacate the seat for Y S Jaganmohan Reddy, who is the managing director and editor of Telugu daily Sakshi. YSR himself was elected from Pulivendala in Cuddapah district. Jaganmohan's office declined to comment on the matter at this stage.

Jaganmohan, in fact, was expected to take the plunge a few months after the 2004 elections. However, at the time Congress president Sonia Gandhi refused to accept the resignation of Vivekananda — who was elected from Cuddapah — to make way for his nephew.

Sources in the Andhra PCC say that while Jaganmohan is reluctant to join politics at this time, the Congress needs all hands at the deck to counter the growing influence of Chiranjeevi's Praja Rajyam Party (PRP) and the TDP. Chiranjeevi is sending shivers down many a political spine in the state, especially with his maiden roadshow that started today — being touted as the grandest Andhra has ever seen, it will showcase the mega star in his new political avatar. The Chief Minister's decision to defer plans to go to New Delhi to attend the National Development Council meeting is being seen as a direct fallout of this.

Thousands are expected to line up to see and hear Chiranjeevi during his three-day yatra. He will cover over 200 km in five Assembly constituencies in coastal Andhra — Srikakulam, Narsannapeta, Tekkali, Palasa and Ichapuram.

But even Chiranjeevi isn't taking any chances. Apart from his star power, the PRP is also banking on the matinee might of older brother Nagendra Babu and younger sibling Pawan Kalyan, who is a youth icon.

"Chiranjeevi's brother Pawan Kalyan is attracting huge, unmanageable crowds of fans at every political programme that he attends with his brother. He is loved by the youth and the party is banking on him to draw young voters into its fold," a PRP spokesperson said on Wednesday.

The effect is showing in the TDP, where Chandrababu is wooing the powerful and popular NTR clan assiduously, including NTR's sons Balakrishna and Harikrishna, and their actor sons Junior NTR and Kalyan Ram. Just a month ago, the son-in-law who was seen to have "usurped" NTR's legacy invited the former chief minister's family for lunch at his Banjara Hills residence. Harikrishna and Balakrishna attended, sons in tow. Harikrishna is also a TDP Rajya Sabha member and accompanied Chandrababu on his 'Mee Kosam' Yatra across the state.

Last Sunday, the extended NTR family converged at Ramakrishna Studios for a grand rally, with thousands of fans

welcoming them and pledging their support to the TDP. "Their (the family's) support is crucial to the party because they have a huge fan following. They have pledged their support to the TDP. They have also assured that they would take time out to join a state-wide campaign tour," TDP MP and politburo member Yerran Naidu said.

If the Chief Minister's son is an ace up its sleeve, the Congress has also found itself a trump card from Tollywood. It has found a match for PRP's Pawan Kalyan in rising star Mahesh Babu — a heart throb and youth icon, popularly known as the prince of Tollywood.

Babu has delivered some of the biggest hits in Tollywood in recent times, including Pokiri in April 2006. The son of veteran actor G Krishna, the former Congress MP from Eluru, Babu claims to be averse to politics but was seen with his father at a couple of political functions last month.

What has also set off a frenzy of speculation is the meeting organised by Krishna for his son's fans at the Padmalaya Studios on Sunday. The Congress must have cheered; hundreds of fans went crazy as Babu arrived.

Heading: The Network Spread - Indian Express
Content:
Under pressure to crack down on terror, and uneasy about rubbing minorities the wrong way ahead of elections, the Government has found a way to put across its message of giving minorities "a good deal and a fair chance" in its four and a half years in power.

Doordarshan has started airing 40-second advertisements issued by the Ministry of Minority Affairs showcasing the Centre's scheme for minorites.

The five spots centre around characters such as Meenu Wadia (a young Parsi doctor), Parvinder Kaur (a Sikh pilot, inspired by Kalpana Chawla) and Abida (a Muslim medical student covering her coaching fees with government assistance).

Under no-nonsense Secretary M N Prasad, a concerted effort has been made to do away with "overt symbols" like beards and topis to portray minorities, as was typical of government advertisements of the past. The new campaign shows them as very much a part of the mainstream.

Though the slogan, 'Aap Badhenge, Desh Badhega (Nation grows, when you grow)' is rather pithy, it also underlines the Government's message of "inclusive growth".

The advertisements are in Hindi and nine other languages, including Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Assamese, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada and Punjabi. While they are currently airing on DD, the Ministry hopes to be able to telecast its five spots on private channels as well from later this month.

The advertisements include one of the PM's 15-point programme for minorities, while the rest talk about each of the scholarship schemes instituted by the UPA — the pre-matriculation, post-matriculation and merit-cum-means scholarship for minorities.

Amitava Mitra, the senior vice-president of Percept/H, the agency that has conceptualised the advertisements, calls it one of their best campaigns ever. Percept/H also made the Bharat Nirman campaign, released earlier this year to coincide with the IPL matches.

"Our brief was clear, to not use visual cliches. Even in the ambience, we have stayed away from mosques, churches and gurdwaras," says Mitra.

Heading: PoK team crosses over, hopes to trade peace - Indian Express
Content:
It were the serial blasts of 1993 which first blurred the lines between the underworld and terrorists - the attacks were a fallout of the determination of one man, Tiger Memon, for "vengeance", funded and facilitated by Dawood Ibrahim.

Today, as investigators grapple to understand the emerging new face of terror — from cultural capitals like Pune, or convent institutes like St Antonia D'Souza in Byculla — what has remained almost constant is the underworld's role, be it in the weapons seized from the accused or hawala transactions.

In separate probes, the investigation is building leads which show an interface between members of the Indian Mujahideen and the Fazl-ur-Rehman gang. One of the gang's members, Riyaz Bhatkal, is believed to be the co-founder of the alleged terror group.

A native of Karnataka, Bhatkal's name emerged in crime sheets in Mumbra as early as 1994. His name also came up during the Malegaon blasts probe. Abdus Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer, who remains missing, assumes significance here as the man who allegedly had connections with the underworld but was also in touch with religious extremists like Md Sadiq Ahmed Sheikh (31). Sadiq is believed to have indoctrinated youth into the network and received terror training at least twice.

The Mumbai Police say that most of the men they arrested since September 24 were natives of Azamgarh and were roped in by Sadiq. Crime Branch interrogation reports show Sadiq got to know Bhatkal through Tauqeer, and soon rose in the terror hierarchy to become the point person for Bhatkal's hawala transactions.

The Delhi Police believe it was Sadiq who gave the final brief to Atif Ameen, the alleged kingpin of the Delhi September 13 blasts who was killed in the encounter at Jamia Nagar. Bhatkal is being investigated for sourcing the explosives from Karnataka.

However, sometimes links with organised crime can prove fatal, as happened with the arrest of Afzal Mutalib Usmani (32). Picked up in connection with the cars that were stolen for the Gujarat blasts, it was Usmani who revealed the names of other members of the IM. The investigators who interrogated Abu Bashar, caught from Azamgarh in connection with the Ahmedabad blasts, say Usmani was not really approved of by the IM — "he was not a namazi in the true sense of the world" — and was more of a recruit from Bhatkal's end.

Usmani has a long history of car jacking and extortion, and it was his crime record — he was also charged in a MCOCA case in the Oshiwara police station — that assisted the Crime Branch in filing MCOCA charges against the 20 arrested. Under MCOCA, at least one of the accused must have at least two chargesheeted offences in the last 10 years.

Meanwhile, a separate team is probing the other common link to organised crime syndicates and these terror groups — hawala. Based on Sadiq's alleged revelations, a total of Rs 26 lakh is under investigation. During the 2006 train blasts case, too, investigators had said an accused, Faisal Shaikh, received hawala packets at his aunt's home on Mohammed Ali Road. Two other couriers with 14,000 riyals and 10,000 riyals — which were sourced to Saudi Arabia via another wanted criminal Abdul Rehman Dawre — were reported to have reached Pune for Faisal.

The case is still pending as the hawala operator could never be found. Ironically, this may be another indicator of the ties between terror outfits and organised crime syndicates. Investigators agree that it was around 2003, towards the time that the ban on SIMI was announced, that ISI decided to route counterfeit money through SIMI, instead of relying on an organised syndicate.

ON THE TRAIL OF TERROR

July 27: Maulana Abdul Halim, a suspected SIMI activist, is arrested from Dani Limda in Ahmedabad. He was allegedly involved in instigating Muslim youth after the 2002 Gujarat violence and sending them to Uttar Pradesh for terror training. Charges are laid on him for sending 33 young men for terror training to Pakistan in 2003.

July 29: Bangalore's Anti Terrorism Squad (ATS) arrest a SIMI activist, Sameer Sadiq, in connection with the blasts. According to the police, Sadiq had played a key role in the Surat riots.

August 15: The Gujarat Police arrest Mufti Abu Bashar and nine others in connection with the Ahmedabad blasts. Bashar belongs to Binapara village in Azamgarh district of Uttar Pradesh, and is believed to be a SIMI activist.

August 16: Gujarat Director General of Police P C Pande says that Mufti Abu Bashar had confessed to being the mastermind behind the Ahmedabad blasts. The nine persons arrested by the police in the case are identified as Jahid Sheikh, Yunus Mansuri, Shamsuddin Sheikh, Arif Kadri, Gyasuddin, Imran, Usman Agarbattiwala, Iqbal Sheikh and Sajid Mansuri. All are in the age group of 20-25. Four were arrested from Vadodara and five from Ahmedabad.

September 19: Mohammad Saif is arrested after the shootout at L-18 Batla House in Jamia Nagar, New Delhi. He is charged with planting a bomb near Regal Cinema in Connaught Place. Mohammed Zeeshan is arrested from Jhandewalan and is charged with planting a bomb on Barakhamba Road.

September 21: The police identify three men who helped engineer the Delhi serial blasts. Saqib Nisar is arrested for his alleged involvement in the Delhi blasts, Mohammed Shakeel is charged with planting a bomb in Gaffar Market and Zia-ur-Rehman for planting bombs in Connaught Place.

September 23: The police announce that they have arrested five more people from Mumbai and Uttar Pradesh who played a major role in the recent blasts. All five are suspected to be part of the Indian Mujahadeen's think tank. The men were: Sadiq Sheikh, said to be one of the founding members of Indian Mujahideen; Afzal Usmani, arrested for planting the bomb at Ahmedabad Civil Hospital and stealing the car which was used in the Surat and Ahmedabad blasts; Arif Sheikh, a specialist in circuit-based bombs; Mohammed Zakir Sheikh, a project engineer with a company in Mumbai; and Mohammed Ansar Sheikh, a software engineer.

September 25: Mohammad Samee Bagewadi is arrested in Bangalore. He allegedly attended most of the training camps organised by SIMI, including those at Castle Rock near Hubli and Vagamon in Kerala. A resident of Bijapur, he was closely associated with SIMI leaders Safdar Hussain Nagori, Hafeez Hussain alias Adnan, Shibly, Tauqeer, Shahbaaz and Abu Bashar. His movements before and after the Bangalore blasts were closely tracked by the police. He was produced before the Judicial Magistrate (Bangalore) and remanded to police custody for 14 days.

October 5 :Five alleged terror suspects are picked up from Pune by the police in connection with serial blasts in Bangalore, Ahmedabad and Delhi.

October 6: The Mumbai Police claim to have arrested 15 men from Bangalore, Mangalore, Pune, Parbhani and Azamgarh.

Heading: Salaries of J-K SPOs held up for four months - Indian Express
Content:
Zulfikar Abbasi could not hide his emotions as he crossed the Kaman Post into India. "We are here to heal wounded hearts," said the chairman of the "Azad Kashmir" Chamber of Commerce as he crossed the Aman Setu this afternoon along with his 18-member trade delegation from Pakistan occupied Kashmir (PoK) to be garlanded by traders and senior Indian officials.

"This is a historical visit and will definitely bridge the divide between the two Kashmirs.
