Elaborate plans are being chalked out, which include a proposal to open a heritage hotel here, besides converting the place into a national monument for tourism purposes.

The move comes barely a few days after the fort was handed over to the civil administration after being manned by various armies for over 150 years.

Deputy Director, Tourism, Surinder Bajaj said the department was seriously considering promoting the fort as a tourist site and various aspects such as the status of the monument and its conservation have to be considered before finalising any project. He maintained that the Tourism Department has already sent a proposal worth Rs 50 crore for conservation of the fort to the Planning Commission. He added that services of technical advisors would be hired to prepare a public-private partnership (PPP) model for this purpose.

"The place is associated with Maharaja Ranjit Singh, whose legacy has always awed the public, besides containing vestiges of the British rule, which are sure to interest the tourists visiting the site," he said. He averred that the foremost aim of the department is to preserve the structure in its original form. "Apart from the structures related to Maharaja Ranjit Singh's time, structures such as the 'Phansi Ghar' and 'Dyer's Bungalow' and other existing buildings would be preserved in their original shape," he said.

Minister for Tourism and Culture Hira Singh Gabria said the Department had sought the help of the Centre. He said though the fort had now been handed over to the civil administration, the Army would continue to occupy a portion of the fort, which would be a restricted area.

Heading: Punjab Meats Ltd under HC scanner - Indian Express
Content:
Global Human Rights Council, along with the VHP, has filed a complaint in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate against cricketer Harbhajan Singh and actor Mona Singh. The duo had dressed up as Ravan and Sita in a television dance show. A copy of the complaint has been sent to the SGPC.

The complainants — Arvind Thakur, chairman of Global Human Rights Council, and Vijay Singh Bhardwaj, spokesperson for Punjab VHP — stated in the complaint that to "save the rich culture of Hinduism", action should be taken against persons who "want to ruin and damage or wound religious feelings of Hindus". The case would be taken up on Monday.

The complainants have demanded that Harbhajan and Mona should tender an apology in writing in court. Similar complaints would also be filed in Amritsar, Jalandhar, Bathinda and Shimla, among other places. The representatives of the two organisations would also visit different cities over the issue. A meeting would also be held with the legal cell of the SGPC.

Bhardwaj, meanwhile, said they would also meet the DGP. "A number of complaints have been registered against Harbhajan Singh in different cases. How can such a person be allowed to continue as DSP. We would meet the DGP on Tuesday and demand that Harbhajan be suspended," said Bhardwaj.

Heading: Fear of terror strikes: Cops sound statewide alert - Indian Express
Content:
Reprimanded for not obeying court directions to install effluent treatment plant

Punjab Meats Limited (PML) Industries, Dera Bassi, is in a soup for not installing an effluent treatment plant (ETP), thereby resulting in pollution in the vicinity. The conduct of the unit, owned by Dr A.S. Bindra, father of ace shooter

Abhinav Bindra, has come under the scanner of the Punjab and Haryana High Court yet again.

A report highlighting the "stubborn" attitude of the unit in not installing an ETP was submitted in the High Court last week.

Taking strong note of the report, Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur had expressed his anguish over the conduct of the unit and questioned its counsel as to why the unit should not be closed down immediately.

The detailed report, which was submitted by the Punjab Pollution Control Board, Assistant Environmental Engineer, Nodal Office, Mohali, has highlighted as to how despite several directions passed by the High Court and Supreme Court of India, the ETP has not been installed and made functional till date.

It is apparent from the report (see box) that the industry has failed to upgrade its effluent treatment plant and achieve the effluent standards laid down by the Board.

M/s PML Industries established its industrial plant in 1995 for the manufacture of boneless meat, bone meat meal and edible oils by slaughtering buffaloes. A complaint was received from residents of nearby villagers in 1996, in which it was alleged that the unit was discharging its waste water into the drain.

The unit was visited by officers of the Board on June 3, 1996, and it was observed that the ETP was not in operation. The unit had also not made proper arrangements for the disposal of waste water.

Notices were issued to the unit for its closure by the department and even its electricity connection was disconnected a couple of times owing to the non-installation of ETP.

Aggrieved, the unit moved the High Court, which granted an interim stay. However, since the company failed to install the ETP, the High Court in 2006 passed orders to close down the unit. However, the unit got a stay on the High Court order from the Supreme Court.

Remanding the case back to the High Court, the Supreme Court had directed the PPCB to take fresh samples of water from the unit. The unit was directed to install the unit by March this year, which it again failed to do.

Irked over this, the Chief Justice last week reprimanded PML Industry for not obeying the court directions. The unit has been given time to file a reply by next week.

Heading: Diamonds worth 1.5 cr looted - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Police have sounded a high alert in the state to avoid terror strikes during the ongoing festive season. Expressing fear that displaced groups of pan-Islamic fundamentalist groups, including Students' Islamic Movement of India (SIMI), Indian Mujahideen (IM), Lashkar-e-Toiba and Huji, were desperately trying to re-organise themselves and were determined to demonstrate their striking potential during the festive season, Punjab Additional Director General of Police (ADGP), in a communiqué to all Punjab deputy inspector generals, senior superintendents of police and inspector generals of police of Patiala, Jalandhar and Border Range Amritsar, has asked to "mount special vigil over places offering public computer/internet facilities as also connectivity through WiFi".

"In the context of Punjab, last year terrorists had stuck on the day of Id in Ludhiana at the Shingar cinema, which claimed seven lives. Babbar Khalsa module was involved in the crime," the letter, a copy of which is in the possession of The Indian Express, says, apparently pointing towards the vulnerability of terror strikes during the festive season.

The letter says that countrywide networking of SIMI, IM, Lashkar-e-Toiba and Huji had been unearthed in the wake of serial blasts in Bangalore, Ahmedabad and Delhi recently, leading to the arrest of dozens of activists of these outfits.

Highlighting the aspect that joining of educated boys well conversant with the use of computers, internet and cyber tricks was a cause of concern, the letter says that "under the new Police Act, SSPs have been given powers to check nuisance at public places".

Enclosing a copy of draft orders under Section 144 of CrPC in that regard, SSPs have been advised to liaise with the district magistrates for ensuring effective covering of cyber cafes. The draft order contains provisions like prohibiting the use of cafes by unknown persons, maintaining a register for identity of visitors, making an entry in the register in the handwriting of the visitor mentioning name, address, telephone number and identity proof and signature of visitor on the register. The draft order also reads that activity server log should be preserved in the main server and its records should be preserved for at least six months.

Heading: More and more people in their 30s, 40s falling prey to stress: expert - Indian Express
Content:
A Mumbai-based diamond trader, Bhupesh Shah, was robbed of diamonds worth Rs 1.5 crore near Phillaur last night. The robbers put chilli powder in Shah's eyes and stabbed him, before decamping with the diamonds. A case has been registered against unidentified persons at Phillaur police station.

Bhupesh Shah had reached Phillaur by Shatabdi Express on Thursday and stayed in a hotel overnight, from where he, along with an associate, took a taxi for Jalandhar in the morning. On the way, the driver stopped the taxi at a deserted place close to Puccapur village, when the robbers attacked the trader and took away three bags from him, including the bags containing diamonds, some cash and his credit cards, said the trader. The robbers took away the taxi too, he said. The associate later took Shah to Phillaur Civil Hospital with the help of some passers-by.

When contacted, SP (detective) Paramvir Parmar said the possibility of the driver being the culprit cannot be ruled out and investigations are on.

Heading: movie review - Indian Express
Content:
In the rapidly changing world and the excruciatingly fast-paced advances, stress levels have increased manifold in the urban population. Psychologists say this is just the right time to imbibe strategies to cope with stress in daily lives.

Psychiatrists maintain that the number of people in their 30s and 40s are now increasingly walking into clinics to seek expert help to cope with increasing professional and domestic pressure.

Dr Kiran Bala, Consultant Psychiatrist, Cheema Medical Complex, Mohali, said that stress needs to be diagnosed at a proper time just to address it effectively.

"Stress is technically termed as a psychological and physiological response to any event that significantly tends to upset psychological equilibrium amongst individuals to varying degrees, depending upon the gravity of situation and sensitivity levels of individuals. While death of spouse, divorce, marital discord or separation, jail-term, death in family, injury, illness, retirement and unemployment are the major reasons for stress amongst individuals, a second category of stressors in the form of environmental, relation triggered and work related factors also affect people to a great extent," said the doctor.

Insufficient salary, office politics and relations with bosses and colleagues are other common reasons for professionals coping with stress at the workplace.

"What is more concerning, however, are the effects of stress triggered by any of these factors," comments Dr Bala.

"Infertility, heart diseases, migraine, diabetes and various kinds of chronic pains are proven to be directly caused due to stress in life. Ulcers, asthma, irritable bowel diseases, pre-menstrual syndrome and skin ailments are in a number of ways showing more incidences among stress affected individuals," adds the doctor.

STRESS ON DE-STRESS

* Optimum stress control and not necessarily total elimination of stress (which may be virtually impossible) has to be achieved

* Saying no is important just as it is crucial to know one's limits and work within those limits

* Irritating people, intolerable and unpleasant news stories and ambiences like overcrowded streets, jammed roads and traffic snarls are best avoided. Contentious issues are best left if one is perturbed by the content

* Being more extrovert and expressive in articulating your pent up thoughts and feelings is a great reliever

* Being assertive many a time is extremely important, adaptability to reach out for compromises and mid-way solutions can be of real help

Heading: Cops short of staff, farmers continue to dry paddy on road - Indian Express
Content:
Hello

CAST: Sharman Joshi, Sohail Khan, Gul Panag, Amrita Arora, Isha Koppikar, Sharat Saxena, Dalip Tahil, Salman Khan, Katrina Kaif; DIRECTOR: Atul Agnihotri

One night in a call centre, there comes a phone call. Really, a phone call in a call centre, cries Salman Khan (playing himself), in mock amazement. Pretty laptop-toting story-teller (Katrina) smiles mysteriously, and begins her yarn. And as yarns go, it isn't too bad. The trouble with Hello, based on Chetan Bhagat's mega-seller, is that isn't too good either.

It's a dark rainy night, and Shyam aka Sam (Sharman) is hurting because the love of his life Priyanka (Gul) has said yes to a rich NRI. Varun aka Vrroom (Sohail) has his eye on Esha (Isha), but all she wants is to become a model. Radhika (Amrita) tries to please her horrible mom-in-law by day, and pops anti-depressants by night because her husband is a two-timing cad. And Military Uncle (Sharat) is upset because his US-based son wants to have nothing to do with him.

These sad sack call centre agents rattle around in a large room with work stations placed miles apart. That's a total wrong number. Except for a barmy systems guy, and smarmy boss (Dalip), there doesn't seem to be a soul else in Atul Agnihotri's scheme of things: he's clearly not aware of all those rows and rows of super-busy souls — sitting elbow-to-elbow, nattering the night away on their headphones and mikes— that seem to be more the norm in these nocturnal work hives echoing with faux American accents.

You could also call Hello a case of six characters in search of a zingy script. Bhagat's novel is not literature, but manages to capture some of the hurly-hurly of New India's preoccupation with instant money, getting ahead and greenbacks. The film's canvas is largely empty, so the good turn by Sharman Joshi gets lost. As does some genuinely funny banter, and the Khan family's full turnout (Salman with his shirt off, girlfriend Kat in a cameo, chhota bhai Arbaaz in a walk on) on account of Agnihotri being the Khans' brother-in-law.

Even that thing that call centre types are allegedly indulging in all the time—making out on down-time in the back of a convenient SUV— pictured here on Sharman and Gul, lacks fire. It's tepid, just like the movie.

Heading: Commission of milk dealers increased - Indian Express
Content:
While farmers from various districts, presently visiting the Panchkula Anaj Mandi in Sector 20, are busy drying the paddy on the main sector road for the last 15 days, the Panchkula traffic police is oblivious to the harrowing time the commuters are facing.

Despite being informed about the unauthorised diversions a number of times, the daily commuters rue of inaction by the police.

To further add to the problem is the fact that the road on which the unauthorised diversion has been done, leads to the Zirakpur-Pinjore National highway thus making the entire area accident prone. "It has been more than ten days now ever since the farmers occupied most of the Sector 20 road. The traffic police officers have been requested a number of times to either remove the unauthorised blockade or press a traffic police official into service so that the commuters on the road do not face any problem," said Rakesh Mahajan, a resident of Sector 20.

Sumit Gupta, another resident, said: "The traffic police seems to be in a deep slumber even when people go about blocking the roads, creating diversions on their own and risking the lives of the commuters. The other day, a family of Sector 7 went ahead diverting the traffic on the main sector 6/7 dividing road, for a wedding. The traffic police took no action against them," added Gupta.

Talking to Newsline, a traffic police officer on condition of anonymity said, "We are really short of staff due to which the traffic police officers cannot be pressed into service at the spot. Besides, we are yet to receive any communication from the Sector 20 police station asking the traffic branch to depute a traffic police officer there."

Heading: PK Sharma is MC secretary - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana Dairy Development Cooperative Federation on Friday increased the commission of dealers and distributors of Vita milk and milk products from 17 paise per litre to 20 paise per litre. This will come in effect from October 16. A decision to this effect was taken in a meeting held by Chandravati, the chairperson of the Haryana Dairy Development Cooperative Federation, with the dealers and distributors of the products.

More than 70 distributors and dealers from across the state and neighboring states like Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand were present.

The raise has been made on the basis of the persistent demand of dealers, regarding a change in the pricing policy. They claimed the raise will help in increasing the sale of products in the state as well as other areas. The federation also decided to raise the transportation charges to 2 paisa per litre, on account of the increase in fuel prices.

Heading: SBoP officers demonstrate against merger - Indian Express
Content:
The UT Administration shuffled charges and additional charges given to various officers on Friday. The decision was taken after Samwartak Singh, Haryana Civil Services officer, was appointed as Director Public Instructions (Schools) and UT Chief Engineer SK Jaitley suffered a fracture.

Samwartak Singh, who, before being appointed as DPI(S), was holding the charge of Municipal Corporation Secretary, has now been relieved of his charge, which is now given to PK Sharma, another HCS officer, posted as Additional Commissioner, Municipal Corporation.

On the other hand, UT Chief Engineer SK Jaitley had to be hospitalised after suffering a hip fracture.

The charge has now been given to Krishanjit Singh, Superintending Engineer (B & R), in addition to his own duties. The orders were issued by the UT Administrator today.

In partial modification, the additional charge of Chief Engineer, Chandigarh Housing Board, was

taken from Krishanjit Singh and entrusted to Surinder Pall, Superintending Engineer (Operations), in addition to his own duties, till the time the Chandigarh Housing Board makes an alternative arrangement or till further orders, whichever is earlier.

Also, the Chandigarh Administration, Department of Personnel's orders entrusting the charge of Joint Chief Electoral Officer, UT, to a Punjab Civil Services (PCS) officer Inderjit Singh Sandhu, was withdrawn. Another PCS officer Manjit Singh Brar, who is also the Director (Information Technology), will continue to look after the charge of Joint Chief Electoral Officer.

Heading: Agriculturists’ murder solved, 1 arrested - Indian Express
Content: Nearly 500 officers of the State Bank of Patiala (SBoP) held a demonstration outside the bank's head office on Friday to protest against the proposed merger of the bank with the State Bank of India. Amar Singh, general secretary, Associate Banks Officers' Association unit, SBoP, said the officers of the State Bank Group have been forced by the management of State Bank of India and the Government of India to resort to agitation as the management has failed to give firm commitments on improvements of superannuation scheme and for abeyance in the merger proposal of the remaining six associate banks.  Singh said that the officers of the State Bank Group will go on an indefinite strike from October 20 if the State Bank management fails to address their demands.

Heading: Banquet owners’ body cries foul over resumption of plots - Indian Express
Content:
The ged murderer of a sexagenarian agriculturist Sher Singh, who was killed in Machhli Kalan village in Mohali on September 26, was nabbed in Fatehgarh Sahib.

Inder Mahato, a farm labourer from Batolia village of Bihar confessed to having killed the landlord with robbery as the motive, Fatehgarh Sahib SSP Dr Kaustubh Sharma told Newsline.

Mahato also admitted to killing another farm labourer Topan Chaudhary alias Poorna Chand of Raniganj village in Acharia district of Bihar on September 16 in the fields falling under Fatehgarh Sahib district, disclosed the SSP.

Sharma said preliminary interrogations revealed that Mahato wanted to make quick bucks and first targeted Topan.

From Topan, confessed Mahato, Rs 2 to 3,000 cash, a cellphone and a radio set was robbed while with a similar aim, he killed Sher.

The SSP revealed that after killing Sher, Mahato rummaged for valuables but found only a few bidis and some food.

A wooden log, allegedly used to execute the murders, and the robbed material has been recovered from Mahato, who was remanded in police custody till October 13.

Mohali district police officials said they will bring Mahato on production warrants after expiry of his Fatehgarh Sahib police remand.

Heading: Election soon to elect Kharar civic body chief - Indian Express
Content:
The Mohali Banquet Owners' Association has cried foul over the recent resumption of four industrial plots being used as marriage palaces and banquet halls in Phase VI in Mohali.

Association leaders Raman Khanna, Ankit Bindlish and Parveen Kumar, accused the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) officials of adopting a "pick and choose" policy and alleged that 90 per cent of the total 200 industrial plots in Mohali are being misused.

They have also sought a uniform policy on the Chandigarh pattern for regularisation of violating the industrial plots in Mohali. "We had applied for the grant of a change of land use (CLU) but GMADA did not give us sufficient time to pursue our case, while no action was taken against any other violator," said an owner whose plot has been resumed.

The association pointed out: "As per the notification by the Punjab and the Central government, hotel falls under the category of an industry, but we have been denied this right by the Industries department in Mohali."

The owners, meanwhile, have now sought permission to register industrial units being used as marriage palaces and banquet halls as hotels, and have sought cancellation of their resumption orders.

While releasing a list of 56 industrial plots, which were carrying out commercial activities in violation of the Allotment Policy, the association claimed that government offices, car showrooms, godowns, transport companies, shops, liquor vends, educational institutes, call centres, dhabas, weighing bridges, iron and steel shops were running from such industrial units.

They alleged that the GMADA was issuing no objection certificates (NOC) to certain industrial plot owners, including those involved in commercial activities for procuring power connection (commercial). "Apart from being a dual policy, it is also causing heavy losses to the Punjab State Electricity Board, as commercial and industrial electricity rates vary by almost 50 per cent," they said.

Rejecting the present policy for regularisation, which requires an 80-feet wide front road and a 200-feet wide front, the Association has urged Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal, to come to their rescue and revise the policy to make it "owner friendly" so that Mohali's industry does not have to face any problems in the future.

GMADA Estate Officer Sukhjeet Pal Singh, meanwhile, said: "We had conducted a survey and all plot owners found violating the allotment norms were either issued or are being issued notices regarding the same. Resumption orders against four plots were issued after completing the procedures and giving their owners ample time to defend their case. Proceedings against the other violators are also moving ahead in a similar way. I never issued any NOC, as alleged, allowing for commercial power connection to industrial plots."

Heading: Counselling, trips — schools aid students to ease exam woes - Indian Express
Content:
SDM appointed convener, to hold first meet next week

Almost a month after the election of 15 new councillors to the Kharar Municipal Council (MC), the way has been paved for the election of the president and two vice-presidents for the civic body.

Though the Punjab State Election Commission had notified the names of the newly elected municipal councillors on September 17, the Punjab and Haryana High Court had, on a petition challenging the reservation for the offices of municipalities in Punjab, stayed the elections of presidents of any civic body in the state.

As the petition was disposed off recently, with which the stay was vacated, the Punjab Department of Local Government has asked Mohali Deputy Commissioner to take immediate steps to conduct the first meeting of the Kharar MC to administer oath to the newly elected municipal councillors and holding election for the top posts.

Confirming the development, Deputy Commissioner Rahul Bhandari told Newsline that he has appointed Kharar SDM Rajeev Kumar Gupta as convener and directed him to complete the process of administering oath and conducting the election as per rules.

Rule 3(1) of the Punjab Municipal (President and Vice-President) Election Rules, 1994, stipulates 14 days from the date of notification of election for holding the first civic body meeting to elect the president and vice-presidents, besides administering oath to the elected members.

Kharar SDM Rajeev Kumar Gupta said he will soon issue a 48-hour notice to the elected municipal councillors to hold the first meeting of the Kharar MC next week.

Meanwhile, lobbying to grab the top posts has intensified as the ruling Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD)-Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) combine, which had made clean sweep in the MC polls, is yet to announce any name.

The candidates considered strong contenders for the post include SAD's Gurprem Singh from Ward 4 and Sukhwant Singh, brother of Chamkaur Sahib MLA Charanjit Singh, from Ward 8. Besides, the names of Roshan Lal from Ward 9, who became the seniormost councillor after being elected for the fifth consecutive time and Jai Bhagwan Singla from Ward 15, who was vice-president of the previous MC house are also doing the rounds.

While Gurprem enjoys the patronage of Punjab Cooperation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh, Charanjit was perusing the case of Sukhwant as Sukhwant's wife Paramjit Kaur has also won from Ward 11 to become the first and only councillor couple in Kharar.

Heading: 24-yr-old dies as speeding car, bus collide - Indian Express
Content:
Examinations are a time of anxiety and nervousness and schools in the city are making every effort to ward off stress and make it an easy ride for the students. Various schools across the city are organising activities, including counselling sessions, for the anxiety-ridden students.

As the Board examinations draw closer, students often get baffled amid pressure to perform.This especially holds true for Class XII students who score high on the stress metre in wake of numerable competitive tests. While schools encourage students to talk it out with counsellors, they also make sure that students are taken on excursions especially organised to de-stress them.

"With so much competition around, students are a worried lot. The stress takes a toll on them especially when the Boards approach. Immediately after the half-yearly examinations, we take students of Class X on a one-day trip so that they can relax," says Sanjay Sardana of Manav Mangal Smart School.

"It is essential for students to unwind if they want to improve their performance," he added.

Schools are also particular about providing the right guidance in terms of career and related matters. For the same, career fests are organised regularly. "Students of Class XII are more hassled especially when they are unable to make a right career choice. Just to relieve them of the confusion, we organise a career fest every year. It not only helps them choose the right vocation but also opens new avenues," says Rakesh Sachdeva, principal, DAV Model School, Sector 15. She adds that the school regularly holds competitions like creative writing and sport tournaments among others to channelise the energy of students, especially of Class X and XII.

Some schools have also taken the spiritual way to reduce the anxiety levels among students. "We hold mediation sessions for students from Class IX onwards. It is an exercise to connect the students with their inner self and give them peace. During examination time, this activity holds all the more significance and benefits students immensely," says Punita Singh, counsellor, Carmel Convent School.

Heading: At PEC campus placement, pay cheques get fatter - Indian Express
Content:
A 24-year-old man lost his life when a speeding bus hit his Innova car in the early hours of Friday. The incident took place in Sector 45.

According to police, Davinder Singh, 24, who worked with a property dealer in Mohali and lived in Phase 11, was going to Sector 17 with his friend Balwinder Singh for dinner at 1.30 am. They had just dropped back home a prospective client who was taken to a site visit.

From Phase 11, the Innova was coming towards Chandigarh, while a Punjab Roadways bus from Pathankot was going towards the Sector 43 bus stand. Eyewitnesses said both the vehicles were speeding and did not slow down on reaching the Sectors 45/46/49/50 light point.

The impact of the collision was such that the car overturned after hitting the divider. The bus driver also lost control over the vehicle and once again banged into the car before coming to a halt. The sound of the collision could be heard a kilometre away, police said.

Passengers of the bus immediately pulled out both Davinder and Balwinder of the mangled car. The two, along with three of the injured passengers, were rushed to the Government Medical College and Hospital, Sector 32. Davinder died on the way. Balwinder's condition is stated to be critical.

The condition of the bus passengers — Pardeep, Shanti Devi and Ashok Kumar — is out of danger.

Police have arrested the bus driver, Davinder Singh, after registering a case of rash driving and causing death due to negligence. "He (the deceased) was driving fast. I tried to avert an accident and applied brakes, but failed to prevent the collision," he said.

The body of the deceased was handed over to the relatives after conducting postmortem at the Government Multi-Specialty Hospital in Sector 16.

Gurnam Singh, a relative of the deceased, said they had not broken the news of Davinder's death to his pregnant wife. Davinder was to take her to doctor for a regular check-up. "We told her he has gone out of station and will return by evening. I don't know how do we break the news to her," he said.

Heading: Expressways inch towards progress - Indian Express
Content:
For the students passing out from the Punjab Engineering College (PEC), the placement season for the 2007-08 academic session, has been nothing less than a fairy tale. Five students were offered hefty packages of Rs 9.21 lakh per annum by Microsoft while five others were offered salaries of Rs 8 lakh per annum by CISCO. The other students have been offered pay packages ranging between Rs 5.5 to 7 lakh.

The authorities at the PEC maintain that the turmoil in the stock markets have had no major impact on the placement activity. Talking to Newsline, K K Garg, Training and Placement Officer, said: "The companies have reduced their intake by almost 30 per cent, but that has not impacted us. It is because the companies look for quality that we are never short of. They are always ready to hire our students."

Of the 66 companies that visited the campus, the prominent names included: D-Shaw, Microsoft, Cisco, Goldman Sachs, Tata Motors, Free Scale and others.

PEC Director Dr Manoj Dutta said, "The trend has shifted from software to core engineering streams and students wish to join companies dealing in core engineering related aspects." He added, "The PEC has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with JCB, CSIO and Phillips."

Heading: Dengue on the rise, PU students organise blood donation camp - Indian Express
Content:
There still seems to be hope for Mohali as 'Future City' — an epithet given by Shiromani Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal —to hop onto the fastrack. Even as 13 infrastructure development projects still languish in the pipeline (as reported in Newsline on Thursday), construction of two Expressways to Mohali is inching ahead successfully.

While the Mohali-Phagwara Expressway will connect the upcoming Mohali International Airport with Amritsar and Jalandhar via Phagwara, the other Expressway will provide direct access to industrial town Lalru in Punjab and industrial hub Baddi in Himachal Pradesh. Both the Expressways are proposed to come up at an estimated cost of Rs 3,400 crore on a design, build, finance and operate (DBFO) basis.

M/s Louis Berger Inc has been named the technical consultant and will submit the preliminary project proposal for both the Expressways within 4 months. Land acquisition notices for both the mega-projects are likely to be issued by the Public Works Department (Building and Roads) later this month, said an official of the Punjab Infrastructure Development Board (PIDB), the executing agency for the project.

According to preliminary estimates, the Expressway around Mohali will involve acquisition of almost 1,500 acres of land while figures for the Mohali-Phagwara Expressway are still to be worked out.

While construction of the 104.2-km long Mohali-Phagwara Expressway, which will start near Kharar, is estimated to cost Rs 2,000 crore, the Expressway around Mohali will cost Rs 1,400 crore. Construction of the 67.7-km long Expressway will start from National Highway-22 near Lalru and crisscross through NH-64 in Banur, NH-95 and NH-21 in Kharar to join NH-21-A near Baddi. This road is expected to ease vehicular movement around Mohali and considerably shorten the distance from Lalru and Mohali to Baddi, Himachal Pradesh's most preferred investment destination.

Details of other infrastructure development projects, including the Rs 100-crore Green Field Super-Specialty Hospital and a Rs-200 crore five-star hotel-cum-international convention centre, are still being worked out.

For the upgrade and beautification of the urban road network in Mohali, a project with an estimated cost of Rs 300 crore, Dickson Rothschild India Private Limited, New Delhi, was appointed design consultant on September 15. The agreement is yet to be signed.

Also in the pipeline is a Fast Food Counter in Kurali worth Rs 3 crore, widening and strengthening of the existing road from Mullanpur to T-junction at Rs 15 crore, computerised inter-state check-points in Mohali, Balongi, Zirakpur and Lalru, a fruit and vegetable market in Mohali to come at a cost of Rs 50 crore and a Rs 150-crore Sports Complex.

Heading: PU Senate polls: votes tampered with, allege contestants - Indian Express
Content: A blood donation camp was organised at the Students' Centre in Panjab University on Friday. The camp was held by the student council in memory of Narender Mohan (former Member of Parliament). Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti, while inaugurating the camp, said that Mohan was an eminent scholar who had made outstanding contributions to the society. More than 50 units of blood were collected during the four-hour long camp. Director of the Blood Bank Society in Sector 37, said that there is a great need of blood supply presently as dengue patients from nearby states are regularly visiting hospitals including PGI and GMCH, Sector 32.

Heading: Alumni do not want PEC to change its name, says director - Indian Express
Content:
Contestants who lost the recently held graduate constituency elections of the Senate have moved a petition to Vice-President Hamid Ansari, who is also the chancellor of the Panjab University, demanding an inquiry in their complaint regarding the tampering of votes.

They have done this in lieu of PU Registrar Professor S S Bari, who was the returning officer for the election, not taking any action against the complaint filed by them.

The contestants who have moved the petition include: Paramjit Singh, Lajwant Virk and Jagdeep.

They had earlier made a complaint to Professor Bari, complaining the tampering of votes by one of the contestants, Maneesh Pal Singh, from Malout. They had complained that Maneesh Singh, had captured the polling booths at many places in Malout as a fall out of which, he emerged victorious in the elections. They had also mentioned the areas where the alleged tampering of votes had taken place.

According to the regulations of the Senate elections, anybody can file a written complaint, which has to be addressed to the returning officer, and after that, complainants can be sent to the chancellor, following which, they might move court.

The contestants, in their written complaint, had earlier demanded a legal opinion, in the absence of which, they later wrote to the chancellor.

Talking to Newsline, Parmajit Singh said: "We are sure that the votes have been tampered with and have demanded legal action. We have moved this petition in the absence of any action being taken and might move court if justice is not met."

Professor Bari, meanwhile, said: "I carried out investigations and my report was that there was no tampering. We had sent 30 observers and based on their reports, we concluded that nothing went wrong. As far as the petition is concerned, I will answer the chancellor accordingly."

Heading: Now, VAT on all items for sale at Students’ Centre - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Engineering College took up as many as 100 consultancy projects in the last year, which resulted in a turnover of Rs 60 lakh for the college, said Dr Manoj Dutta, director of the institute at a press conference today.

The college authorities said they aim to increase the number of such projects to 150. Elaborating upon the controversy regarding the change of the name of the institute, Dutta, said a decision would be taken, after consulting the views of the alumni.

A committee had earlier been formed regarding this, after the college had been granted the status of a deemed university. No decision could, however, be taken.

Dr Dutta said: "There is no controversy regarding the change in name. It's just that the alumni don't want PEC to lose its originality and as a result, we have not reached a conclusion yet."

The convocation of the Punjab Engineering College is to start on Saturday.

Giving details of the consultancy projects, the authorities said these were regarding the energy audit of Chandigarh, construction of a steel bridge, the Hydro electrical project among others.

Dutta said, "We have many ongoing projects and are expecting more. Our aim is not to commercialise our services but if they can be put to use for important projects, we are always ready."

The campus has also signed MoU's with different companies and has undertaken projects for them as well.

Dr K K Garg, Training and Placement Officer, said placements in the campus have grown better with an increase in the packages offered by the companies by 20 per cent.

Heading: Home Secy releases book on tourism - Indian Express
Content:
Shopowners at the Students' Centre in Panjab University are a disgruntled lot as they received a communication from the Administration today demanding imposition of VAT on all food items. After the imposition, food items are expected to get expensive by around Rs 4 to 5.

Both shopowners and students at the university have opposed the move and plan to meet the officials from the Administration regarding the same. Talking to Newsline, Brinder Dhillon, president, SOPU, said: "The shopowners approached us saying that they have received a communication from the Administration regarding the imposition of VAT. Panjab University, being an educational institute, services here should be made available at subsidised rates and in case the decision is not reversed, we plan to launch an agitation against the same."

One of the shopowners said: "We shall take up the matter with the vice-chancellor and request him to approach the Administration regarding the same. We are already selling goods at subsidised rates and VAT as such, should not be applicable to us."

While members of the student's council have already approached Dean Students Welfare Professor Naval Kishore, and are expecting a relief, students maintain that in case the decision is not reversed, they along with the shopowners, will go on strike.

Heading: ‘I aspire to be a public servant and pursue my passion for dance’ - Indian Express
Content: Home Secretary Ram Niwas released a book titled Chandigarh-A Tourist Paradise on Friday. The Chandigarh Tourism department extended its full support to author and veteran educationist R K Thaman, who has compiled information for the book. The book provides handy information about Chandigarh which will benefit local as well as foreign tourists. The book is on sale at all the tourist information centres and counters. The Home Secretary said, "The book should be available as a reference material to tourists in all the rooms of CITCO hotels." He appreciated the efforts by the Tourism department and Thaman in bringing out the book. Finance Secretary Sanjay Kumar, Vivek Atray, Director Public Relations and Cultural Affairs-Cum-Director, Chandigarh Tourism and Vinod Kalia, Deputy Director Tourism were also present among others at the function.

Heading: Last bite with  Adah Sharma - Indian Express
Content:
Ten-year-old Urvi Manocha, a student of Manav Mangal School, Sector 27, has many accolades to her credit. To start with, she was the youngest recipient of the National Bal Shree Award in 2007, in the creative performance category, presented to her by President Pratibha Patil at the Rashtrapati Bhavan on June 10 this year.

"It was a dream come true to receive the award from the President. I have always admired her for rising to the highest office in the country being a woman and meeting her was a great experience," she says.

She had no doubts about winning, Urvi says. "My parents had full confidence in me and I too, had faith in god," she smiles.

Always among the top five in class, Urvi, enjoys an excellent academic record. Famous danseuse Shovana Narayan, she says, is her inspiration. "She is a civil servant and a dancer. I aspire to be like her: a public servant and pursuing my passion for dance at the same time," she says.

Like other children of her age, she too, loves painting, reading books, playing badminton and swimming. Her favourite subjects include Mathematics and Science. Apart from that, she is also learning classical music and has given a number of performances in the city.

Her father, she says, is a source of constant support. He made sure that Urvi started training in Kathak when she was four years.

Apart from such pursuits, Urvi loves watching cartoons and dance shows on television. She quips, "Pogo is my favourite channel."

Heading: Wines come of age - Indian Express
Content: My last memorable meal was one day before the release of my film 1920 at this place called Ranjit Panipuriwala at Kala Ghoda. I went there with my mother and a very dear friend. I was a little nervous about my film, but I made sure I ate a lot. We ordered for pani puri, dahi puri, bhel puri and ragda pattice. I can still feel the taste lingering in my mouth. I am a slave to pani puri and couldn't resist a second helping. Our stomachs were bursting by then and we couldn't drink anything. I vividly remember the taste of the food, and the company too which was the icing on the cake. I love chat at any time of the day and in a large quantity. Since the restaurant is situated close to my home, I head there at least twice a week.

Heading: Small Talk - Indian Express
Content:
The Sommelier is projecting itself as the city's first family wine restaurant and endeavours to drop the 'elite' tag from the spirit

A sommelier or wine steward, is a trained and knowledgeable wine professional, usually found working in fine restaurants, who specialises in all aspects of wine service. The role is more specialised and informed than that of someone who merely serves. This is exactly what The Sommelier, a multi-brand domestic wine restaurant, located on Baner Road aspires to be for the people of Pune. Owned by Jagdish Patli and Vinod Deokar, the restaurant aims to turn wine drinking into a part of our regular dining experience.

Wine has been coming of age in India and with consumption increasing in leaps and bounds India is headed for a wine revolution." Wine consumption is mainly concentrated in Mumbai and Delhi, places like Pune and Bangalore too have the right kind of crowd to appreciate fine wines, subject to awareness and availibility," says Jagdish Patil.

Although the restaurant will stock a few International wines, it believes in promoting Indian wines and offers a wide selction from Chateau Indage, Renaissance, Sula and much more. With the issuing of the E-2 licence, it has become possible for the retailers to buy directly from the manufacturers, thus cutting costs by 24 per cent. "This benefit gets completely passed onto our customers." Hence a 90 ml glass of white wine costs Rs 50 while Champagne costs Rs150.The wines are paired appropriately in the menu, which offers Indian and Chinese food. Also available are wine-based cocktails such as Cool Café, (red wine, lime juice,orange juice and choco) and Whispering Palm, (Litchi, white wine, strawberry crush and Limca).

The Sommelier also conducts wine tasting sessions, trips to wineries and vineyards and airs documentaries on winemaking. With the interiors being a shade too bright and contemporary to be elegant and the menu being a bit too commonplace to be exclusive, the Sommelier does not, infact, assume to be elite, what it does aim though is to bring wine culture to the masses.

Heading: Tribute to a legend - Indian Express
Content:
Racing Art

For all the race-lovers, this derby weekend promises much more than just glamour and gallops. Once again giving the discerning art lover an opportunity to view fine art and sculpture, Neena Shahani presents Art on the Turf, an art exhibition showcasing the selected works of 23 established Indian contemporary artists, at The Royal Western Turf Club. Renowned artists like D S Rane, Anjani Reddy, Rini Dhumal, Girija Mirchandani, Rohan Sonavan and Ravi Mandlik will have their creations on display today from 11 am to 9 pm.

Heading: River pollution: Annual voyage from Alandi flagged off - Indian Express
Content:
The doyen of Kathak Rohini Bhate has left behind a void that her disciples and admirers know will never be filled

Rohini Bhate has passed away. And with her has ended a chapter in the history of Kathak. Groomed by her guru late Lacchhu Maharaj and late Mohanrao Kalyanpurkar, Rohinitai evolved a unique and innovative style of her own that greatly enriched the dance form.

Senior Kathak disciple, Manisha Sathe, though not a disciple of Rohinitai, said, the celebrated guru had witnessed a number of her performances, and the fact that she was watching was a great motivation for her. "My guru Gopi Krishnaji took Kathak to international standards and on similar lines, at a time when performances by women were not looked at with respect, Rohinitai brought respect to this dance form not only in India but also across the globe. She absorbed the initial shocks and laid an easy path for us. With this an era in the history of Kathak has ended," said Sathe.

Yogini Gandhi, senior Kathak and Odissi dancer, said Rohini Bhate was amongst the very few artists whose life was an extension of her art. "She represented some of the highest tenets of classicism and it is these values and principles that will continue to inspire generations of dancers. Over the years many things that she has said have remained with me as beacons of light that show you the correct path. One of them that come to mind now is her belief that a dancer should be illuminated from within; it is the inner radiance that reflects upon the face and not the light from outside. She guided and led through example and the greatest tribute to her would be to be true to one's art and carry on the quest for perfection," elaborated Gandhi.

Actor and dancer Sharvari Jamenis called Rohinitai her guru, mother and guide. "I have spent almost 20-25 years of my life closely observing Rohinitai. In fact I took up dancing seeing her perform. Rohinitai was a living legend and an expert all-rounder in aspects related to Kathak like music, literature, languages and so on. Every student of Nrityabharati, strived to be like her," said Jamenis.

Rujuta Soman, Kathak dancer and Rohinitai's disciple, referred to her the embodiment of dedication, knowledge and determination. "Even after her by-pass surgery she had the stamina and energy to give an hour-and-a-half long performance. We are lucky to have got a guru like her. It is now our responsibility to carry on the legacy of Rohinitai," said Soman. According to dance critic Sunil Kothari, "There was a certain grace and gentleness associated with her. Nrityabharati was a cultural index of life. The institution and Rohini made Maharashtra proud. For Rohini, recognition came late in life. Hers was the quality that the Sanskrit writers convey by the phrase Sthiradyuti Jyoti — the steady dance."

Heading: Docs shut clinics; demand action against assault on fraternity - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to spread awareness on water pollution and conservation, city-based NGO, Jaldindi Pratishthan, flagged off its 12-day annual voyage from Alandi on Thursday. Beginning from the upper-basin of the Bhima river, the 150 pilgrims will pass through 148 villages on the way to the Pandharpur. Analyses of water samples of 35 rivers including Tapi, Godavari, Krishna, Panchganga, Mithi, Koyna, Ghod and so on will be made by Shrishti Eco-Research Institute.

"Wari (trip) and dindi, (troupe) have a strong significance in Maharashtrian culture. We aim at the confluence of the age-old traditions with the current-day lifestyles to make water preservation an important and recurrent activity to ensure protection of river eco-systems and mankind," said Dr Vishwas Yevale, a gynaecologist from the city who initiated this expedition in 2000.

Giving an insight into the present situation, Dr Sushma Yevale said, "The industrial waste that is discharged at the upper end is consumed by the villagers living downstream. This not only raises the concern of water contamination but also puts forth the health issues of these users who survive by the river water." Considering it as a social responsibility Babanrao Kachi, a 66-year-old warkari who voyages every year, said "With the rising levels of pollution, it's our responsibility to spread awareness amongst the masses consuming this water. The children, who are flag bearers of the society tomorrow, are not aware of the consequences of water pollution." "Although Wari is a religious activity, the message behind Jaldindi is not restricted to any particular community," said Yevale.

Advocating the adage 'Cleanliness is next to Godliness', speakers from various religious communities came to push the word forward. Gulam Gaus Rizvi, Maulana, Yeravda Hajrat Shadawal Baba Dargah said, "Islam gives a lot of importance to water and its usage. Both Quaran Sharif and Hadis have mentioned about safeguarding and preserving water resources." While Pandit Devi Prasad Tiwari, priest of Vajreshri Mata Mandir at Vishrantwadi and Jasveer Singh, Granthi at Tingrenagar Gurudwara, who are members of the dindi every year said, "Such activities are not restricted to a particular religion. It is a social cause and everyone should participate."

Heading: 70 films to be screened at sixth Asian film fest - Indian Express
Content:
City doctors on Friday observed a strike by shuting clinics and dispensaries. They also took out a rally to the Collectorate protesting increasing attacks against members of their fraternity.

According to president of the city unit of the Indian Medical Association (IMA) Dr Avinash Bhondwe, clinics, consulting rooms and dispensaries remained closed and out patient department of major hospitals were shut. However, provisions were made for emergency cases, Bhondwe said.Doctors of IMA, General Practitioners Association and other peripheral doctors' association supporting the strike held a meeting at the B J Medical College. Maharashtra unit President of IMA Dr Devendra Shirole and President of the GPA city unit Dr Prasad Ambikar also spoke.

Doctors submitted a memorandum of their demands to the District Collector. Over 1,000 doctors participated.

Doctor's cell of the National Congress Party, BJP and Congress also supported the token stir. A street play was organised by Dr Vivek Billampelly that highlighted the mob violence against doctors.

In their memorandum, the doctors have pointed out that there were several incidence of assault on doctors, destroying hospital property, equipment, humiliating the family members and hospital staff, at Malad in Mumbai, Amrawati, Beed, Warora in Chandrapur distrcit, Chembur and others.

On October 8, the Cabinet had proposed the amendment of IPC 427 by introducing IPC 427(A) and increasing the years of imprisonment for damage to the special properties which includes hospitals, but it is pertaining to the damage to the property only. Our long standing demand, to bring ordinance for assault on doctors and employees working in medical establishments on the lines of Andhra Pradesh and other states, will not be met with by this amendment and damage to individual and his reputation is irrevocable and that needs to be addressed by bringing out the ordinance and making the offence cognizable and non bailable, said Shirole.

Heading: President launches loans for women SHGs - Indian Express
Content:
Seventy films from 16 countries will be the highlight of the seven-day Sixth Asian film festival beginning on October 16. This is the first time that the festival will be held in Pune as well as Pimpri Chinchwad.

Organised by Ashay films in collaboration with Indira School of communication, the festival will be inaugurated by Tarita Mehendale, chairperson, Indira Group of Institutes at City Pride, Kothrud at 6.30 pm. The inaugural film for the festival is King Siri, a Sri lankan film that narrates the story of a poor boy's intellectual celebration. Virendra Chitrav, director, Asian film festival said, "The festival over seven days will include a number of films under the categories- Spectrum Asia, Indian vista, My Marathi, Off beat In honour, Tribute, Best of Asia, Retrospective and Filmmaker in focus. The last category will include Japanese director Keusuko Shinota's films. Added attractions of the event are interactions with a number of national as well as international film personalities under the category- Open forum." An important feature of the festival will be Zenith Asia Award that has been instituted for the past three years. The recipient of the award this year is noted film actor Naseeruddin Shah. The award will be given by Dr Mohan Agashe, convener of the festival, after the inaugural film. Also screened as an honour to Naseeruddin Shah would be films like Nishant, Akrosh and A Wednesday. The festival will conclude with a screening of the film Mahak by director Kranti Kanade.

Heading: Corporator denies SIMI links, says will campaign against terror - Indian Express
Content:
Giving the much-needed impetus to the self-help groups (SHGs), President Pratibha Patil on Friday launched the loans at four per cent interest for nearly 142,218 SHGs women groups in the state. The President, who made the formal announcement of the scheme at a function here, called for all SHGs to be covered under this scheme. She said that presently, only 45 per cent of SHGs (women) are covered by the banks in the state and there was a need of the remaining 55 per cent to come into this bracket. "With only four per cent interest, these groups will be able to make use of this scheme," she said. She said the government should introduce facilities that can help the SHG women sell their products in malls and shopping complexes. With the SHG movement bringing the necessary economic independence among women, the President said the movement had created waves in Bangladesh with Grameen Bank led by Dr Mohammed Yunus and Ila Bhat in Gujarat. She said there is widespread reach in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu and now Maharashtra too has taken the lead by launching this scheme. She said the movement resulted in the much-needed social change for poor rural women by contributing to their family income, which earlier solely depended on the farming sector. She recalled her days with the Women's Economic Development Corporation (WEDC) 33 years ago and said that the SHG movement had a strong role to play in women empowerment. "This issue is very close to my heart," she said.

By making women independent, it also helped in the overall growth of the Indian economy, the President said and went on to cite the changes brought about by this movement in the naxalite regions.

Earlier, Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh said the government was keen to include all women SHGs in the state and will come out with some guidelines for marketing their products in malls. The insurance factor too will be considered, he said. Governor S C Jamir, Deputy Chief Minister R R Patil, Women and Child welfare and Marketing Minister Harshvardhan Patil and Guardian Minister Ajit Pawar spoke on the occasion. The President also gave away loans to two SHGs from Pune and one each from Solapur, Satara and Nashik.

Heading: MIMH’s new rehab centre for mental patients - Indian Express
Content:
"SACCHA Musalman kabhi blast nahin kar sakta... (A true Muslim will never cause explosions)," said Javed Shaikh, an NCP corporator with the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC). Thirty-five-year-old Shaikh finds himself suddenly pitch-forked in public glare after rumours began flying thick and fast that he had been picked up the Mumbai Anti-Terrorist Squad late on Thursday for alleged links with Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI).

While some news channels reported that Shaikh has been arrested, a section of the media said a Muslim corporator of PCMC had been picked up. The police, however, have denied the same. The corporator, meanwhile, developed "severe chest pain" and got himself admitted to Diwan Hospital in Nigdi. "I become nervous after repeatedly receiving phone calls from friends, relatives and the media across the State, enquiring about the factual position... I kept denying, but the canards were so thick that people believed that I have links with SIMI," he told The Indian Express on Friday.

Shaikh said that if anybody proves that he has links with SIMI, he will commit suicide. "I will hang myself in public if anybody proves that I am related to SIMI." Those behind blasts are not true Muslims, he said. "Such dastardly acts have no pardon...God will never forgive such people," said Shaikh, who holds the unique record of being elected unopposed to the PCMC from Akurdi ward in the 2007 civic elections.

"Islam says that if your neighbour is hungry, whoever he might be, a Muslim has to take care of him by providing food. Islam is all about love, peace and brotherhood. But a small section of its followers are bringing a bad name to the religion by killing innocent people," he said. "Islam says if anybody is trying to harm him, request him thrice not to do so. If he doesn't listen, leave it to Allah."

Denying that the police interrogated him, Shaikh said that in the last couple of weeks, he was away in Delhi where he and other women activists were honoured by President Pratibha Patil for the work done by the self-help groups supported by him.

Shaikh said he would seek police and the district administration's permission to carry out a campaign against terrorist in Pune. "I want to help out the police in exposing those planning terror activities," he said. According to Shaikh, he was targetted because he got a wine shop located close to a temple closed down, exposed a fake currency racket worth Rs seven lakh and took cudgels against the police and the civic administration. "Last year, I attended aartis of 60 mandals. I had planned a big Navratri programme this year. But owing to the fear of blasts, I cancelled it," he said.

Heading: Grade separators: 1 giving trouble, PCMC to open 2 more - Indian Express
Content:
On World Mental Health Day on Friday, the Maharashtra Institute of Mental Health (MIMH) laid the foundation stone for a day care centre in Yerawada for the rehabilitation of mentally ill patients.

Director of MIMH Dr Alka Pawar said that its earlier centre at Sassoon General Hospital premises was a cramped one. Though the 12-acre plot was in the possession of MIMH since 1994, it was only this year that the institute has been promised a generous grant of more than a crore. Acting dean of SGH Dr Nirmala Borade participated in the event. She checked several posters that were displayed at the exhibition held at Sassoon hospital.

Heading: Two inaugurations and a dispute - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation is struggling to keep the Pimpri grade separator up and running, it is all set to inaugurate two more grade separators — one at Chinchwad and another at Akurdi on the Pune-Mumbai highway within its jurisdiction. The inauguration will take place in the presence of NCP chief Sharad Pawar and District Guardian Minister Ajit Pawar around 3 pm on Saturday.

At 730 metre in length, the Chinchwad grade separator is the second longest of the three. It is nine metre wide and includes in its range two chowks — Mahavir and Shivaji. The Akurdi grade separator is 560 metre in length and nine metre in width. The work on both the grade separators started in March 2006, three months after Pimpri grade separator was thrown open to the public. The Pimpri grade separator which is the longest at 795 metres was constructed at a cost of Rs 18 crore, but has failed to remain motorable.

The construction of both Chinchwad and Akurdi grade separators have generated a lot of heat, especially after their costs jumped astronomically. The Akurdi one was initially set to cost Rs 14 crore, but later the civic adminstration said it would cost Rs 29 crore. Similarly, the Chinchwad grade separator has been constructed at cost of Rs 39 crore. Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh had stalled the construction of the Chinchwad grade separator after Congress leader Srirang Barne raised certain objections. A few months later, Deshmukh lifted the stay after hearing out the civic adminstration.

With the construction of the two grade separators and the one already in place at Pimpri, the time taken to reach Nigdi from Bopodi on the Pune-Mumbai highway will come down drastically. Then municipal commissioner Dilip Band, during whose tenure the Pimpri grade separator was completed and two other grade separator work started, had maintained that it would take eight minutes to travel from Bopodi to Nigdi once grade separator work is completed. After Bopodi, there will be only one major signal — that is at Nashik Phata chowk. Here too, the PCMC has planned an overbridge which will fly over road, rail and river and is being described as the unique one. Despite its inauguration over four years ago, the bridge work is yet to get cracking.

The entire Pune-Mumbai highway from Nigdi to Phugewadi has been concretised. Now, the only major irritant on the Pune-Mumbai highway is that of the nearly two kilometre stretch in Dapodi area where the army wall stands tall. City engineer Eknath Ugile said the Army compound wall will be pushed inside 19 metres and a new compound wall will be constructed by the PCMC. "The compound wall design, height and other related things are being discussed with Army officials. Once that is approved, we will start phase-wise removal of the wall."

Meanwhile, Municipal Commissioner Asheesh Sharma promised that the two new grade separators will live up to the standards set by the civic administration. "Both of them are looking good. I can assure about their quality. I have been keeping a watch on the work every alternate day," he said. "Instead of inter-locking grids, we have gone for tarring of the road. Despite heavy rain, the tarred surface has remained in order," said PCMC executive engineer D M Shirke. Inter-locking grids, said Shirke, had created problems on the Pimpri grade separator which had remained closed several times since its inauguration two years and half years ago.

Heading: Gift of the Games: some roads & a stadium - Indian Express
Content:
Pawar takes credit for CYG work

Hours to go for the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) to begin, there is no end in sight to the tug-of-war between the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) and the Congress to take credit for the development works.

On Friday, District Guardian Minister Ajit Pawar, while praising NCP, took a dig at city MP Suresh Kalmadi for hogging the limelight.

"Despite being rejected by the citizens in the last municipal elections in Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad, some people (Kalmadi) have not yet matured. People pulled them (Congress) out of power, but I don't understand what more jolts they need to grow up," Pawar said, adding, "Citizens of Pune are clever enough to choose the right candidate in the election."

Pawar was speaking at the inauguration of a subway near Balewadi. Mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale and Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi were also present.

Pawar, without mentioning Kalmadi, said, "The Balewadi stadium was built through the timely efforts of NCP chief Sharad Pawar. When the statue of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was unveiled last week at the stadium, not even Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh, let alone Sharad Pawar, was invited. Politics is being dragged into everything. This might be because he (Kalmadi) is not attached to the people of Maharashtra. There is no need to show who loves the Marathi people more."

"Till the NCP came to power in the PMC, roads were in dire straits. That created a bad impression about Pune and deterred industries from others states from investing money in the city. The rain continued to play havoc in the last two years as well, yet we did not compromise on the quality of works. Overcoming all odds, we laid down good roads. This is mainly because we took decisions, keeping in mind the requirements of the coming 25-30 years. But we are not looking at publicity."

"However, they (Congressmen) are splashing their pictures all over and projecting themselves as the change-makers. In reality, this is being achieved through the efforts of the PMC, PCMC and the state as well as Central governments," he said.

Reacting to statements made by Pawar, Kalmadi came out with a press note in the evening urging the citizens to remove posters showing his name and photographs.

"Remove all posters containing my name and photos. It is not only me who is responsible in making the Commonwealth Youth Games successful. It is due to the collective efforts of all of you (citizens), which is making this event a success," Kalmadi said in the press note. He has appealed to citizens to give more publicity to the mascot of CYG, Jigrr.

City gets its first CNG station

The Maharashtra Natural Gas Limited (MNGL) on Friday started the first compressed natural gas (CNG) station in the city. MP Suresh Kalmadi launched it at Bharat Petroleum Company Limited (BPCL) outlet, Vardhaman petrol pump, in Warje area. The station will cater to the CNG buses of the Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML) that will run during and after the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG).

While the CNG will come in caskets from Mumbai for the 20-odd buses supplied by Ashok Leyland, the city is also getting ready for its first piped natural gas (PNG) connection next week.

During the CNG station launch, R K Goel, chairman of MNGL, announced that the residents of Pimpri-Chinchwad area will get PNG within a week. "Once the ongoing pipeline tests are done, the mother station at Chikhli will start functioning. The MNGL will start PNG supply to 1,000 households in the city and Pimpri-Chinchwad by March 2009," Goel said.

Dr U D Choubey, Chairman and Managing Director, Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL), announced the commissioning of the 250-km pipeline for supplying natural gas to the city. "The 30-inch diameter pipeline has been laid from a tap-off point at Kargaon on the Dahej-Panvel-Dabhol pipeline of GAIL to Pune," he said. Goel said MNGL had signed MoUs with 10 industrial units in and around Pune for the supply of CNG. He refused to give details.

Kalmadi, who also flagged off the first CNG bus, said, "Just as the first CNG station has coincided with the CYG being promoted as green Games, the first piped gas connection could be given to the hostel of Shiv Chhatrapati Krida Nagari (Balewadi)."

Announcing further ventures, Goel said MNGL plans to set up two more daughter booster stations by next week and three more by mid-November. "There will be at least 14 CNG stations by the end of March 2009," he said.

The investment envisaged for the city gas distribution project in Pune in the first phase is Rs 220 crore by December 2009.

"In the first phase, around 40,000 vehicles including buses and autos will be converted to CNG. The stations are expected to go up to 29 by then," said Choubey. The total investment in Pune is to the tune of Rs 460 crore over 10 years, he added. The Centre has allocated 0.4 million standard cubic metre per day (MMSCMD) of natural gas for Pune, while the total potential of natural gas for the city gas distribution network for Pune is estimated at 2.5 MMSCMD. Santosh Kumar, director (Projects), GAIL, Subrao Patil, chairman and managing director, PMPML, Shama Sundara, managing director, MNGL and others were present for the function. MNGL is a joint venture company promoted by GAIL and BPCL to implement gas distribution projects.

Heading: Rohinitai, the kathak legend, passes away - Indian Express
Content:
The Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) are here. Once they end, what will the city remember them by?

For MP Suresh Kalmadi, the legacy of the Games will be the spruced-up Balewadi Stadium complex. "The sports city will become a tourist venue," he said. The Garden of Youth on the complex would be another memento, he said.

Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi sees it from another perspective: "The infrastructural improvements that will remain with the city include the completion of the railway underpass, the VIP Airport Road and the Baner, Sinhagad, Ganeshkhind and Nehru roads. Development of many of these roads had been held up because of land acquisition disputes and court stays. The CYG enabled us to reach a consensus and acquire all," he said.

He cited the actual cost of CYG work at Rs 434 crore instead of Rs 2,500 crore - which included projects not specific to the CYG. "The Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) contributed 50 per cent of this amount," he said.

He mentions many projects undertaken by the PMC: two subways, beautification of the Pashan and Katraj lakes, a bio-diversity park at Baner, rehabilitation of four slums, better streetlights, street signs and furniture, 53 km of footpaths, 200 new civic buses and another 300 buses on hire, 200 km of storm water drains and reinstating of electrical wires under pavement blocks.

"All of these are fundamental changes. Of course many superficial things have also been done but they are also necessary to give the city a good look," he said.

The projects that couldn't be completed include the Alandi link road and a parking lot at Baner Road, he conceded.

Activist Vijay Kumbhar, president of the Surajya Sangharsh Samiti, feels the only legacy that will remain is that of the sports city. And it will not benefit the common man much. "The last-minute haste at which the infrastructure work was done casts doubt over its quality. It will not last. The city expected and deserved much more from the CYG," he said.

Heading: ‘Cuticon - 08’ to kickstart today - Indian Express
Content:
Software engineer Mohammed Mansoor Asgar Peerbhoy (31) had been identified for indoctrination as far back as 2004.A group people scouting for young Muslim men spotted Peerbhoy in an Arabic class. The group then kept tabs on Peerbhoy, alleged Indian Mujahideen suspect Asif Bashir Shaikh told the Mumbai Police Crime Branch dring investigation.

Describing Asif as a "bad apple" in the class, Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria said: "The classes or the institutes that teach Arabic have nothing to do with such groups. People like Asif scout for such recruits at these places, without the knowledge of the institutes."

The group kept a watch on Peerbhoy. In 2006 he was again trailed from the local mosque in Pune. "Once it had fully indoctrinated him, the group sent him for the ethical hacking course. He was later sent to Bhatkal for other training," said Maria.

Maria also said that "quite a few" men who had been indoctrinated went on to leave the group as they felt that it was the wrong thing to do. "There are many like them who have given us leads and were helpful in the investigation," he said.

Peerbhoy has allegedly told the investigators that the terror e-mails he sent were on Riyaz Bhatkal's brief.

Peerbhoy, Mubin alias Salman Kadar Sheikh (24) had conducted a recce for non-secure WiFi connections on five separate occasions. "On July 26, they left Pune at 10 am and reached Sanpada. They spent their time having lunch and strolling in the garden nearby," adds Maria.

On the third occasion, they were supposed to send the mail at 6.20 pm but it got delayed till 6.26. "It was the day before the immersion and the crowd around Chembur was so large that they struggled to park their car," adds Maria.

Interrogation has also established the manner in which the mails were sent. "Peerbhoy, Salman and Arif Badruddin Shaikh (38) would be driven down by Mohammed Akbar Ismail Chaudhary in a blue Esteem. Chaudhary and Arif would stand outside, masking the number plates from both sides, while Peerbhoy and Mubin would send the e-mail," said Maria.

Investigations have also shown that the Gujarat blasts had been initially planned for September 19. "The blasts were later shifted to September 26," said Maria, adding that the cars placed in Ahmedabad had been fitted with four additional LPG cylinders for maximum impact. Investigators are now probing how these cooking gas cylinders were procured.

Heading: Schools celebrate Dussehra - Indian Express
Content:
Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH) is holding the 34th annual conference of "Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists & Leprologists" (IADVL) (Punjab, Chandigarh and Himachal chapter) "CUTICON 2008" on October 11. The conference is being organised by the hospital's Department of Skin and VD , under the guidance of Dr Alka Dogra, professor and head of the department.

Prem Gupta, secretary, DMCH Managing Society, would be the chief guest. Eminent speakers of dermatology from all over India will address the conference. The founder of pulse therapy, Dr. J.S. Pasricha, former head of Department of Skin, AIIMS, New Delhi will speak on pulse therapy.

Dr Satish Sawant, Head of Dermatology, Department at Nanavati Hospital, Mumbai will address about dermato surgery. While Dr Anil Ganjoo will share his views about laser. Dr Hema Jeranjani, Head of Department, LTM Medical College, Mumbai, would talk on rotational therapy in Psoriasis. Dr Atul Kochhar would discuss the latest on male pattern baldness.

The theme of conference is "Evolving concepts in general and aesthetic dermatology". Dr Daljit Singh, Principal of DMC&H, said that this conference would go a long way in devising new strategies for improvement of patient care.

Heading: Multi-disciplinary approach for treating mental illnesses stressed - Indian Express
Content:
Bharatiya Vidya Mandir, Kitchlu Nagar, celebrated Dussehra festival with enthusiasm.

The tiny-tots of class I and class III came dressed up as various characters of Ramayana. While the students of class III to V participated in Choaupayee Gyan competition, Class VI-IX students took part in dialogue recitation contest related to Ramayana.

A drawing competition was also arranged by the Pidilite Industries in which students from class I to X participated.. Santosh Mehra, the school principal, congratulated the staff members, teachers and students on the occasion of Dussehra.

BCM Senior Secondary School, Chandigarh Road, organised the picnic for the students of class 1 and UKG as part of Dussehra celebrations on Friday. The students were taken to PUDA park. They participated in games and activities based on their talents. The teachers of respective classes told the students about the importance of this festival. The winners of games and activities were honoured with prizes by D.P. Guleria, the school principal.

However for the senior students, the school organised Diwali craft competition in which about 200 students from Class VI to XII participated. In this, events like candle decoration, gift wrapping, covering pooja thali, making shagun envelopes, greeting cards etc were organised. D.P. Guleria, the school principal, appreciated the innovative ideas of the participants and congratulated the winners.

Heading: Mega event ‘Face of Punjab’ slated for Dec - Indian Express
Content:
College of Nursing, Christian Medical College & Hospital (CMCH), organised World Mental Health Day on the theme "Making mental health a global priority."

Prof Triza Jiwan, Principal, College of Nursing, felicitated the chief guest Dr Kim Mammen, Deputy Director, CMC & Hospital, who emphasized on the importance of diagnosing the mental illnesses and their treatment. He mentioned that there should be multi-disciplinary approach for diagnosis and treatment of mental illnesses. He congratulated College of Nursing, CMCH for stepping forward to organise this event.

Charlotte Ranadive, lecturer, College of Nursing, CMCH, introduced theme to the general public. She emphasized on the need of creating awareness among public regarding the various mental illnesses such as schizophrenia, mania, depression, anxiety, and clearing misconceptions regarding mental illnesses.

The inauguration of the exhibition was done by the chief guest. The exhibition was put up by the M.Sc (N)-1st year students regarding the theme. B.Sc (N) 3rd tear students also enacted a role play on awareness regarding mental illnesses and cleared many misconceptions.

Heading: Theft attempt at Oriental Bank of Commerce - Indian Express
Content:
Global Sale Process is going to hold a national-level mega event "Face of Punjab - 08' in Ludhiana in December. Giving details, Pankaj Arora, CFO, and Chander Shekhar Arora, CEO, said, "The competition is open to the people of Punjab in which children are also participating. The event has been divided into three parts. In the category of 2-15 years, children can participate while in 16-25 years category men and women can take part. To take part in it, the forms are available up to October 23 and in each category, 10 top selectors will be made in auditions and process of voting will be held on December 7."
