The winner of each category will be given the contract of music album for one year also. The selected candidates will also have the privilege to meet the Bollywood stars of international fame.

Darshan Arora, chairman of Ludhiana Citizens Council, performed curtain raiser ceremony. Arora said that helpline number of the event was 97811-22705.

Heading: Wildlife awareness lecture held - Indian Express
Content:
Some unidentified thieves broke into the Tagore Nagar branch of the Oriental Bank of Commerce (OBC) by cutting open the grills of a window. Though the thieves managed to enter the bank, they did not succeed in stealing anything from there. It may be mentioned that this is the same bank from where last year, two youths had looted Rs 7 lakh on pistol point.

Ironically, this bank is situated hardly at a distance of 100 meters from the Police Lines area. According to sources, the unsuccessful theft attempt came to light this morning when a sweeper came to the bank for cleaning purposes. He found the grills of a window cut open. At this, he immediately informed the matter to the bank officials.

Sources said that when the bank officials came and opened the branch, they found the grills of the window had been cut open. Then inside the branch, the thieves had tried to cut open the lock of the strong room and of the safe. But they could not succeed in doing either. The matter was reported to the police, which have started investigating the matter.

It may be recalled that last year on September 6, two youths had looted a sum of Rs 7 lakh from the bank employees on gun point in a broad day-light before fleeing from the spot.

Heading: Lack of education facilities made Tata sidestep Punjab: Ashwini - Indian Express
Content:
Cape-India today organised wildlife awareness lecture and exhibition at Government High School, Salem Tabri. The programme was hosted by Dr Babita Jain, a state awardee. Various posters and banners related to wildlife were displayed on the occasion.

The lectures on lions, tigers, deer, global warming and punishment for wildlife crimes were listened to with great interest by the students as well as the teachers. The key-note speaker, Dr Sandeep K. Jain, Chief Coordinator, CAPE-India and Hony Wildlife Warden, said that Asiatic lions had become extinct from whole of Asia except India and that too in Gir forests (Gujarat).

It was interesting to note that children were aware of the punishment for hunting of wild animals, thanks to the much publicised Salman Khan case. But most of the participants were not aware of punishment which entailed teasing the wild animals in zoos, which is Imprisonment for six months or fine of Rs 2,000 or both. Sunurinder Kaur, Principal, Ramesh Kumar, Sukhdev Singh of Ecoclub, Dr Babita Jain also addressed the students and stressed the need to conserve nature and wildlife.

Students were also told about peacocks, deers and the banned animals in circuses/street shows etc and asked to protect the wildlife and its habitat. Surinder Kaur, principal, Ranjit Singh, Varinderpal Singh, Rakesh Jain and Parma Nand Shukla, both animal welfare officers, M.R. Singhal, advisor, CAPE-India, and Anju Jain were present on the occasion.

Heading: This devotional singer has a passion for spreading the word of God - Indian Express
Content:
Tata wanted to come to Punjab to set up Nano plant and they had even asked for 1,000-acre land but with a rider that it should be near Mohali. Because the staff of Tatas were particular about "quality education" for their children, which according to them, they could not get in any other part of Punjab, said Ashwini Kumar, Union Minister of State for Industry.

According to Kumar, who visited Trident industries here on Friday, the state was not able to give 1,000 acres near Mohali. Ths state government offered many other options but Tatas did not agree for any other site and hence project did not materialise.

However with this, he also gave a message to the state government to think seriously on the education front, in which that state was lacking badly. "Education standards are not up to the mark in Punjab and this is the reason for wide-spread unemployment in the state as well," said Kumar.

However talking on the same issue, Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, who was in the city today in connection with Sangat Darshan programme, stated that former CM Capt Amarinder Singh did not do much to materialise the deal although the SAD-BJP government in the state did their best after Tatas decided to pack up from Singur.

Talking to ENS, Kumar however said that fright corridor project costing Rs 28,000 crores from Ludhiana to Sonmarg (in Calcutta) will reduce the distance of 72 hours to just 24 hours and this project will be a boon for Punjab in reducing trasaction cost.

Ashwini Kumar however agreed that tax holiday to neighbouring states had hit Punjab hard. But again, he grilled state government saying that they did not show much initiative on this front. Giving example, he said, "Trident expanded its units in M.P, where the units are flourishing well. Which is good for Trident but painful for Punjab to bear that loss."

"The packages will be over by 2009 and hence afterwards Punjab will get a level-playing field," Ashwini Kumar tried to lift the gloom. A logistic hub will be created in Ludhiana, Amritsar, Patiala, Jalandhar and Bhatinda to reduce trasactoon costs, he added.

However again for small industry of Punjab, Kumar added that state industry was not yet upgrading itself which it must to keep in step with growth shown by other states.

Ashwini Kumar listed a good number of projects like education institutes, including IIM in Mohali, which according to him, had been gifted by UPA government to Punjab. He also stated that at the moment, the Central government was giving priority to textile, leather, electronics, hardware and skill upgradation industry of Punjab.

Heading: Mumbai trader robbed of diamonds worth Rs 2 crore - Indian Express
Content:
Vinod Aggarwal, a businessman and bhajan singer, has 103 CDs to his credit

Can capitalism and spiritualism go hand in hand?

For Vinod Aggarwal, a Bhawandi (near Mumbai)-based businessman, the answer is an empathetic yes.

Aggarwal has visited cities across India as a bhajan singer and was in Ludhiana to perform at the Hari Naam Sankirtan on Friday.

He said he never underwent professional training for music but the way he changes from one raga to another gives him away.

His unique style of weaving the laya and taal with couplets simply enthrals the audience.

Says Aggarwal: "In 1978, I started singing at the Kalbadevi Gaddi every Sunday. Now, when I am out of station owing to a performance, my younger brother sings there."

When he sings, tears start rolling down his cheeks spontaneously.

"I don't know how it happens. I cannot explain what I feel while singing but later I find my face drenched with tears," says Aggarwal.

"My Guruji (Bathinda-based Swami Mukund Hari) has asked me to spread the word of God. Since then, I have been following the path shown by him."

This 53-year-old devotional singer started at the age of eight and has 103 CDs to his credit now including Shyam Tum Bhool Gaye, Pritam Kya Apraadh Hamara, Mohan Teri Gali Mein, Shyam Ghan Kab Barsoge, O Rangeele Rasia and Shyam Main to Khoi Khoi.

Many of his live and recorded programmes have also been telecast on TV channels like Aastha and Sanskar.

Aggarwal adds: "I love to teach bhajans to the younger generation. Many a time, I personally go with my students when their CDs are recorded."

Heading: CM advocates privatisation but mum over unbundling of PSEB - Indian Express
Content:
Four unidentified youths and a taxi driver injured a businessman and escaped with diamonds worth Rs 2 crore near Phillaur late on Thursday evening.

The trader, Bhupesh Shah, had come to Ludhiana from Mumbai on Thursday.

In his complaint, Shah stated that he hired a taxi from the Aarti Taxi stand, near Aarti Cinema, around 6 pm on Thursday to go to Amritsar.

When the taxi reached Bakhapur village near Phillaur, the driver stopped the vehicle on the pretext of relieving himself.

Shah said four youths were already standing at the spot and he asked the driver to move on but the driver did not pay attention.

Seconds after the driver left, the youths attacked the businessman with a sharp-edged weapon. Shah was stabbed in the back and thighs.

The assailants then threw red chilli powder in Shah's eyes and dragged him out of the car.

The four boarded the taxi and the driver rejoined them. Then all the five fled the spot.

Phillaur police sources said sketches of the four youths have been prepared and efforts are on to trace them.

Ludhiana police are also helping Phillaur police in the investigations.

Heading: CM’s outburst: ‘most unorganised Sangat Darshan’ - Indian Express
Content:
"Privatisation improves work efficiency and makes for better services," said Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, while advocating privatisation of Sahnewal Airport. He was speaking at a sangat darshan programme in the city on Friday.

He quickly changed his stand, however, when asked about the delay in unbundling of the Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB).

He said: "We are still studying the project reports to decide whether unbundling is required or not. In many states, privatisation of the electricity board has failed miserably."

Badal also announced a comprehensive plan, to the tune of Rs 5,500 crore, for projects involving the upgrade of sewerage, roads, water supply and streetlights of all towns in the state. "And all the projects will start before the Lok Sabha elections," he added.

For Ludhiana in particular, Badal came up with a Rs 240-crore package to revamp the sewerage system and a 220 KV grid station, to be set up by the end of 2008 at a cost of Rs 20 crore. Two new land registration offices will also be opened.

Later, Badal said all the work estimates would be thoroughly checked by a team of experts headed by Technical Advisor to the Punjab Government Lt Gen (Retd) B S Dhaliwal.

"The team will include chief engineers (quality control) from the Public Works Department (Building and Roads) and Mandi Board so that the projects are implemented efficiently within the stipulated time," said the CM.

Badal was accompanied by Tourism and Cultural Affairs Minister Hira Singh Gabria, MP Sharanjit Singh Dhillon, Chief Parliamentary Secretary Harish Rai Dhanda, Mayor Hakam Singh, MLA Darshan Singh Shivalik, DC Sumear Singh Gurjar, DIG Ludhiana Range Ishwar Singh and SSP Ludhiana R K Jaiswal and members of SAD and BJP.

Content:
Carmel Convent School, Sector 9 will face St Stephen's School, Sector 45 in the final of the Chandigarh Sub-Junior Girls Football Championship for Dr. Kamesh Bhargava Memorial Trophy being conducted by the Chandigarh Football Association at the Sector 17 Football Stadium here on Saturdat at 9.30 a.m. 0In the semi-final matches played on Friday, St Stephen's School snuffed out the challenge of Mount Carmel Convent, Sector 47 by 3-0 and Carmel Convent overcame a  spirited challenge from Sacred Heart of Sector 26 with an aggregate margin of 5-3 on penalties after the teams were locked one-all in the regulation period. Carmel Convent converted their penalties through Meghna, Namrata Kochhar Geising, Sarika Kumar and Ekta Kochhar Geising. Devika Pathak muffed her spot kick. For Sacred Heart, Parinaa and Arshjot successfully converted their penalties. Manpreet and Ibaddat failed with their efforts.

Heading: Farmers from neighbouring villages also stake their claim - Indian Express
Content:
PIL against commercial use of Surat land pending before HC

Court had stayed govt bid to develop the agricultural land for tourism, entertainment infrastructure

The government's decision to transfer 1,100-acres of land to the Tatas for the Nano car project from an area, the Anand Agriculture University (AAU) was supposed to use for agricultural research, has not hit any roadblock so far. But an earlier edition of such a move by the government is lying foundered on legal shoals.

The Gujarat government had acquired 65,000 sq metres of land from the Cotton Research Centre run by the Navsari Agricultural University (NAU), located at one of Surat's prime locations on Ghod Dod Road, barely two years ago.

The Gujarat High Court accepted a PIL that maintained that no land meant for agricultural research could be given away for a commercial project, and stayed the government's move. It still remains stayed, and the next hearing in the case is scheduled for October 21.

The court came into the picture after the Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC) released an advertisement inviting expression of interest to develop the said piece of land for tourism and entertainment infrastructure. Incidentally, the Cotton Research Station, established by the East India Company in 1896, had carried out research on indigenous varieties of cotton seed on that land, before it was handed over to the Gujarat Agricultural University, and thereafter to NAU.

After the PIL was moved, the Chhatrala Hotel Group, which staked its claim for 'developing' that property, joined the issue as a respondent, along with the Gujarat government, GIDC and NAU. The petitioner, a local farmer, told Newsline on conditions of anonymity that he was now under tremendous pressure to back off.

"There has been much pressure on me ever since I filed that petition, in public interest. All we are saying is that when there is so much land lying with the government, why does it want to set up industries that have nothing to do with farming in land meant for agriculture research?" he said.

Meanwhile, the Anand Agricultural University (AAU) authorities refused to comment on the 2,200 acres of land it transferred to the Gujarat government, of which 1,100 acres were 'transferred' to the Tatas on Thursday.

The transfer was formally effected by the revenue officials, before the industrial group made any initial payment, as "pricing modalities are still being worked out," as an official said.

Ahmedabad District Collector Harit Shukla said that no financial transaction has yet taken place in the deal, though the land has been officially acquired by the Tatas in Sanand.

The payment modalities, which are in the last stages of finalisation, are being worked out as the rates are yet to be fixed by the State Valuation Committee.

This is being kept strictly under wraps, and the state government has refused to divulge the MoU with the group signed as a State Support Agreement as well.

AAU Vice-Chancellor M Varshneya refused to say anything about the land transfer or land usage, while University sources disclosed that the land in question was used for jatropha field trials. In any case, the AAU has sought alternate land from the state government.

Heading: Godman lands in jail for his sexcapades - Indian Express
Content:
Say Britons had taken the land from their ancestors on a 100-year lease

As the narrow road from Chharodi bus stand to the proposed site for the Nano plant suddenly bursts into unfamiliar commotion, rumblings of resistance seem to be gaining momentum among a section of farmers in the nearby villages regarding land rights and compensation issues.

Farmers from Khoda, Bhod, Amareli and Modasar are staking claim to the 1,100-acre land that has been given to the Tatas for setting up the Nano plant. They are saying the land belonged to their forefathers.

"The land was given to the British government by our forefathers on a 100-year- lease during the great famine. In 2002, when we asked for the land, we were told that the government had acquired the land in 1911," said Meghrajsinh Chauhan from Bhod village.

He said: "We had no clue about the entire episode. We have been running from pillar to post to get our rights, but no one has ever bothered to give us a hearing." But he is quick to add that the farmers have nothing against the Tatas coming here. "But we are the real owners of the land and we have got nothing in the deal. We should get our share of compensation. We'll fight till the end for our rights. It was on our land that the Anand University campus was built," he said.

He said their struggle for land rights did not start after the Tatas came here. "We have been fighting for the land, and it has gone unheard so far. We are now trying to resolve the issue through the court, if things don't work out soon. We may have to resort to stronger measures like hunger strikes and so on," he added.

Mukeshsinh Vaghela from Khoda village said: "We are talking to the lawyers to move the courts, but we need some more evidence to prove our rights. At present, we are trying to get those papers."

He said the state government is hiding a lot of facts. "While on one hand they say the land was acquired in 1911, they have failed to give us the documents of acquisitions," he added.

On his part, Ahmedabad Collector Harit Shukla said the land was taken by the British in 1899 on a lease and that the farmers were paid a compensation of Rs 2 lakh in 1911. "We have enough documents to prove that the compensations were paid," said Shukla, adding that as the land has already been acquired, the government is not bound to pay any compensation.

Heading: Labour’s pain: Shunned by hospital, tribal woman delivers on roadside - Indian Express
Content:
His wife, an accomplice in crime, also behind bars

A Godman in Dahod, who had named his ashram Kunwarika Bhavan, and had kept three young women as his devotee-sex slaves for over a couple of years, has landed behind the bars.

According to the police, Sabur Baria (45) alias Naklank Bhagwan had lured two of the girls into his two-room brick house at Kalji-Sarwani village, with the promise to personally sire babies for them with his supernatural powers. The police said the godman had also convinced the parents of the two girls, aged 21 and 22, from Fatehpura and Suthvasa villages, to let them stay with him. One of the girls, incidentally, delivered a baby boy a few months ago.

The police said the third girl was barely 15 years old when she was reportedly abducted by the godman and his wife from the nearby Kadwa village and kept with the other two, and raped. Baria's sexcapade, which had the active support of his own wife, ended after the minor's grandfather approached the police. The girl's grandfather traced her and went to the Jhalod police a couple of days ago. The police have now sent all three girls for medical examination.

The godman and his wife, Sevli, have been booked under Sections 366, 366 (a), 376, 493, 497, 295(a) and 34 of the Indian Penal Code pertaining to rape, kidnapping and abduction and hurting religious sentiments.

Heading: US meltdown singes Surat diamond trade - Indian Express
Content:
A tribal woman from Madhya Pradesh had to deliver twins by the roadside in Dahod town after she was denied admission by a private hospital in the city. Her family members alleged that they were shown the door by Aashirwad Hospital following their inability to bear the expenses.

A similar incident was reported in Gondal earlier, wherein a tribal woman from MP, working as a casual labourer, was forced to deliver a child by the roadside after a private hospital refused to admit her on financial grounds.

Eta Parmar gave birth to twins near Darpan Cinema in Dahod town in the early hours of Thursday. Elsewhere, the hospital authorities claimed unawareness about the entire episode. Dr B Patel, Chief Medical Officer, Aashirwad Hospital said: "I am unaware of any such case. I have to get the details from the staff about any such patient."

Eta's family members had brought her to Dahod in the early hours on Wednesday after she complained of acute pain. Her husband Bhusa said they took her to the hospital, but the nursing staff denied her admission in the belief that the family would be unable to bear the expenses for a caesarean surgery. Later, Eta delivered two baby boys on her way to another maternity home in Dahod after the jeep in which she was travelling, broke down.

Heading: Gujarat, the chosen one for WB-aided coastal zone management project - Indian Express
Content:
Export takes a blow; Several factories advance Diwali holidays by nearly 20 days

The global financial crisis and the recession in the US have started showing their effect on Surat's diamond industry. Several factories have declared a 45-day Diwali holiday, even as nearly 20 days are left for the festival.

The diamond polishers of Surat, where nearly 90 per cent of the diamonds in the world are cut and polished, have started leaving for their respective hometowns in Saurashtra and other places in north Gujarat.

The export of diamond studded jewellery and gems, which is worth Rs 82,000 crore, has been the worst affected, as the US has several centres for business of such jewellery.

Surat Diamond Association president C P Wanani said: "The recession in the US has hit the diamond industry hard. We had not seen such a great recession in our life before. Earlier, our industry used to have a 30-day Diwali vacation, which starts from the day of the festival. But this year, several units have been shut after Dussehra, as they do not have sufficient diamonds for cutting and polishing."

Praveen Nanavati, joint secretary of the Gujarat Hira Bourse, and former president of the South Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industry said, the majority of the players in rough diamonds are settled in the US and "this year they too are facing a great crisis." He added: "Even the exporters of studded diamond jewellery are suffering a lot. Both big and small players in the industry are facing losses on different scales. We are waiting for the US to get stable.".

Diamond Trader Association member Babubhai Godhani said they are not getting sufficient demands from the exporters based in Mumbai and Surat. "Many exporters from Mumbai and Surat have shut down their offices in New York and Los Angeles," he said, adding that the sale and purchase of diamonds have also gone down.

Babu Jirwala, president of the Diamond Workers Association, said the condition of diamond workers has become worse in the wake of the recession. "We have learnt that many diamond polishers are planning to settle down in their hometowns and return to farming," he said.

The industry has been facing loses of late, as a result of which diamond traders, factory owners and even the workers have changed their routine business. Many of the diamond merchants have jumped into the textile business, while some have opted for construction business.

As per the statistical data available with the Surat Diamond Association, there are around 4,200 diamond factories functioning in the city, providing livelihood to over six lakh people.

Heading: Early morning bomb mischief sends residents into a tizzy - Indian Express
Content:
Rs 215-cr project aims at protecting marine bio-diversity and maintaining the eco-system

Gujarat has been selected for the World Bank-aided Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM) project, under which, the state government will get financial assistance to protect the marine bio-diversity and maintain the eco-system of the coastal zone, especially in the Gulf of Kutch.

The World Bank has also opted for two more marine states – Orissa and West Bengal – for the Rs 600-crore project. The premier international funding agency has already given an in-principle approval for Gujarat's component of about Rs 215 crore.

The Gujarat Ecology Commission (GEC), a nodal agency appointed by the government to implement the project in Gujarat, has launched efforts for its effective implementation.

The GEC will convene a two-day workshop on "Identification of Training Needs" for the ICZM project on October 17-18 at the Infocity Resort and Club in Gandhinagar. Apart from leading marine scientists and environmentalists from all over the country, senior World Bank representatives attached to the project will attend the workshop.

"We have already submitted a State Project Report (SPR) to the World Bank, following which it gave its in-principle approval for the ICZM programme. A final project report will be submitted to the Bank by this month end. We expect the Bank to give its final nod to the project by next month," said Gujarat's Principal Secretary (Forests and Environment) S K Nanda.

Nanda, who also heads the GEC, told Newsline on Thursday that the project would further boost the government's efforts to protect the marine life and also restore and maintain the marine bio-diversity in the Gulf of Kutch. It will also help involve people's participation in preserving the marine flora and fauna in the state.

GEC's member secretary and Chief Conservator of Forest E Balaguruswami pointed out six components to be implemented under the project by as many agencies which include Marine National Park, GEER Foundation, Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB), Jamnagar Municipal Corporation and Bhaskaracharya Institute for Space Applications and Geoinformatics (BAISAG), besides the Gujarat Ecology Commission.

The main objective of the project is to promote multi-sectoral and multi-disciplinary involvement in services and management of the state's coastal zone. While the Marine National Park will undertake the restoration of mangroves under its areas, the GEC will take up a large-scale mangrove plantation in the non-forest areas.

Gandhinagar-based GEER Foundation will mainly focus on research activities related to the marine bio-diversity, including sea algae, coral, seaweeds and mammals, and fish. The Foundation will set up a central research station at its Gandhinagar headquarters, and also establish field research units in coastal areas of Kutch, Saurashtra and South Gujarat. Researchers at these stations will study the various environmental aspects and their impact on marine diversity.

Balaguruswami said the GPCB will carry out a detailed study on how to check marine pollution in the Gulf of Kutch, while the Gandhinagar-based BAISAG will conduct a survey and mapping of mangrove areas by using the geographical information system (GIS). It will help the government to know about the latest status of mangrove cover in the entire coastal zone.

Under the project, the Jamnagar Municipal Corporation will set up a sewerage treatment plant to release the treated water into the sea off the Jamnagar coast so as to ensure the protection of marine life. The project will have to be implemented in five years.

Heading: BJP slaps Talala nagarpalika members with showcause for defying party whip - Indian Express
Content:
Panic gripped the residents of Haripura area when they were awakened by the sound of a few explosions in the early hours of Friday. However, it turned out to be the mischief of some unidentified persons, who had planted firecrackers on Masjidiya Street.

According to the police, the first firecracker exploded outside the main door of the house of one Mukesh Mevawala around 3.30 am. Mevawala immediately came out on the road with his family members. Within a couple of minutes, three more bombs, one outside another house and two on the roadside, exploded.

Following this, the residents came out on the road and informed the police. A police team, along with the Bomb Disposal Squad and sniffer dogs, rushed to the spot. During a search in nearby areas, they found three live firecrackers at different places tied with incense sticks.

The police also recovered a letter from the spot. The letter, which bore the signature of one Taufik, supposedly a member of the Indian Mujahideen, stated: Yeh to trailer tha (this was a trailer).

Chowk Bazaar police Inspector B L Vavaiya said that though they were investigating the incident, it appeared to be a mischief. "Diwali is around the corner and somebody might have purchased firecrackers to spread panic just for some sheer mischief. The miscreant had tied the firecracker with incense stick so that they could escape from the spot after planting them," Vavaiya said.

He added, "The people of the Masjidiya Street are scared, so we have deployed our police personnel at the site."

Heading: CDs to replace sealed question papers at GTU - Indian Express
Content:
BJP has issued a showcause notice to the nine elected members of Talala Nagarpalika for overruling the party whip and voting in favour of an independent candidate for the president's post of the civic body last week. And, with independent candidate Moosa Bhai Sodha pipping the BJP candidate to the post, it has brought

an end to the party's two-and-half-year rule in the civic body.

With nine of the 16 BJP members voting for Sodha, he has defeated his rival with a margin of seven votes.

When contacted, Junagadh district BJP unit president Thakershi

Javia said: "A show cause notice has been issued to the nine BJP members who had defied the party whip and voted against the party's official candidate."

Javia has also said that strict action would be taken against the six if they fail to furnish a reply by October 11, which could also include suspension.

The new Nagarpalika chief has, however, jumped to the rescue of the nine councillors. "These nine have put their faith in me. We will work together to improve the civic amenities in the town," he said.

Heading: Ajanta clocks a quick paradigm shift - Indian Express
Content:
Discs will be locked with three layers of password to check question leak

In an attempt to check the leak of question papers, the Gujarat Technological University (GTU) has decided to send the questions in Compact Discs (CDs) to its engineering and pharmaceutical colleges for the next semester examinations. The CDs will be locked with three layers of password.

The method, which will be a first of its kind in Gujarat, will be used during the examination of first-year beginning December 15. This system has already been followed in a few technical universities of the country for the last six years.

There are nearly 200 colleges affiliated with the GTU in the state, having around 55,000 students in the first year. Almost all the colleges have welcomed the move.

N N Bhupatani, Registrar, GTU, told Newsline: "Instead of sealed envelopes, we will send two sealed CDs which will contain files of question papers to all the colleges. It will reduce the possibility of paper leak."

The principals will be sent the passwords through e-mails 30 minutes ahead of the examination, Bhupatani said. He added, "We will also appoint a person for every college who will reach the examination centre with an extra CD as backup."

A senior official from the State Education Department said that in the past, in spite of several security measures, incidents of question paper leak have been reported. "Earlier, we used to remain worried as to whether the question papers would reach the centres on time or not. The possibility of tampering with the question papers during transportation will also not be there anymore," the official said.

Heading: Koshy designs ‘demystification of Indian concepts’ - Indian Express
Content:
Clock-makers come out with e-car to be priced between Rs 85K and 1 lakh

Following the popularity of the electric bikes (e-bikes) in the market, several companies have now started research and development on small electric cars (e-cars). One of them is the Ajanta Group at Morbi in Rajkot, which has now launched the demo model of its small e-car under the brand name of 'Oreva' at a showroom in Rajkot.

The Ajanta Group, which mainly manufactures clocks and several household electronic gadgets under the Orpat brand name, started work on the research and development of small electric cars last year. The only e-car available in the market at present is the Reva, but the company plans to compete directly with Tata's Nano. The non-AC demo e-car, manufactured at the company's Samakhiyali unit in Kutch district, where the Oreva e-bike is also made, is likely to be priced between Rs 85,000 and Rs 1,00,000.

Yogesh Tank, owner of the Oreva Auto showroom in Rajkot, said: "Our e-car is in direct competition with Tata's Nano, but nothing is final on its launch. We might launch it before Nano or maybe later."

He added: "People were amazed to see the e-car when it was put on display at the company's showroom. People came to inquire about the car and also about the booking, but we had to tell them that nothing has been finalised."

Tank said the R&D on the air-conditioner is in progress, and with the AC version, the price is bound to shoot up.

Rakesh Nathwani, National marketing head, Oreva e-bike, told Newsline: "We have just manufactured a demo car. The R & D work is still on. We have not set up any manufacturing plant for the vehicle."

He added: "As of now, I will not be able to reveal anything about the launch of the Oreva e-car in the market. Neither will I be able to comment on whether we will start its mass production or not. Even the pricing part cannot be fixed. In short, nothing has been decided yet. But I can just say one thing; whatever product comes out of our manufacturing unit is value for money."

Heading: Ahmedabad blasts: Hasan, Rehman sent into 13-day police custody - Indian Express
Content:
NID director's book, with a foreword by Ratan Tata, released by governor

A book on Indian design, written by Darlie Koshy, the director of the National Institute of Design (NID) in Ahmedabad, was released by Governor Nawal Kishore Sharma on Friday.

Titled 'Indian Design Edge', the foreword is written by Ratan Tata, whose leadership qualities have put the Indian industry on to the path of irreversible innovation and design.

Sharma said: "I always use to think that design is mostly related to the fashion world and it's meant for the young people. Even when I got the invitation to be the chief guest at the function, I wondered what an old man like me would do at the book release function. But my doubts became clear today after I visited the exhibition at the NID. Now I know that design is beyond the fashion world and it is much more than fashion."

Darlie Koshy said the main concept behind writing this book was to influence the new generation of design innovators. "In this book I have tried to speak about the inevitability of design and innovation found in the Indian industry and society. In India, there is a talent crunch, and Indian design scene is a speaking example of the 'National Design Deficit'. The number of designers, required in tandem with the number of technologists falls far below the requirement," he said.

He added: "This book may simply demystify the concept of design and make it more comprehensible for the larger cross-section of people in India and across the world. It may serve as a bridge for designers to travel to the domain of management and design."

Heading: Police yet to make headway in Raikhad rape-cum-murder case - Indian Express
Content:
The designated Metropolitan Court, hearing the Ahmedabad blast case, remanded Jaipur blast case accused Mehandi Hasan and Atiq-Ur-Rehman, who have been brought to the city on a transfer warrant, to police custody till October 23 on Thursday.

The Rajasthan Police had arrested the two on August 25 from Kota in connection with the May 14 serial blasts, which had claimed 68 lives.

The Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB), the investigating agency in the Ahmedabad blast case, stated in the remand application that both the accused had attended the Halol training camp along with the other arrested in the case. The DCB further said that Hasan and Rehman were part of the conspiracy for the Ahmedabad blasts.

The DCB wants to question the duo about the Halol camp and also gather details of the journey they made from Kota to Halol. The call details of the cellphones used by them during the camp are also under the scanner.

The investigating agency has so far taken into custody 22 people who had allegedly attended the training camp organised by the banned outfit Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) in January. All of them stand accused of being a part of the conspiracy behind the Ahmedabad serial blasts.

The police also want to know more about the links that Hasan and Rehman had with Imran Ahmed, another Jaipur blast accused who is currently in the judicial custody.

Ahmed has also been made an accused in the Ahmedabad blast case and is being brought to the city on a production warrant from Jaipur. He is likely to be produced before the Metropolitan Court on Saturday.

Heading: Two shopkeepers arrested for purchasing goods pilfered from parcels at railway stations - Indian Express
Content:
Even as four days have gone by since a six-year-old girl was found raped and murdered in the slums of Raikhad in Ahmedabad, the Gaekwad Haveli police are still grappling around in the dark to find the accused.

The girl had gone missing from her hut in the Raikhad slums on Monday late night. Following which, the girl's mother, Batulbibi Shaikh, registered a missing complaint. Her body was discovered during the search operation. The post-mortem revealed that she was raped before being murdered.

Inspector G H Khan said, "We are trying to find the accused. However, no breakthrough has been made in the case yet." He did not elaborate on the lines of investigations being followed to crack the case.

Responding to a query as to whether one or more persons were involved in the crime, Khan said, "That can be ascertained only after we get the FSL (Forensic Science Laboratory) report on the semen samples recovered from the body."

Heading: Prisoner re-arrested in Jasdan town - Indian Express
Content:
The Railway Protection Force (RPF), which has busted a racket of pilfering goods from parcels in railway coaches has arrested two shopkeepers from Anand and Ahmedabad. According to the police, the two purchased the stolen goods at reduced rates. The RPF officials are also suspecting the involvement of some more railway employees in the scam, which had been going on for atleast the last two months.

The two shopkeepers have been identified as Qadar Pathan (28) from Anand and Manoharlal Sejwani (52) from Ahmedabad. While Pathan is a salesman at Arati Selection, a readymade store, Sejwani runs a shop, Maheshwari Traders, at the Chokha Bazaar (Rice Market) in the Kalupur area of the city.

The two were arrested after the three earlier arrested in the case had confessed to their role in the scam.

The three arrested earlier include railway guard M A Qazi, his son Saeed Qazi and Nirmal Sewakramani. Sewakramani is believed to be the main accused in the scam.

Investigating Officer Uday Singh said; "With the help of M A Qazi, the accused were pilfering goods from parcels in the train. To conceal the misdeed, they pilfered small amounts, about five kg from a 50 kg parcels. The stolen goods were later purchased by shop keepers like Pathan and Sejwani."

The police have recovered 33 pairs of denim trousers from Pathan's shop and 41 kg cardamom and 8 kg cashew from Sejwani's shop. The police said the market price of cardamom is around Rs 800 per kg and Sejwani was getting the stolen material at half that price.

Singh said that the scam is a nexus between some railway employees, private shopkeepers and others.

"During investigations, we came across the names of some other railway guards who are also involved in the racket. They will be arrested after we collect enough evidence against them," he said. He did not rule out the possibility of arresting some more shopkeepers.

Heading: Dengue strikes Vadodara, VMC swings into action - Indian Express
Content:
A prisoner convicted for life, who had escaped from the prisoner's ward of Rajkot Civil Hospital on Wednesday evening, was nabbed by the Rajkot Rural Police from Jasdan town on Friday.

Ajit Chaku Devipujak, a prisoner in Rajkot jail, was convicted for the murder of his mother-in-law in 2005. He, however, came out on parole in 2006, but was again arrested in for the murder of local disco dandiya tutor Darshan Ganatra.

On September 29, Ajit was shifted to Rajkot Civil Hospital's prisoner ward after he complained of a breathing problem. On Wednesday evening, Assistant Sub Inspector Savji Thavraji Zaria permitted Ajit to go out of the prisoner ward to get cold water from the water cooler situated near ward no.7 of the hospital. Though constable Dinesh Ravji Chuhan was sent along with Ajit, the latter managed to escape from the hospital campus.

After Ajit's escape, Rajkot Police alerted the entire state police through emails. Meanwhile, K B Zala, Inspector, Local Crime Branch

(LCB) of the Rajkot Rural Police received information that Ajit has gone to Jasdan to see his wife Versha and daughter Komal, who never came to meet him after he was convicted by the court. Thus, Zala deployed his entire staff in

Jasdan and arrested Ajit near the bus station on Friday.

According to LCB officers, Ajit confessed that he fled because he was tired with his breathing problem and was desperate to see his wife and daughter.

Heading: VMC undertakes repair of NH-8 water pipes - Indian Express
Content:
All four patients tested positive for the disease are children in the age group of 8-15 years, residents of Moti Chepwad and Mandvi areas of the city

With four confirmed cases of dengue being reported in the city, the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) has swung into action and is leaving no stone unturned to check the disease.

Incidentally, all four patients tested positive for the disease are children- Keta Shah (13), Jayanti Shah (15), Manav Shah (8) and Bhoomi Shah (12).

They were admitted to a city-based private hospital on Tuesday. They are residents of Moti Chepwad and Mandvi areas of the city.

Keta's father Mukesh Shah said: "She has been suffering from high fever and other symptoms (of dengue) for the last few weeks. Test reports confirmed the disease. Her blood platelet count has increased drastically and she is currently under observation."

The Health Department claimed that the unhygienic in-house water storage system led to the disease outbreak.

Shah said, "They surveyed our house as well as the entire area, and found that the stagnant water around the premises of the under-construction building behind our apartment was the source of the disease."

Meanwhile, the VMC has launched a surveillance programme in the affected areas. Dr Mukesh Vaidya, additional health officer, VMC, said: "Maximum number of dengue cases are reported during these months. We had taken up massive fumigation and other anti-larval precautions before and during the monsoon. We have launched an immediate surveillance programme in the areas and households where the cases have been detected."

He added: "Almost all the precautionary measures have been taken up to curb any further cases of vector born diseases. However, we frequently face strict criticism from some religious communities for taking up fumigation and anti-larval measures."

Heading: Bhavnagar University: ABVP bags two senate seats - Indian Express
Content:
The repair work has affected water supply to areas such as Chhani, Sama, Lalbaug, Sayajigunj, Manjalpur and Jail Road.

The Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) on Friday took up massive repair work of the three cracks in the water pipelines on National Highway 8 near the Gujarat state Fertiliser's and Chemicals Ltd (GSFC) crossroads.

The officials identified three places where the pipes were cracked, during surveillance.

The identified areas will be patched during repair work, said VMC city engineer V N Tailor

He said: "We have completed almost 50 per cent of the work. The work will be completed by the midnight."

Though the VMC authorities aim to complete the work by Friday night, the concerned areas receiving water supply from the French wells will receive regular supply only from Saturday onwards.

"We will resume the water supply 24 hours after the

repair work gets over. We have over 25 men working at the site," said Tailor.

The disrupted water pipes are connected to the French wells which forms a major source of water supply to many parts of the city.

The repair work have affected water supply to areas such as Chhani, Sama, Lalbaug, Sayajigunj, Manjalpur and Jail Road.

GIDC officials said that with the disruption in the water pipes, the daily course of water supply, which is over 150 lakh gallons, has now reduced to 40 lakh gallons.

Heading: Muslims cycle from Godhra to Ajmer carrying message of peace - Indian Express
Content:
The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad on Friday bagged the senate seats of the Science and Arts faculties of the Bhavnagar University, while the seat of Engineering faculty went to the National Students' Union of India.

The university authorities had, on October 5, announced re-election after polling for six senate seats, including these three, had taken place on September 28 elections. The re-election for the Commerce, Law and Education faculties will take place on November 10. The decision was taken in view of the use of duplicate identity cards and dummy voters during polling.

Heading: GMC councillors trade charges over Dussehra mishap - Indian Express
Content:
A group of 12 young Muslim men have taken on the daunting task of cycling all the way to Ajmer Sharif from Godhra to pray for peace in the country. The cycle rally organisers say the group will reach Ajmer in seven days, covering 90 kilometres in a day.

District Rashtriya Janata Dal chairman Inayat Mehar Pathan flagged off the rally in the presence of former Congress MLA Rajendra Patel on Thursday.

He said it has become a very difficult time and perpetrators are lending a bad name to the entire community.

"People must see that there are thousands of others who want to work for the country. For these young people, it is not just a physical task, but also to show how people will receive 12 Muslim youths on cycles in different villages during their journey from Godhra to Ajmer," he said.

Incidentally, Inayat's son Asif is also participating in the rally. Asif, who left Modasa in the morning along with 11 others, said the weather was excellent for cycling.

"Today, we took it a little slow. The distance from Godhra to Modassa took us eight hours. Tomorrow onwards, we will cycle fast. We hope to enter Rajasthan by the evening. We have adequate supplies of dry fruits and glucose. We have also been provided with a torch light," said Asif over the phone.

The 12 young men are residents of the Polan Bazar area in Godhra.

While two of them are students, the rest work in their family businesses. Inayat said arranging money for the cycles was never an issue.

Besides Asif, the other members of the group are Mazan Pathan, Subhan Pathan, Rasid Razzaq Mistry, Mehmood Mistry, Irfan Mallick, Iqbal Saiyyad,

Sultan Charkha, Ehsan Pathan, Altaf Mallick, Shafi Liyaqat Khan and Tausif Mistry.

Tausif and Iqbal are studying computer hardware at the Industrial Training Institute in Godhra.

Heading: Now, Metro gets commercial green light - Indian Express
Content:
Sources say effigy blared up, as the foundation of the Ravan model was made of wood instead of iron rods

A day after firecrackers burst abruptly during the

Ravan Dahan ceremony on Dussehra at Lal Baugh Tekri bus stand, injuring 10 people, councillors of the Godhra Municipal Council (GMC) are trading charges over the incident.

On Thursday, BJP councillor Murli Moolchandani had levelled allegation that GMC president Gangan Harwani left the spot immediately even as several people were lying injured.

Reacting to this, Harwani said he left the spot as he was also injured in the incident. "It is wrong to call people irresponsible, when I myself got some injuries. Many councillors and locals were taking care of the injured. Whoever is saying this wants to bring Godhra into a controversy," said Harwani.

Sources said the effigy blared up, as the foundation of the Ravan model was made of wood instead of iron rods. Godhra Town police Inspector M S Patel said they are waiting for the report of the Forensic Science Laboratory, which has collected samples of the firecrackers for examination.

The injured, which included a journalist and a daughter of another journalist, were rushed to the Godhra Civil Hospital. Dr P Sagar, Civil Surgeon of the hospital, told Newsline that out of the 10 brought there for treatment, only two persons had major burns.

There were also cases of superficial injuries due to stampede that followed. One Raju Faruki, an artist from Uttar Pradesh who burnt the effigy, was severely injured and was admitted to the SSG Hospital.

Heading: Day after 9 feared washed away, kin give up hope, await bitter news — officially - Indian Express
Content:
Can develop property at, along, even atop stations; no land-use restrictions, says committee

The Delhi Metro can now develop property at its stations and use land whichever way it deems fit, without the government's go-ahead, to ensure all its future projects are cost-effective.

The decision was taken at a high-level meeting of the empowered committee under the Cabinet Secretary on Friday.

It was decided at the meeting to "relax norms" for Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) about property development in existing or proposed stations. The DMRC can now use the profit earned from property development to procure rolling stock.

Till now DMRC had to seek the government's permission to develop property on its premises.

A senior government official who was part of this development said the idea behind relaxing norms is to ensure DMRC can fund its own projects and procure stock without waiting for government assistance. "They have been allowed to develop property even in the past but now they no longer need permission from the Urban Development Ministry," the official said. "Nor will they have to follow strict regulations on land-use.

"For instance, if DMRC has been given land for a station but finds the area suitable for another purpose, they can go ahead. Or if they have surplus land they can use it in any fashion they deem fit."

The rules have now made it possible for DMRC to develop property on top of the Metro stations, officials said.

An official in the Urban Development Ministry said this model of relaxed land norms for metro railway system would now be implemented across the country. "We will, of course, monitor how the Delhi model unfolds and then recommend it to other states developing Metro rail system," the official added.

With restrictions from the Urban Development ministry out of the way, the only clearance that DMRC now needs is clearance for building from local agencies such as the MCD, NDMC and DDA among others. Before this relaxation, Delhi Metro was allowed to develop 500 meters of land commercially on either side of its stations.

"This land, however, cannot be auctioned since it is on lease," the Urban Development ministry official said. "So any commercial activity will have to take place within a lease period and then given back to the Metro."

Haryana station projects get panel's okay
The Empowered Committee on Friday also cleared a proposal of the Haryana government to increase its development around three stations of its elevated stretch on the Delhi-Gurgaon route. The route ends at Sushant Lok in Gurgaon. The committee has decided to include service roads along the stations to help commuters. This would be developed at an additional cost of Rs 5 crore: Haryana government will provide Rs 4 crore of this, and the Centre will pitch in with the rest Rs 1 crore.

Heading: In Tihar Jail, HIV-positive woman inmate bites matron’s hand - Indian Express
Content:
Residents of Gali Number 10 in West Delhi's Anand Parbat spent all day waiting to hear from the authorities. There was little activity in the locality, home to mostly labourers of small-scale units dotting the area, as relatives and neighbours waited for news about the nine people feared drowned on Thursday during immersion of the locality's Durga idol.

Till now only the body of one Jitender, 16, has been recovered. According to police, a farmer from Jagatpur area found Jitender's body at Shyam Ghat, on Yamuna banks.

The police, fire department and municipal officials failed to recover any body on Friday. Victims of those missing, though, have as good as given up hope. On Thursday evening, nine people had gone missing after getting into the Yamuna at Sonia Vihar Pushta, North Delhi, to immerse Durga idol.

Locals said some 40 people had gone for the immersion from their Taali Basti in Anand Parbat. All packed in a tempo, they headed for Wazirabad but, denied permission since their Durga Puja is not registered, they changed course and headed for Sonia Vihar Pushta instead.

"The entire group got in the river and most of them lost footing in the rapid current," Deenanath Saha, an eyewitness, said. While the others scampered back, the nine got tangled in the marsh on the shallow edge and were washed away, Saha said.

Raj Kumar, elder brother of one of the victims, Rajman, said there's no news from the authorities as yet: "He has a five-month-old son and was the family's only earning member. Who is going to take care of them now?"

Sonu, 13, is also missing. His father Daya Ram, unemployed himself, had found solace a few days ago — when Sonu got a job at one of the small factories in the area. Daya Ram has five other children, and the anxiety to feed so many mouths is showing. "This was the first time Sonu went to the ghat for the immersion," he said. "He insisted on accompanying his uncle; now see what has happened..."

Aftab had gone for the immersion with his elder cousin Asif. Now both are missing. Aftab's father Nizam Ali said at least one member from the family goes for the immersion with local youths every year. Aftab's mother Lalli Rahisan said, "It feels as if I have lost two sons. We were going to get Aftab married in two months."

Heading: 26th victim of Delhi blasts, second one in family - Indian Express
Content:
A matron deputed at Tihar Jail was admitted to hospital after being bitten by a Nigerian woman inmate last week. The inmate is HIV-positive.

According to sources, the incident occurred around 6.45 pm on Saturday when matron Renu Yadav asked the inmate (identity withheld) to take her medicine. She first ignored the matron and when she insisted, turned violent and bit her hand. It took around five minutes and over a dozen other women jail staff to overpower the Nigerian inmate.

"While staff members tried to restrain her, she lunged forward to attack Yadav," a Tihar Jail official said.

The inmate was brought to jail a few months ago in connection with a case under the Narcotics Drug and Psychotropic Substances Act and was under treatment as she is HIV-positive.

"She would often lose her temper without any reason and on Saturday crossed limits," said a senior Tihar Jail official. Sources said Yadav was immediately taken to a doctor and is admitted at Deen Dayal Upadhyay Hospital.

"She is under constant supervision of doctors at the hospital," a source in the jail said. "They (doctors) have started medication to avoid any risk as the inmate was HIV-positive."

An FIR has been registered at Hari Nagar police station. The incident has been recorded by jail CCTV cameras and there is substantive proof of the scuffle, jail officials said.

Confirming the incident, the public relations officer of Tihar Jail, Sunil Gupta, said, "A case has been registered against the inmate at Hari Nagar police station and proper action will be taken against her."

Heading: Go Air emergency landing: Engineer suspended for missing the missing wheel - Indian Express
Content:
Santosh (22) became the 26th victim of the Delhi serial blasts at the neuro-surgery ward of the Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital on Friday. She was among those critically injured in the Gaffar Market blast and was in coma ever since.

"Santosh had received severe skull injuries in the blast. There was no improvement in her condition in the past weeks," said a senior doctor at the hospital.

Santosh breathed her last at 11 am today.

The September 13 blasts spelt tragedy for Santosh's family. Her father, Rama Nadibatt (48), who is recuperating in the Orthopaedics ward at the same hospital, lost his second daughter Pooja (17) on the day of the blast, while his wife Krishna (44) is still admitted in the hospital after having a miraculous recovery, oblivious of her daughters' death.

Nadibatt performed the last rites of his daughter. "He could not perform the last rites for Pooja as he was himself in a serious condition, and was told about her death after almost a fortnight. We, however, took him for Santosh's cremation," said Devi Dass, a relative.

Originally from Rajasthan, Rama and his family had been living in Gali number 42 in Karol Bagh for years now.

Heading: Real estate in dumps, developers offer freebies to sell houses - Indian Express
Content:
A day after a Go Air flight made an emergency landing at IGI Airport with one of its nose wheels missing, the flight safety engineer was suspended on Friday.

The wheel of the Mumbai-Delhi G8-456 flight fell on the runway in Mumbai airport soon after the aircraft took off on Thursday afternoon.

None of the 123 people on board was hurt in the incident.  

According to a senior airport official, initial investigations reveal that the aircraft had undergone maintenance work earlier on Thursday. "There was some problem in the wing and it seems the nose wheel had been removed while repairing it," the official said. "But the engineer probably forgot to fix it back."

The Director General Civil Aviation (DGCA) today sought a detailed inquiry. "We have directed (Go Air) to suspend the air safety engineer and further inquiry is being carried out," DGCA's Kanu Gohain said.

The Airbus A-320 aircraft was inducted in the Go Air fleet in November 2007. The DGCA will also question officials from Airbus about the incident.

On Thursday, within minutes of the take-off at 2.23 pm, a Mumbai airport employee who was on runway to scare away birds, noticed the wheel missing. He alerted the Mumbai Air Traffic Controller, which informed the airline. The problem escalated for the airline staff since there was no way to ascertain whether the nose wheel or the rear wheel was missing.

The pilot, Captain Hardeep Singh, was informed about the missing wheel barely 35 minutes before landing. He did a low fly past to identify which wheel was missing and engineers on ground at IGI identified it. The aircraft finally landed on the primary runway on its rear wheels, with the pilot ensuring that the front wheel touched down as softly as possible.

The passengers in the first 11 rows were moved back and enough fuel was burnt to make the aircraft light.

The DGCA, meanwhile, has appreciated the pilot's efforts.

Heading: Let the beer flow: Oktoberfest comes to town - Indian Express
Content:
To drop up the fall in real estate prices, developers in the Capital's outskirts have opened an expensive gift shop to drum up demand for property.

A set of duplex flats is being offered along with a BMW or even a Mercedes as bonus. Some others come with tickets to the Alps or a seven-day sojourn in London. And the most lucrative gift of them all? A flat free if you buy in bulk of five to 10.

Diwali has always brought freebies from the developer community. But this year's festivities have come with a liquidity crunch coupled with a drop in sales, builders told Newsline.

A Gurgaon-based consultant said: "The National Capital Region (NCR) has emerged as a mature market over the last three years. Investors are finding it difficult to hold on to property for long. This would mean there are genuine buyers and end-users in the market. Developers are now trying to tap the more significant segment of end-users."

Several property shows are on at the moment in the NCR region, where buyers can check out homes as well as the attractive schemes that come with it. Many developers are offering heavy discounts like assured returns, payments under construction-linked plans, or direct discount at the time of a project's launch.

Delhi-based Services (India) Pvt Ltd have fairs going on in Noida and Gurgaon till October 12. Nearly 25 big and small developers are presenting their projects, along with that something 'extra'. Real estate company Omaxe has also pitched in this time — its Home Loan Mela at Sector MU in Greater Noida is running to a packed house.

Managing Director of Omaxe Rohtas Goel said: "We are inviting dealers, direct customers and prospective buyers to the event. Many bankers would be present for on-the-spot approval of loans. Looking at the overwhelming demand for all our projects, we have also decided to give gifts to our customers. At the moment, demand has shifted from investors to end-users, who do consider discounts when they decide to purchase a home. We hope to perk up sales with what is on offer."

ING Vysya Bank, a prominent private sector bank, will hold a two-day Property Mart this weekend at Pragati Maidan. The properties on sale range from Rs 25 lakh to Rs 2.5 crore. The bank's country head (Retail Banking) Uday Sareen said: "We have noticed there is heavy demand from first-time home owners to buy property around this time."

However, some developers are not telling the whole story. Many are not discussing these schemes openly. Noida-based consultant Rajiv Mehrotra said: "Projects which have a good saleability do not have schemes. These are selling at market rates. Developers who are not well-known, or homes that are not conveniently located are offering schemes like assured returns."

What's on offer
* Assured 12% return on commercial property
* Discount @ Rs 50-100 per sq ft on basic property rate
* Construction linked plan: Some developers seek 50% of total amount during construction of project; rest to be made at the time of possession
* Inaugural discount of Rs 100 per sq ft or more at launch

Heading: Bail paid, no surety to get back money - Indian Express
Content:
If you are the kind who likes to drink, sing along and make merry, this is for you. The German festival for beer drinkers, Oktoberfest, has reached Indian shores. And the Capital will have the privilege to be the first city in India to host the festival. Unlike the original German sixteen-day festival, the Indian variant, "The Oktoberfest of India" will be spread across three days (October 10 to 12) and will see the best of German culture, food and music in the sprawling lawns of the Select Citywalk Mall, Saket.

This gala event is being put together with a little German assistance. S Oliver, the famous European apparel brand, which launched their store on Thursday, followed it up with the opening of the fest. "It has always been our endeavour to expose customers to different cultures," says Anjalie Wadhawan, head of marketing, Select Citywalk Mall.

Oktoberfest is a sixteen-day festival known for exotic beers, held every year at Munich in Bavaria, Germany in late September. A world-famous event, it draws around six million people every year.

For admission tickets worth Rs 2,800 per couple and Rs 1,400 per person, one gets to feast on unlimited food like pretzels, sausages, burgers and unlimited beers. The venue will have six conical tents, with one large tent supplying famous German Bitburger Beer from 7 to 10 pm. To provide a touch of authenticity, log benches and chairs have been set rather than the conventional seating arrangement.

A German brass band "Wisen Fest" has also been roped in to play popular German folk songs.

"We are hoping the crowd will sing along as in Germany this is an occasion to unwind and enjoy with friends. We intend playing popular English songs along with German Oktoberfest songs like 'Proset' and '99 Luft Balloons'," says Sebastian Lehmann, 26, lead singer of the band, who has previous experience of playing at various Munich beer festivals.

Guests will be served chilled glasses of beer in tall Pilzner beer glasses by hostesses dressed in traditional Bavarian costumes called Dirndls.

So, if an air ticket to Bavaria is not in your budget this year, then pay a visit to the mall for a slice of German hospitality.

Heading: Rain pain? Tomato prices make city see red - Indian Express
Content:
Here is a warning for people paying money to get others to stand as sureties to get bail for their relatives. And then expecting the guarantor to return the surety money after the accused gets bail.

While a criminal court may grant bail, caring little about the source of money being deposited by a surety, a civil court will not come to the aid of the person who alleges breach of promise by the surety — who acts like a guarantor in such cases — when the latter refuses to pay back.

Reason: as per legal provisions and several decisions of higher courts, paying someone to stand as a surety is "unlawful". Thus, it has no sanctity in the eyes of law to warrant a court's intervention. Such an agreement is opposed to public policy as the consideration (money) is unlawful for achieving the purpose (getting bail), according to relevant laws.

In a recent case, Anil Kumar, who had allegedly given Rs 15,000 to a friend for standing surety for his brother in a criminal case, learnt the lesson the hard way: he had to forego the money. Kumar had deposited the sum as fixed deposit in the bank account of R P Pandey, who stood surety for his brother three years ago. The document regarding the deposit was submitted in the court while securing the bail.

Pandey had allegedly promised to return the amount after the trial's completion.

After Kumar's brother came out clean, the court passed an order to release the bail bond amount along with the fixed deposit money and Kumar insisted on getting back the money along with interest. But after Pandey refused, Kumar approached a civil court by filing a suit for recovery. Civil Judge Tarun Yogesh, however, snubbed Kumar for entering into such an agreement. "Where money has been paid for obtaining a surety, such agreement is contrary to the provisions of law," the court, citing an Allahabad High Court judgment, observed.

Holding that the court could not come to rescue of a man who engaged a surety in an unlawful manner, the judge cited the concerned provisions of the Indian Contract Act and said that such an agreement was not enforceable. "The consideration and object of the agreement being illegal and unlawful, the plaintiff cannot claim to be entitled to the recovery of the amount," the court ruled.

Bail: terms and conditions
"Bail" is broadly used to refer to the release of a person charged with an offence, on his providing a security that will ensure his presence before the court or any other authority whenever required.

Bail is granted after a person, his relative or friend, stands as a surety for him and promises to ensure his presence whenever required.

As a pre-condition for release, a monetary value of the security, known as bail bond, is set by the court having jurisdiction over the prisoner. The security may be cash, papers giving title to property, or the bond of private persons of means or of a professional bondsman or bonding company. Failure of the person released on bail to surrender himself at the appointed time results in forfeiture of the security.

In case the accused gets acquitted, his bail bond, along with the surety bond is returned to him in accordance with the CrPC.

Heading: De-silting on, no shortage at Sonia Vihar plant: DJB - Indian Express
Content:
The submergence of tomato cultivating areas on Yamuna's banks following last month's heavy rains has led to a decline in production, causing prices to shoot through the roof.

Tomato prices in the retail market have gone up to Rs 40 to Rs 50 per kg because of a huge gap in demand and supply. In many upscale colonies, retailers are asking for as much as Rs 60 per kg.

Only 100 tonnes of tomato are being supplied at present — this is against the city's regular demand of 250 tonnes. Delhi government officials have attributed the poor supply from neighbouring states such as Himachal Pradesh and Haryana to the heavy rains that washed away the crop being cultivated in low-lying areas. "Supply from Ratlam and along the river bed of Yamuna in Haryana and Delhi has hit (cultivation) hard, therefore the shooting-up of prices.

But the situation will ease within the next five days," Braham Yadav, chairman of Delhi Agricultural Marketing Board, said. He said the new crop of tomatoes will arrive from Rajasthan and Karnal soon.

Heading: Delhi govt official held for fraud gets bail - Indian Express
Content:
Although the Sonia Vihar water treatment plant is not getting its due water supply from Tehri Dam through Upper Ganga Canal, Delhi Jal Board has clarified that it is a scheduled de-silting of the canal that takes place every year at this time.

"The Upper Ganga Canal, which starts at Haridwar, is closed at Muradnagar for 15 days every year for cleaning and de-silting. This is a pre-planned process, which doesn't mean that Delhi is not getting its water supply," said a senior official of the DJB.

"The capacity has gone down slightly, but we are filling it up with alternative arrangements. Yamuna water is being diverted and brought to the Sonia Vihar and Bhagirathi Plants," he said.

The 140 MGD capacity plant at Sonia Vihar and 100 MGD Bhagirathi plant are said to be currently suffering from a raw water shortage, as they rely on Ganga waters from the Tehri Dam, which is now closed.

Heading: DDA to spell out rates for enhanced floor area in hotels - Indian Express
Content:
Following detention of about a month, a senior Delhi government official, arrested by Anti-Corruption Branch for committing a fraud in the purchase of materials for shelters run by the Social Welfare Department, has procured bail as investigators said they would miss the deadline for filing the chargesheet.

Fifty-three-year-old Bimla Chaudhary was accorded reprieve on Monday in her second attempt after her first bail plea was turned down on September 16.

The favourable order came after Special Judge A S Yadav inquired from the Investigating Officer (IO) whether the prosecution would be able to file the chargesheet within the stipulated period of 60 days in order to keep her in custody.

While accepting that the prosecution had in its possession various incriminating documents, the IO told the judge that the prosecution would in fair probability miss the deadline and that another accused, Ravinder Goel, was also released by the court on account of delay in filing the chargesheet.

"It is not the intention of law to keep a person in pre-trial detention if the same is not required. The accused is a woman. She is in custody for the last about 30 days and no useful purpose would be served by keeping her in pre-trial detention," said the judge, allowing the bail plea.

Chaudhary was then asked to furnish a bail bond along with a surety bond of Rs 50,000 each as a pre-condition of her release.

The Anti-Corruption Branch of Delhi Police had registered two FIRs against the officials of Social Welfare Department and another person on June 24 for alleged misappropriation of funds meant for people below poverty line.

Chaudhary, a superintendent with the department, had allegedly made huge purchases of clothing, bedding, dietary and general items for inmates of social welfare homes on the basis of forged quotation in complicity with some other public officers and private persons.

Apart from her, Rajender Prasad Singh, a district officer and Goel, Sanjay Gihar, Judu Joseph and R K Sharma have also been named as accused in the case. The FIRs were registered under the Prevention of Corruption Act and Indian Penal Code accusing them of committing conspiracy, forgery, cheating and other offences.

According to the police, the purchases were made through limited tenders by the use of fake quotations rather than open tenders. Other methods of fraud like inflating the number of inmates and bogus claims had also allegedly come to light.

Heading: Three Afghans get 10 years in jail for drug trafficking - Indian Express
Content:
In an important amendment to Masterplan Delhi 2021, the Delhi Development Authority had earlier this year granted hotels the right to enhanced Floor Area Ratio (FAR). While the FAR before the MPD modification was 150, the authority decided to allow hotels an FAR of 225. This means if there is a plot of 100 square feet, a hotel owner can now carry out vertical construction up to 225 square feet.

The modification was thought to have paved the way for an addition of almost 8,000 rooms in the Capital in anticipation of the Commonwealth Games 2010. The authority will now notify the charges fixed for availing the benefit of enhanced FAR for hotels.

According to the terms set by the DDA, all hotels eligible for availing the enhanced FAR will have to pay 100 per cent of the Zonal Average Auction Rate (ZAAR). "The ZAAR, essentially, is the average rate of all the hotels plots auctioned in a certain zone," a senior DDA official said.

Under such terms, those hoping to avail the enhanced FAR by constructing additional rooms will have to shell out a huge sum. However, another clause says hotels which are able to complete and ratify their additional rooms by August 31, 2010 will avail a 25 per cent concession on the Zonal Average Auction Rate.

"Hotels which are able to add rooms in the Capital in time for the games will be given a concession on the rates for enhancing FAR," a DDA official said. However, new hotels which have been granted a five-year tax holiday will not avail this concession.

Heading: Labourer killed, three others injured as cylinder bursts at IGI airport construction site - Indian Express
Content:
A city court sentenced three Afghan nationals to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment on Friday for their involvement in drug trade. The court also pulled up the Delhi Police for shielding the "high and mighty" involved in the case, saying the trade was being used to fund terror in India.

"Investigations show the present case has international ramifications. Apart from the accused, some high and mighty persons in India might have been involved in the case... Police have subverted the course of investigation and shut their eyes...," said Special NDPS Judge Babu Lal.

The court suggested the chief of police order an inquiry into the matter. The court's observations came after it noted that though the police had recovered cellphones from the accused identified as Mohd Nasir, Fazal Haq and Mohd Rahim, all residents of Afghanistan, it never tried to get their mobile numbers or identify their contacts in India.

"This shows the police deliberately took no steps to ascertain the whereabouts of people linked to the accused and even if they had come to know about their identity, they have (shielded) them," the court noted. The court imposed a fine of Rs two lakh on one of the convicts, Mohd Nasir, and a fine of Rs one lakh each on Fazal Haq and Mohd Rahim, besides the sentence, after holding them guilty under various provisions of the Narcotics Drug and Psychotropic Substance Act.

The court further ordered that a copy of its judgement be sent to the Commissioner of Police for a thorough inquiry into the lapses committed by the police.

The accused were apprehended from Nabi Karim police station area with 4.5 kg of heroin on April 2, last year.

Heading: Woman recovers from genital TB to give birth at AIIMS - Indian Express
Content:
A labourer was killed and three others suffered injuries when a gas cylinder exploded at a labourer's camp near the construction site of the third terminal at the Indira Gandhi International Airport. Angry labourers protested for nearly two hours and went on a rampage around the camp. Extra police force had to be called in to control the situation.

"A worker was cooking food in the kitchen at the labourers colony in T3 Project Site around 8:00 am when a cooking gas cylinder caught fire," said the Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL) spokesperson.

The LPG cylinder caught fire and panic-stricken labourer pushed the cylinder into the open. "He dragging the flaming cylinder and placed it in the open after the security guards asked him to do so, an eyewitness claimed.

Workers then tried to extinguish the fire by putting a rucksack over the cylinder which continued to burn for about half-an-hour after which it exploded, injuring four persons. The injured were rushed to Ayushman hospital in Dwarka.

"Jawahar Mahto (40), hailing from Bihar's Siwan district, suffered serious injuries and later died in the hospital during treatment," a senior police officer said.

Another labourer Babol Singh from Kanpur in Uttar Pradesh also sustained serious injuries. Singh was later shifted to Indian Spinal Injuries Centre at Vasant Kunj.

A group of workers pelted stones at security personnel and the canteen. Labourers alleged they had informed security officials about the burning cylinder but no one took action.

Heading: Three arrested, heroin worth Rs 70 lakh seized - Indian Express
Content:
In a first of its kind operation, a woman who had previously been treated for genital tuberculosis underwent a successful in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) in March this year. The 31-year-old gave birth to twin girls following a Caesarean section on Thursday.

According to AIIMS officials, the woman was diagnosed with genital tuberculosis in January 2003. She was treated with anti-tuberculosis drugs and was unable to conceive following the treatment. The woman from Ghaziabad approached the IVF facility in AIIMS in March this year. "For a woman who has been treated for genital TB, chances of conceiving even after IVF are extremely rare. It has been a landmark achievement for us," said Dr Sunita Mittal, HoD, Obstetrics and Gynaecology at AIIMS.
