Content: The Gurgaon police arrested three youths from the Railway Road in Civil Lines on Thursday and recovered 600 gm of heroin from their possession. The arrested have been identified as Dinesh, Parvesh and Sukhvir, all between the age group of 20 to 22 years, said Joint Commissioner of Police Manjit Singh Ahlawat. Ahlawat said Dinesh, a resident of Gurgaon, has been in the drug trade for long. Ahlawat said Parvesh and Sukhvir are children of jail superintendents at Bhondsi Jail and students at a private institute. The drugs allegedly recovered are worth Rs 60 to 70 lakh in the market. A case under NDPS Act has been registered.

Heading: Early start on the learning curve - Indian Express
Content:
S PETTIGREW LIVES FOR A DAY
CAST: Frances McDormand, Amy Adams, Ciaran Hinds;
DIRECTOR: Bharat Nalluri
One could call Miss Pettigrew Lives For A Day a light-weight comedy of manners. However, that wouldn't be doing justice to this "satire" on the fashionable set. In the hands of the sensitive McDormand and the vulnerable Adams, it as much mocks the crowd as empathises with it. There's not to judge, they say, and they don't.

Adapting Winifred Watson's 1938 bestseller, Indian-origin director Nalluri captures, through one day in the life of Miss Pettigrew, the excesses and anxieties of life, in the excesses and anxieties of a London at the brink of World War II.

Delysia Lafosse (Adams) is a singer at a famous London nightclub hoping to be a Hollywood star. Her ticket, she believes, is the 19-year-old son of a theatre producer who is unapologetically and enthusiastically two-timing her with another aspiring actress. Delysia, who knows when to charmingly turn a blind eye, also has two other boyfriends — one the nightclub owner who takes care of her financial needs and the other a man who sees past her beauty and loves her for who she is.

Miss Pettigrew (McDormand) finds herself here one fine day after she has lost yet another job as a nanny and is left without food, clothes or money. Her practical straightforwardness stands out in a place where almost nobody is telling the truth. Unwittingly, she gets roped in as Delysia's "social secretary". Alone and clueless, Delysia starts counting on Miss Pettigrew to sort out her complicated love life, and hence on her complicated life.

As she gets to see the glamorous set up close, the sensible Miss Pettigrew is shocked at first but soon realises that there's little to separate her from them in what they are all lacking: companionship. At one point, Delysia, irritated at Miss Pettigrew again telling her to choose heart over head, says: "You speak as if you are an expert on love." Miss Pettigrew replies: "I'm not an expert on love, I'm an expert on the lack of love." Not profound perhaps, but aptly expressive of a profound loneliness.

The film, in fact, has several such moments where a world lies beneath a few words. At another point, Miss Pettigrew and a lingerie designer (Hindas), who has taken a strange liking to her, sit quietly in the lobby as others rush out to watch military airplanes fly by in a loud drone. "They don't remember the last time," mumbles Miss Pettigrew. "No, they don't," answers he.

Delysia also encapsulates her insecurities and her seeming cheerful flittishness in one short outburst during a carriage ride, immediately giving her story a timeless currency. The clothes she is wearing, she says, is all that she owns. "For all the fancy apartments and fashion shows, do you know how close I am to having nothing? Every day I wake up and I think, if I make the wrong move, I could be out on that street."

While both the wide-eyed, luminous Adams and the scene-stealer McDormand are examples of great casting, Hindas and other actors who fill in the picture are equally subtle, especially Shirley Henderson in the role of a cold salon owner.

Miss Pettigrew... is uncomplicated; both Delysia and Miss Pettigrew walk right down the expected path. However, as the film shows, there are some things better said straight.

shalini.langer@expressindia.com

Hello
CAST: Sharman Joshi, Sohail Khan, Gul Panag, Amrita Arora, Isha Koppikar, Sharat Saxena, Dalip Tahil, Salman Khan, Katrina Kaif
DIRECTOR: Atul Agnihotri
One night in a call centre, there comes a phone call. Really, a phone call in a call centre, cries Salman Khan (playing himself), in mock amazement. Pretty laptop-toting storyteller (Katrina) smiles mysteriously, and begins her yarn. And as yarns go, it isn't too bad. The trouble with Hello, based on Chetan Bhagat's mega-seller, is that isn't too good either.

It's a dark rainy night, and Shyam aka Sam (Sharman) is hurting because the love of his life Priyanka (Gul) has said yes to a rich NRI. Varun aka Vrroom (Sohail) has his eye on Esha (Isha), but all she wants is to become a model. Radhika (Amrita) tries to please her horrible mom-in-law by day, and pops anti-depressants by night because her husband is a two-timing cad. And Military Uncle (Sharat) is upset because his US-based son wants to have nothing to do with him.

These sad sack call centre agents rattle around in a large room with work stations placed miles apart. That's a total wrong number. Except for a barmy systems guy, and smarmy boss (Dalip), there doesn't seem to be a soul else in Atul Agnihotri's scheme of things: he's clearly not aware of all those rows and rows of super-busy souls — sitting elbow-to-elbow, nattering the night away on their headphones and mikes— that seem to be more the norm in these nocturnal work hives echoing with faux American accents.

You could also call Hello a case of six characters in search of a zingy script. Bhagat's novel is not literature, but manages to capture some of the hurly-hurly of New India's preoccupation with instant money, getting ahead and greenbacks. The film's canvas is largely empty, so the good turn by Sharman Joshi gets lost. As does some genuinely funny banter, and the Khan family's full turnout (Salman with his shirt off, girlfriend Kat in a cameo, chhota bhai Arbaaz in a walk on) on account of Agnihotri being the Khans' brother-in-law.

Even that thing that call centre types are allegedly indulging in all the time — making out on down-time in the back of convenient SUVs — pictured here on Sharman and Gul, lacks fire. It's tepid, just like the movie.

shubhra.gupta@gmail.com

Heading: Yet another comeback on the cards for Tara - Indian Express
Content:
With dreams of winning a Grand Slam, nine-year old Shramay earns his first title

The u-10 Roshanara Open junior title is Shramay Dhawan's first catch in his five-year long career. And for his debut win, Shramay thrashed Ratik Kapoor 8-2 in the best of fifteen games final on Friday.

Despite his small frame, Shramay has a deceptive forehand that has served him well every time he steps on to the court. The fact that the closest winning margin for him in this tournament was a 6-4 scoreline in a best of 11 games in the second round is testimony to the fact.

For the final, however, he didn't have to sweat too much, something that he admits. At the same time, though, a win here seem like nothing compared to his dreams. "He once dreamt of playing at Roland Garros against (Rafael) Nadal in the final. He said he lost the first game, but went on to win the match to lift the French Open (in his dream)," says Ritu Dhawan, Shramay's mother.

"It's not only his passion for the game at this age, but his insistence on perfection and complete knowledge about the game. You can ask him about any tennis player on earth and he will be ready with the answers. In fact, he is so serious about the game that sometimes, in his quest for perfection, he ends up carrying a tennis kit double his size," she adds.

Looking up to Pistol Pete
In his quest for 'perfection' and 'discipline', Shramay has found his idol in Pete Sampras. Despite never having seen the legend in action, Shramay was hooked on to the game — and Sampras — after watching a documentary on a popular sports channel. It is for the lack of this very 'discipline' that he doesn't like Rafael Nadal or even Boris Becker, who was a part of the show.

During Friday's final, though, he admits to having let his idol down by making faces on losing points. "I like Sampras for his humbleness and try to follow his on-court attitude. But today I lost my temper and made faces at my opponent at least twice. I will try to avoid that in future," says Shramay.

According to his coach Yogesh Kumar, the youngest trainee at the Siri Fort Sports Complex has many things uncommon to his age-group. "He keeps hitting balls all the time — on court, on the wall, against any surface he gets hands to. He will keep watching Yuki (Bhambri) for hours. And when everyone else has left, you can see him still working hard. He keeps a complete account of international tennis, even visiting Grand Slam websites to catch a glimpse of the matches he missed," says Kumar.

In fact, even his selection at the Siri Fort complex for training was not a matter of routine. "We generally don't take in children of his age as kids so young are very indecisive about continuing with the game after a couple of years. However, with Shramay we had no hesitancy in deciding to take him in. His commitment and the amount of time he spends on court were enough to convic us about his seriousness," Kumar says.

He adds that Aditya Sachdeva (Yuki Bhambri's coach) also played a big role in ensuring that Shramay got to play at the Siri Fort complex. "He keeps an eye on him all the time," adds Kumar.

Grand plans
And while his parents plan to train him in Germany, Shramay points out a couple of weaknesses that need immediate attention. "None of my volleys work.

Every time I end up hitting into the bottom of the net. I also miss a lot of my drop shots," Shramay adds as he gets off the court with a kit bag double his size.

Other final results: Boys u-14: Rahul Singh beat Amitya Aggarwal 7-2; U-12: Shubhankar Bahl beat Amitya Aggarwal 7-2

Heading: And Macca Gently Weeps - Indian Express
Content:
Tara Iyer won the comeback battle the last time she attempted it — two years ago, to be precise. The memory of that, perhaps, gives her the confidence to turn things around when she begins her climb up the rankings again.

Back in 2006, Iyer stepped on to the DLTA courts after a long injury break, with not a single ranking point. She picked up pace as the tournaments wore on, getting a place on the Fed Cup team and picking up a string of titles in 2007 at home and abroad. But, just when she seemed to be getting into the form of her life, injury struck again.

In January this year, Tara moved back to the US to continue her education at Duke University, bidding adieu to professional tennis for the time being.

But having opted for an accelerated course so she could return to competitive tennis by the middle of 2009, the 20-year-old is now looking forward to playing on the tour. "I haven't been to India in more than nine months. I'm absolutely looking forward to playing there once more. I hope to return to Siri Fort and train there," Tara told Sportline.

Charting her own path
But as the college tennis vs pro tennis debate continues, Tara appears to have it all sorted in her mind. She has also noted the exploits of Somdev Devvarman, along the same path. "I think it is important to get a college degree at some point in one's career. For me, this timing made sense. Of course, it will be a bit tough coming back to the women's tour but I'm looking forward to it," she says. "College tennis is pretty competitive. Somdev did great at the University of Virginia and I'm hoping I can follow in his footsteps. One of the reasons I chose Duke was so I could benefit from a good fitness programme and get healthy again. Duke not only has a good tennis team but also an excellent sports medicine department."

The rigours of pursuing an academic course along with sports mean Tara's schedule is pretty much without breathing space, and she laughs off inquiries about 'free time'. "Free time... you can't be serious. There is no free time at Duke. I'm either in the library, or on the tennis courts, or in the gym. Combining studies with tennis isn't for the fainthearted, but I'm somehow managing."

In 2008, the Hyderabad-born player was the No 1 singles player for her university; at the same time, she managed to get A grades and be on the Dean's Honour list. Asked about her take on returning to the women's circuit, she said: "I will probably start playing from next July. It is tough to lose all points but it'll also be fun to start from scratch. As long as my game and fitness is good I'll be fine. I'm looking forward to it."

Heading: All in One - Indian Express
Content:
Musician Nitin Sawhney's latest album London Undersound has a series of high-profile collaborations and Paul McCartney singing about his breakup with Heather Mills

When the tabloids blitzed London with the bitter split of the former Beatle, Paul McCartney, and his former wife Heather Mills, the musician Nitin Sawhney couldn't help calling up Macca, his friend of 12 years, and ask if he wanted to write down his feelings in a song. That's what The Beatles always did. The call eventually resulted in a maudlin, acoustic, love ballad called My soul and features in Sawhney's latest album, London Undersound.

"Paul came down to my house for a couple of days and we started putting together the track which delves into the paparazzi infiltrating his life during the breakup. More than just about the split, it's also about his soul being stolen," says Sawhney, who also penned the lyrics of the song with McCartney. The alimony is not part of the song that goes, "I long to know all your secrets/ I want to walk through your fire/ Light up my eyes with your smile", which is also believed to be McCartney's dedication to Mills and has a tinge of Indian classical vocals in the background.

But it is not just one collaboration that Sawhney has lined up. "The entire album is a series of collaborations and represents the changing dynamics of London as a city, and hence the name," says the 44-year-old, who is concerned about the fear trickling in the city after 9/11 and 7/7. "There's a lot of unease about issues like race and civil liberties in London and across the world," he says. Sawhney who, along with Sanjeev Bhaskar, created the music for the hit series Goodness Gracious Me, says the British-Asian community is perceived differently now than when the funny series was conceptualised. The shadow of terror is there in the album as well, with the reggae artist Natty interpreting his first-hand account of the 7/7 bombings in Days of fire.

Sawhney has also collaborated with Tina Grace and Anoushka Shankar in Transmission and Charukeshi respectively. "I've always known them through their music, but this album is special as it reflects the vision of various artists," he says.

Sawhney, who is of Indian origin, now plays many roles in London — a club DJ, a songwriter, composer, classical pianist and flamenco guitarist. After composing the score for Mira Nair's The Namesake, he's also working on four more films, including Deepa Mehta's next, Exclusion. Meanwhile, his first performance in India is yet to be. In the diary, he has marked the 2010 Jaipur Festival, but he is hoping it happens sooner.

Heading: Maharaja and I - Indian Express
Content:
The IIC Experience will bring together morning ragas, Mughal cuisine, masked dancers from Tawang, plus a play from Israel

It's that time of the year when, sandwiched between the bright colours of Dussehra and the brighter lights of Diwali, Delhi plays host to one of its most elegant cultural events — the IIC Experience, which kicks off on October 16. The city's intelligentsia forms the audience, as critically acclaimed artists or unknown art forms move to the platforms on the lawns.

Sure, it is festive season in the Capital, from food festivals to theatre weekends, from classical soirees to art shows, but rarely does an event combine them all. If it's the "diversity of art forms" that theatreperson MK Raina enjoys, it's the beauty of it all that makes Sadia Dehlvi a part of the IIC Experience this time.

The IIC Experience turns five this year, but the celebrations have been dimmed by terror and tragedy. "The spectacular diya illumination on the lawns will be restricted to the inaugural and concluding days rather than being a daily feature," says Premola Ghose of the India International Centre. Most events, as usual, will be held in the open air, with white tents flapping in the autumn breeze.

Setting the tone for things to come, the opening act will be a procession by masked dancers from the Monpa community of Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh. Kumudini Lakhia will follow with her Kathak composition. Dance and music performances are peppered through the week — from Ulhas Kashalkar's morning ragas and Rajasthani folk tunes by the Langa and Manganiyar communities to Swiss performer Eliana Burki's dexterity on the alphorn.

Burki will have company in other international performers. "This year will see the largest number of foreign artists," says Ghose. From Hungary comes the famous gypsy band Parno Graszt, while Israeli theatreperson Ruth Kanner will present her award-winning play Alternating Perspectives. Raina's critically acclaimed Stay Yet Awhile will also be staged. If you missed its first show in Delhi in January, be there on the last day of the festival. "The play is more a documentary drama about the intellectual relationship between Mahatma Gandhi and Rabindranath Tagore. Based on a book called The Mahatma and the Poet, the play shows how the two great men were at loggerheads about everything, but had mutual respect," says Raina.

It isn't high-brow and serious all the way. The daily film festival is all comedies and thrillers, while the food festival will feature a cuisine every day. Dehlvi will be presenting Delhi Ka Dastarkhana on the first evening, with shab degh, a Mughal dish which has mincemeat balls cooked with turnips and an assortment of spices, biryani and an array of vegetarian delights.

The IIC Experience will be held from October 16 to 22, from 10 am to 9 pm on most days. Entry is free.

Contact: 24624044

Heading: Flashback Canvas - Indian Express
Content:
Duleep Singh, the last maharaja of Punjab, comes alive, along with a host of other forgotten people in Navtej Sarna's new novel The Exile (Penguin, Rs 450). On the eve of its launch, Sarna says that he first heard of the maharaja from his mother, nearly 40 years ago. But it wasn't till 2000 that he started reading extensively about the history of the British Annexation of the Punjab.

"Here is a man whose life was such a calculated exercise by the British — a childhood beginning with the loss of his kingdom, his realisation of the treatment meted out to him by the British who had promised to take care of him and his urgent need to return to his land and his people. I wanted to tell the story of this man and the Sikh people, to give voice to characters who've been nothing but a footnote in history books," says Sarna, who believes that there is no objective truth, as history is usually written by those in power to suppress the truth of those who aren't.

The challenge, Sarna says, was in striking a balance between facts and the human dimensions that he wanted to portray in the novel. "When I began writing in 2003, I knew that a third-person narrative would not work, neither would a non-fictional genre. A novel seemed to be the best way to tell this story," says Sarna. It is told in Duleep Singh's voice and that of four others in such a way that each personal tale adds to the story of Duleep Singh and the history of Punjab. It also contains an unsparing examination of British imperialism as well as the greed of the Indian princes that fed it. "The story in essence, is about loss, about being separated from something that is rightfully yours. The exile is not only from geographical locations, it is about the exile within oneself," says Sarna.

Heading: Direct to Home - Indian Express
Content:
They stood on two sides of the political spectrum, but between themselves, Hungarian artists Sándor Bortnyik and Endre Bálint embraced the main art trends of the 20th century — cubism, expressionism, constructivism and surrealism. An ongoing exhibition of their prints at the Hungarian Cultural Centre, thus, provides a glimpse into the European art history of the last century.

Bortnyik, who died in 1976, pushed forward the avant-garde movement of the early 1920s and the exhibition shows how he represented his subjects — a railway station or a group of people — from multiple perspectives through geometrical figures. Bortnyik was a left-wing artist, quite close to Socialist Realism movement, and there is a small black-and-white portrait of Lenin to remind you of that.

Diametrically opposing his geometrical figures is Bálint's surrealistic style. "Bálint's prints are a total denial of the communist aesthetics of those days," said Imre Lázár, director of the Hungarian Cultural Centre. His macabre collages denounced the Soviet system that ruled Hungary after World War II. The influences of Sigmund Freud's theory of the subconscious are evident in his surrealistic works that depict ideas such as death, fear and torture in a rather surprising way. Nuclear Cross, for instance, features the smoke of a nuclear blast with a fork and a knife in the middle. "There cannot be only one interpretation," says Lazar.

The exhibition is on till November 7

Heading: Metro Cash & Carry gets licence to do business, cannot touch retail - Indian Express
Content:
An outbreak of viral pneumonia and doctors going on festival leave en masse combined to result in the death of 25 infants at the government-run Berhampore Sadar Hospital last week, senior medical officers in Murshidabad said on Friday.

During the four days, from Eid on October 2 to the commencement of the pujas on October 5, several infants admitted to the hospital died, prompting protests from their families and political leaders. Incidentally, Jangipur area of Murshidabad is the parliamentary constituency of External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee and all three MPs from the district belong to the Congress.

Dr Bhaskar Samanta, superintendent of District Hospital, Murshidabad, told The Indian Express: "There was an outbreak of viral pneumonia in the area. The sudden rush over the pre-festival weekend caught the hospital staff unawares. The paediatrics ward of the Sadar Hospital has only 25 beds but on October 4, 64 cases had come in."

He added: "Some doctors were yet to return from Eid leave then. All the doctors were called urgently and are on duty now. Though we have only five paediatricians, we have put up two additional wards, increasing the beds to around 100." Samanta added that most of the cases were referred from primary health centres of interior areas of the district. "Most of the children were cases of premature birth. They were underweight and undernourished, which made them prone to infection. Their condition was serious when they were brought to the hospital, many of them from far flung areas. Nineteen children died in two days at the hospital."

Berhampore MP and Congress leader Adhir Chowdhury said: "The Sadar Hospital operates out of a building that has been declared non-usable by the local municipality. The infrastructure is terrible and there are no facilities for mothers. Doctors told me it's impossible for them to operate in such conditions."

He added: "We have been demanding that the newly-constructed district hospital and the Sadar Hospital be brought under one roof to streamline medical care but the government is more interested in fighting for the Tatas."

Chowdhury also said: "Local MPs had offered to provide facilities in the hospital out of their MPLADS funds but the municipality and district administration showed little interest. The Centre is providing aid but there is no sign of progress."

Murshidabad District Magistrate Pervez Ahmed Siddiqui said the situation was under control now and no inquiry has been ordered into the incident.

"The government has its limitations. No death has been reported since October 6. We have procured medicines from the open market and increased the number of oxygen cylinders," he added.

Heading: Encephalitis claims a life in Kolkata - Indian Express
Content:
With Nano having set back West Bengal's industrialisation by a few paces, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee got some reprieve on Friday when his so-far stubborn colleagues in the Forward Bloc issued a fresh trade licence to German wholesale major Metro Cash & Carry to continue business in the state.

The state's Agriculture Marketing Board, controlled by the Forward Bloc, handed out the trade licence within deadline — October 10 — though government offices were closed because of Durga Puja. The licence will be valid till March 2009.

The permit came after the state government signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the German firm, which says the company can sell commodities to only those who have a trade licence. The MoU also specifies Metro can do business on agro-products with those who have an Agriculture Produce Marketing Committee (APMC) licence like it. The company cannot enter into direct or indirect retail business or opt for contract farming, the memorandum states.

The Bloc also climbed down from its earlier stand that the German firm cannot do business below a ceiling of Rs 5,000. The new agreement puts the minimum billing limit to Rs 1,000. However, the agriculture board imposed a one per cent market fee on both the sale and purchase of every commodity.

The Forward Bloc had a serious stand-off with the chief minister on the stipulations that would decide business norms for Metro Cash & Carry. The Bloc had also threatened to withdraw its ministers from the Cabinet. However, nerves were calmed at a Left Front committee meeting.

Chairman of the marketing board Naren Chatterjee said on Friday: "We have made it clear that Metro will not enter the retail business. We have also ensured they cannot go for contract farming."

The company's officials said they would start operations within six to eight weeks. A member of the company's executive board of directors in India, Frits Van Peski, said: "We are delighted to be given the licence. We shall cater to business establishments like hotels, restaurants, caterers, kirana shops and the like. We believe our trained staff of 350 will be able to serve the interests of the people here."

Metro Cash & Carry had readied long ago its operational space of nearly 100,000 sq ft on EM Bypass — at an investment of Rs 140 crore. The project got delayed due to disputes between the state government and land owners.

It was granted a licence to trade in APMC commodities in 2005, which was subsequently renewed twice in 2006 and 2007 and was valid till March 2008. However, in June 2007, the licence was unilaterally withdrawn by APMC authorities.

Heading: Spruced Almighty - Indian Express
Content:
After several deaths caused by dengue and malignant malaria in the city, Japanese Encephalitis (JE) claimed one life, adding to the death toll of vector-borne diseases in Kolkata.

Pralay Choudhury (34), a resident of 87 Sabarna Para Road, died on Thursday at the School of Tropical Medicine (STM). Locals and relatives of the deceased blamed the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) and the STM for not taking adequate measures to save his life.

Ajay Chatterjee, a relative of Choudhury, said: "He was suffering since July. Initially, he was admitted to a private nursing home and then shifted to the SSKM Hospital. There he was treated as a patient of enteric disease."

He added: "His blood sample was collected as late as on August 27 and sent to the STM. But we received the report on September 20. In the meantime his condition had worsened."

After being diagnosed as a patient of JE in the report, Choudhury was taken to the Assembly of God Church Hospital but when his condition started deteriorating, the authorities discharged him, stating that his condition had become too critical to be treated at the hospital.

He was rushed to the STM but he could not be admitted there because no bed was vacant in the school. He finally got admission after local councillor Shyamadas Roy and KMC chairman Nirmal Mukherjee intervened in the case.

Locals complained that no anti-larval measure has been carried out in the area. Roy said: "Chodhury had not gone outside the city in the last eight years. So there is no possibility that he caught the infection outside. He was infected in the city. The civic body should give special attention to the area but nothing has been done yet."

Heading: Bye Bye Maa Durga... - Indian Express
Content:
Film: Hello
Direction: Atul Agnihotri
Cast: Sharman Joshi, Gul Panag, Sohail Khan, Amrita Arora, Eesha Koppikar, Sharat Saxena, Dalip Tahil, Suresh Menon
Rating: *****
Running at: Inox (Forum, City Centre, Swabhumi)
And who said Indian Gods still sit amid annoying boring white clouds and ogle at dancers in ill-fitting golden bustiers? And who said they have to take mostly hybrid shapes still, to straighten things out on Earth. Welcome to the Gen Y God — who makes a call, and sorts out everything from a confused girlfriend, errant husband, to a hostile son and slumping careers in a jiffy. And Hello, for those who have not read Chetan Bhagat's bestseller, is the story of a bunch of call centre executives dealing with problems like the mentioned, until there's a call from God…

Atul Agnihotri, for starters, had a tolerable story in hand that he knew had gone down well with a generation high on popular fiction/cinema/media. So, the task in hand was casting and a screenplay. As for the first, he had a showstopper in Sharman Joshi as a slightly egoistic, subtle and cool headed Shyam. Sohail Khan, as the funky, jovial Varun comes second in order of performance. The rest of the cast, Eesha Koppikar (as an obsessed aspiring model), Amrita Arora (as a simpering devoted wife), Gul Panag (as a temperamental, haughty girl running away from marriage) and Sharat Saxena (as a pining grandfather) are above average.

The screenplay, credited to Agnihotri and Bhagat, is not brilliant but also not lacklustre. The film doesn't lose sight of pace and the dialogues are crisp in intervals.

However, what the film did not need were the jarring bhangra-meets-electronica songs that drop in at the weirdest junctures possible. Salman Khan's opening song is completely without bang and he seriously needs to reconsider his physique which looks straight out of grainy 80's WWF playing cards compared to the fitness levels set by Bollywood today.

Which brings us back to Sharman Joshi. Who can do without ripping off his shirt, gyrating to inane songs. And still be a show-stealer. It's amazing how one score emotions flit across his face with complete ease, completely in tune with the demands of the scene. It's a pity that Bollywood uses so little of him.

P.S. If God was who he/she was in the film, what would happen to pure Hindi first and atheism then?

Heading: Sialkot Stallions to play in Champions League T20 - Indian Express
Content:
... asche bochor abar hobe. Till then Kolkata can keep herself occupied with a host of other distractions

So the party is over. The ghats of Shobhabazar are abuzz with bhashan crowds. Maa Durga has been smeared with sindoor, fed with sweets and the auspicious pan. While many Puja associations of the city will obstinately cling on to the idol for as many days possible, the more traditional ones' have already bid her goodbye. But ask any Bengali by heart and he or she will tell you that there is something vaguely embarrassing about the sight of a Durga pratima in a pandal post Dashami. Like a child pretending that it's his birthday everyday.

Which is why, it's best to let go. No matter how hard it is to shake off the Puja hangover, it's time to smell the coffee. So we urge you to stop romanticising empty pandals and the symbolic diyas, and look forward to other, somewhat-neglected events that makes the Kolkata calendar.

Big releases
If you want to escape reality, do what the wise men have always advised you to do, rush to the nearest multiplex. And sink back in your richly upholstered seat while an over-the-hill Salman Khan tries to pull off another shirtless act (Hello). Or Vin Diesel's last-ditch effort to a Hollywood career (Babylon AD). If both these films don't seem inspiring enough, then you have a host of biggies to look forward to in the coming months. The Diwali releases this year include Madhur Bandekar's "unflinching" take on the fashion industry, innovatively titled Fashion (Priyanka Chopra, Kangana Ranaut), and the multi-starrer Gol Maal Returns (Ajay Devgan, Kareena Kapoor, Arshad Warsi). The other big releases include Subhash Ghai's Yuvraaj (Salman Khan, Katrina Kaif) and Karan Johar's Dostana (Abhishek Bachchan, Priyanka Chopra, John Abraham). Hollywood beckons you with the long awaited Russell Crowe-Leonardo Di Caprio starrer Body of Lies.

Kali Puja, Diwali and others
Baro mashe tero parbon (13 festivals in 12 months). Need we say more? Yes, drawing alpona in Lakshmi Puja, after the grand celebrations of Durga Puja, may seem a wee bit tame, but there is always Kali Puja. Clubbed together with Diwali, this festival is one of the most dazzling festivals of them all. If you haven't already burnt a hole in your pocket with all the puja shopping, then you can indulge yourself with some more retail therapy. After all, the shopping malls and departmental stores insists that you should.

Christmas
If there is any other festival that rivals the gaiety of Durga Puja in Kolkata, it has to be Christmas. A decked up Park Street, piles of plum cakes and ridiculously scraggly Christmas trees in almost every Kolkata household — Kolkata sure knows how to embrace the yuletide spirit. If two and a half months' wait seems too long, then look at it this way, Christmas means winter, winter means a new wardrobe, wardrobe means shopping.

Heading: Delhi calling: Manoranjan all set to coach Hindustan Football Club - Indian Express
Content:
Chairman of the Champions League Twenty20 and BCCI vice-president Lalit Modi today announced that Sialkot Stallions, Pakistan's newly-crowned Twenty20 champions, will be part of this year's Champions Twenty20 League. Sialkot, led by Shoaib Malik, notched up a narrow seven-wicket victory in the final over Shahid Afridi's Karachi Dolphins at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore on Wednesday.

"The participation of Sialkot Stallions in the inaugural Champions Twenty20 League makes the tournament complete in all respects.

"We are very happy to have Sialkot Stallions among the participating teams. The Pakistani team, led by Shoaib Malik, will make the inaugural Champions League Twenty20 more competitive and interesting," Modi said.

Sialkot Stallions will join two teams each from India, Australia and South Africa and England's Middlesex in the eight-team competition.

The teams are, Rajasthan Royals and Chennai Super Kings (India), Western Australia Warriors and Victoria Bushrangers (Australia), Titans and Dolphins (South Africa), Sialkot Stallions (Pakistan) and Middlesex (England).

The ten-day inaugural tournament will be played in Mumbai, Chennai and Bangalore from December 3 to 10.

The Champions League Twenty20 is a new concept in cricket and is aimed at producing more players capable of competing at the highest level.

The Champions League Twenty20's mission will be to promote and develop cricket from the grassroots level upwards and promote the spirit of cricket among all the players and participating teams.

Heading: Now or never for Mohun Bagan - Indian Express
Content:
Kolkata snubbed him as a failure. Delhi extends a warm welcome.

If everything goes to plans, former East Bengal coach Manoranjan Bhattacharya will take charge of the Hindustan Football Club of Delhi this month.

"I had a talk with them. Though I haven't decided yet, it's likely that I will try my luck there," Bhattacharya told The Indian Express today.

The former India international had a failed campaign with East Bengal in the Kolkata league. He was basically forced to resign as Stanley Rozario was appointed before the start of the I-League.

But why Delhi? "It's always better to be attached with the game rather then cooling the heels. This club has a professional approach. They are aiming to get an entry to the second division of the I-League. I think it's worth taking a chance," Bhattacharya said.

Bhattacharya had helped the red-and-golds stave off the relegation blues in the last year's I-League. But things went haywire since the start of this season. After the loss against Chirag United in the Kolkata league, Bhattacharya was made the scapegoat and had to face the fans' ire. It prompted him to put in his papers.

With the Delhi club, his initial contract is for four months. If the club qualifies for the second division of the I-League, it could be extended.

Hindustan FC is one of the oldest clubs in Delhi that was formed in 1948. It has produced some very exciting talents like Sunil Chhetri.

It's not very common for the Kolkata coaches to pursue a career outside Bengal. Amal Dutta was an exception. Subhas Bhowmick is now in charge of Salgaocar. Bhattacharya will add to the list.

Heading: IIT-Kharagpur study shows new pill for diabetes, cholestrol: yoga - Indian Express
Content:
It's now or never for Mohun Bagan. If the green-and-maroons want to keep their title hopes alive, they have to win against Sporting Clube de Goa in the I-League third round match at Margao tomorrow.

It's going to be very difficult though. Sporting are on a high after two successive wins over Vasco Sports Club and Mohammedan Sporting. Bagan, on the other hand, have only one point after two home matches. They lost to Mumbai FC and drew against Air India.

Though there is still a lot to be played for, it will be almost an improbable task for the Kolkata giants should they falter tomorrow.

Injury is a huge cause of concern for Bagan. Baichung Bhutia is yet to recover from a calf muscle strain. Without him, Bagan attack loses venom. Jose Barreto is not a force any more. So, the Kolkata league champions will start as underdogs.

Coach Karim Bencherifa, however, put up a brave face. "We had a decent start as our team performed well but were unlucky as we missed good scoring chances.

"We have worked out on our mistakes and hopefully the team will perform to its potential and come out winners to set the clock moving," he said on the match eve. The coach is under pressure.

That Dipak Mondal and Habibur Rahaman will return to strengthen the defence is good news. But without a play-maker, attacks don't get shape. The onus is on Lalkamal Bhowmick to fill the vacuum.

Sporting midfield has gelled very well. Harmanjot Khabra, Micky Fernandes, Wilton Gomes and Joseph Pereira have combined like a well-oiled machine. Pereira's partnership with Gomes on the left has resulted in teasing crosses that kept the rival defence guessing.

Then there is Junior Obagbemiro upfront who has already scored three goals. Another Nigerian, Natalin is likely to make his debut tomorrow.

Sporting defence is yet to concede a goal in this tournament. Naturally, their coach Vishwas Goaunkar is confident of maintaining the winning streak.

"After our impressive performance against Mohammedan Sporting, we are on a high.

"We want to keep the momentum going. The boys have the potential to perform even better. Natalin will give more sharpness to our attack," he said.

Time for Bagan to pull up their socks.

Heading: Three die in train accidents - Indian Express
Content:
A study conducted by the Indian Institute of Technology-Kharagpur has found that yoga has the ability to lower blood sugar levels and cholesterol barely three weeks after taking to the exercise mat.

The School of Medical Science and Technology (SMST) conducted medical tests on 60 people belonging to various age groups between July 18 and August 12 — the same time period within which these people practised yoga each morning. The study showed that after the yoga classes were over, blood sugar levels showed a considerable drop in 30 per cent cases of diabetes, while in 60 per cent cases a decrease in cholesterol was reported.

Eight teachers taught yoga to the participants in the presence of IIT-K professors. All participants underwent medical tests, including blood sugar levels, triglycerides and cholesterol, before July 18. The same tests were conducted after the classes were over in August.

SMST Director Professor A K Roy said: "Though we are still analysing the results and a conclusive report is expected soon, there have been improvements in various medical parameters of the participants."

Almost all participants claimed that the yoga session has alleviated pain in various parts of their bodies, he added. "We taught only basic yoga exercises to the participants since they had no previous exposure to yoga. For the first 15 days, we followed preliminary exercises and for the next seven days we moved to the next level," said Kallol Roy, the state in-charge of the Patanjali Yog Peeth, West Bengal.

Participants performed pranayam and other neuro-motor exercises along with yogasanas like mayurasana, mukundasana, bhujangasana and makarasana.

Some participants also showed other improvements. "Before the session, a woman had a 5-cm fibroid in her ovary; after 21 days of yoga, it reduced to 2 cm," said Roy.

Heading: 3 arrested for poaching - Indian Express
Content:
Three persons died in separate train accidents in North 24 Parganas on Thursday.

All the accidents occurred between Titagarh and Barrackpore stations, Railway police said.

Shipra Chandra (38), a resident of Karimpur in Nadia, was mowed down by a Ranaghat local while she was crossing the tracks at a level crossing.

In another accident, 21-year-old Subodh Hela was electrocuted when she came in contact with an electricity pole along the tracks. She was travelling in an overcrowded train.

The third person, Rabindrananth Dey (26) of Titagarh, was crushed by a fast-moving train.

The police said that Dey might have committed suicide.

Railway police sources said that all the cases were being investigated.

Heading: Clean Ganga after immersion, courtesy NGOs, civic body - Indian Express
Content:
Three persons have been arrested in connection with the recent poaching of a tiger in the Sunderbans. Atanu Raha, Principal Chief Conservator of Forests and Director of Sunderbans Biosphere Reserve, said: "The case has been handed over to the CID. Three persons were arrested on Friday and investigation is on." The CID, however, denied the arrests. Inspector General CID Sanjay Mukherjee said: "We do not have any information on arrests. A team, led by a senior IPS officer, had visited the area on October 8. We got a few leads and are still on the lookout for more clues."

The Wildlife Protection Act provides that a poacher could be jailed for up to seven years and a fine of Rs 25,000 can be imposed on him. The carcass of an adult tiger was spotted in the Bidya river in Gosaba area of Sunderbans on Monday by tourists, who immediately informed the forest officials.

On Tuesday, a postmortem was conducted on the big cat that revealed that it had two bullet injuries on its body — in the head and neck. The one that hit the head passed through the brain, causing haemorrhage and killing the animal instantly.

Field Director of the Sunderbans Tiger Reserve Niraj Singhal said, " It is likely that the tiger was killed 72 hours ago between October 4 to 6." The postmortem report also said the bullets were fired from country-made revolvers. However, no part of the carcass was missing. The skin and claws of the tiger, which fetch good money in the international market, were intact. The case was then handed over to the CID for investigation after the Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee expressed concern over the incident.

Heading: Docs on leave, 25 babies die at Behrampore Hospital - Indian Express
Content:
A clean Ganga after Dashami has always been a distant dream. But this year, there are reasons for concerned citizens to smile, as environment watchdogs of the city have been successful in bringing down the pollution levels of the Ganga.

The level of dissolved oxygen in the water has gone up to 3.8 mg/L from 2.5 mg/L last year. Though a far cry from the level required to make it possible for flora and fauna to survive, city officials and NGOs feel it is at least a start to curb pollution during immersion.

With the recent High Court order against throwing used flowers into the water during immersion and using toxic-free paints on the idols, the river this year seems to have got a respite from the chemicals that pollute the waters.

This time, however, it is not only the NGOs but also the KMC authorities who have ensured a cleaner Ganga.

With KMC officials posted at most city ghats, from Babughat to Ratanghat and Baghbazar Ghat, and restricting the number of people during the immersion, the ghats present a cleaner picture.

Vats have also been placed for flowers, frames and incense sticks. The civic body has deployed temporary volunteers, while the Kolkata police have deployed its personnel to help keep the ghats clean.

"There has definitely been an improvement in the efforts to clean the river, which is visible this year. Although the level of dissolved oxygen in water should ideally be 7 mg/L, it is 3.8 this year, which is an improvement," said Sudeepta Bhattacharjee of SAVE, an NGO working for the cause.

"Another important factor was that many of the award committees had announced they would give more points to the Pujas which were environment-friendly," he said.

Subhash Datta, environmentalist, also spoke on the same lines. "With the Puja organisers curbing the use of paints, there has been a change in the pollution levels in the water. With big budget Pujas, including that in FD-Block in Salt Lake, doing a good job, things are better now."

While the river may still be far from being clean, with the level of oil and grease particles reaching a level of 10, while the permissible limit is 5.1, and suspended solid particles 4,197 when the permissible limit is 100, both Datta and Bhattacharjee credit a cleaner Puja due to efforts made by NGOs and the KMC.

Mayor Bikash Bhattacharya confirmed that with KMC officials posted at 18 ghats, there has been a cleaner immersion this year.

"After the immersions we will collect all waste materials and remnants of the idols to make sure they do not pollute the water further," said the Mayor.

Kolkata police have also beefed up security at the ghats. Bajaghat and Kadamtala Ghat have been provided with tight security. A bomb disposal squad has already surveyed surrounding areas.

Habibur Rehman, a Kolkata Police officer, said: "There are enough security personnel deployed at the ghats. The immersion ceremony started off yesterday and will continue till tomorrow. There will be a huge rush of idols on Friday."

Meanwhile, tourists from Canada, Europe, and America have thronged the city to witness the grand festival.

They were seen at the ghats taking photographs while enjoying their holiday in Kolkata.

Rendian Miller, who has come from the USA to Kolkata for the first time during Durga Puja, said: "I have never seen this in my life."

On the immersion ceremony, he said, "People are dancing and singing all the way. It is fantastic."

Content:
With Nano having set back West Bengal's industrialisation by a few paces, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee got some reprieve on Friday when his so-far stubborn colleagues in the Forward Bloc issued a fresh trade licence to German wholesale major Metro Cash & Carry to continue business in the state.

The state's Agriculture Marketing Board, controlled by the Forward Bloc, handed out the trade licence within deadline — October 10 — though government offices were closed because of Durga Puja. The licence will be valid till March 2009.

The permit came after the state government signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the German firm, which says the company can sell commodities to only those who have a trade licence. The MoU also specifies Metro can do business on agro-products with those who have an Agriculture Produce Marketing Committee (APMC) licence like it. The company cannot enter into direct or indirect retail business or opt for contract farming, the memorandum states.

The Bloc also climbed down from its earlier stand that the German firm cannot do business below a ceiling of Rs 5,000. The new agreement puts the minimum billing limit to Rs 1,000. However, the agriculture board imposed a one per cent market fee on both the sale and purchase of every commodity.

The Forward Bloc had a serious stand-off with the chief minister on the stipulations that would decide business norms for Metro Cash & Carry. The Bloc had also threatened to withdraw its ministers from the Cabinet. However, nerves were calmed at a Left Front committee meeting.

Chairman of the marketing board Naren Chatterjee said on Friday: "We have made it clear that Metro will not enter the retail business. We have also ensured they cannot go for contract farming."

The company's officials said they would start operations within six to eight weeks. A member of the company's executive board of directors in India, Frits Van Peski, said: "We are delighted to be given the licence. We shall cater to business establishments like hotels, restaurants, caterers, kirana shops and the like. We believe our trained staff of 350 will be able to serve the interests of the people here."

Metro Cash & Carry had readied long ago its operational space of nearly 100,000 sq ft on EM Bypass — at an investment of Rs 140 crore. The project got delayed due to disputes between the state government and land owners.

It was granted a licence to trade in APMC commodities in 2005, which was subsequently renewed twice in 2006 and 2007 and was valid till March 2008. However, in June 2007, the licence was unilaterally withdrawn by APMC authorities.

Heading: Nano exit makes local firms jittery,hope for call from Sanand - Indian Express
Content:
With renewed tension between the CPM and the Trinamool in Block II of Khejuri, the area has caught the political and administrative attention. A recent report submitted by the Intelligence Bureau to the Centre says that political violence in Khejuri could spill over to neighbouring Nandigram before the Lok Sabha elections.

Two CPM supporters were admitted in the Tamluk hospital on Wednesday, after they sustained injuries during clashes with Trinamool members. They were attacked with sharp weapons in Changramari village of Khejuri Block II, right next to Nandigram. Intelligence agencies that have been following the developments in Nandigram and Khejuri during the last two years are apprehensive that there may be a spurt in violence in the area before the Lok Sabha polls.

An officer of Central IB said: "Our report says that the two political parties are becoming increasingly violent and it may affect situation in Nandigram."

The CPM has both the Lok Sabha seats in East Midnapore— Contai and Tamluk. The Contai constituency has seven Assembly constituencies - Ramnagar, Bhagabanpur, Egra, Contai South, Contai North, Khejuri and Mugberia. Among these, the Trinamool had wrested two seats from the Left in the last Assembly elections.

A local Trinamool leader said, "The focus is now on the Khejuri Assembly seat." At present, the CPM holds the seat, which comprises Khejuri I and II Blocks. Though the CPM continues to hold the panchayat samiti of Khajuri I Block, in Block II, the Trinamool won two of the five gram panchayats and the panchayat samiti from the CPM in the recent rural polls.

"This has made the CPM jittery and the Khejuri Assembly seat has become important for both the CPM and for us," said the Trinamool leader.

Politial analysts feel that the balance of the Contai constituency hinges on Khejuri. Police suspect there would be an increase in violence in the coming months. "There may be political violence in Khejuri Block II because the Trinamool has gained substantial ground, pushing the CPM on the back foot," said a police officer of the district.

Local CPM leader Himanshu Das said, "Trinamool cadres have been beating up our supporters and creating ruckus at the gram panchayat meetings." Trinamool leader Subhendu Adhikary said, "The CPM has been deliberately instigating the Trinamool supporters."

Absconding Nandigram troublemaker arrested
Thirty-five-year-old Naru Maity, a CPM worker accused of organising attacks on villagers of Nandigram, was arrested from an East Midnapore village on Thursday night, police said.

He was produced before the additional chief judicial magistrate's court at Contai and remanded to police custody till November 7.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) had arrested Maity along nine other people from Janani brickfield on March 17, 2007 — three days after the police firing in Nandigram that killed 14 people. A large cache of arms and ammunition were also seized from the brickfield.

The CBI then handed the arrested persons to Khejuri police and later the case was transferred to the CID. All of them were later released on bail after the CID failed to file a chargesheet against them.

In December 2007, the CBI moved a petition before the additional judicial magistrate court demanding the custody of the 10 arrested people for interrogation.

On April 30, this year, the court issued a warrant against them but the police failed to trace them.

On Thursday night, when Maity came to visit his home in Gonara village under Patashpur police station, locals came to know about it and they gheraoed his residence at midnight, said Asoke Prasad, Superintendent of Police (East Midnapore). Following this, police reached there and arrested him.

Heading: City’s real estate prices register a slump - Indian Express
Content:
The departure of Tata Motors from Singur has left small firms, which had purchased land very close to the small car factory to be a part of the vendor park, in a fix.

Till date, they have not received any official word from the Tatas about their relocation to Sanand in Gujarat, where the Nano car factory will be set up.

In such a situation, the owners of these firms are setting their eyes on the October 16 vendor meet in Pune.

"More than 95 per cent of our work had been completed at Singur. We will be attending the meet on October 16 and are hopeful that some modalities will be worked out regarding relocation and compensation," said Udayan Banerjee, Executive Director, Sharda Motor Industries Ltd.

Banerjee's company was supposed to supply exhausts, convertors and suspension to the Tata Motors plant, and they had leased seven acres of land at Singur.

Similar concerns were expressed by Endurance Technologies Pvt Ltd, which was supposed to supply aluminum castings for Nano.

"Till date we have received no official word from Tata Motors. We will definitely be moving with the Tatas but nothing has been finalized yet. The Pune meeting will possibly make things clearer," said Biswajit Choudhury, VP (marketing) of the firm.

Chairman of Tata Motors, Ratan Tata, is likely to address the vendors at the Pune meet. This will be the first national level vendor meet in the last two years.

Mayur Enterprise, which had leased 1.8 acres land at Singur and was supposed to supply sunwisers and bellows for the small car, plans to write a letter to West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) expressing its willingness to return the leased plot.

"Ideally we would like to get a refund. If not, we will see if any legal action can be taken," said Rajesh Gupta, managing director of Mayur Enterprise.

Heading: Singur farmers to meet Governor, demand Tata return - Indian Express
Content:
The real estate boom which had sent residential property rates sky-rocketing in the city and its suburbs last year has now reached a plateau.

In the last two quarters, Kolkata's residential market has registered a lower growth rate as compared to the previous year. In 2007, the sale of residential property had registered a growth of nearly 30 to 40 per cent which has dwindled by 10-15 per cent in 2008, claimed a mid-year market review of NK Realtors.

Though the overall sales growth rate has come down, the volume of sales has remained the same. This is because Kolkata is an end-user market and the bulk of the property bought by consumers is for use and not for investment, said experts.

The demand for residential property was mostly in the middle income group segment throughout the last two quarters and the demand for higher income group apartments have slowed down.

"It could be because the latter is seen more as an investment and there is a lot of speculation involved in it. The stock market slump could have had an influence. But the end-user market, mainly reflected by the demand for middle income group apartments, is still going strong," said Biswadeep Gupta, general manager, Eden Realty Ventures Private Limited.

Premium apartment prices in upcoming suburbs like Rajarhat are stagnant between Rs 2500 and Rs 3,500, which is almost at par with last year's level. In fact, property prices in New Town have risen by as little as 3 per cent.

In contrast, property prices in prime locations like Loudon Street, Queens Park, Ballygunge have seen the maximum rise. By the end of 2007, prices in these locations were in the range of Rs 7000- Rs 11,000 per square feet. This year, however, property prices reached Rs 10,000 to Rs 13,000 per square feet.

Heading: Maya will sit with clerics to discuss problems of Muslims - Indian Express
Content:
Singur farmers, who willingly gave up their land for the Nano project, and suppliers of raw material to the factory have decided to meet Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi on Monday.

Bijoy Mal, a member of the material suppliers' syndicate, said: "The Governor had intervened (in the Singur crisis) before. We will request him to intervene again and bring the Tatas back to Singur, if not for Nano than for some other project."

Though they do not have an appointment with the Governor, they are determined to come down to Kolkata to meet him. Sources at the Raj Bhavan said no appointment has been given so far to them.

"No one has approached us for any appointment. It is unlikely that the Governor can manage time at the last hour," said the source.

Mal, however, said nearly 5,000 people, including farmers, will meet the Governor. Many people gathered at the spot in Singur on Thursday evening where Banerjee had organised her dharna earlier. They set on fire effigies of Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee, Medha Patkar, activist Anuradha Talwar, local Trinamool MLA Rabindranath Bhattacharjee.

They also burst crackers to mark their protest against the pullout of the Tatas from Singur. Nearly 200 farmers and material suppliers are on an indefinite dharna at Sanapara near the Tata factory since Tuesday. "We want the Tatas to return," said Samir Dhal, a local farmer.

Heading: As killer weed ripens in Saharanpur, two children lose their lives, 7 fall ill - Indian Express
Content:
In an attempt to counter the Samajwadi Party, which is trying trying to strike a chord with Muslims by taking up the cause of youths facing terror charges, the ruling Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) is gearing up to organise a convention where the participants will discuss Problems of Muslim community in India, its causes and solutions".

The convention will be held in Lucknow on Monday where Chief Minister, Mayawati will be the chief guest.

Many prominent Muslim clerics have been invited to attend the convention. Among those expected to attend are All India Muslim Personal Law Board member Maulana Khalid Rashid Firangi Mahali, Muslim Personal Law Board member Maulana Hamidul Hasan, Imam of Lucknow's Tilewali Masjid Maulana Fazlur Rehman Nadawi and prominent Shia cleric Kalbe Javvad.

Ever since Delhi police busted an India Mujahideen module, which comprised youths from Azamgarh, police of different states have visited various parts of the Uttar Pradesh in search of suspects.

The SP has accused the state government of failing to protect youths of the minority community. It has also raised questions over the Jamia Nagar encounter and demanded a judicial inquiry.

BSP parliamentarian from Azamgarh Akbar Ahmed Dumpy's visit to Azamgarh to meet families of terror accused has not mollified other Muslims leader in his party, who are feeling uneasy over SP's renewed bid to consolidate Muslim support at a time when Lok Sabha elections are approaching.

"Interaction with the political and religious representatives of the Muslim community is a necessary step for the BSP to assess the situation that has emerged after SP's open support to the terror suspects. Mayawati will try to assuage their feelings by giving them a patient hearing," a BSP leader said.

Mayawati will also talk about the empowerment of Muslims and use the occasion to tell Muslim leaders about what her government had done for the welfare of the community, the leader said. She will try to project BSP as a different party where Muslim leaders do not hold symbolic positions but important assignments. The most obvious example is PWD Minister Naseemuddin Siddiqi.

But while projecting herself as a "benefactor of the Muslim community," Mayawati, however, will shun away from talk of special privileges for the community because the BSP does not want communal polarisation in the state, it is learnt.

Earlier, Mayawati had asked her MLAs not to intervene in issues related with terror suspects or criminals. 'The idea is to avoid the involvement of party MLAs in any controversy at the local level over the issue of terrorism," said a party source.

At the same time, she wants genuine concerns of the community be addressed. Two days ago, DGP Vikram Singh had issued circular asking police officers not to illegally detain any person in the name of "interrogation." He directed them to make an entry in the general diary whenever a person was detained.

Heading: Dacoit-turned-politician Seema Parihar joins SP - Indian Express
Content:
With the ripening of Kasaundi or Cassia occidentalis fruits — the killer weed — two children have already died and seven others are seriously ill in Saharanpur district after they allegedly consumed seeds of the plant. This has caused an alarm in the district administration.

Last year, as many as 48 children had died in the district after unsuspectingly eating the seeds of the weed. All the nine children who consumed the seeds last week are from Sangha Khera village. The experts had forewarned the state Health Department that the weed was poisonous and had caused the deaths of the children in the district. They had even said that it was not Japanese Encephalitis (JE) which was causing death in the district as considered by the administration. "Initially, we registered these cases as acute encephalitis syndrome as there were clinical similarities. However, when the blood tests did not confirm JE, we investigated the cases and found that all of them had eaten Kasaundi seeds," said Dr O P Singh, nodal officer for AES in Saharanpur.

Earlier this month, when the children fell ill, their parents tried some home remedies. "When a four-year-old girl and a five-year-old boy died on October 4 within two days of consuming the weed, the pradhan approached us and we brought all the children to the district hospital. Their condition is stable now," said Dr Usha Tomar, Chief Medical Officer of Saharanpur.

The Health Department has now begun awareness activities in the village and its adjoining area. "We have distributed pamphlets carrying picture of the weed and asking people not to eat it. Gram Pradhans are being educated, they are being asked to organise group meetings and tell the people about the danger from the weed," said Tomar.

The department has also submitted a proposal to the district administration for eradication of the weed under National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme.

Recently, during a high-level meeting in New Delhi called by the Director General of Health Services, Government of India, the issue of the killer weed was discussed. At the meeting, it was decided to give the task of conducting a multi-centric study on the weed to Indian Council for Medical Research (ICMR) in collaboration with the Indian Academy of Pediatrics (IAP).

"A study was done by the National Institute of Nutrition, Hyderabad, but it was not comprehensive. It was decided to give this task to ICMR and IAP," said Dr Vipin M Vashishtha, a member of the IAP.

Heading: Farmers lock horns over sugar price - Indian Express
Content:
Following the footsteps of bandit queen Phoolan Devi, dacoit-turned-politician Seema Parihar joined Samajwadi Party (SP) at a function in Aurraiya on Friday.

In 1997, Phoolan Devi had taken the membership of SP in a function at Numaeesh ground at Aurraiya. Eleven years later, Parihar chose the same venue to join SP in the presence of party president and former chief minister Mulayam Singh Yadav.

This is not the first attempt of Parihar to enter the political arena. In the 2002 Assembly elections, she had supported Shiv Sena. Later, she joined the Indian Justice Party and contested the Lok Sabha election from Bhadohi in 2004.

On January 10, 2008, she joined the Lok Janshakti Party, and just 10 months later she crossed over to the SP. Parihar has also been a protagonist in the movie "Wounded", which was based on her journey from a simple village girl to a dacoit.

According to Parihar, the reason behind her changing parties was the growing disappointment with political leaders. "I have faith in the ideology of Samajwadi Party," she said.

Asked whether she will again contest the Lok Sabha elections, she said: "I have still not decided. At present, I am focussing on campaigning for the party in Aurraiya and the adjoining districts."

She added, "I will consider contesting the elections only if the party agrees to it." On Parihar's joining SP, Mulayam said, "Parihar had started her political career soon after her surrender, and there is no harm in her joining our party."

Former SP legislator from Aurraiya Kamlesh Pathak told The Indian Express, "Parihar wasn't a dacoit. At a tender age of 13, she was kidnapped by dacoit Lala Ram from her residence in Bavaeen village." He said that since her surrender, Parihar was not involved in any criminal activity. "We are not using Parihar as a star campaigner, but are portraying her as a woman of courage," added Pathak.

For 18 years, Parihar ruled the ravines of Chambal and had alleged killed 70 people and abducted over 200 people. In June 2000, she surrendered before the Aurraiya police. Named in 29 criminal cases, Parihar has been acquitted in 15 of them. At present, she has secured bail in the remaining 14 cases. Most of her pending cases are in the districts of Etawah, Aurraiya and Jalaun.

Heading: Girl found dead in Chitrakoot, human sacrifice suspected - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh government's efforts to evolve a consensus over the state advisory price (SAP) of sugarcane for the current cane crushing season have failed. While the farmers demanded that they will not accept less than Rs 160 per quintal, sugar industry representatives said they were not in a position to pay more then Rs 112 per quintal.

The state government had set up a committee to determine the SAP for the current cane-crushing season. The price is usually announced in the last week of October, ahead of Deepawali. 

On Friday, the core committee, headed by Chief Secretary Atul Gupta, invited the representatives of both the parties to discuss the matter.

Cane Commissioner Har Sharan Das, who is a member of the committee, said the committee would soon finalise its recommendation and submit a report to the government.

In the season 2007-08, the state government had fixed the SAP at Rs 125 per quintal. Private mills had challenged the rate fixed by the government in the Allahabad High Court. Later, the Supreme Court, while upholding the state government's right to determine the SAP, had fixed the interim price at Rs 110 per quintal.

The Uttar Pradesh Sugar Mills Association (UPSMA), a body of the private sugar mills, has consistently opposed the fixing of SAP by the government, holding it illegal and arbitrary. The body, however, favours the statutory minimum price (SMP), which is determined by the Centre. The SMP is always lower than the SAP; for the current season, the Centre has fixed the SMP at Rs 81.18 per quintal at 9 per cent recovery.Yogesh Dahiya of the Saharanpur District Cane Cooperative Union said the farmers of his district will not sell their produce to the mills at less then Rs 160 per quintal.

"The gur and khandsari units were already paying Rs 140 per quintal and the price of sugarcane in neighbouring Haryana and Punjab was Rs 160 per quintal. We are under no compulsion to sell sugarcane to the mills of UP," he said.

According to the cane department, the area under cane cultivation in 2007-08 was 28.50 lakh hectares, which has been reduced to 21.40 lakh hectare in the current season. Sugarcane production is estimated to be 1,200 lakh metric tonne in 2008-09, as against 1,600 lakh metric tonne in 2007-08. Hence, the sugar production target has been reduced by the department to 70 lakh metric tonne, against 1crore metric tonne in 2006-07 and 74 lakh metric tonne in 2007-08.

Heading: Allottees say no to LDA’s Nehru Enclave plot cancellation plan - Indian Express
Content:
A six-year-old girl was killed in an alleged witchcraft act in Nadin Kurmiyan under Rajapur police station in Chitrakoot district late on Wednesday night.

The police found the body of the girl in a pond and arrested five members of a family, including three women.

Kanchania, daughter of Chipka Gupta, had gone missing on Wednesday morning.

After a frantic search, her relatives informed the police who later found the girl's mutilated body in the nearby pond.

The cops also found vermillion, a lemon, half-burnt incense sticks and flowers near the body, suggesting that it could be a case of human sacrifice. The villagers alleged that a woman named Rania could be behind it, as she allegedly practised witchcraft.

At Rania's house, the police found material that looked similar to those found near the girl's body. Blood marks before deities were also spotted.

The police also recovered an axe from her house.

Family members of Rania, however, told the police that they had sacrificed a pig. But they failed to show its carcass.

The police then arrested the family members. The axe and blood samples have been sent for forensic tests.

Additional Superintendent of Police D P N Pandey, who visited the village, said, "It appears to be a case of witchcraft. The arrested persons are Rania, her son Kallu and his wife Nathia, another son Saddul and his wife Piyaria."

Angry villagers demanded that the accused be stoned to death in the open.

About a decade ago, two village boys had mysteriously disappeared and later their mutilated bodies were found.

Then too, the villagers suspected Rania, but the police failed to find any evidence against her, said village pradhan Prayagraj Singh.

Heading: Medical university to set up probe panel - Indian Express
Content:
For the second time in recent weeks, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) board on Monday decided to consider the proposal of canceling the allotment of 538 plots in Nehru Enclave.

While the LDA is ready to return the amount it had collected from the allottees, the allottees have said they will not accept the refund and

will stage a dharna near the LDA office.

The proposal was last tabled before the LDA on September 6, but a decision was deferred. The allottees had then given a memorandum to LDA officials, asking that they should be given possession of the plots or alternative plots in Gomti Nagar.  

LDA Vice-Chairman Mukesh Meshram confirmed that a proposal about Nehru Enclave is likely to be taken up in the board meeting. Anand Tiwari, a spokesman of the Nehru Enclave, Gomti Nagar Bhukhand Avantee Sangharsh Samiti said, "We are not going to accept refund from the LDA. It is the responsibility of LDA to give us possession of the plots."

"But before that we will meet LDA vice-chairman to request him one more time to either provide us possession of allotted plots or allot land of same size at some other place in Gomti Nagar," he added. 

The LDA had launched the Nehru Enclave scheme in 1991 and had planned to develop over 800 flats and offer 538 plots. It had completed the allotments before January 1993, when the Army claimed ownership of the land. Since then, the dispute has been pending in the High Court.

Subsequently, the LDA, came up with a proposal to refund the allottes money.

Heading: Alaska probe finds Palin 'abused her power' - Indian Express
Content:
An emergency meeting of executive council of the Chhatrapati Shahuji Maharaj Medical University (CSMMU)  has been called on October 14 to discuss the irregularities in admission process.

The irregularities recently came to surface when many candidates, who had left their Optical Mark Recognition(OMR) sheets blank in the entrance examinations, figured in the list of selected candidates for the courses of dental hygienists and dental mechanics.

The initial enquiry revealed the anomalies in the examination process, following which the university cancelled the exam and declared the new dates. CSMMU V-C Dr Saroj Chooramani Gopal said: "The emergency meeting has been called to form a disciplinary committee to conduct an inquiry and take action against the guilty."

Nearly 180 candidates had participated in the examinations in September and the results were declared the same month.

During the examination, an examiner had noticed that some candidates had left blank OMR sheets.

The examiner grew suspicious and took photographs of the sheets. It was found later that nine such candidates had made to the merit list.

The university is suspecting the role of an insider in the scam.

The CSMMU had already changed its examination controllers soon after the scam came to the limelight.

"We have decided the new examination dates and we assure that only deserving candidates would make it to the final list this time," said Gopal.

Heading: McCain urges supporters to respect Obama - Indian Express
Content:
Alaska Governor Sarah Palin, the running mate of John McCain, 'abused her power' in seeking to get her former brother-in-law fired as a state trooper, an ethics report has found, dealing a blow to the Republican Presidential nominee who is struggling to hold ground against Democrat rival Barack Obama.

44-year-old Palin 'knowingly permitted a situation to continue where impermissible pressure was placed on several subordinates in order to advance a personal agenda. To get Trooper Michael Wooten fired,' the 263-page state legislative investigative report said Friday night.

The investigation looked into Palin's sacking of Public Safety Commissioner Walter Monegan, who claimed that he was dismissed because he refused to bow to pressure to fire Wooten, who was involved in a bitter divorce and custody battle with the Governor's sister. Palin insists the firing was over a budget dispute.

The legislative panel, which authorised the investigation, released the report, but did not immediately vote whether to endorse its findings, The Boston Globe reported.

However, the report, which found that Palin violated the state's ethics law banning public officials from using their offices for personal gain, did not say whether Palin should be censured by the Legislature or whether the matter should be referred for criminal investigation, the paper reported.

As the November 4 Presidential race narrows, the report thrusts a new issue into the campaign when Palin's reputation as a reform-minded candidate is already being subjected to scrutiny. The Republicans may also face Democrats' attacks on the matter.

Heading: UN asks EU nations to curb sexual violence against women - Indian Express
Content:
Republican John McCain has called on his supporters to stop hurling abuse at Barack Obama at his rallies, saying he admired and respected his Democratic White House rival.

"We want to fight, and I will fight, but we will be respectful. I admire Senator Obama and his accomplishments and I will respect him," McCain told a Minnesota rally, as a new Newsweek poll gave his rival a 11-point lead nationally.

"I want everyone to be respectful and let's make sure we are, because that is the way that politics should be conducted in America," McCain said on Friday.

Crowds at the rallies of McCain and his running mate Sarah Palin have become increasing inflammatory shouting out "terrorist" and "liar" when Obama is mentioned. At one Florida rally, someone even shouted "kill him."

The US Secret Service said it was investigating the alleged death threat. "We take every threat very seriously. Every time we receive or are reported information like that, we follow up," said Secret Service spokesman Ed Donovan. Obama has also rebuked McCain for preaching a politics of "anger and division."

"In the last couple of days we have seen a barrage of nasty insinuations and attacks and I am sure we will see much more over the next 25 days," he said at a rally in Ohio.

"It's easy to rile up a crowd by stoking anger and division. But that is not what we need now in the United States, the times are too serious."

For the first time in a 'Newsweek' poll, Obama was given a double digit lead, with 52 per cent to 41 per cent for McCain, with voters saying the economy was their top concern.

The last poll by the magazine a month ago, before the economic crisis began to bit, had the two men tied on 46 per cent.

Heading: No reason for Pak to be apprehensive on N-deal: India - Indian Express
Content:
The United Nations Development Fund for Women (UNIFEM) has asked European Union (EU) states to take steps in preventing sexual violence against women in conflict and post-conflict situations.

"We are not here for another talking shop, where we lament the terrible and systematic nature of violence," UNIFEM Executive Director Ines Alberdi said at the "From Commitment to Action" meeting organised in collaboration with the European Commission on Friday.

"We look forward to supporting practical responses that ensure that sexual violence is no longer dismissed as an inevitable part of conflict," she said during the one-day event in Brussels. That meeting came on the heels of an EU-commissioned report which highlights gaps in providing security to women in war zones. Reviews of Security Council resolution which addresses the impact of war on women have also found serious failings in preventing of high levels of sexual violence, particularly in continuing conflicts, and in setting up security and justice systems to end impunity.

A joint UNIFEM and UN Department of Peacekeeping Operations (DPKO) conference in May found that UN and African Union (AU) peacekeeping missions' policies regarding prevention of attacks on women civilians have not been systematically implemented.
