The current risk aversion in the international financial markets to emerging market economies could, therefore, have some impact on the Indian corporate sector's ability to raise funds from international sources and thereby, impede some investment growth. PSUs have now become borrowers in the domestic market.

Corporates would, therefore, have to rely relatively more on domestic sources of financing, including bank credits, which in turn could pressure domestic interest rates, RBI Deputy Governor Rakesh Mohan said at the IMF-Financial Stability Forum meeting.

"Moreover, domestic primary capital market issuances have suffered in the current fiscal year so far in view of the sluggish stock market conditions. Thus, one can expect more demand for bank credit, while non-food credit growth has indeed accelerated in the current year," he said.

"This (risk aversion due to the crisis) could, in turn, put some upward pressure on domestic interest rates," Mohan said. Domestic investment is largely financed by domestic savings in India, but the corporate sector has in recent years mobilised significant resources from global financial markets for funding — both debt and non-debt — their ambitious investment plans, he said.

Several countries had recently cut interest rates to tackle the financial crisis. The RBI has cut CRR by 1.50 per cent to improve the liquidity.

Heading: Street theatre - Indian Express
Content:
ICICI Bank, India's second biggest bank, on Friday said the bank has enough liquidity and reiterated that it has never used rupee funds for its international growth initiatives. ICICI Bank shares, which plunged as much as 28 per cent to a four-year low on the bourses in the morning session, then made a partial recovery in the afternoon trade after the bank asserted it had adequate rupee liquidity. It finally closed with a loss of 19.71 per cent at Rs 364.10.

Chanda Kochhar, joint managing director & CFO, ICICI Bank, said, "The bank has adequate rupee liquidity in the context of the current environment. It also has liquidity of Rs 12,000 crore in its overseas subsidiaries. The bank has never used rupee funds for its international growth initiatives." "Our financial position continues to be strong, whether in form of net worth, capital adequacy ratio or current liquidity position," she said. Earlier in the day, a finance ministry official said the government did not see any problem with the bank.

Meanwhile, HDFC Bank overtook ICICI Bank as the second most-valued banking stock with a market cap of Rs 44,473 crore. ICICI's market cap fell to Rs 40,532 crore. SBI, the topper in the sector, has a market cap of Rs 85,845 crore. Significantly, ICICI's market cap is below its net worth (equity plus reserves) of Rs 46,471 crore, indicating that the stock is going cheap. On the other hand, HDFC Bank's net worth is only Rs 13,317 crore as per the financial results for the quarter ended June 2008.

Kochhar said the reduction in CRR is a welcome step given the current rupee liquidity conditions. "This should have a cooling effect on the market and ease liquidity," she said. ICICI is likely to get around Rs 4,000 crore from the RBI move to cut CRR and release Rs 60,000 into the system. ICICI Bank share price, which has lost 44 per cent since the mid-September Lehman Brothers' collapse, fell 27.8 per cent during the week. On the fall in market value, Kochhar told PTI that "the bank's market value is plummeting because the perception was getting destroyed by rumours."

Heading: Make it new - Indian Express
Content:
The way the financial crisis has been covered in the American mainstream media says something for that country's extreme fascination with Wall Street. Bankers, financial traders, the crash of the nineteen-thirties — these have always been popular themes in books and movies. But, in the nineteen-eighties, a trend emerged, of movies — popularly called 'yuppie movies' — that echoed a new yearning for money and entrepreneurial success in the Reagan era of tax reform and industry deregulation. Films like Risky Business, Working Girl, The Secret of My Success and Cocktail were typical, representative of the new ethos. But even more representative was the subgenre of movies about the investment banker, the stockbroker and the bond trader.

Oliver Stone's 1987 film, Wall Street, with Michael Douglas in the memorable role of the unscrupulous corporate raider Gordon Gekko and Charlie Sheen playing his ambitious understudy was probably the defining film of the decade. It released, coincidentally, the same year as Tom Wolfe's wildly successful novel, The Bonfire of the Vanities, which had as its central protagonist a New York bond trader called Sherman McCoy.

The dizzy world of high finance captivated audiences through the 1990s with books such as Liar's Poker and The Money Culture by the former insider Michael Lewis, Den of Thieves by the Pulitzer-winning James B. Stewart and Barbarians at the Gate: The Fall of RJR Nabisco from Bryan Burrough and John Helyar; the last was made into a film, to join such others as Rogue Trader. Television picked up the trend at the beginning of the decade with the racy 2000 entertainer, The $treet and the more recent reality show, Wall Street Warriors.

The trading room with its frenzied goings-on, the market, with its daily unpredictability, the manipulative strategies and cut-throat competition was an understandably exciting setting for dramatic narrative but the main attraction in this genre was and is clearly the figure of the Wall Street executive. Indeed, thanks to his rise to affluence in a speculation-friendly environment and his spectacularly extravagant lifestyle, the Wall Street trader (and his counterparts in the tower blocks of financial districts across the world) has become probably the most aspirational figure of the last three decades. 

Recent weeks however have seen this much-hyped figure not just fall but plummet from its stratospheric perch. Widely believed to be the cause of the current crisis in the US economy, the Wall Street trader has been at the receiving end of widespread condemnation. In America and the world over he is being described in the most derogatory terms possible — "greedy", "reckless", "irresponsible", "robber", "asset-stripper"— amidst calls for tightening controls and reining in speculation. From golden boy to effigy — is it time for the Wall Street trader to shed his mystique?  

Not quite. Despite the worldwide wave of revulsion against the suited trader, it does not necessarily follow that the Wall Street trader will lose his privileged position in the public imagination. To understand why one needs to consider how much, and in what manner, perceptions affect practice. To begin with, think of, for instance, how the stories in each of the books and films listed above played out.  

In Wall Street, Gordon Gekko and his accomplice get their come-uppance: Gekko loses a fortune on the market while the latter goes to jail. In Bonfire of the Vanities, Sherman McCoy the smug, self-centered prodigiously wealthy bond trader, after a dramatic encounter with life on the other side of the tracks, ends up losing everything he had. Lewis's books are a scorchingly critical account of his stint as a bond salesman for a Wall Street investment bank. Den of Thieves and Rogue Trader are about serious debacles involving flamboyant market players such as Ivan Boesky, Michael Milken and Nick Leeson.  

The point here is that American popular culture has always offered a perception of the post-1980s Wall Street banker/trader that is identical to that being voiced by angry protesters in the wake of the US crisis today. Americans, and the world at large have always viewed him as venal, covetous and lacking in social responsibility. But that has not dimmed interest in the figure, or his influence as a role model. 

The reason for this is perhaps because the trader's attractiveness is not based on values at all but on externals: the dark suit, the trophy girlfriend, the house in the country, luxury holidays and the much-envied look of eternal youth. Status symbols and the ability to acquire them with ease and speed is what makes him a redoubtable fantasy figure. The American public may be baying for his blood but this is the guy living out our dreams. Demolishing him won't be easy. That only happens in the movies.

Mumbai-based Shah is the author of 'Hype, Hypocrisy and Television in Urban India'express@expressindia.com

Heading: A different encounter - Indian Express
Content:
My parents asked me to return home to Kolkata for Pujo, but I refused. Other Bengalis in office took leave for four days, but I stayed put, and felt miserable. I began thinking of all the things I loved and missed about the Kolkata Pujo week.

By the time it's panchami, a huge pandal grows outside the walls of my Kolkata house, in the middle of a narrow street. Well — almost suddenly, if you have ignored the pounding and swearing of workers for the previous two months. Then, one day, you wake up to the sound of the dhaak. It is the most joyous sound in the world. But there are other sounds accompanying it as well: announcements for lost children/husbands/mother-in-laws. These go on through the night. Just when you think you're finally going to hit the sack, more out of exhaustion than anything else, a hoarse voice cries out for Babushona. Considering that some five million boys in Kolkata are named Babushona, Babushona stays missing for quite a while, till he is found. Then, there's another announcement — now, for his parents. My father called up to inform me that this year, there were fewer announcements. He thinks it's because mobile phones are very cheap now.

I also found myself missing everything about Pujo that I hated: the disastrous pujo fashion, the kids who eat everything while pandal hopping, the sweaty crowds, the giant wheel that stops for five minutes when somebody above your chair car gets sick, the shehnai music that whines at every pandal, and the pandals themselves. The funniest pandal I recall was the Titanic one in 1999. Durga and her children were stuck inside a doomed ship, along with dummies of Jack and Rose! I've decided to go back home for Pujo from now on, because you just can't take the Pujo out of a Bengali.

Shubho Bijoya!

Heading: Float, be liquid - Indian Express
Content:
It is not the first time that you have seen a beleaguered minority community go into a mood of complete denial. It happened with the Sikhs in the mid-eighties. There was widespread non-acceptance of the idea that the Bhindranwale phase, and the subsequent phase of terror, was indigenous, local, and mostly voluntary. For a long time, it was all blamed on Indira Gandhi's and Zail Singh's machinations. Bhindranwale was widely believed to be their creation. Initially, as his gunmen targeted policemen and leaders of the Nirankari sect, the dominant view within the Sikh community was that somehow this was part of a diabolical operation run by Indira Gandhi to embarrass the Akalis and give the Sikhs a bad name. Immediately thereafter, as hit squads began to pull Hindus out of buses and massacre them, or in one case shoot everybody inside a barber shop, most ordinary Sikhs you met told you, with genuine conviction, that there was no way a real Sikh could have done this. With Sikhs and Hindus, joined like fingers and nails, how is such a thing possible.

It was much later, around 1992-93 as armed terror bands began to hold sway over the countryside that the sad reality, inevitably, came to be accepted. Those running the terror campaign were "our own" and were doing a great disservice to the "qaum" and Punjab. From then on, it took just a few months for terror to wind up. I can never forget conversations with a large number of militants who had surrendered as their campaign ended and were kept on the Punjab Armed Police campus in Jalandhar. Many of them, still in their early 20s, answered to the ranks of "Lt-Gen" and "Maj-Gen". The story of one 21-year-old "Maj-Gen" was typical: "Until now people used to welcome us to their villages, even gave us food and shelter; now they began throwing us out, reporting us to the police."

This long preamble is no digression, or a session in storytelling. The Muslim community today is caught in shocked denial as well, particularly after the Jamia encounter and subsequent arrests in many states. It feels isolated, targeted, maligned and, above all, abandoned by the political class, particularly those it has always voted for. It has no leaders of its own to talk to and it no longer trusts those of the UPA, the political formulation closest to them. They feel victimised and see no hope. At the same time they do not believe even a fraction of the claims made by the police forces of six states and a union territory working in close coordination. Not only are they not willing to believe the story of the Jamia encounter, they believe the whole thing, the bombings, the arrests and "framing of young Muslim boys", is one giant conspiracy against them. Why the police forces of the Central government, Modi's Gujarat and Mayawati's Uttar Pradesh, among others, would join hands to hatch such a comprehensively diabolical conspiracy is not a question that is asked often.

On the specifics of the Jamia encounter, there are detailed answers to questions most commonly asked: why was Sharma not wearing a flak jacket, why was the bullet that killed him not found, how did two boys manage to escape from such a tight grip. These questions have been answered in a series of stories reconstructing the encounter in this paper earlier this week. Without repeating any of those details, here are two relevant points. Our policemen are no novices to the business of "encounters", such as they usually are. But one principle has been followed in all such "encounters", that nobody is taken alive. It is really suicidal to kill some people in an encounter and keep an eye-witness alive, as happened in this case. Second, if the whole thing was a fake encounter or a cover-up for a friendly fire death in a Keystone Cops operation, where was the need for the police to say that two suspects had escaped? Our encounter cops are by now far too experienced at this business to be so stupid with a cover-up.

But all these are matters of mere detail. The main reason for this denial, anger, frustration, the feeling of being cornered, comes from the fact that nobody had even held a conversation with them. Nobody, particularly from the Congress or the UPA, has ever tried to explain to them what happened. Nobody held out a hand of solace and comfort, to say that while terrorism has to be fought, we will never allow any profiling or isolation of 15 per cent fellow Indians, that while it is sad that these boys have been caught, they are a very, very, very minuscule minority and nobody would allow fingers to be raised at the entire community. It is hard enough for a minority to be told that some of its members may have been responsible for doing some of the most terrible things to their country. But it is cruel when the only people talking to them are the police, and that too mostly through TV channels.

You do not expect the BJP to go and do this communicating. But why has the Congress been so shy? It owes its power to the fact that Muslims and other minorities vote for it in states where it is seen as the main challenger to the BJP. Yes, Congress leaders say they are worried they may lose the Muslim vote. But are they more likely to retain it by themselves being in a state of denial? The inability, or the disinclination, of its senior leaders to hold an honest conversation with their own constituents is astounding. This is compounded by a few of them at the middle-level joining, instead, the insinuation-suspicion-denial group, driven partly by constituency pressure and partly by a strange every-man-for-himself mindset.

Similarities with the decades of trouble in Punjab should chasten anybody halfway complacent. Then, too, the political class had slunk back into silence, some out of cynical calculation, some fear, and some for lack of conviction; and for nearly a decade the Indian state talked to the people — Sikhs in this case — through the police. India, Punjab, Sikhs and Hindus all suffered as a result. The consequences of the political class leaving the Muslims to the same fate will be disastrous. Good, sincere politics must fill that dangerous vacuum.

Heading: Lassie come home - Indian Express
Content:
The Reserve Bank's decision to cut the cash reserve ratio (CRR) to 7.5 per cent from 9 per cent is a timely step in the right direction. The Indian banking system has been facing a liquidity shortage of more than Rs 60,000 crore every day. From mid-September onwards, Indian banks have been borrowing this amount on the repo market on a daily basis. This extreme tightness in liquidity was becoming chronic and needed to be addressed immediately as firms were faced with a huge liquidity crunch. The RBI has done well to take urgent and immediate action to reduce the CRR by 1.5 percentage points, releasing Rs 60,000 crore into the market from Saturday.

With growth in industrial production in India in August down to 1.3 per cent, the fear of a slowdown is greater than before. In addition to this is the impending recession in the global economy that is going to affect our exports and economy in the coming few quarters. In the face of this situation it is important for growth to be put on the front-burner. The RBI should continue on this path of easing liquidity and making sure that there is adequate liquidity in the system. One of the reasons for the recent shortage in liquidity has been the RBI's sale of dollars. A sale of $10 billion means that the RBI sucks out Rs 48,000 crore from the market. A cut in the CRR of 1 percentage point can

put back about Rs 40,000 crore into the system. In the coming weeks if the RBI continues to intervene in the currency market it should rapidly cut CRR rates down to 3 per cent, the statutory minimum.

The best policy now would be for the RBI to focus on providing enough liquidity to the market. The rupee should be allowed to float, that is, to find its own level. This would prevent monetary policy from being hijacked by the currency as it has been for many years now.

Domestic monetary policy requires today that liquidity should be eased. Manipulating the rupee, this time to prevent depreciation, conflicts with this objective of policy and the needs of the Indian economy. As other central banks in the world have done, at a time of a global liquidity crunch concerns about inflation need to take a backseat. That is not the biggest problem at the moment. Selling dollars to address the inflation issue is the wrong recipe because it makes the bigger problem — that is, the liquidity crunch — worse.

Heading: Dabwali tragedy: victims’ kin question posting of ‘guilty’ DC - Indian Express
Content:
After Sister Alphonsa, who will be declared the first woman Catholic saint from India on October 12 at the Vatican by Pope Benedict XVII, a dozen clergy from Kerala, God's Own Country, are going through the long-winding process of canonisation before being finally elevated to the altar of sainthood. Sister Alphonsa and a majority of others waiting in line for sainthood hail from central Kerala's Kottayam district.

Prominent among those who are a step closer to attaining sainthood is Elias Kuriankose Chavara. The priest was declared 'Blessed' along with Sister Alphonsa in 1986. Others in the category of the 'Blessed' are Sister Euphrasia, Sister Mariam Thresia Mankidiyan and Father Augustine Thevarparambil. A step below the 'Blessed' are the 'Servants of God'. Bishops Mathew Kavukattu, Thomas Kurialassery and Ivanios fall under this category, as do nuns Rani Maria and Celine. Priests Mathew Kadalikkattu, Joseph Vithayathil and Zacharias are the other 'servants of god' from the state.

Father Auralian, another candidate for sainthood, falls in the 'Venerable' category — a stage between the 'Blessed' and the 'Servant of God'. Zacharias and Auralian were Spanish missionaries who lived and died in Kerala.

Except Fr Chavara and Sister Rani Mariya, all others lived in the first half of the 20th century.

Sister Alphonsa and Fr Thevarparambil lived in the neighbouring villages of Bharananganam and Ramapuram, respectively, in Kottayam. Sister Celine lived in the communist citadel of Bernassery in north Kerala's Kannur district. She died at the age of 26 in 1957.

Conferring sainthood to a Catholic is a long process. First, the demand for initiating the process should come from within the local community, which should establish that the candidate lived a saintly life amidst them. If the demand merits attention, the local diocese constitutes a special body to look into the life of the candidate. If they find that the prospective saint is worth proceeding with, the diocese presents the case at the Congregation for the Cause of Saints in Rome. If the Vatican is convinced, it confers the title of 'Servant of God' on the candidate.

Then the real process begins. A postulator — a church official who oversees the canonisation process — must prove that the candidate lived by Christian virtues. Documents and testimonies are collected and presented to the Vatican Congregation.

In the next stage, the 'Servant of God', if found to be virtuous enough, is declared 'Venerable.' At this juncture, the postulator has to prove that a living person received a miracle from God through the intervention of the 'Servant of God'. If this is done, the candidate is declared 'Blessed' by the Vatican.

During the 'Blessed' period, proof of another miracle caused by the intervention of the candidate must be established. If this is done, the 'Blessed' is declared a saint.

According to Syro-Malabar Church spokesperson Father Paul Thelakkattu, the process of canonisation can be started five years after the death of a person. Though both Sister Alphonsa and Father Chavara were declared 'Blessed' on the same day in 1986, only the nun has attained sainthood so far. An initiated process of canonisation could run to several centuries, he said.

Meanwhile, 10,000 people are expected to participate in the canonisation of Sister Alphonsa at the Vatican on October 12. The official delegation is being led by Union Minister Oscar Fernandes and the Government of Kerala will be represented by Public Works Minister Mons Joseph.

Heading: NE rail projects to get non-lapsable fund - Indian Express
Content:
It is a sad day at the Siachen base camp. A soldier died at the Kaziranga post on the glacier two days ago and his body has still not been brought down due to bad weather and heavy snowfall. A Cheetah helicopter has been flying daily from base camp to the post, but has not been able to land and pick up the body.

Despite a rigorous selection procedure and extensive medical examinations before the posting, the soldier suffered a heart attack. Another one, doctors say, of the unpredictables while serving at extreme altitudes.

While days like these bring out the cost India is paying for maintaining troops at the highest battlefield in the world, casualty rates at the Siachen glacier have come down to an all time low.

Casualties peaked to almost 70 per year during the 1999 Kargil war, but the rate has come down to single digit in the past two years. New equipment, better medical facilities, faster evacuations and the ceasefire agreement has brought down fatality rates in the glacier to about four a year.

Till 2003, before the ceasefire agreement came into place, the Army was losing close to 30 soldiers on the glacier every year. The figure went down to 10 a year after the agreement. However, heavy snowfall and the 2006 earthquake raised the casualties to 26 that year.

The past two years have, however, been stable. The Army lost four men on the glacier in 2007 — two cases of medical complications and two pilots who died in a helicopter crash on the LoC. This year, four soldiers have died on the glacier, again mainly due to medical complications.

The main reason, officers say, is the good quality of clothing and special equipment procured in recent years to equip men on the glacier. Most of the clothing — jackets, gloves, sleeping bags — has improved over the past two years and is being imported from Italy, France and Austria.

"We now have better medical facilities and equipment. Any case that looks bad is evacuated immediately. We don't need to take any chances on the glacier anymore," a medical officer says.

Heading: Meghalaya CM to take up Massar issue at MPA meet - Indian Express
Content:
In a considerable fillip to the funding and execution of major railway projects in the North Eastern Region (NER), the Government is ready to set up a non-lapsable North East Rail Development Fund worth Rs 9,067 crore to ensure that these projects get completed within a stipulated time period and do not get delayed for want of funds.

The idea — in the works for almost a year now — has finally got the go-ahead from the Prime Minister's Office and will now be put before the Union Cabinet for approval.

"Currently, works on nine major railway projects (see box) in the North Eastern Region (NER) are on. All of these have already been declared as national projects and the setting up of this non-lapsable fund is primarily aimed at accelerating their progress," said a railway ministry official.

As per current estimates, investments worth Rs 9,067.7 crore are required to complete these nine projects, which include six new lines, two gauge conversions and a major road-cum-rail bridge over the Brahmaputra. These projects touch six states of the region excluding Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim.

The new line projects touch the states of Assam, Manipur, Tripura, Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram.

"Being non-lapsable, this fund will also cover any future projects that may be declared as national projects in the region," an official from the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER) said. While the Railways Ministry will contribute 25 per cent of this non-lapsable fund, the remaining 75 per cent will come from the Consolidated Fund of India.

Significantly, the setting up of this fund has also meant that target dates have been fixed for the completion of these projects. "Normally, railway projects don't have a pre-fixed deadline. However, with an assured fund supply now, these nine projects have been assigned specific completion dates."

Heading: B’desh too worried about HuJI: BDR - Indian Express
Content:
As public pressure to remove Meghalaya Mining and Geology Minister Donkupar Massar from the Cabinet and arrest him gains momentum, Chief Minister Donkupar Roy said he would take up the issue at the Meghalaya Progressive Alliance (MPA) coordination committee meet next week.

Massar has been accused of assaulting and threatening to kill four labourers in Borsora, West Khasi Hills District. Three of them have filed an FIR with the Ranikor police station in the district. A senior district police officer said: "We have registered the case, but need to follow procedure and get the Assembly Speaker's permission before we proceed against the minister."

On Monday, ten NGOs met Roy and handed over a letter demanding Massar's arrest and removal from the Cabinet. The letter said the minister had beaten up four labourers — Roming Jyrwa, Robert Ramseij, Ribok Nongsiej and Protis Ramsiej — without any provocation. "The MPA coordination committee will discuss the issue and decide whether to drop Massar," said Roy.

Heading: Ahead of deadline, more hands at work to complete trade route - Indian Express
Content:
Bangladesh is "gravely concerned" over the alleged involvement of Bangladesh-based terror organisation HuJI in terror activities in India, and will jointly fight the terror outfit, said Bangladesh Rifles (BDR) chief Major General Shakil Ahmed.

Ahmed met BSF Inspector General P K Misra at the Dawki-Tambil border outpost in eastern Meghalaya on Thursday and exchanged greetings on Vijaya Dashami.

"Both sides will have to work together to fight terrorism and insurgents in the common interest of peace and security," said Ahmed. He added that Bangladesh was also a victim of the HuJI and would do everything to stamp out the menace.

Underlining Bangladesh's commitment to fighting terrorism he said, "We have already been cooperating with BSF by sharing intelligence related to cross border terrorism activities." He stressed the need for joint efforts between the BSF and BDR to deal with all cross-border criminal activities, adding that much progress in fighting criminal activities had been made after the two countries decided to jointly patrol the border.

On charges that Bangladesh was habouring India-based insurgent groups, Ahmed said Bangladesh "does not and will not" allow any criminals to function from within its soil. "Recently, we (Bangladesh) handed over 18 criminals at Akhura checkpost and four criminals from across Mymensingh district to India," he said.

Regarding ndia's request to deport detained ULFA general secretary Anup Chetia, wanted for several murder cases, Ahmed said Chetia had approached the Dhaka Court pleading for political asylum in Bangladesh claiming that he was a "freedom fighter". He, however, said deportation of Chetia has been on the agenda at every discussion between India and Bangladesh.

Heading: Leh line: Rly ministry conducts feasibility study in HP - Indian Express
Content:
On Uri Kaman road, workers of the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) are putting in extra efforts to complete the blacktopping of the road from Salamabad to Aman Setu (Peace Bridge) so that they do not miss the deadline. The Jammu and Kashmir Government has said the blacktopping of the historical road should be completed before trucks roll out later this month.

"We are doing extra work to complete the road as targets have been fixed for us," said Bishan Das from Bengal, who has been on the job for the past one month.

"We have little time but are hopeful this patch will get completed before the trucks start plying on the road," said another worker, Md Jamal.

Huge cutters, too, have been employed to widen the road. Fresh bridges are being laid out at different places and walls are being constructed to make the road fit for trade.

At Salamabad, work on warehouses and storage facilities for trade goods are complete. "Our men are working overtime to make this road fit for traffic," said a defence spokesperson. "We have also engaged more labourers."

Though final dates for starting the cross-LoC trade have not been finalised yet, officials are planning to start the trade through two points at Kaman in Uri, and Chakandabagh in Poonch on October 21.

Initially, officials had said that the number of trucks permitted to cross the Kaman bridge from either side would be minimal. But, India and Pakistan have agreed to increase the frequency of trade once it begins. "We have been told that after every three months there will be a review meeting in which more items will be included in the cross-LoC trade list," said Zulfikar Abasi, who heads the PoK trade delegation that is presently in Kashmir.

His counterpart in Srinagar said, "We are hopeful that in the years to come, there will be full-fledged trade activity between two parts of Kashmir," said Mubeen Shah, president, Kashmir Chamber of Commerce.

Heading: Singapore PM tells Asian economies to prepare for tough ride - Indian Express
Content:
After the Himachal Pradesh Government cleared the pre-feasibility survey for the ambitious Manali-Leh rail link under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) mode, the Ministry of Railways has initiated a move to get a special feasibility study done for the strategic project.

A team of the railway officials, headed by senior official Buta Singh, was in the state and had visited Keylong —headquarter of Lahaul-Spiti districts — for preparing a survey report.

Union Minister of State for Railways R Velu, who was in Kangra district last week, has confirmed that the proposal for a pre-feasibility survey has been given the green signal.

The team members have met Deputy Commissioner, Lahaul-Spiti, C Paul Rasu and have asked for official data

on geographical conditions and traffic movement in the sector.

The route, used by the Army to send supplies to Leh-Ladakh and Kargil, will also cater to special and strategic needs of the Armed Forces.

Sources close to Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal, who was the first to moot the idea of a railway project in the wake of China taking up a railway line to Lhasa, confirmed that a survey would be conducted. "It's a welcome move, but we are not sure if the ministry will be able to attach any seriousness to the proposal, or whether it will only be looking for economic viabilities," a senior official said.

Rakesh Saran Mathur, managing director of Trans-Himalayan Railway Private Ltd, a subsidiary of Delhi-based engineering company ICC Holdings, says, "The project will require huge investments. But we are happy that our partners are willing to invest, keeping in view the scope of generating new economic activity in Lahaul-Spiti and Kullu".

The railway line will be 480 km long and will be laid at a height of 1,500 to 4,000 meters. Since the area is ecologically fragile, the company proposes to use the latest technology in drilling tunnels and laying the railway line.

Heading: On the railway map, at last - Indian Express
Content:
The Asian countries cannot avoid the impact of weakening US, European and Japanese economies, said Singapore Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong here on Friday.

"We must prepare for a tough ride at least over the next year, and quite possibly longer," he said, addressing a gathering on the first day of the mini Pravasi Bharatiya Divas jointly organised by CII and the Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs.

Lee said it would take some time before the trust in the banking sector was restored. In a way, Asian banks had been lucky to have avoided the problems afflicting the US and European banks, he said, adding, however, that the equity markets in Asia had been hit by the events at Wall Street.

While Loong along with Indian Minister for Overseas Indian Affairs Vayalar Ravi raised the pitch for long-term synergy between the two countries, former Singapore prime ministers Lee Kuan Yew and Goh Chok Tong used the occasion to delve deep into the making of modern India and its role in the years to come.

Lee Kuan Yew, the first prime minister of Singapore, in a candid discussion witnessed by over 700 delegates, said the recent Singur controversy that compelled the Tatas to shift the Nano-manufacturing plant to Gujarat epitomised India's problems.

"Even though the CPI(M) Government had allowed the setting up of the Nano plant in Singur, the Opposition mobilised the farmers and the plant had to be shifted. This is where the problem lies," he said. "Political parties must go beyond political interests to ensure that the right decision is taken."

Yew added that India must stop 'idealising' villages and move towards industrialisation. "In Singapore, we shifted the entire rural population from the outer islands and put them all on one island. We ensured better health care, education and jobs, and today there is not a single village in Singapore," he said, referring to Finance Minister P Chidambaram's notion of "gradualism".

"Developed India is urban India, and given the present circumstances, I don't see India being a leading global power," Yew said, answering a question on India's prospect of being a leader.

Appreciating India's liberal democracy, Yew said the Government along with the Opposition would have to take decisions together.

Goh Chok Tong, who succeeded Yew as prime minister, said coalition politics and state-Central development meant that reforms would not be easy in India. There was a need to change the red-tape mindset of the Indian bureaucracy.

Tong said agricultural reforms and improvement in education were the key challenges before India. "With better infrastructure and improved connectivity, the economy will be on a much stronger footing," he added.

The Prime Minister said the Singapore Government was planning to set up an Indian Heritage Centre to trace the history of the Indian diaspora in Singapore and document its contribution to the country's development.

Heading: Jalgaon murder: chargesheet against two more - Indian Express
Content:
It was Dogra ruler Maharaja Pratap Singh who first explored the possibility of a railway line to Kashmir in 1898. Since then, there have been many failed attempts.

1902: Britain proposed a rail link between Srinagar and Rawalpindi along the Jhelum

1905: Britain again proposed a link between Srinagar and Rawalpindi. But Maharaja Pratap Singh wanted an electric-powered rail line between Jammu and Srinagar

1947: After Independence, a rail link between Pathankot and Jammu was proposed, to be extended to Srinagar. But it was put on hold due to high cost

1983: PM Indira Gandhi set aside a budget of Rs 50 cr and a time-frame of 5 years for a railway project, connecting Udhampur to Jammu. Costing Rs 515 cr, it was completed after 21 years

1994: Union Railway Minister Jaffer Sharief proposed a rail link connecting Jammu with Baramulla

1996: PM P V Narsimha Rao announced

Rs 2,600 cr for Kashmir rail link

March 1997: PM H D Deve Gowda laid the foundation stone of a 290-km Udhampur-Baramulla rail link in Udhampur

July 1997: PM I K Gujral laid the foundation stone for the Udhampur-Baramulla railway link in Baramulla

2002: The Vajpayee Government declared a rail link to Kashmir as a national project. The project cost was put at Rs 6,000 cr and August 15, 2007 was set as the deadline

2003: PM A B Vajpayee laid the foundation stone of a railway bridge at Udhampur

2005: PM Manmohan Singh inaugurated the 55-km Jammu-Udhampur railway stretch after more than two decades of construction

April 2008: Railway Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav said he would not set a deadline for the Kashmir rail

Heading: 3 girls rescued, ‘godman’ arrested - Indian Express
Content:
The CBI on Friday informed the Bombay High Court that it has filed a supplementary chargesheet in the Jalgaon trial court against Damodar Lokhande and Leeladhar Narkhede in the controversial Prof V G Patil murder case. The president of the Jalgaon District Congress Committee was murdered on September 21, 2005.

Last year, the Congress leader's widow, Rajani Patil, moved the High Court, contending that the real conspirators in the case were President Pratibha Patil's brother Dr G N Patil and former Congress MP Dr Ulhas Patil. She claimed that though Raju Mali and Raju Sonawane were the actual assailants, Lokhande and Narkhede were the intermediaries who gave them the supari at the behest of G N Patil and Ulhas Patil.

Senior counsel Mahesh Jethmalani, appearing for Rajini, told the court that the CBI has not taken cognisance of evidence against President Pratibha Patil's brother. Jethmalani argued that the CBI filed a chargesheet in June only against the two assailants, one of whom, Mali, died in judicial custody under mysterious circumstances. It has now named two more, Lokhande and Narkhede.

Jethmamalani contended that this was done only after the petitioner submitted a written submission in August 2008, presenting incriminating evidence collected by the CBI itself not only against Lokhande and Narkhede but also against G N Patil and Ulhas Patil. Jethmalani argued that it is obvious that the CBI is doing its best to exonerate G N Patil and Ulhas Patil because of their connections.

"Let someone in the CBI take responsibility by filing an affidavit that the evidence available with it supports exoneration of G N Patil and Ulhas Patil. It is a question of accountability. Whose decision is it to absolve the two? This must come on record," Jethmalani submitted. Counsel for CBI Raju Subramaniam argued that the HC should end the monitoring of the CBI investigation since they have filed the chargesheet before the trial court. The Division Bench of Justice F I Rebello and Justice Ashutosh Kumbhkoni has allowed Rajni Patil to file an affidavit, giving details of her statement to the police, by October 14.

Heading: Two Naxals killed in Orissa - Indian Express
Content:
A 'Godman' who named his ashram Kunwarika Bhavan (Virgins' Home) and kept three young female devotees as his sex slaves for over two years, has ended up behind bars in Jhalod, Dahod district.

According to the police, the man lured two of the girls into his ashram — a two-room brick house at Kalji-Sarwani village in Dahod — by promising to personally sire babies with supernatural powers for them. He had even managed to gain the trust of the victims' parents, who allowed their daughters, both in their early twenties, to stay with him. One of the girls delivered a baby boy a few months ago.The third victim was reportedly abducted from a nearby village and kept at the ashram where she was sexually exploited. The 45-year-old godman, Sabur Baria alias Naklank Bhagwan, was allegedly assisted in his unholy pursuits by his wife, Sevli. Their 'sex racket' came to an end when the abducted girl's grandfather traced her and alerted the cops.

According to the Jhalod police, the girl was barely 15 years old when she was kidnapped by Baria and his wife from Kadwa village and taken to the ashram where she was raped repeatedly.

Heading: CIC dismisses ex-RAW official’s RTI appeal against ‘rival’ author - Indian Express
Content:
After getting their noses bloodied by the Maoists repeatedly over the last few months, the Orissa Police on Friday claimed that they killed two Maoists, one of them a hardcore woman cadre, in the forests of Koraput district.

A joint team of the Andhra Pradesh Police's Special Task Force and the Orissa Police scouring the area managed to kill the two — part of a three-member Naxalite team — in the Almonda area of the district under Narayanpatna police station on the Andhra Pradesh-Orissa border on Friday afternoon.

The woman, identified as Jyoti (25) was a member of the Koraput Divisional Committee(KDC) of the Peoples' Liberation Guerrilla Army. A native of Srikakulam district in Andhra Pradesh, Jyoti took part in several high-profile rebels attacks including the one on the Nayagarh police training school in February this year.

The identity of the other deceased Maoist is not known. The third member of the group, Raju, the area commander of the KDC, however, escaped with some injury. Panda said with the killing of the two Maoists, the KDC has been visibly weakened as it comes after two of their active members — Aruna and her boyfriend — eloped leaving the Naxal bosses fuming.

Heading: Dispute over another agri varsity land - Indian Express
Content:
Incensed that the CBI had not taken any action against former intelligence officer B Raman for revealing "official secrets" in a book but had penalised him for his own published work on the workings of the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW), Major General (retd) Vinay Kumar Singh was left disappointed when his RTI appeal against Raman was dismissed by the Central Information Commission (CIC) on Friday.

Singh's RTI appeal stemmed from the fact that the 'revelations' in his own controversial book, India's External Intelligence: Secrets of Research and Analysis Wing, had left him facing charges under the Official Secrets Act (OSA) and Indian Penal Code (IPC). However, the CBI had not taken any similar action against Raman, who penned The Kaoboys of R&AW: Down Memory Lane.

Claiming that his appeal was beyond the scope of its jurisdiction, the CIC directed Singh to petition the CBI director against the former RAW operative.

Singh, also a former RAW official had highlighted 28 instances in Raman's book which "appear to violate the provisions" of the OSA, 1923 and the IPC, 1860.

"Yet the CBI has not contemplated any action against the author or publisher of the book under the OSA or the IPC. But similar disclosures in my book have left me facing charges under the OSA and IPC," Singh submitted on Friday in a hearing before Chief Information Commissioner Wajahat Habibullah.

The CBI had registered an FIR under Section 5 (wrongful communication of information) of the OSA against Singh in September 2007. The agency had then followed it up with a chargesheet against the author on April 11, 2008.

The CBI, meanwhile, stood firm with a stoic reply that they would have taken action against Raman had there been a specific complaint against him.

"There has been no specific complaint on this work (Raman's)," Superintendent of Police (CBI) Sanjay Singh repeated in his submissions before the Bench.

Reacting to the CBI's reply, Habibullah has now advised Singh to "petition the CBI Director for action to be taken".

"You can express your dissatisfaction to him (CBI Director). You can demand action to be taken. I cannot do anything as your query is beyond my jurisdiction," Habibullah observed.

Heading: Now, Gujarat farmers stake their claim on Nano site - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat Government's transfer of 1,100 acres - carved from land that was originally meant for research by the Anand Agriculture University (AAU) - to the Tatas for the Nano small-car project may not have hit any major roadblocks yet, but a similar move by the Government earlier is lying foundered on legal shoals.

Barely two years ago, the Gujarat Government had acquired 65,000 sq metres of land from the Cotton Research Centre under the state-run Navsari Agricultural University, located at one of Surat's prime locations at Ghod Dod Road. However, the Gujarat HC accepted a PIL that maintained that no land meant for agricultural research could be given away for a commercial project, and stayed the Government's move. The stay has not been lifted and the next hearing of the case is on October 21.

The court had come into the picture after the Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC) released an advertisement inviting expressions of interest in developing this land for tourism and entertainment infrastructure.

After the PIL was moved, the Chhatrala Hotel Group, which staked its claim for developing the property in question, joined issue as a respondent, along with the Gujarat Government, GIDC and NAU. Talking to The Indian Express, the petitioner, a local farmer who asked not to be named, claimed he was now under tremendous pressure to back off. "There has been a lot of pressure on me ever since I filed that PIL. All we are saying is that when the Government already has so much land, why must it set up industries that have nothing to do with farming on land meant for agricultural research?"

Meanwhile, the AAU refused to comment on the 2,200 acres the university transferred to the Government, of which 1,100 were allocated to the Tatas.

Heading: Protests over PM’s visit, two killed in police firing - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Government of Gujarat celebrates the arrival of Tata Motors' Nano plant, rumblings of discontent are gradually becoming louder among a section of farmers from villages near the proposed site in Sanand.

In a refrain that echoes the concerns of the farmers at Singur, a number of villagers are beginning to bring up issues regarding land rights and compensation. Farmers from Khoda, Bhod, Amareli and Modasar are staking their claim on the 1,100 acres that has been given to the Tatas for the Nano factory, saying that the land belonged to their forefathers.

"During the great famine, our forefathers gave the land to the British government on lease for 100 years so it could be used as a grazing ground," claims Meghrajsinh Chauhan from Bhod. "When we asked for the land in 2002, we were told that the government had acquired it in 1911. Since then we have been running from pillar to post to get our land rights, but no one has ever heard us," he says.

Although Chauhan is quick to add that the farmers have nothing against the Tatas or the Nano plant being set up here, he makes it clear that the farmers expect more benefits. "We are the real owners of the land and we have got nothing in the deal. We should get our share of compensation too. We'll fight till the last for our rights," he asserts, adding that the Anand University campus was also built on the farmers' land.

"Our struggle for land rights did not start after the Tatas came, but even though we have fought for so long, nobody is listening to us. We are now trying to resolve the issue through the legal system, but if things don't work, we may have to resort to stronger measures like hunger strikes," he adds.

"We are talking to lawyers to move courts," confirms Mukeshsinh Vaghela from Khoda village. "But we need some more evidence to prove our rights. We are currently trying to get those papers. The state Government is hiding a lot of things from us. They say the land has been acquired in 1911, but it has failed to give us the documents to prove this," he adds.

According to Ahmedabad District Collector Harit Shukla, however, the farmers do not have much of a case. Acknowledging that the land was leased to the British Government in 1899 for 100 years, Shukla says the land was acquired in 1911 and the farmers were paid a compensation of Rs 2 lakh then.

"We have enough documents to prove that they were compensated," says Shukla, adding that the government does not owe the farmers any more compensation.

Heading: Manmohan Singh’s menu has no space for Wazwan - Indian Express
Content:
Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's Kashmir visit on Friday triggered a shutdown and sparked off massive protests in the Valley. Two protestors were killed when the CRPF opened fire in downtown city while 75 persons were wounded — four of them critically — in police action across the Valley.

The call for the protests and strike was given by the Coordination Committee — a body formed by the separatists to spearhead the latest 'Azadi' groundswell across Kashmir — to protest against the visit of the Prime Minister. The separatists have called for a "civil curfew" on Saturday.

Senior Superintendent of Police, Srinagar, Syed Ahfad-ul-Mujtaba told The Indian Express that two protestors were killed in the security force firing.

The protest march began from Nowhatta locality where hundreds of young men took to streets soon after the Friday prayers. The protestors, who were shouting anti-India slogans, were soon intercepted by the police who fired teargas shells at them and the protestors retaliated by pelting the police with stones.

"We had taken out a rally after the (Friday) prayers in Habba Kadal. The CRPF men fired teargas shells at the bridge to disperse us. They started firing straight at us immediately after that," says Tauseef Ahmad Bhat, a college student. "One bullet hit me between the legs and I ran from the bridge towards the road. Then I fell down."

The medical records at the SMHS's post-operative ward reveal that Tauseef has been hit in his penis shaft and glands. "He has about 10 stitches in his penis, and we don't know whether his organ has got any serious damage," says Tauseef's cousin, Ajaz Ahmad Ganai.

Heading: Putting Valley on track: Four trains to run daily, Rs 15 fare - Indian Express
Content:
When PM Manmohan Singh sits down for dinner with his wife Gursharan Kaur on Friday evening, the chefs of the J-K Government's Hospitality and Protocol Department will, to put it mildly, face an unusual situation. Famous for their mastery of the traditional multi-course Wazwan (Kashmiri) cuisine, primarily comprising spicy meat-based delicacies like Roganjosh, Rista and Kababs, they will instead have to cook "without oil", make tea "without sugar" and dish out a meal "without spice".

The mouthwatering Wazwan cuisine, more a ritual than a mere meal, will not find its way to the PM's table as the menu for his two-day visit will be vegetarian and will be cooked without oil, sugar or even the saving grace of spice. A detailed note on the "dietary preferences" of Singh and his wife sent by Sisir Das, the PM's tour officer was communicated to the J-K Government. It includes, apart from dietary preferences, other requirements as he stays overnight in an undisclosed house at Cheshma Shahi hills.

Singh will begin his day with the "Marie biscuits" and "bed tea with a little sugar". Breakfast will consist of "fresh coconut water" followed by "papaya " and then a bowl of corn flakes or dalia with toast and home-made butter. An "egg white" will mark the only difference between the plates of Singh and his wife. The cooks will, however, face their real test at lunch when the menu of "tawa chapattis" with "a little dal" alongside two "sabzis" (vegetables) with curry means they will be unable to serve a single Kashmiri speciality unless they include ''dum aloo'' and ''haak'', the only two Kashmiri vegetarian dishes.

"He eats almost nothing—one roti with vegetable and two spoons of curd," says Deputy Director of Hospitality and Protocol, Manzoor Ahmad, who has served the PM during his Ladakh trip. In the evening, Singh will be served "tea with no sugar" along with the "Marie" biscuits, and the menu for dinner will not substantially differ from that of the lunch.

While the PM has to be in "close proximity" to NSA M K Narayan and other officials from his office, the J-K Government has been instructed that "no intercom should ring in the PM's suite". There must be two hotline connections, one direct BSNL line, a fax machine, a computer with a broadband connection, a laser printer, a photo-copier and a shredder in his suite. There is also a direction about Prime Minister Singh's bed. "It should be a hard mattress with a cotton- rich bed spread," the note says. The television set in the PM's room requires five news channels along with other popular channels. According to the note, there must be a music system and an electric treadmill available for the PM.

Heading: Eye on Muslim votes, CPM treads soft line on Abdullakutty - Indian Express
Content:
The Valley's first rail service, set to be flagged off by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on Saturday, will provide four daily trains on the 66-km section between Anantnag and Rajwansher on the Quazigund-Baramulla section in Jammu and Kashmir.

Singh is also likely to take a brief ride on the train. However, the move is subject to last-minute security considerations.

Two pairs of Diesel Electric Multiple Unit (DEMU) trains, numbered 1 AR, 2 AR, 3 AR and 4 AR will start operating on the section from Sunday. All the rakes operating on this route will have eight coaches, with each coach having 90 seats in chair car configuration. The Railways will charge Rs 15 as fare for a single trip.

"The 2 AR Rajwansher-Anantnag DEMU will depart from Rajwansher at 7.10 am and arrive at Anantnag at 8.45 am, while the 4 AR Rajwansher-Anantnag DEMU will depart from Rajwansher at 2.25 pm to arrive at Anantnag at 4 pm," said a Northern Railway official.

"In the return direction, the 1 AR Anantnag-Rajwansher DEMU train will depart from Anantnag at 9.05 am and arrive at Rajwansher at 10.40 am, while the 3 AR train will depart from Anantnag at 4.15 pm to arrive at Rajwansher at 5.50 pm," he said.

All the trains on the route will halt at all the seven stations — Badgam, Srinagar, Pampore, Kakapore, Awantipura, Panjgam and Bijbehra.

Having already secured a safety certification to run passenger trains at maximum permissible speeds of 100 kmph from the Commissioner of Railway Safety, the Railways now plans to allow trains to run at optimum speeds.

Heading: Banning OBC dereservation next on agenda: Paswan - Indian Express
Content:
Fearing erosion of Muslim votes in the ensuing Lok Sabha polls, the CPM in Kerala plans to go soft on its MP A P Abdullakutty, who had several times challenged the Communist line by openly proclaiming his staunch faith inGod, and asking the party to change its negative attitude towards religion.

Indicating that the party does not want Abdullakutty to emerge as a martyr for Islam, CPM Kannur district secretary P Sasi said the MP has not committed any offence by saying he is a Communist who believes in God.

Sasi said the CPM was not against religion. "If Abdullakutty has any doubts in this regard, the party would be happy to clear them." Sasi is a close confidant of party state secretary Pinarayi Vijayan, who has identified Abdullakutty with the faction led by CM V S Achuthanandan.

Downplaying the controversy created by Abdullakutty's demand for room for religion in the CPM, Sasi said the magnitude of a party activist's faith in religion would depend upon the extent to which he has imbibed materialism after joining the party.

Recently, in an article published in a Malayalam daily, Abdullakutty had brought to light a Communist leader's craving for religion and rituals. Abdullakutty also participated in Id prayers in Kannur last week. He had invited the party leadership's wrath when he performed the pre-Haj Umra in 2007 and had recently taken up Nadi astrology.

Though the CPI(M) official faction has virtually sidelined Abdullakutty, the party is afraid of initiating any action against the young leader, who enjoys considerable support among Muslims. Any action against him would affect the party's fortunes not only in his constituency of Kannur in North Kerala, but also in other Muslim pockets of the state.

In Muslim-dominated Malappuram district, the Indian Union Muslim League, an ally of the Congress, has already tried to cash in on the political situation arising out of Abdullakutty's confessions about his faith in God. The party raised huge cut-outs of Abdullakutty's article in the Malayalam daily across the district to tell the Muslim community "how life has been miserable for an Islam follower in the Communist party".

Sources close to Abdullakutty said his observations of the mental agony a believer faced in CPM have found many takers. Several party leaders, including MPs, have covertly patted him for having spoken on behalf of many in the party. The present political situation in Kerala has also helped Abdullakutty emerge unscathed. Though several Muslim organisations have rallied behind CPI(M) over its stand on the nuclear deal, the recent hunt for SIMI activists launched by the Left Government has made Muslim groups restless.

Heading: First day, first show: huge crowds turn up for Chiranjeevi’s roadshow - Indian Express
Content:
After approving the enactment of a law to end "de-reservation" of SC/ST quota, the UPA Government is now gearing up to bring a similar Bill to protect 27 per cent reservation for the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in Central Government jobs and educational institutions.

Union Minister and Lok Janshakti Party chief Ramvilas Paswan, who played a pivotal role in pushing the provision with regard to the SC/ST quota, told The Indian Express on Friday that the Government would now bring a similar Bill to ensure that the OBC quota was not de-reserved. He hinted that the Government wanted to bring it during the forthcoming session of Parliament.

"Our Government is committed to uplifting the deprived sections of society. After SC/STs, we are committed to bringing a similar enactment to ban de-reservation of seats reserved for OBCs in services and educational institutions," he said.

Paswan said earlier reservation quotas for SC/STs used to be implemented through a Government Order (GO), leaving scope for de-reservation of vacant seats after some time. "But now a law will be in force to check de-reservation," he added.

Already, the UPA Government has tried to woo the OBCs with the Cabinet recently raising the annual income ceiling for "creamy layer" among OBCs from Rs 2.5 lakh to Rs 4.5 lakh.

The proposed ban is sure to invite fresh controversy as the SC had recently said that seats remaining vacant after implementing the 27% OBC quota in Central educational institutions should go to general- category students.

Earlier, the SC/ST/OBCs were clubbed together in the Bill. However, after intense lobbying from Dalit groups that SC/STs were different from OBCs in quotas, the Government in June this year seperated the two.

Last Wednesday, the Union Cabinet had approved enactment of a law to end dereservation of quotas meant for SC/STs with a penal provision for action against offices not implementing the quota. "Posts reserved for SCs and STs will not be de-reserved, and they (vacancies) will be carried over," Finance Minister P Chidambaram had said after a Cabinet meeting.

Heading: Amar softens on Jamia probe - Indian Express
Content:
Though he started on a nervous note, filmstar-turned-politician Chiranjeevi's first roadshow received a tremendous response on the first day in Srikakulam on Friday. Chiranjeevi, going to the public for the first time after he joined politics, was overwhelmed by the massive crowds which thronged the route as his convoy winded through Srikakulam towards Narsannapeta.

"Chiranjeevi was totally humbled by the love and affection he received from the people here. They urged him to go ahead in politics and promised their full support to him and his party," a spokesperson for Chiranjeevi said.

Chiranjeevi started off from Srikakulam at 9 am but the progress of his convoy was painfully slow as crowds came out on the roads and stopped his convoy, insisting on garlanding him and requesting him to address them. By 4 pm, the convoy, comprising some 30 party vehicles and more than 100 vehicles of his fans, was in Narsannapeta, an Assembly constituency on the northern-most tip of Andhra coast bordering Orissa. "He stopped to address the crowds at a number of places along the way. We are totally overwhelmed by the response from the people," said an official of Praja Rajyam, Chiranjeevi's party.

The filmstar will return to Srikakulam on Friday night. On Saturday, his convoy will travel to Itchapuram, another constituency bordering Orissa.

Heading: BJP slams Amar’s induction in NIC - Indian Express
Content:
With the Centre rejecting the Samajwadi Party's (SP) demand for a judicial inquiry into the Jamia Nagar encounter that followed terror blasts in Delhi, the party on Friday climbed down from its earlier demand and called for setting up an independent committee to clarify the misgivings about the encounter.

"If the judicial probe is not possible for the Government, it should consider setting up a committee of eminent persons to look into the misgivings about the Jamia Nagar encounter," SP general secretary Amar Singh told reporters here on Friday. Singh even suggested that the regular committee could be headed by former chief justice of India A M Ahmadi.

While judicial probes hold more teeth as they are constituted under the Commission of Inquiry Act, fact-finding committees could be set up by an executive order. The Government is bound to table the reports of judicial inquiries to the legislatures and submit an action-taken report, but this is not mandatory in case of fact-finding committees.

Singh's climbdown comes amid the realisation within the party that it may find it difficult to force the Government to constitute a judicial probe while it wants to assuage the misgivings of its minority support base. The SP can now claim to have stood for the sensitivities of its minority support base without making it difficult for the Government to heed to its demands.

Heading: 3 die in police firing in MP town after communal tension - Indian Express
Content: The BJP has slammed the appointment of Samajwadi Party leader Amar Singh as a member of the National Integration Council (NCM). "It is unfortunate that PM Manmohan Singh has appointed a person to the National Integration Council who while glorifying terrorists, raises doubts over the great sacrifice of Inspector M C Sharma in the Jamia Nagar encounter," said BJP spokesperson Prakash Javadekar. "This is a payback for the services rendered by him for the survival of the UPA Government by manufacturing majority through a cash-for-votes scandal. It appears that the PM wants to use his services to vociferously lead the demand for banning the Bajrang Dal."

Heading: Uddhav lacks confidence, says Rane - Indian Express
Content:
Three persons were killed in police firing and more than two dozen injured in stone pelting and firing in the communally-sensitive Burhanpur town of Madhya Pradesh on Friday.

Prohibitory orders were in force since late Thursday when trouble started over the procession of a Hindu deity in the town. Hindu organisations allege that the procession was stoned by Muslims and it could not reach its destination.

The incident was followed by arson, for which members of the two communities blamed each other.

In protest against Thursday night's incident, Hindu organisations organised a dharna at Gandhi chowk while Muslims gathered in large numbers to offer Friday prayers.

The circumstances that led to the police firing are unclear. Additional DGP Surendra Singh said three persons died in police firing and 18 others, including five police personnel, were injured in the violence. He said four police station areas have been brought under curfew and extra forces from outside have been brought in as there was no let up in tension.

NCP MLA from Burhanpur Hameed Kazi blamed the violence on Hindu organisations and accused the police of using force only against minorities. "They did not fire at Bajrang Dal and other Hindu activists," he alleged.

Heading: VHP, Bajrang Dal file court complaint against Bhajji - Indian Express
Content:
Launching a scathing attack on Shiv Sena executive president Uddhav Thackeray, Maharashtra Revenue Minister Narayan Rane on Friday described him as a "man without confidence".

"Uddhav lacks self-confidence as a person. How can he take care of the party?" Rane told reporters on the sidelines of a workers convention here.

"If I was Balasaheb's son, I would have avoided bringing him (Bal Thackeray) to Shivaji Park and making him speak at the Dussehra rally. It could be seen that Saheb is really not in good health," he said. "As his son I would have assured him that I would carry forward his work in the same manner as he did for 42 years."

Lashing out at the Sena leader for saying that Mumbai belongs to "our fathers", Rane asked, "How can Mumbai belong to people who do not pay taxes? Our fathers' names are also there on the land records and property cards."

Rane also said that Uddhav's speech at Thursday night's rally was "useless". "He has spoken nothing except criticising Raj Thackeray, myself and the Congress. He has not outlined any agenda for the development of Mumbai and Maharashtra," he said.

Speaking on the occasion earlier, Maharashtra Congress Campaign Committee Chairman Gurudas Kamat wondered aloud if Uddhav had purchased all of Mumbai. "Rane, who is the Revenue Minister, should check the land records to see if Uddhav and his family have purchased the megapolis. Mumbai belongs to our fathers also and to the entire country," he said.

Heading: CBI court issues NBWs against former minister - Indian Express
Content:
Harbhajan Singh's 'Ravana act' in a TV dance reality show has now earned the ire of the VHP and other Hindu outfits who have filed a complaint in a local court against the cricketer.

Chief Judicial Magistrate Kanchan Mahi fixed the hearing on Monday after Punjab VHP spokesperson Vijay Singh Bhardwaj and others alleged in their complaint that Harbhajan, his co-participant TV actress Mona Singh and the channel that aired the programme Ek Khiladi, Ek Hasina had "intentionally and deliberately" hurt the religious feelings of Hindus.

Arvind Thakur, chairman of Akhil Bhartiya Rajput Council, and the Punjab Unit of Bajrang Dal are also party to the complaint. The Akal Takht, the temporal seat of Sikhs, had earlier taken exception to the 28-year-old Sikh cricketer's behaviour, which, it said, had caused severe resentment among the community and had sought an apology from him.

"To wear a tilak on the forehead and to dress like Ravana and dance with a woman publicly is highly disgusting. The act was shown on several TV channels and the Sikh community can never tolerate such behaviour," Jathedar Gyani Gurbachan Singh had said on Wednesday.

Two years ago, Harbhajan had apologised after the Shiromani

Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC), the apex religious body of the Sikhs, slammed the bowler for leaving his hair uncovered in an advertisement.

Heading: Ally on board, Bengal gives go-ahead to German firm - Indian Express
Content:
A special CBI court on Friday issued non-bailable warrants against former minister of state for urban development P K Thungan for his failure to appear before the court in connection with a case of out-of-turn allotment of houses.

Besides Thungan, 17 others, including the additional personal secretary of the then urban development minister Sheila Kaul, were accused by the investigating agency in 1996 of allegedly receiving illegal gratification from over 100 government employees for granting them out-of-turn accommodation, during 1993-95.

"Issue non-bailable warrants against accused P K Thungan for October 20," said Special CBI Judge R K Yadav in his order while rejecting Thungan's plea seeking exemption from appearance on personal grounds. He further directed the probe agency to ensure Thungan's presence on October 20, the next date of hearing.

The FIR against all the accused was lodged on February 14, 1996, following a Supreme Court order on a public interest litigation, challenging the controversial government policy on house allotment.

According to the chargesheet filed in the case, D D Arora, the then additional personal secretary of former urban development minister Sheila Kaul, had at the time hatched a criminal conspiracy with his son Virender Arora and others, and compelled the government employees to pay bribes for out-of-turn allotment of houses.

Heading: Group spotted Peerbhoy at an Arabic class in 2004 - Indian Express
Content:
German wholesale major Metro Cash & Carry was finally given a fresh trade licence on Friday by the Forward Bloc-controlled Agriculture Marketing Board of the West Bengal Government. The APMC licence, valid till March 2009, was issued after an MoU was signed between the state Government and the German major. The state had promised to give the licence by October 10.

The green signal for Metro Cash & Carry comes after a serious stand-off between the CM Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee and ally Forward Bloc. Though the FB leadership had threatened to withdraw its ministers from the Cabinet, an understanding was reached at a Left Front meeting.

As per the MoU, the firm will sell commodities only to those traders who have a trading licence and, in case of agro-products, an APMC licence. It can never enter into any direct or indirect retail business and cannot opt for contract farming, the MoU stated. The FB also climbed down from its earlier stand that the company should not be allowed to do business below Rs 5,000. The ceiling on minimum-billing limit has now been kept at Rs 1,000. However, the Board has imposed a 1 per cent market fee on the sale and purchase of every commodity.

"We have ensured that Metro Cash & Carry will under no circumstances be able to enter into any retail business. We have also ensured that they will not go for contract farming," said Agriculture Marketing Board chairman Naren Chatterjee.

Officials of the German company said they would start their operations in the city in six to eight weeks. "We are delighted that we have received a fresh APMC licence. We will cater to business establishments like hotels, restaurants, caterers and grocery shops," said Frits van Peski, member of the company's Executive Board of Directors.

Metro Cash & Carry had got its operational space of about 1,00,000 sq ft ready with an investment of Rs 140 crore long ago. However, the project got delayed due to land disputes. The company was granted a licence to trade in APMC commodities in 2005, which was subsequently renewed twice in 2006 and 2007 to be valid till March 2008. However, in June 2007 the licence was withdrawn by the APMC.

Heading: Indian crew of hijacked ship freed unharmed by Somali pirates - Indian Express
Content:
Software engineer Mohammed Mansoor Asgar Peerbhoy (31) was identified for indoctrination as far back as 2004. A group of people scouting for young Muslim men had spotted Peerbhoy in an Arabic class. The group then kept tabs on Peerbhoy, alleged Indian Mujahideen suspect Asif Bashir Shaikh told the Mumbai Police Crime Branch during investigation.

Describing Asif as a "rotten apple" in the class, Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria said: "The institutes that teach Arabic have nothing to do with such groups. People like Asif scout for such recruits at these places, without the knowledge of the institutes."

In 2006, he was again trailed from the local mosque in Pune. "Once it had fully indoctrinated him, the group sent him for the ethical hacking course. He was later sent to Bhatkal for other training," said Maria.

Maria also said that "quite a few" men who had been indoctrinated went on to leave the group as they felt it was a wrong thing to do. "There are many like them who have given us leads and were helpful in the investigation," he said.

Peerbhoy reportedly told the investigators that the terror e-mails he sent were on Riyaz Bhatkal's brief.

Peerbhoy and Mubin alias Salman Kadar Sheikh (24) had conducted a recce for non-secure WiFi connections on five separate occasions. "On July 26, they left Pune at 10 am and reached Sanpada. They spent their time having lunch and strolling in the garden nearby," adds Maria.

On the third occasion, they were supposed to send the mail at 6.20 pm but it got delayed till 6.26. "It was the day before the immersion and the crowd around Chembur was so large that they struggled to park their car," adds Maria.

Interrogation has also established the manner in which the mails were sent. "Peerbhoy, Salman and Arif Badruddin Shaikh (38) were driven down by Mohammed Akbar Ismail Chaudhary in a blue Esteem. Chaudhary and Arif srood outside, masking the number plates from both sides, while Peerbhoy and Mubin sent the mail," said Maria.

Investigations have also shown that the Gujarat blasts were initially planned for September 19. "The blasts were later shifted to September 26," said Maria.

The explosives, sourced from Karnataka, were taken via Pune and later to Surat through state transport, said Maria.The group had called Mohd Arif Shaikh to Karnataka to assemble the circuits, with certain parts of the circuit sourced from Mumbai.

Heading: Communal clash spreads to another Orissa district - Indian Express
Content:
Armed Somali pirates on Friday released three Indians and 26 other members of the crew on board a hijacked cargo ship after keeping them in captivity for more than one- and-a-half months. All were unharmed.

"The vessel has been released by Somali pirates and all crew are safe and healthy," the Directorate General of Shipping said in a release.

The Indian crew released are Jeevan Kiran D'Souza of Kasargod in Kerala, Akbar Ali Rafeeque Juwale of Ratnagiri in Maharashtra and Anthony Clive Themudo of Goa.

The ship, MV Iran Deyanat, carrying 40,000 tonnes of iron ore en route from China to Netherlands, was hijacked on the Red Sea by Somali pirates on August 22. Besides Indians, the ship had Iranians and Croatians. The pirates with weapons had come in speed boats and seized the ship. India had sought the assistance of the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in the matter.

It was not immediately clear if any ransom had been paid for the release of the crew members and the ship.

The merchant vessel was headed from China for the Netherlands, carrying minerals and industrial products when it was hijacked on August 22 along with a German and a Japanese ship off the Gulf of Aden.

Jeevan Kiran D'Souza (28), one of the three Indians, rang up his residence near the border town of Uppala, about 20 km from here, at 1.30 pm and said all the crew members were set free and would be back home within a week, Jeevan's father Ligouri D'Souza told PTI.

"My son has informed that he would call his family after crossing 100 nautical miles and we are expecting his call any time," a relieved D'Souza said.

"For almost a week, my son had suffered agony mid-sea due to lack of proper medical treatment."

Heading: EC meets today on J-K polls: Will it be now or with LS? - Indian Express
Content:
The fire of communal conflict in Kandhamal district has spread to the adjoining Malkangiri district where 12 people from both Hindu and Christian communties were injured, some of them critically, after they clashed on Thursday night.

According to the police, the children belonging to the Telugu Christian community and the Oriya Hindus in Padia village had a fight over gambling on Wednesday.

The matter came to a head when the members of the Christian community attacked some puja pandals leading to clashes between the two communities. Malkangiri SP SK Gajbhiye said the critically injured had been sent to the district headquarters hospital.

A unit of Special Operation Group of Orissa police has been rushed to the spot to contain any further violence.

Though Kandhamal continued to be peaceful on Friday, over 4,000 Kondh tribals belonging to four grampanchayats gheraoed the block office of Tikabali demanding that the murderers of Laxmanananda Saraswati be arrested forthwith. The protestors, most of them women, were asking for a stop to midnight arrests and withdrawal of CRPF from the district.

Heading: India invites Pak team for inspection of Baglihar project - Indian Express
Content:
The Election Commission will hold a full meeting - with Chief Election Commissioner V Gopalaswami and Election Commissioners Navin Chawla and SY Quraishi present — on Saturday to take a final call on Assembly polls in Jammu and Kashmir.

With the task of holding the election on time appears to be tougher than expected, the EC could even consider clubbing it with the Lok Sabha polls due early next year.

However, the security establishment is keen on early elections. Saturday's meeting will decide if the polls will be held in November or along with the general election.

A team from the Election Commission returned from a two-day trip to the State on Thursday, after meeting various political parties and others. On Friday, Home Secretary Madhukar Gupta, accompanied by the Joint Secretary (Kashmir) and Joint Secretary (Police), met the three Election Commissioners to discuss the deployment of forces for polls and the security situation.

The EC is weighing its options of: conducting polls on time and providing a forum for political activity, hoping that the ferment in the state gets channelised; and risking a disastrous turnout, which the EC, credited with holding two free and fair elections in the Valley, does not like to have to its credit.

Given the level of preparedness on the part of security forces required, there is a view that it may be a better option to conduct the exercise at one go with the Lok Sabha polls, instead of mounting the same preparations twice over in less than six months.

After the thwarting of its "freedom march" by security forces on October 6, the Hurriyat has declared that it will give a call for its "freedom march" to Lal Chowk on the first day of the poll.
