Heading: Kalapani martyr’s memorial lost in filth - Indian Express
Content:
Though the police are tightlipped about the involvement of Mohit Sharma, sources said he has been arrested and the booty has been recovered from him. Mohit runs a jewellery showroom on the College Road in the city

In a sensation turnaround in the case of robbery of the Mumbai-based diamond merchant on Thursday evening, a senior police officer's son is allegedly involved in the theft.

Though the police are tightlipped about the case, DIG Jalandhar Range Narinder Pal Singh confirmed that the son of Patiala SSP (Vigilance) Shiv Kumar, Mohit Sharma, is involved in the theft that took place near Phillaur. The SSP, when asked about it feigned ignorance and said he does not know anything about it.

Mohit, who runs a diamond jewellery showroom on the College Road here, however, has been arrested and the diamonds have been recovered from him.

Bhupesh Shah was looted of diamonds worth Rs 1.5 crore by some unidentified people when he was on his way from Ludhiana to Amritsar in a taxi hired from the city.

The merchant had come from Mumbai for a business transaction and was staying in a hotel on the Ferozepur Road here.

However, when they neared Phillaur, the taxi driver stopped to relieve himself.

Bhupesh Shah is said to have restrained him to stop there as he saw few men standing suspiciously but the driver stopped the car nevertheless. As the driver went out, four people attacked him with sharp-edged weapons. They fled from the scene after injuring him along with the taxi driver in the same car.

Heading: PEC convocation: 323 awarded degrees - Indian Express
Content:
In 2005, Maha Sabha— a non-governmental organisation — took upon itself the task of cleaning 1.25 acre garbage dump in Sunet village.

The aim was to make a memorial trust at the site in the memory of Baba Bhan Singh, a resident of the village who was deported to Andaman and Nicobar in 1915 following his involvement in the Lahore conspiracy. Bhan Singh died while serving the kalapani sentence and his name is still mentioned in the list of martyrs at the Cellular Jail.

Though a green belt had been developed at the site after collecting voluntary donations, the change was short lived.

The residents and even the MC staff are using the area next to this memorial as a garbage dump since 2005. Despite repeated complaints by the Maha Sabha members, authorities have not bothered to remove the garbage.

Though the land belongs to the Ludhiana Improvement Trust, MC staff throw the garbage after collecting it from various colonies. Col J S Brar, President, Maha Sabha said, "Not only the residents but even villagers also throw garbage near the memorial site. We have written to the MC authorities a number of times but to no avail. We have already cleared a huge dump from one site and now another has come up at a nearby place."

Area councilllor KL Chabra said, "The garbage is spilled by the villagers and MC staff. But health officers are not looking at this problem and are not providing a proper garbage dump site. Not even a bin has been placed at the site. I have complained to them in writing a number of times but no action has been taken. The authorities should feel ashamed of the way they are disrespecting a martyr."

Heading: Citadel of peace - Indian Express
Content:
"We have now come to a stage where to remain competitive, the mantra is innovation," said Satish Kumar Kaura, chairman and managing director, Samtel Colour Ltd, who was the chief guest for the convocation held at the Punjab Engineering College (PEC) on Saturday. Jarnail Singh, secretary, Border Management, MHA Government of India was the guest of honour.

Kaura congratulated the 323 students who were conferred with their respective degrees. He emphasised that there is enough talent in the country and if students have the will and commitment, they can take on any challenge.

The Training and Placement Cell of the college shared its achievements where they stated that in the year 2008-09, a total of 66 companies had visited the campus.

While addressing the graduates, chairman of the Board of Governors of PEC (Deemed University) Chandra Mohan said "Two decades of grooming by your parents and teachers is all a preparation to enable you to soar into the blue skies of the world on your own. No sacrifice is too great. No roadblock can hold you. Working for it gives you endless satisfaction." Professor Manoj Datta, director, PEC, expressed his gratitude towards the Chandigarh Administration for adopting a positive approach in tackling the problems of the college.

He also acknowledged the faith shown by industries in the students of the college.

Heading: The cross I bear - Indian Express
Content:
After sending peace envoys across the city, Mumbai's first Jain temple decks up for its 200th anniversary

Amidst the clutter of the noisy and crowded Bora Bazaar Street at Fort, the powdery white Shri Shantinath Jain Mandir stands out. The blue wooden windowsills and the under-renovation façade, with hints of bright hues, do not give away the fact that it is the first Jain temple of Mumbai and that it completes 200 years this month.

As I enter the massive premises, I am ushered to Munishri Jay Prabh Vijayji Maharaj, a saint and one of the caretakers of the Shantinath Mandir, with strict instructions to "keep safe distance" from him "as the religion does not allow them to touch a woman". He greets me with a benign smile and the story of this ancient temple unfolds thereafter.

The Jain community forms an integral part of Mumbai. Historical accounts ascribe the tentative date of early Jain settlements in the city to the late 18th century. But the establishment of Shri Shantinath Jain Mandir in 1809 was a turning point in the history of the community in Mumbai. The community has since flourished and today forms nearly five per cent of its population.

The foundation of the temple was laid by Sheth Moti Shah, a prosperous Jain businessman from Gujarat. The earlier settlers of the community were concentrated near Bora Bazaar in Fort. However, despite having moved to Mumbai for over a decade, the Jains did not have any place of worship. "This inspired Moti Sheth and he constructed a small temple in a wooden shack at Bora Bazaar and dedicated it to Shri Shantinath Bhagwan, the 16th of the 24 Jain deities," explains the Maharaj.

Development of the temple to what it is today—a three-storey structure—happened gradually. The temple structure that stands today, however, is 120 years old. With renovation of the interiors as well as the exteriors underway, the temple will hardly look a day old when ready in January for its anniversary celebrations.

The temple has had a glorious history as most significant and popular Jain acharyas in Mumbai have been associated with it. The Maharaj, who prefers to be referred to as JP Guruji by all, also believes that the peaceful neighbourhood can be attributed to the deity of the temple, who represents tranquility in Jainism.

To mark the 200 glorious years, the temple has grand celebration plans. On the auspicious day of Dussehra, the temple trust sent out a group of peace envoys to all major religious institutions in Mumbai. "In wake of the recent incidences of violence and terrorism, we wish the city well and would like to pass on the blessings from our Gods on to every religion," says JP Guruji as he switches from chaste Hindi to fluent English.

The peace envoys will cover 200 places of worship of all faiths, including the Siddhivinayak Temple, Haji Ali and other significant temples, mosques, churches and agiaries of the city, over 20 days. "When our envoys visited the Bora Bazaar mosque, they were given a grand welcome and were invited for their anniversary celebrations in the forthcoming years. Religious discord is only in the head of a few miscreants," asserts the caretaker.

Apart from the peace drive, a 16-day religious celebration in January is on the itinerary, where the guest list will include President Pratibha Patil, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and important Jain businessmen in India.

As JP Guruji hands over an invite for the celebration, a young disciple walks in to inform him of the long queue of followers waiting outside to meet him. As he excuses himself, he gives me his signature smile and his blessings in the form of chandan powder that he sprinkles over my head that leaves me smelling good all day long.

Heading: Splurge and splash - Indian Express
Content:
The first incidences of violence against Christians in India broke out in parts of Karnataka. They started in August and have, over two months, spread across the state and spilled over to Orissa, affecting thousands across the country. I am one of the victims.

I am a Hindu girl married to a Catholic, and, I must admit, I consider myself quite an example of marital bliss. Every time my friends enquire about my "equation" with in-laws, I have nothing but good to say. I am as much the apple of their eye as their bratty son is. What maybe works for us as a family is the fact that we respect every member's individuality and, at the same time, have the ability to laugh at ourselves.

But something has changed over the last few days—ever since the news of the senseless violence broke out. My in-laws are still their loving and jovial self; it is me who has changed. Mornings are no more spent in friendly banter. The arrival of the newspapers which would earlier spark off news debates now marks my quiet withdrawal into my bedroom.

Every day has reports of violence against Christians in our country. Their crime? That either they or their forefathers chose Christianity over Hinduism. Over the last two months these villages have continued to burn. And so have I, in shame. My secular heart bleeds as I read of the death of these innocent believers of Jesus. As a Hindu in Christian household, who is treated more than equal in all aspects, I feel responsible.

Despite being religious, my family is sensible enough to understand that not all Hindus share the hatred for Christians as the hooligans have displayed. Yet, somewhere, I feel kinship with the criminals.

I fasted through Navratri and Ma (mum-in-law) made sure there was always something appropriate for me in the kitchen. Though a devout Catholic, she enjoys the odd episode of Mata Ki Chowki. In an attempt to understand my faith, she even followed the eight-day special programme on the show that delved into the significance of Navratri.

Ironically, Navratri felt more like Lent. I mourned for my fellow countrymen who had to give up their lives to keep my faith alive.

I have spent the last few weeks avoiding all discussions about the violence that are likely to take place in our living room. Talks of participating in the peace march for fellow-Christians have made me go red in my face. Last month, when the violence reached Mangalore, I wanted to call a Mangalorean friend's parents (she too, is a Christian — a fact that had never been of any consequence before) to confirm their well-being. Instead, I merely enquired the same over an SMS.

Can someone tell me how I — a Hindu daughter-in-law of a Catholic family, who has retained her faith after marriage — am supposed to react when I read that Christians in Orissa are being forced to convert to Hindusim? The thought, like a demon, refuses to leave me, and the dilemma keeps me somber all day. Yes, it's the cross I have to bear, and, like Jesus, it has been inflicted upon me by people who I used to call my own.

(diptinagpaul@gmail.com)

Heading: New releases - Indian Express
Content:
The rains are gone and it's time for those super Sunday swim and brunches

Artist David Hockney knew what he was talking about when he painted the masterpiece The Splash (1967) that fetched 2.6 million pounds at Sotheby's London auction in 2006.

Dedicated to hedonism and languid afternoons, the work encapsulates everything that an urban soul trapped in the circle of life craves for.

Lying on one's back, looking up at the sky and floating in a mercifully cool pool of aqua is the best way to forget the anthill that is Mumbai, its denizens and the infernal traffic. As you reach for a beer and snack on some plump buffalo fries, you can feel like a million bucks, without actually spending that amount. Welcome to Sunday brunches by the poolside, pampering at a spa and a quick invigorating dip in the pool.

You don't have to be a millionaire or a member to take a dive and splash around. Many of Mumbai's suburban hotels offer Sunday brunch at the poolside and a dip—provided you're willing to risk the warning of 'no lifeguard on duty' at some of the venues like The Orchid. Although Sea Princess in Juhu offers not only a lifeguard but swimming lessons: The brunch and pool package is at an affordable Rs 800, while the swimming lessons are Rs 4,000 for a three-week course.

The Shanti Spa package of Trident, Nariman Point, is a bit higher up in price range and style statement. It offers a weekend spa package for Rs 9,000 (single) and Rs 12,000 (couple) where everything from breakfast, the pool, the gym and the spa is at your fingertips. "Frequent flyers, business travellers and well-heeled Mumbaikars like to avail of the facilities that we have to offer on the weekend. It's a good way to unwind, with a sauna, a dip in the pool or just order in and chill in our luxury rooms that come with the package," says Devendra Bharma, executive vice president, Oberoi Hotels.

"I've done Sunday brunch and gone swimming, but usually these are separate activities," says model Nina Manuel with a laugh. Privacy is naturally on top of the list for this diva and she prefers to take a dip with friends around in a more exclusive space like the JW Marriott, the Sun 'n' Sand and the uber elite Breach Candy Club. Jesse Randhawa is another model who frequents the pool at the Marriott. "I like the poolside there because it faces the beach and it's really peaceful, besides I have a membership there," she says.

Biggies like Shah Rukh Khan and Aamir Khan have their own pools. So chances of spotting them in their Vilebrequin trunks are few. But you may see a few demigods like Upen Patel and Dino Morea sporting their Adonis bodies at similar venues.

If not too keen to wet your toes, there's always a sumptuous buffet on offer.

Heading: Three-cheers for Mumbai FC - Indian Express
Content:
Dead ringer
Hello
One night in a call centre, there comes a phone call. Really, a phone call in a call centre, cries Salman Khan (playing himself), in mock amazement. Pretty laptop-toting story-teller (Katrina Kaif) smiles mysteriously, and begins her yarn. And as yarns go, it isn't too bad. The trouble with Hello, based on Chetan Bhagat's mega-seller, is that isn't too good either.
It's a dark rainy night, and Shyam aka Sam (Sharman Joshi) is hurting because the love of his life Priyanka (Gul Panag) has said yes to a rich NRI. Varun aka Vrroom (Sohail Khan) has his eye on Esha (Isha Koppikar), but all she wants is to become a model. Radhika (Amrita Arora) tries to please her horrible mom-in-law by day, and pops anti-depressants by night because her husband is a two-timing cad. And Military Uncle (Sharat Saxena) is upset because his US-based son wants to have nothing to do with him.
These sad sack call-centre agents rattle around in a large room with work stations placed miles apart. That's a total wrong number. Except for a barmy systems guy, and smarmy boss (Dalip Tahil), there doesn't seem to be a soul else in Atul Agnihotri's scheme of things: He's clearly not aware of all those rows and rows of super-busy souls—sitting elbow-to-elbow, nattering the night away on their headphones and mikes—that seem to be more the norm in these nocturnal work hives echoing with faux American accents.
You could also call Hello a case of six characters in search of a zingy script. Bhagat's novel is not literature, but manages to capture some of the hurly-hurly of New India's preoccupation with instant money, getting ahead and greenbacks. The film's canvas is largely empty, so the good turn by Sharman Joshi gets lost. As does some genuinely funny banter and the Khan family's full turn-out (Salman with his shirt off, girlfriend Kat in a cameo, bhai Arbaaz in a walk-on) on account of Agnihotri being the Khans' brother-in-law.
Even that thing that call centre types are allegedly indulging in all the time—making out on down-time in the back of convenient SUVs , pictured here on Sharman and Gul-lacks fire. It's tepid, just like the movie.
SHUBHRA GUPTA

Savior or sinner?
Babylon AD
IN Babylon AD Vin Diesel, the slowest-moving action hero in movies, travels over land and under water from somewhere in the former Soviet Union to New York City in the company of a nun (Michelle Yeoh) and a young woman named Aurora (Mélanie Thierry). Aurora is either some kind of biological weapon or some kind of messianic figure. Our judgments, in any case, may be superfluous, since the director, Mathieu Kassovitz, has already publicly described it as "pure violence and stupidity".
He did not mean that in a good way, and while I hate to contradict an artist's assessment of his own work—Kassovitz blames 20th Century Fox for compromising his political and metaphysical vision—a purely violent and stupid film might have been kind of fun. This one, while it has some nice futuristic design touches (including grubby East Bloc housing projects and a splendidly renovated Harlem brownstone), combines badly executed action sequences with mystic mumbo-jumbo that I suspect not even a two-disc Director's Cut DVD could make comprehensible.
AO SCOTT/NYT

An Animated Force
Star Wars: The Clone Wars
EXPECTATIONS were set so low by George Lucas's lousy trilogy of Star Wars prequels that the latest from the Lucas film factory, a feature-length digital animation called Star Wars: The Clone Wars, comes as something of a surprise: it isn't the most painful movie of the year.
As a mechanical thrill ride, however, The Clone Wars has an uncluttered look and furious pace that make it more or less as satisfying as its wildly over-designed predecessors, although it's neither as agile nor as well made as the terrific series of short, animated Clone Wars installments shown on the Cartoon Network from 2003 to 2005.
The director, Dave Filoni, has cited Thunderbirds, the 1960s British animation series with marionettes, as an inspiration for the, uh, wooden style of his picture, but the stiff, self-important characterisations; corny space-war talk; and overheated militarism kept reminding me of Team America: World Police.
NATHAN LEE/NYT

Tying Knots
The Edge of Heaven
THERE are six principal characters in The Edge of Heaven: two mothers, two daughters, a father and a son, all arranged in more or less symmetrical pairs. In the course of this extraordinary film by the German writer-director Fatih Akin children are lost, lost parents are never found, and generational and geographical distances grow wider. At the beginning, Yeter (Nursel Kose), a Turkish woman who works as a prostitute in Bremen, Germany, is confronted by two menacing enforcers of Islamic morality, who demand that she renounce her sinful ways. "I repent," she says through gritted teeth, and though her words are more a rebuke than an apology, they establish one of Akin's themes.
Toward the end of the film, Yeter's daughter, Ayten (Nurgul Yesilcay), is confronted by Susanne (Hanna Schygulla), a German woman (the mother of Ayten's lover, Lotte) who has suffered a terrible loss, brought about partly by Ayten's actions. Speaking no German, Ayten tries to express her overwhelming remorse in rudimentary English. Forgiven is the only word she can find, as if she is offering absolution instead of asking for it.
AOS

Divorce of sensibility
The Accidental Husband
THE toughest genre of filmmaking is a rom-com. Yet it is oft-tried, for the gob-smacking successes of films like Pretty Woman, The Wedding Singer and Love Actually have made Hollywood mush-o avaricious. But what often comes out is pure cheesecake, and that is the case with Griffin Dunne's (Frasier, Saturday Night Live, Law & Order: Criminal Intent) The Accidental Husband.
In a role reversal of The Truth About Cats and Dogs (but nowhere near its charm), radio show hostess and author Uma Thurman (shrieking) is love guru called Dr Emma Lloyd famous for her black-and-white approach to love. Her fiancé and publisher Richard (Colin Firth, wasted) is a straightjacket she finds comfort in until she finds herself accidentally married to a fireman, Patrick Sullivan (Jeffrey Dean Morgan, Grey's Anatomy). What happens next is anybody's guess, but there's an excellent cameo by Isabella Rossellini and a terrible no-speaking role for my friend Sarita Choudhary.
Yes, there's a kitschy Indian family to add to the inanity, but you'd rather stay home with the spouse and eat khichdi.
NAMRATA SHARMA ZAKARIA

Heading: Air-India claim kabaddi title - Indian Express
Content:
Local minnows down Mahindra United 1-0

If it is an impact that Mumbai FC wanted to create on the city's football scene that is exactly what they did on Saturday as they dealt local giants Mahindra United their third straight defeat in the ONGC I-league.

Through their narrow 1-0 win, the giant-killers not only added the jeepmen to their growing list of slain opponents, which already includes Kolkata's Mohun Bagan and East Bengal in their opening two games. But they also won the hearts and adulation of the packed crowd at Cooperage, which seemed to be engulfed in a sea of yellow.

The winning goal may have come in the 23rd minute from the boot of mid-fielder K Kulothungan, when he scored from close range off a cross from Subhas Chakraborty. But the real match-winner for Mumbai FC proved to be Ghanian defender James Dissiramah, who deservingly was named the man-of-the-match. Dissiramah was instrumental in breaking down a number of Mahindra attacks, especially late in the second-half when Sushil Kumar Singh entered the fray, replacing an out-of-sorts Nigerian striker Edeh Chidi.

The 24-year-old Ghanian, who has played in the Maldives and in Thailand under team-coach David Booth, revealed that it was crucial to go a goal up early, especially against a stronger opponent. "We beat East Bengal with a similar tactic, and I am very happy that we were successful yet again," he said. He revealed that he was surprised by the crowd support that his team received at Cooperage.

Team manager Henry Menezes had predicted in the build-up to the game that he expected a number of yellow jerseys representing Mumbai FC at the ground and he was proven right, as every move by the newcomers was followed by drum-beats and music from the stands.

Surprisingly, Mahindra coach Derek Pereira said his team dished out a better show compared to their previous two outings which they had lost. "I must say we are going through a bad patch. It happens with every team. I feel our boys played well today but poor finishing did them in. We definitely had our chances but somehow or the other we failed to convert them," observed Pereira. "We still have a long way to go with so many matches still left. I hope we will bounce back,"he added.

Booth said that he was happy with the way things were going. "To collect three more points feels good but we have to take every match as a learning experience. Let any opposition be there but we have to play to our potential if we need to keep the momentum."

Mumbai FC, who find themselves on top of the league table, now go on to meet defending I-league champions Dempo in Goa. And after seeing three of the country's most established teams being clinically finished off, the Goans may well be wary of the giant-killing newcomers, who are headed their way next.

Heading: Maharashtra Police gun down Customs - Indian Express
Content:
TOP contenders Air-India destroyed an off-colour Western Railway 33-13 to claim the Rajaram Sheth Lad Gold Cup in the Shivneri's Sewa Mandal-URL Foundation Kabaddi Festival at Dadar on Saturday. The Gold Cup final proved to be an anticlimax as the other three finals played earlier in the day seemed to give the spectators their money's worth.

In the Radha Lad Cup for women, Shivshakti avenged last year's loss by beating Veer Jijamata 14-12. Suvarna Bartakke, with her all round abilities, saw Shivshakti through, and also went on to be adjudged the best player in the tournament. The Gold Cup final was expected to be a close one and the initial phase saw both the teams live up to their respective reputations. Gaurav Shetty drew first blood for Air-India and Ravi Radke responded for the railmen. Radke had had Shetty and Pankaj out in one raid. Down 5-10, after Ajay Thakur scalped three in one raid, Western came back to trap international Dinesh Kumar.

It helped them claw back to 9-13 at the interval and remain within striking distance of their rivals. The failure of Kunal Yadav in attack started hurting Western thereafter and their woes were compounded as Ajay Thakur struck splendid form for Air-India.

The lean and lanky raider showed excellent technique to toe-touch the rival corner defenders and once even got three rivals out in a raid. Kumar, not to be left behind got three and two opponents out in successive raids to put his side in cruise mode. At 26-11 with five minutes left the match was reduced to a formality. Air-India gave the second 'lona'and finished the issue off 33-13.

Shivshakti seemed determined to erase last year's bad memories as they set out to avenge their loss to Veer Jijamata. And they succeeded in their venture, despite the loss of international Meghali Korgaonkar to Dr Shirodkar club and the absence of Gauri Wadekar.

Heading: Phenomenale for Pune Derby - Indian Express
Content:
Maharashtra State Police (MSP) scored their first win in three games, beating Mumbai Customs 3-1 in a Group B match of the MFL Elite Division Football League at the RCF Sports Club ground in Chembur on Saturday. Azhar Shaikh was declared the Budweiser man-of-the-match.

The policemen combined well today and in the 8th minute of play were awarded a penalty, thanks to a dangerous tackle by Customs'stopper and senior citizen Milton Fernando. Parag Sawant easily converted to put MSP one up. Reduced to 10 men after Fernando was red-carded, Customs showed a lack of application when their left back gave away a ball to Santosh Telang, who cleverly relayed it to Azhar Shaikh. The latter ran into the box and seeing goalkeeper Bunty Dhiman on top of the box chipped the ball into the far corner of the goal. MSP were two up in the 26th minute.

Mumbai Customs substituted Dhiman with Adhish Maity, who initiated a move in the 59th minute that resulted in Customs'first goal. Maity passed to the right back Gautam Sardar, who in turn sent in a long ball to Sandeep Nadar. Azhar Shaikh scored his second goal in the 81st minute.

Heading: Big B hospitalised on birthday - Indian Express
Content:

Heading: Bachchan has many projects lined up - Indian Express
Content:
Bachchan, who turned 66, is stable, under observation; suspected to be suffering from sub-acute intestinal obstruction, incisional hernia

Bollywood superstar Amitabh Bachchan, who turned 66 on Saturday, was rushed to Nanavati hospital in Vile Parle this morning after he complained of acute abdominal pain late on Friday night. After preliminary investigations he was shifted to Lilavati Hospital in Bandra where he is under observation.

Bachchan's son Abhishek later said that the actor is stable and doctors have advised him to remain in hospital for at least two days. "Right now he is under medication. He is responding well to medication. He will be in the hospital for 48 to 72 hours. There is slight improvement in his condition. He will be in the hospital for at least 48 hours," Abhishek told reporters.

Lilavati Hospital spokesman Mohanrajan said, "There is no cause for worry or concern. We are giving him the best possible treatment. He will soon be up and above and go back to work." Bachchan has undergone blood investigation and CT scan of the abdomen and reports are awaited, a bulletin read by Mohanranjan said.

Sources said the superstar is suspected to be suffering from sub-acute intestinal obstruction as well as incisional hernia. An incisional hernia is known to occur due to an incompletely healed surgical wound. In 2005, Bachchan was operated for Diverticulitis, a problem of the small intestine.

Hospital sources also said that Bachchan had been put on nasogastric intubation, also called suck and drip treatment, a process involving the insertion of a plastic tube through the nose for feeding and for administering drugs.

According to an earlier statement released by the hospital, "Mr Amitabh Bachchan has been admitted to Lilavati Hospital today afternoon, with a history of abdominal pain, which has been relieved by medicines. The cause of pain is being investigated by a team of doctors. The reports will be available (in the) coming morning. The family - Mrs Jaya Bachchan, Abhishek Bachchan, Aishwarya Rai and other relatives are present at the hospital. Mr Amitabh Bachchan has undergone blood investigation and CT Abdomen, reports of which are awaited. Further treatment will be decided based on the report. Bachchan is admitted on the 11th floor of Lilavati Hospital."

Dr Jayant Barve, the Bachchan family physician, is heading a medical team taking care of Big B. Dr Ashok Hatolkar, medical superintendent of Nanavati Hospital where Bachchan was rushed to first in the morning, said, "The hospital was not informed about his condition. He came to the hospital's radiology department for abdominal CT scan and the Bachchan's family physician rushed him to Lilavati Hospital for further treatment."

While coming out of Nanavati Hospital, Bachchan, in a woollen cap and shawl, looked pale but refused to take a wheelchair and walked to the ambulance with son Abhishek, daughter-in-law Aishwarya and daughter Shweta by his side. Family friend and Samajwadi Party leader Amar Singh and other close friends who were due to take part in Bachchan's birthday celebrations visited him in the hospital.

(With inputs from PTI)

MEDICAL HISTORY
* In 1982, Amitabh Bachchan had a near fatal intestinal injury while shooting for a fight scene for the film Coolie in Bangalore. He required an emergency splenectomy and remained critically ill in hospital for months.
* In June 1984, Bachchan was diagnosed with a neuromuscular illness called myasthenia gravis.
* In November 2005, Bachchan was admitted to Lilavati Hospital's ICU after complaints of abdominal pain. He underwent surgery for Diverticulitis, a digestive disease which develops due to the formation of pouches in the small intestine.

Heading: Despite BMC notice, Ambanis yet to pay octroi for aircraft - Indian Express
Content:
Amitabh Bachchan is shooting for three films. He has just started Leena Yadav's Teen Patti and has some portions left for Sujoy Ghosh's Aladdin (where Bachchan plays the Genie) and Shoojit Sircar's Shoebite. He is also committed to projects with Sanjay Leela Bhansali, Ravi Chopra, Pritish Nandy Communications and Rakyesh Mehra.

Moreover Big B's company, AB Corp, is being revamped with a mega budget historical titled The Legend of Kunal to be directed by Dr Chandraprakash Dwivedi. Big B plays the role of King Ashoka in the film. Bachchan has also said that he may soon sign a Hollywood film.

This year, Bachchan's releases like Bhootnath, Sarkar Raj, The Last Lear and God Tussi Great Ho didn't set the screen on fire. The high point of the year has been The Unforgettable Tour. Bachchan, along with Abhishek and Aishwarya, toured 12 cities in four countries — UK, USA, Canada and Trinidad & Tobago — over two months. Bachchan had fallen ill during the concert also, coming down with a viral fever and chest infection during the Los Angeles leg.

The year has not been without controversies. The Bachchans were targeted by Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray during his campaign against migrants from north India earlier this year. Thackeray had hit out at Bachchan saying he was more loyal to his home state of Uttar Pradesh than Maharashtra where he earned fame and riches. He again targeted Jaya Bachchan last month for her remark that she would speak in Hindi at a Bollywood event. While Bachchan rebuffed the allegations on both occasions and proclaimed his love for Mumbai and Maharashtra, he also apologised if Jaya's remarks had hurt Maharashtrians in the latest controversy.

Heading: Women working as waitresses move HC against  restrictions on working hours, allege harassment - Indian Express
Content:
More than a month after the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation issued notices to the Ambani brothers for allegedly evading octroi on the aircraft they bought, officials said that neither of them had paid up and Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Commercial Developers Pvt Ltd had in fact asked the Bombay High Court to quash the notice.

A petition was filed in the court last week and a notice was sent to the Octroi Department which said, "We are not liable to pay octroi as the item (aircraft) is not for consumption, sale and use in Mumbai and therefore it does not attract the Schedule H- Sec 192 (1)".

The petition was filed days after the company had assured BMC that it would pay octroi. Octroi Department officials said that RCPDL executives had met them soon after the octroi evasion notice was served. "They had promised to pay the charges. But now suddenly we were served the notice and a copy of the petition on Friday," said one official who spoke on condition of anonymity. The office of the spokesperson for Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries did not respond to requests for its comments.

On the other hand, Anil Ambani's Reliance Transport and Travel Private Ltd and Global Vectra have also promised to pay up but are yet to do so, the official added. "We are yet to take a decision on whether both the firms should be charged with penalty along with octroi charges or not. The companies will be informed accordingly," said the official.

On August 29, the BMC had issued notices to three firms for octroi evasion. It included Rs 16 lakh for Mukesh Ambani's Falcon aircraft and Rs 14 lakh for Anil Ambani's Bombardier plane and Rs 4 lakh for a helicopter.

The two aircraft and the helicopter were registered in Delhi but the place of business was recorded as Mumbai and therefore attracted octroi, BMC had said. According to Schedule H- Sec 192 (1) of the octroi rules, "0.1 per cent duty is attracted for airplanes of full kind including helicopters, components, parts and accessories of any of them".

Heading: Lord Khandoba of Jejuri attracts another German for research - Indian Express
Content:
Seeking to be treated on par with their male counterparts, the Womanist Organisation of India and the Bharatiya Bar Girls Union have approached the Bombay High Court to "protect the interests of working women."

The organisations claim that their members, especially women working in restaurants as waitresses, have been "facing extreme harassment from the police" and since they are not able to work and earn a decent living many are being driven to prostitution, thereby putting their own lives and the lives of others at risk.

The members contend that those who have been working as waitresses in restaurants after the ban on dance bars are not being permitted to work or even remain present in the establishments after 9.30 pm and are allegedly harassed and arrested and falsely charged for indecent behaviour, even if they are only having dinner after 9.30 pm.

They are now challenging the restrictions on establishments that stop them from working after 9.30 pm in restaurants and after 8.30 pm in permit rooms where liquor is served, which is contrary to a recent Supreme Court judgement where a similar legislation was held as unconstitutional.

The petitioners argue that authorities are bent upon enlarging the scope of the prohibition on employing women in restaurants and cited an earlier affidavit filed by a DCP in a different case where it was informed that the authorities were planning to amend rules to curb working hours. Therefore, the petitioners are now challenging the validity of section 33 (3) of the Bombay Shops and Establishments Act, 1948, which restricts women from working beyond 9 30 pm.

However, under Section 4 of BSEA, the government can grant exemption to certain establishments. The Petitioners have questioned whether the provisions can be sustained in view of the fact that women are now seen working round the clock on aircraft, in hospitals, call centers and other government establishments.

Their advocate, Vishal Thadani says that the exemption granted to gymkhanas, three-star and above hotels is discriminatory and arbitrary. Citing apex court judgments, the organisations have urged the court to declare the provisions illegal and unconstitutional. The petition will come up for hearing this week.

Heading: Cops look for tempo that carried ‘parcelled’ dead bodies to Kurla station - Indian Express
Content:
Almost three decades after German Indologist Gunther Sontheimer took Lord Khandoba — the king of hunters, warriors and shepherds— on to the world map from the mountains of Jejuri near Pune, a student from the same country has chosen to follow the same path.

Fascinated by Sontheimer's texts and articles spanned over two decades and his study on living folk cultures and traditions of the Hindu civilization, Pablo Marius Holwitt, 25, from Nuensttr in North-West Germany has come down to the small hamlet in Maharashtra to understand the traditions better.

"Khandoba is a very interesting subject. So much has been written about the Lord worldwide, that I decided to get a deeper understanding on him," said Holwitt, who has chosen Lord Khandoba, local rituals and Navratri-Dusshera festivals as his subjects of study.

One of the main rituals in Jejuri include possessing of the devotees' bodies called 'angat yene' in Marathi and is like a body-trance.

"It's a unique experience to see the devotees get possessed. I am not questioning if it's for real or they are acting. The whole act is interesting¿ and, no, I was not frightened," he said, sharing his experiences in Jejuri. The second part of his study would be about what these rituals mean to the devotees, and it will focus on the divination rituals.

Dr Prakash Khandge, head of Mumbai University's Department of Performing Folk Arts, who was friends with Sontheimer owing to same research subjects, said it was encouraging to see students like Holwitt as not many student— local or foreigne— study the Lord anymore. "Sontheimer was pioneer in studying Khandoba and starting the trend abroad, following which many researched on Maharashtra. Now there are very few who study the history of the deity," said Dr Khandge, who is now guiding Holwitt.

Traveling to Jejuri was an experience Holwitt has been waiting for ever since he finalised his study subject. "It was fascinating to see all the texts coming alive in front of my eyes. The temple architecture is beautiful," he said, adding that he is glad to have witnessed the ritual where devotees throw turmeric powder, an offering to Khandoba, in the temple. "I was totally simmered with turmeric powder. This ritual took away all the difference and I became one amongst them," he quipped. "I hope to finish the study by December".

Apart from Jejuri, the tribal Siddhis of Gujarat, mental health in India and Dalits and political movement are the other topics chosen for field study by a group of five students from Westsaelische Wilhelms Universitaet (university) of which Holwitt is a part.

They are in India with the help of Tata Institute of Social Science, Mumbai.

Heading: BJP leader miffed at civic body’s stay on caretaker policy - Indian Express
Content:
The Railway Police at Kurla are on a search for a red-coloured three-wheeler tempo in which two parcels carrying three dead bodies were carried to the Lokmanya Tilak (Kurla) Railway Terminus recently. The tempo driverowner could give a break through in the triple murder case as the cops have still not been able to establish the identity of the dead.

On October 8, the officials at Muzaffarpur railway station in Bihar unloaded two parcels from the Pawan Express that originates from Kurla. As no one came to claim the parcels and the smell started emanating from them, the railway officials became suspicious and opened the parcels, and found inside three bodies — of a 40-year-old man, 35-year-old woman and a four-month-old infant.

"We have tried reaching the tempo drivers/owners through their associations to help us if they have any lead. The identity of the tempo owner/driver will be kept secret and he would also be rewarded," said Vasant Koregaonkar, DCP, Central Railway (CR).

"Since the identities of the dead are yet to be established, we are trying hard to crack the case," he added.

The bodies bore no marks of the external injuries, but the police have registered a case of murder. "We are waiting for the post-mortem report. We have also sent a team to Bihar to look into this matter," Koregaonkar said.

"These parcels classified as 'domestic items' were booked by one Sunil Jha on October 6 at the Kurla Terminus. The owner of the parcel was also travelling in the same train and the parcels were to be unloaded at the Muzaffarpur railway station," said Sriniwas Mudgerikar, chief spokesperson of the CR. The name and address, as per the railway records, turned out to be bogus, the police said.

On how these parcels were loaded without being checked, Mudgerikar said: "We do conduct random checks in case of parcels. But it is practically not possible to check each of them. We also have sniffer dogs who help us in the random checking."

Heading: Fake branded watches worth over Rs 10 cr seized - Indian Express
Content:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's (BMC) decision to issue a stay on the controversial 'caretaker policy' appears to have not gone well with BJP spokesperson and founding member of the NGO 'I Love Mumbai', Shaina NC. The BMC had decided to impose a total stay on adoption of any kind of open space by private bodies last week. Additional Municipal Commissioner R A Rajeev had said, "The state government fears that adopted plots can be converted under the caretaker policy and structures that house facilities like club and gyms can be constructed on it."

Miffed over the BMC's decision, Shaina whose NGO had taken up the development work of the Bandra Talao, said, "We approached the civic body four years ago to undertake the development work of the Bandra Talao. We've discussed our plans in detail with officials of every department in the civic body. The BMC did not have any clue on the condition of this talao," said Shaina. The civic body has now decided to appoint private contractors for the maintenance of open spaces, she said.

"The BMC has all our plans and designs. We fear it will blatantly copy our designs. If it does so, that will be a sheer breach of intellectual property rights. We'll not shy away from taking the legal course. We've spent around 2.5 lakh on the plans and are very serious about this project," said Shaina.

Refuting Shaina's claims, civic officials in the BMC said that there would be no going back in their decision. "These allegations are absolutely baseless. Only the civic body can carry out development work on public properties. Private bodies come to us with development plans, but only we've the authority to carry out the work," said Additional Municipal Commissioner (western suburbs) Kishore Gajbhiye. "We've appointed an architect to work on this project. We can assure that we've not copied any designs," said civic official.

The civic body started conceptualising the development work on the Bandra Talao last month. According to sources, this project would be known as Bandra Talao Revival project. The civic body, however, has not yet chalked out the correct estimation required for the job. BMC's Municipal Architect Nutan Ghogate confirmed the development works.

"We've made the final drawings and appointed structural engineers. The work on the talao will start in two months," said Ghogate. She also said she was unaware of the controversy revolving around the talao, but confirmed that the drawings were original. "I'm not aware of any accusations. Our plans are original ," added Ghogate.

Heading: Religious intolerance, a threat to the world: Pratibha Patil - Indian Express
Content:
Acting on an information received from the Enforcement of Intellectual Property Rights (EIPR), the MRA Marg police on Saturday raided four shops in the Musafirkhana area in South Mumbai and seized watches with fake brands worth over Rs 10 crore.

According to DCP (Zone 1) Vishwas Nangre-Patil, they had got information that watches bearing fake brand names were being sold in a few shops in the Musafirkhana area. "Sale of such items bearing fake world-famous brands violates the copyright laws. So, we formed teams of policemen and along with agents of the EIFR, raided the four shops. From the shops, we seized 448 watches bearing fake labels of renowned brands like Rolex, Cartier, Mont-Blanc, Vacheron, Piaget and others. We have also arrested four persons for selling the watches," Nangre-Patil said.

The arrested accused have been identified as Rakesh Jain (27), Fayyaz Tahir (32), Mohammad Nasir Shaikh (19) and Mohammad Mehmuddin Shaikh (32). "These four will be charged with cheating under the Indian Penal Code and also under provisions of the Copyright Act and would be produced them before the magistrate's court," the DCP said.

He said the seized watches, worth about Rs 10,04,51,000, would be used as evidence during the trial and shall be destroyed in accordance with the law once the formalities are over.

"The four arrested are merely the foot-soldiers of such operations. We are conducting further enquiries to trace the identities and whereabouts of the persons who actually run such rackets in the city," he added.

Heading: Youth murdered in Kothrud - Indian Express
Content:
President Pratibha Patil called for cooperation and coordintation between countries to fight the ills of religious intolerance at the Sant Shree Gulabrao Maharaj Sahitya Sammelan in Alandi.

Patil said that Alandi will become the centre of knowledge as the temple of Sant Gulabrao Maharaj — being constructed by Shree Sant Gulabrao Maharaj Sarvodaya Trust — will house a library, research center, hostels."

"Western nations have a materialistic outlook towards life. But they seek India when they want to look beyond materialism. Hence, it is necessary that the books and the teachings of Sant Gulabarao Maharaj should be transalated into various languages.

In a lifespan of 34 years (1881 to 1915), Gulabarao wrote more than 130 books, 2,099 abhangs, 2,252 pade, 1,250 songs, 23,000 ovi sankhya and thousands of shloks and poems.

The president also visited the shrine of Sant Tukaram Maharaj in Dehu Road on the occasion of his 400th birth anniversary. Speaking at a function here the President said, "The abhangs of Sant Tukaram are still relevant. The over 4,500 abhangs written by Tukaram Maharaj touches the soul of Marathi society."

On the occasion, Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh announced a grant of Rs 15 lakh to publish the writings of Sant Tukaram which can be made available to the general public at a subsidised price.

He also announced that the state government will spend about Rs 434 crore in the next three years for the development of pilgrim centers of Dehu and Alandi.

Energy Minister Dilip Walse-Patil, Devisingh Shekhawat, Governor S C Jamir, Guardian Minister Ajit Pawar, Pimpri- Chinchwad mayor Aparna Doke, and Pune mayor Rajlaxmi Bhonsale were also present at both the functions.

CM assures warkaris

Commenting on the Dow issue Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh said "No decision on the issue will be taken without considering the opinion of the warkaris.

'Man-woman equality should be inculcated in young minds'Eulogising the contribution made by Sadhana, a Marathi weekly and its founder and freedom fighter Sane Guruji, Pratibha Patil on Saturday said that the message of man-woman equality and other values that protagonist Shyam's mother instills in Shyam's mind in the book Shyamchi Aai, is the lesson that should be inculcated in today's young minds right from the primary education.

She was speaking at the closing ceremony of Sadhana's diamond jubilee year celebrations. Patil said, "Sadhana is a periodical with a difference and with a different mindset. Putting forth thoughts on the social, political, scientific and other fronts, Sadhana always strived to transform the literates into thoughtful, conscientious and action-oriented people."

She added, "Be it the Bhoodan movement started by Vinoba Bhave, Anandavan created by Baba Amte for the lepers or his son Prakash Amte's work for the tribals in Hemalkasa in Maharashtra or the social causes like de-addiction, rehabilitation of people and fight against superstition, Sadhana has always stood for these causes. It also came forward to help the people in distress during the calamities like floods or tsunami."

Expressing a high regard for Sane Guruji and his writings, president said, "Shyamchi Aai is a kind of hymn sung by a son about his mother. The book depicts how a mother from a meager family instills good values in his son's mind, which should be followed in young minds in the primary education today."

Chief minister Vilasrao Deshmukh said, "Now, when the magazines and the media bacame commercial to run a thought-provoking magazine like Sadhana is in itself quite creditable." He announced to hand over the remaining Rs 50 lakh to Sadhana, out of the total Rs 100 cr.

Heading: Opening his second innings in IOC, Kalmadi set to bag 2020 Olympics - Indian Express
Content:
A 19-year-old man was brutally murdered in broad daylight near Prithvi restaurant in Dahanukar colony area on Saturday.

The deceased has been identified as Heera Jayra Pujari, a resident of Gosavi Vasti in Kothrud. The Kothrud police have booked eight youngsters including Dhananjay Chavan for allegedly killing Pujari. Police suspect previous enmity as the cause of murder.

According to the police, due to some past rivalry, Chavan along with seven accomplices attacked Pujari with sharp weapons near Prithvi restaurant around 12 noon. He died on the spot. A local resident called the police at around 12.30 pm. Police Inspector Anant Rajeshirke is investigating the case. Search has been launched to nab the suspects.

Heading: Meanwhile, Sena to stage protest during opening ceremony - Indian Express
Content:
MP Suresh Kalmadi was reelected as the president of the Indian Olympic Association during the annual general body meeting of the IOA on Friday.

Speaking about the general body elections Kalmadi said, "All the 33 federations and 27 state representatives were present for the elections. On the occasion, it has been decided that a total of Rs 700 crore has been alloted for the training of athletes for the Commonwealth Games and the 2012 London Olympics. The package includes training for 300 days, out of which 100 days will be done abroad. This way the athletes will get to train under foreign coaches. A new schedule to suit the needs of the athletes will be prepared. This will also include a nutritious diet and better living facilities."

Kalmadi said, "It is important that the third Commonwealth Youth Games go smoothly in Pune. This will help us make a positive bid for the 2020 Olympics. We hope to bring the Olympics to India."

About the national games, Kalmadi said, "The national games will be held in December this year in Ranchi and Jamshedpur. The 2009 national games will be held in Kerela and the 2011 games in Goa. This year onwards, people from the union territories of Diu and Daman will be allowed to participate. Also, athletes from states like Tripura are also welcome to participate. However, the states will not be officially acknowledged."

Speaking about the CYG stadium Kalmadi said, "the training facilities at the stadium are world class. We have had representatives from at least 20-25 countries, asking us to let them use the facilities at the stadium for the 2010 Commonwealth Games. Besides, we plan to make this a world class training ground for our own athletes. We want our local, national and international athletes to train here."

Heading: MCC launches course in dramatics - Indian Express
Content:
Feeling ignored and left out from the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) proceedings, the Shiv Sena is all set to make their presence felt for the games, before President Pratibha Patil, by staging a protest during the opening ceremony at 4.30 pm on Sunday.

In an open declaration to the media, area chief Balasaheb Bhande said that Sena members will gather in huge numbers to protest Indian Olympic Association and chairman of Organising Committee Suresh Kalmadi's high handedness.

Bhande said that none of the Sena members were invited to the installation of the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's statue at the Balewadi sports city last week. We have not received any invitations to the opening ceremony either. He said that Kalmadi had not kept his promises and assurances to the villagers of Mhalunge and Balewadi.

"Kalmadi is showcasing the games as a Congress event. It is an international event with the cooperation of all parties, but he does not acknowledge it,''said Bhande in the letter. All the key members led by Bhande and Sena city chief and key members will protest during the inaugural event.

The event organisers have drawn the ire of Sena members for not being invited to the installation of the statue last week.

Khed MP Shivajirao Adhalrao Patil, Shiv Sena members Sharad Dhamale, Gajanan Babar, PCMC city chief Bhagwan Valhekar, Mulshi taluka chief Gyandev Shedge, area chief Bhande, Mhalunge sarpanch Rekha Padale will participate in the agitation.

Heading: This boxer knows his punch-lines too - Indian Express
Content:
Beijing saw Akhil Kumar fight like a lion to beat world champion Sergey Vodopyanov of Russia in the Bantamweight pre quarterfinals. This 27-year-old Indian made history on Independence Day, giving the country a chance to dream. The¯ senior-most of the Bhiwani boxers can be credited to have started the buzz at Beijing that went on to become a booming victory-song, capped by Vijender Singh's eventual bronze medal.

When asked how he felt after defeating the world champion, Akhil Kumar said he still felt exultant. 'Oh it feels great. Now when I think of that match, I get the same good feeling,' he added.

In the quarter final match that followed, however, it was not his day. "I admit that I lost to a better opponent. When the draw was called I did not have the slightest hope of going all the way to the quarters. That itself was a great achievement," he says.

About his overall experience in Beijing, Akhil had no complaints. "They looked after me very well. Things were completed on time." He compared the response of the officials to a bulb vis-a-vis a tube light. "An incandescent bulb comes on immediately when it is switched on. A tube still flickers. The officials were like the bulb," he quipped.

Speaking about the boxers who would be representing India at the Commonwealth Youth Games in the city, he said, "I am very hopeful about them. They are hard working and I am sure they will perform to the best of their ability. I am very optimistic about the youth of our country. They are now getting good sponsors, so they should put it the required effort on their part."

Akhil and his contemporaries will play a vital part as role models for the youngsters. And he insisted that it was a legacy that needed to be carried forward with the same zeal and commitment. "We have put the country on the international map as far as boxing is concerned. We have carved a path. Now it is up to the youngsters to maintain that pace and create new roads so they carry on the glory. I would love to advise the juniors and give them invaluable tips. At the same time I have not given up learning. I am still seeking knowledge and I welcome any kind of good advice. This much I know though - I will never stay away from boxing. I would like to serve this sport as best as I can," he added.

He is currently training for the World Cup that is scheduled to take place in December. "I started training a little late. It is nobody's fault really. I was getting over the loss of Beijing. It was a bigsetback for me, and I took time out to recover. But I am gearing up now and training is underway. I am very focused," he informed.

What's worth emulating is also his attitude – to not settle for second-best, ever. "According to me there is only one medal, and that is the Gold medal. I admire Abhinav Bindra. He has reached the pinnacle of success. I respect all my co athletes and the effort they put in, but for me it is either gold or nothing," he stressed.

The message he would like to give the readers is, to dream big! "For me a dream is not something you experience after sleeping. For me it is a realization of the hard work and concentration, the sweat and toil and the ambition that comes out of it," he signed off.

Akhil and his contemporaries will play a vital part as role models for the youngsters. And he insisted that it was a legacy that needed to be carried forward with the same zeal and commitment. "We have put the country on the international map as far as boxing is concerned. We have carved a path. Now it is up to the youngsters to maintain that pace and create new roads so they carry on the glory. I would love to advise the juniors and give them invaluable tips. At the same time I have not given up learning. I am still seeking knowledge and I welcome any kind of good advice. This much I know though - I will never stay away from boxing. I would like to serve this sport as best as I can," he added.

He is currently training for the World Cup that is scheduled to take place in December. "I started training a little late. It is nobody's fault really. I was getting over the loss of Beijing. It was a big set back for me, and I took time out to recover. But I am gearing up now and training is underway. I am very focused," he informed.

What's worth emulating is also his attitude – to not settle for second-best, ever. "According to me there is only one medal, and that is the Gold medal. I admire Abhinav Bindra. He has reached the pinnacle of success. I respect all my co athletes and the effort they put in, but for me it is either gold or nothing," he stressed.

The message he would like to give the readers is, to dream big! "For me a dream is not something you experience after sleeping. For me it is a realization of the hard work and concentration, the sweat and toil and the ambition that comes out of it," he signed off.

Heading: Dead ringer - Indian Express
Content:
In a unique collaboration with the City University of New York (CUNY) School of Law, Symbiosis Law School (SLS) on Friday announced a programme that will help provide deprived people in the society an access to justice. Primarily the programme will provide legal help in cases of juvenile crime, sexual harassment, domestic violence and trafficking. Vidya Yerawadekar, principal director of Symbiosis International University, Shashikala Gurpur, principal of SLS, Fred Rooney, director CUNY School of Law and senior lawyer Ram Jethmalani jointly announced the programme in a press conference on Friday. The programme will provide legal help of senior lawyers to poor people who otherwise cannot afford their fees. "The programme is an extension of the social activities of Symbiosis, which have been going on for years," said Yerawadekar. The CUNY School of Law has been engaged in such kinds of programme for the last ten years. "In New York, more than 70 per cent people remain deprived of legal help due to non-availability of funds. For the last ten years we have been working for these people by providing them the help of senior lawyers to fight their litigations almost free of cost. The same concept will be replicated in Pune," said Rooney. Rooney said the plight of marginalized people in India was not very different from the US.

"Initially, we have identified Pune as our jurisdiction for the activities. Symbiosis Foundation will invest Rs 5 lakh as seed money for the programme. We will go to NGOs for raising funds for the further activities under this programme," said Yerawadekar.

Gurpur said the students of SLS would also get benefited, as they would get a chance to directly participate in the process with the senior lawyers.

Jethmalani said the programme would help raise the degree of respect of legal profession, which is at the lowest watermark in the society.

"In my career, I have fought 80 to 90 per cent of cases almost free of cost. But I did make money from remaining cases. It can be achieved by any lawyer if there is a will," he said.

Heading: Savior or sinner? - Indian Express
Content:
Movie name: Hello

Directed by: Atul Agnihotri

Cast: Katrina Kaif, Arbaaz Khan, Isha Koppikar, Amrita Arora, Sharman Joshi

Showing at: City Pride Satara Road, Fame Akurdi, Mangala, Inox, Gold Adlabs,

E-Square, City Pride Kothrud One night in a call centre, there comes a phone call. Really, a phone call in a call centre, cries Salman Khan (playing himself), in mock amazement. Pretty laptop-toting story-teller (Katrina Kaif) smiles mysteriously, and begins her yarn. And as yarns go, it isn't too bad. The trouble with Hello, based on Chetan Bhagat's mega-seller, is that isn't too good either.

It's a dark rainy night, and Shyam aka Sam (Sharman Joshi) is hurting because the love of his life Priyanka (Gul Panag) has said yes to a rich NRI. Varun aka Vrroom (Sohail Khan) has his eye on Esha (Isha Koppikar), but all she wants is to become a model. Radhika (Amrita Arora) tries to please her horrible mom-in-law by day, and pops anti-depressants by night because her husband is a two-timing cad. And Military Uncle (Sharat Saxena) is upset because his US-based son wants to have nothing to do with him.

These sad sack call-centre agents rattle around in a large room with work stations placed miles apart. That's a total wrong number. Except for a barmy systems guy, and smarmy boss (Dalip Tahil), there doesn't seem to be a soul else in Atul Agnihotri's scheme of things: He's clearly not aware of all those rows and rows of super-busy souls-sitting elbow-to-elbow, nattering the night away on their headphones and mikes-that seem to be more the norm in these nocturnal work hives echoing with faux American accents.

You could also call Hello a case of six characters in search of a zingy script. Bhagat's novel is not literature, but manages to capture some of the hurly-hurly of New India's preoccupation with instant money, getting ahead and greenbacks. The film's canvas is largely empty, so the good turn by Sharman Joshi gets lost. As does some genuinely funny banter and the Khan family's full turn-out (Salman with his shirt off, girlfriend Kat in a cameo, bhai Arbaaz in a walk-on) on account of Agnihotri being the Khans' brother-in-law.

Even that thing that call centre types are allegedly indulging in all the time-making out on down-time in the back of convenient SUVs , pictured here on Sharman and Gul-lacks fire. It's tepid, just like the movie.

Heading: Divorce of sensibility - Indian Express
Content:
Movie name: Babylon A.D

Directed by: Mathieu Kassovitz

Cast: Vin Diesel, Michelle Yeoh

Showing at: City Pride Satara Road, Fame Akurdi, Mangala

In Babylon AD Vin Diesel, the slowest-moving action hero in movies, travels over land and under water from somewhere in the former Soviet Union to New York City in the company of a nun (Michelle Yeoh) and a young woman named Aurora (Mélanie Thierry). Aurora is either some kind of biological weapon or some kind of messianic figure. Our judgments, in any case, may be superfluous, since the director, Mathieu Kassovitz, has already publicly described it as "pure violence and stupidity".

He did not mean that in a good way, and while I hate to contradict an artist's assessment of his own work—Kassovitz blames 20th Century Fox for compromising his political and metaphysical vision—a purely violent and stupid film might have been kind of fun. This one, while it has some nice futuristic design touches (including grubby East Bloc housing projects and a splendidly renovated Harlem brownstone), combines badly executed action sequences with mystic mumbo-jumbo that I suspect not even a two-disc Director's Cut DVD could make comprehensible.

Heading: An Animated Force - Indian Express
Content:
Movie name: The Accidental Husband

Directed by: Griffin Dunne

Cast: Uma Thurman, Colin Firth

Showing at: E-Square, City Pride Kothrud, INOX, Gold Adlabs

The toughest genre of filmmaking if a rom-com yet it is oft-tried, for the gob-smacking successes of films like Pretty Woman, The Wedding Singer and Love Actually have made Hollywood mush-o avaricious. But what often comes out is pure cheesecake, and that is the case with Griffin Dunne's (Frasier, Saturday Night Live, Law & Order: Criminal Intent) The Accidental Husband.

In a role reversal of The Truth About Cats and Dogs (but nowhere near its charm), radio show hostess and author Uma Thurman (shrieking) is love guru called Dr Emma Lloyd famous for her black-and-white approach to love. Her fiancé and publisher Richard (Colin Firth, wasted) is a straightjacket she finds comfort in until she finds herself accidentally married to a fireman, Patrick Sullivan (Jeffrey Dean Morgan, Grey's Anatomy). What happens next is anybody's guess, but there's an excellent cameo by Isabella Rossellini and a terrible no-speaking role for my friend Sarita Choudhry.

Yes, there's a kitschy Indian family to add to the inanity, but you'd rather stay home with the spouse and eat khichdi.

Heading: OF Derby and designers - Indian Express
Content:
As against past, when derby was only about hats and glares, classy styling has come to stay for the biggest day of the racing season

It's racing time again! A time when the sport and glamour combine, as impeccably accoutered men and women stroll the turf. It's the time to show off that classic cut or that daring flair. From the flamboyant to the formal the Nanoli Pune derby today promises to sport a mix of styles and trends.

"I think lighter colours and smart linen and cotton suits is the way to go this time. People have been doing away with fancy frills and elaborate dresses. The look to go for is essentially sporty at such an event", says designer Sushila Gugle, wife of racehorse owner Anil Gugle.

Nivedita Sabu on the other hand feels that since derbies have always been about hats and dresses, high heels and pumps its best to stick to traditional derby fashion with a few variations. "Smart informal jackets, linen skirts and one-piece outfits look fantastic on women. Printed, patterned dresses are also very much in vogue. Accessories should be minimal and sophisticated. Like diamonds or a string of pearls."

Neelam Seolekar has decided to go simple and classy this year with a frilly shirt and jeans. " It really depends on the weather. If it's a fine day then I will definitely wear a dress, but if the rainy weather persists then its boots and hats for me." As for accessories, "Well nothing special, just a stylish pair of shades."

Mala Thakkar has decided upon a western ensemble inspired by a chic fashion magazine. "At first we used to put on anything and go for the races, but lately, especially at Panchshil races day and the Poonawallas Millions an element of glamour has seeped in." A beige top of netted material, with pink flowers and scallops, teamed with off-white pants and a matching handbag is what she has chosen to wear. "As for accessories, pearls or stones, not over the top glitter for me," she says.

Shernaz Damaniya will probably be the one with the delicate feminine touch at the Derby. "I might wear this gorgeous Satya Paul sari in aqua green, it has an Om motif and crystals at the shoulder, or maybe a flowing skirt and backless top ensemble by Ritu Kumar. For accessories, I quite like the stone, Eye of the Tiger!"

While for some the weekend is an occasion to glam up, for others it is a time to forget the nitty gritty of the week and relax at the racecourse. " Since there is always such a lot of walking to do I prefer being comfortable first," says Bakhtawar Chinoy, wife of trainer Bezan Chinoy. " I will probably wear trousers with a long shirt and some light jewellery. I really do not like to stand out so I choose something in sober cool colours usually."

Attended by the dashing and the debonair, the stunning and the svelte, The Nanoli Pune Derby, like all derbies, promises to be an event for racing enthusiasts as well as fashion aficionados.

Tough Turf

The most awaited race of the Pune Racing Season, the Nanoli Stud Farm Derby will take place today. The Nanoli Stud Farm, one of the leading stud farms in India is a 250-acre property, located between Mumbai and Pune on the banks of the Indrayani River. Started in 1994 by K N Dhunjibhoy, Nanoli has been sponsoring the Pune Derby since 1996.

This year will be the 25th running of this classic and the stakes have just got bigger. This year there is a record purse of Rs 52.7 lakh for the taking, apart from a host of other prizes worth Rs 2 lakhs to be won. Nanoli itself has increased its contribution to 20 lakhs. As added attraction will be the high-end BMW displayed on the lawns by co sponsors BMW Bavaria Motors.

Although with a small field and just six horses running, the race still promises to be an exciting one. "It is not about the number of horses running but the quality," says Vivek Jain, chairman, marketing, RWITC. "This is a grade 1 race, the only one of its kind this season. Every race takes something out of the horse, since it is strong field with about four or five of the best in the running, there were not many entries."

The Pune monsoon-racing season commenced on 24th July and will end on 25th October with attendance having risen by 10 per cent this season. With elite racing enthusiasts from Mumbai and Pune present, a record audience is expected to cheer home the winner.
