Heading: No child's play - Indian Express
Content:
"Landscapes are not all about mountain, trees and river; the beauty of nature is beyond ones' comprehension. While some find the beauty in meadows and hills, I feel that the strength of nature is more defined in chiseled muscles of a horse,'' says M Narayan, artist, for whom the derby has been a favourite subject for many of his paintings.

The bleak future for full-time artists in India could not dampen his spirit as he gave up on higher education to take up painting full time. "I firmly believe in hard work and confidence. I was never deterred from the fact that artists in India don't get recognition and money. I followed my heart, and by God's grace, I am able to secure a satisfied life for my family. Faith sets everything right," feels Narayan.

When asked about his dedication to the four-legged miracle, as he calls it, he says, "We all evolve with time. Even I had started with landscape but later I realised that I am game for painting horses in motion. Rural India and Mother Teresa are also among my favourite subjects. All of them are an epitome of inner beauty. This love for horses not only satisfied my artistic urges but also gave an identity to me among the derby crowd. This has taken me across borders."

After attaining a diploma in fine arts from Bangalore, Narayan started his career in 1991 in Pune. He sold his first painting of a landscape for Rs 10,000 in 1992, while his latest painting of a horse race went for a whopping Rs 20 lakh last year.

Narayan's paintings have been on display from October 10 to 12 at the Turf Club. His paintings not only adorn the walls of various clubs and derby lovers' homes, but they have also found a place in Vijay Mallya's luxury ship, claims Narayan.

"Big and bright always attract me. So I moved on from standard to wider and bigger canvas. Bigger canvas gives me full freedom to express my imagination. I am game for bright fiery and earthy hues. Shades of red, orange, yellow attract me the most, as it helps me to express the high level of the energy of the horse. Bold strokes are best matched with bright hues," he says, adding, "I don't confine to any one medium and use all, be it water, oil or acrylic.

Heading: Missing techie back after six months, but  mystery still intact - Indian Express
Content:
Tu Dost Mahya shakes the adults out of their reverie making them realise the impact of their professional life on the kids

She was compelled to confine herself to a revolving chair. And that is where nine-year-old Tanvi let her thoughts go wild. Swirling and swinging on the chair she strived to scatter the feeling of loneliness off her life. For this was the place that triggered a trail of thoughts in her mind making her drift in another world where she conjured her own world of imaginary characters. Painting the plight of single kids in nuclear families will be the play Tu Dost Mahya where two kids come together to voice their opinion loud and clear.

Under a newly acquired name- Kala Kendra, the ex students of Lalit Kala Kendra have come together to stage the play, which is a poignant portrayal of the urge to be loved, bonded and connected. "Children need time, attention and someone to be solely interested in them and their world. In today's urban set up, both the parents work to give a quality life to their children. Families are mostly nuclear. We see many cases of latchkey kids who stay alone at home all day long. They are accustomed to this scenario and it has become a part of their system but they feel lonely from within. That is what we want to bring across from our play," says Vibhawari Deshpande, director and scriptwriter of the play.

For the youngsters to get in the shoes of the kids in order to conceptualise the play was not an easy task. A lot has been put in by the actors to get in the role of the protagonist. 25-year-old Renuka Kulkarni who plays Tanvi in the play had an interesting time doing the groundwork for her role. "For hours I used to recall how my childhood was. I also spoke to the kids I know who live alone on their own. I probed them to find out what they do to pass their time. I spent some time with some of them to observe how they behave then only I got a feel of how to go living the role," shares she.

In one hour 20 minutes, ten actors of the play weave the complicated layers of the dilemma these children face thus exposing the audience to the inner struggle that they experience. What also creates an impact is the final song with which the play ends. The characters make an appeal to the adults to see a child's world through his or her eyes, just once.

(The play will be staged in Delhi on October 13 in NSD's International children's theater festival- Jashn E Bachpan)

Heading: Activist wages a battle for RTI stamps - Indian Express
Content:
Don't know how I went missing, where I was for six months: Meghna Subhedar

Missing IT professional Meghna Subhedar has been found, her reappearance as dramatic as the twists and turns the highly-publicised case had taken. But on how she went missing, Meghna herself is unable to throw any light.

"I don't know how I went missing. I don't remember where I was for the last six months," she told her father in the presence of mediapersons on Saturday.

Her father Mohan Subhedar, who is a doctor in Chhattisgarh, received her call on Friday afternoon from a phone near Pune railway station. He asked her to immediately reach the house of his uncle Vinayak Karkare at Sankalp Society on Paud Road. When Meghna reached the place, she was in shabby clothes. Her father reached Pune on Saturday afternoon.

Meghna was believed dead after her father identified a highly decomposed body found in June on a Goa beach as Meghna's. But her mother had doubts and DNA tests proved the body was not Meghna's. A search for her began afresh after that.

Her father, a well-known ENT specialist in Chhattisgarh, tried to figure out what may have happened to her. He says Meghna used to read a lot of books on "black magic" which may have something to do with it. "After she went missing, we took a look at the books she read. There were some on witchcraft and black magic. Some were on how to disappear'," he said and added,"It may be possible that the books disturbed her mentally." Incidentally, Meghna had written a blog and had posted an article on vampires sometime back.

It seems Meghna had lost her memory. She told her father that someone hit her on the head with a hard object on Friday morning. An injury mark was found on her head. "The whack on the head may have been responsible for her recovering her memory," Mohan said. "She remembered the telephone number. She also remembered where Karkare (the uncle) stayed as she had been to the city several times when she used to work in Pune a couple of years back," he added.

Meghna married a software professional in 2003. Within six months, they were divorced.

Her father denied that she was under tension. "There was no pressure on her. She was a brilliant girl. There was no financial pressure either. She has left several jobs, but we never objected. She left her Bangalore job a few days before she went missing," Mohan said.

Meghna had gone missing on April 11. "She flew from Bangalore on April 10 and reached Mumbai around 11.30 pm. She said she would spend the night in Mumbai and board a train for Chhattisgarh," he said. Early on April 11, Meghna took a taxi to Dadar and on her father's advice, went to CST to board the train. "She again called me saying she would reach Bilaspur around 1.30 next day. But she went missing. Now she does not remember anything," he said.

Her mother Anjali is a gynecologist. Her parents run a nursing home in Chhattisgarh.

On April 14, a missing report was registered with CST Railway police station. Assistant Commissioner Bapu Thombre of Mumbai railway police initiated investigations. Police confirmed she had withdrawn money from ATMs in Mumbai after she went missing. She had withdrawn Rs 15,000 from an ATM in Andheri on April 15. Police found bank account details and CCTV footage from an ICICI ATM in Goa confirming she had withdrawn Rs 15,000 from Goa on April 15.

On June 26, Goa police found a body at Candolim beach, 10 km from Panaji. Meghna's father identified the decomposed body as her daughter's. On June 28, Calangute police registered a case of murder.

But when her mother raised doubts, a DNA test was done. "DNA tests confirmed the body was not Meghna's. Now that she is back, we have informed the Goa police," said Thombre. "Meghna needs medical treatment. Maybe later she may be able to explain how she went missing, where she had been for the last six months and how she turned up in Pune," he added.

Meghna is a relative of state Anti Terrorism Squad (ATS) chief Hemant Karkare who moved the police machinery immediately after knowing that she had called her father on Friday. "Hemant Karkare is not a close relative, but has a family connection with Meghna's father," said Vinayak Karkare.

Meghna had only three rupees on her when she called up her father. "I asked her to reach my uncle's house at Paud road. I don't know how she reached there. She may have begged for money," said her father Mohan Subhedar. "Meghana has a bank balance of about Rs 68,000. But she does not remember her account details. We don't know how she survived for so many days. She is looking malnourished," he added.

His uncle Vinayak Karkare said: "We were waiting for her because her father called us up. Initially we could not identify her because she was in dirty clothes. We let her in after she said she was Meghna." Meghna told mediapersons: "I do remember my father and my family members. I also know my company's name. But I don't know what happened to me."

Heading: Wheelchairs enter ad ring, get noticed - Indian Express
Content:
A stamp from the postal department for making RTI applications less cumbersome is what a city-based social activist, Vihar Durve, has been demanding for over two years now. He had made the appeal in letters sent to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and also the then President APJ Abdul Kalam.

Ahead of the third year of implementation of the Right To Information Act, 2005 (RTI), which came into effect on October 12, Dhurve has sent another letter to President Pratibha Patil and Prime Minister Manmohan Singh.

Durve wants stamps, in the denominations of Rs 10 and Rs 20, to make it easy for people to make use of the RTI.

There being different departments of the Central governments, it is difficult for the common man to understand details of the fee, said Durve. He believes if the stamps are used, objections to an application on the grounds of fees, cannot be raised. "It will make the process uniform and simple for the layman," he said.

As per provisions under the RTI Act, the fee is payable by cash, banker's cheque, bank draft or postal order. It's payable to the accounts officer of the concerned public authority. "Neither bank managers nor post master generals seem aware of this facility. Few postal officers accept the appeals. There is a serious problem in filing the requisition," said Durve, who himself faced problems while filing an RTI application. He has also said that a documentary should be made by the information ministry to create awareness on the RTI Act.

RTI activist Arvind Kejriwal, when contacted, said it was high time the government woke up to this concept that would simplify the process of filing an RTI. "The government should introduce the stamp at the earliest," he said.

Heading: CYG guests fume at chaos, delays on eve of kickoff - Indian Express
Content:
Life has come to a standstill for the Sharma family, after they lost their only son, Ankush (22) in a car accident on Friday night.

Ankush, a resident of Sector 25 in Panchkula, was on his way back home after distributing invitation cards of his friend's marriage, when their Indica car was hit by a speeding Innova near the Mansa Devi T point late on Friday night. The driver of the car, Jasbir Singh was arrested and the vehicle impounded on Saturday.

"My brother was of a very jovial nature and loved me the most. He was going to celebrate his birthday on October 14. We had ordered a cake in advance, but look what was has happened," cried his sister Monica.

Monica added that as it was the marriage of his best friend, Harshit, a resident of Mansa Devi complex, he was helping him to distribute his marriage cards. "Ankush took diesel from the petrol pump near Mansa Devi T point and was going to drop Harshit at his place. The moment they started from the petrol pump, an Innova came from wrong side, which resulted in a head-on collision between the two cars. While the Innova driver fled from the spot, it was Harshit who called in the police and the two were rushed to the General Hospital at Sector 6," said Monica.

Sources added that Ankush was not wearing a seat belt, which led to the steering of the car hit his chest resulting in his death. He was cremated today after the postmortem was conducted at the hospital. Harshit was later discharged.

His family members said that Ankush was into family business and had got engaged recently. He was going to visit Canada soon to meet his fiancée.

Heading: ‘I would have never vied for Indian Idol tag’ - Indian Express
Content:
Himesh Reshammiya got a sexy hairstyle, shaved his chest and got into shape for Karzzz. Still, he can't seem to comprehend why a classic hero must be Adonis-like

Himesh Reshammiya knows that he can never be like Clark Gable or James Dean. He maintains that he isn't an archetypal Hindi film hero, nor can he ever be. This, despite the fact that his second film, Karzzz, is releasing on October 17 with a phenomenal 1,200 prints, there are queues of people waiting to interview him and his film's music is already a sell-out success. "The first criterion of becoming a hero is that you have to be good-looking. That, in itself, disqualifies me," he says.

We aren't going to deliberate on what he looked like earlier, but now, he's got himself a cool new hairstyle, shaved his chest hair and gotten into shape. "You have no idea how tough it has been. I had to go on a strict diet (I didn't work out at all), undergo hair transplant, wear extensions... it was crazy. And still people accuse me of trying to emulate Rishi Kapoor. He is one of the most effortlessly handsome faces of his time. However, I believe that Karzzz is a tribute to Rishi Kapoor from an ardent fan."

With Karzzz, the flashbulbs will be trained on Reshammiya, the actor. "In that sense, Karzzz is my real acting debut. My acting skills will be put to test on October 17. We're treading rather carefully. Bhushan Kumar has spent lots of money to make this film. After careful consideration, we brought the release date forward from December and work is going on at breakneck speed. We're getting ready for the verdict." It's true. Although the 35-year-old has been accepted as entertainer par excellence, he is yet to set the big screen ablaze with histrionics. "This is my attempt to win over my critics," he resolves.

In a creative outburst, he composed the music for Tandoori Nights over a meal of grilled chicken. "I was getting too frustrated controlling my diet, eating boiled, bland and grilled meals. That has found expression in Tandoori Nights. It's doing so well now."

Although Karz, the 1980 original, won Laxmikant- Pyarelal awards, Reshammiya has a feeling that his music may not quite bring home the coveted trophy. "I don't know why I am saying that. I just have a feeling. Anyway, I made Pyarelalji listen to my rendition of Ek Hasina Thi. He loved it. And FYI, I have abandoned my nasal twang in this one, I've sung it normally."

Reshammiya's date book looks quite scribbled in. "I am doing five films, and they are all in the big-budget category. Then, I'm making music for others. I intend to take it easy on films for fear of over-exposure," he says.

Clearly, Reshammiya is the most famous package to come out of Gujarat. He says, "I am a good Gujju boy at home. I refrain from talking about my family because they are media-shy. They are happy being in the background. My 10-year-old, Swayam, is my biggest fan and critic. He's going to give me feedback on Karzzz tonight. You also pray for me, okay?" Okay.

Heading: Arun Jaitley blames UPA for country’s ills - Indian Express
Content:
Funny girl
After winning hearts in the reality show Zara Nachke Dikha, Delnaz Paul, one of the most popular comic actors on Indian television is making an entry in Paani Puri's October 11 episode as Sumeet Raghavan's character, Vikas Puri's childhood friend, Sapna. Her entry will lead to a love triangle. She is doing a running cameo wherein she'll keep making appearances on the show. Talking about her character, Delnaz says, "For the first time, I will be doing a love triangle.
I am playing a Punjabi girl who is full of life." Delnaaz, for whom comedy comes naturally, is coming back to what she does best - tickling the funny bone.

Twists of fate
AFTER sharing sizzling chemistry with her co-host Karan Singh Grover in reality show Zara Nachke Dikha, pretty and petite Shweta Gulati has joined as a new intern on the show Dill Mill Gayee. Shweta will be playing Dr Nikita who goes on to become best bud with Riddhima. Nikita actually enters the hospital when Dr Armaan is away at a conference.
When the two bump into each other after his return, it is revealed that Armaan and Nikita happen to be friends from college days. Obviously audiences are looking forward to see sparks fly once again.

Singing star
REALITY TV star, singer or VJ —how would one describe Anushka Manchanda? The ex-Viva girl has entered yet another reality show, Voice of India 2 in a bid to connect with the audience again, years after she and four other girls won Channel [V]'s Pop Stars. But it's still rough riding for the singer, as the other contestants are not at all happy that she's entered the show midway.
But the lady herself is confident that she can handle the pressure.
My singing will do it for me," she says.

Heading: Congress to hold farmers’ protests against Maya’s land acquisition policy - Indian Express
Content:
Senior BJP leader Arun Jaitley on Saturday blamed the Congress-led UPA government for failing to curb the growing incidents of terror attacks. He also held the Centre for failing to effectively tackle the ongoing global financial crisis.

Jaitley, who was in the state capital to attend a function organised by his party to commemorate the birth anniversary of Jai Prakash Narain, said the failure of the UPA government has caused a sense of insecurity among the people in the country. "We have effectively taken lead to raise questions like rising inflation, terrorism, corruption, the Ganga expressway and Bundelkhand, which have been affecting the lives of the people," he said.

Meanwhile, senior BJP leaders termed the firing incident in Shrawasti "inhuman and state-supported terrorism". The state unit of the BJP has formed a three-member committee to probe the incident.

Heading: Assailant shot dead by police within 24 hrs - Indian Express
Content:
The state unit of the Congress party is all set to counter the ruling Bahujan Samaj Party's development plank by projecting the state government as anti-poor and anti-farmer. Taking the cue from Congress president Sonia Gandhi's recent remarks at a rally in Dadri, the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee (UPCC) will try to hit Chief Minister Mayawati on the issue of land acquisition.

District-level party workers have been asked to garner support from the farmers on the issue. They have also been asked to hold protests demanding changes in the land acquisition policy of the state and to bring it at par with the Haryana government.

At the state-level meeting of "Kisan Khetihar Majdoor" — a wing of the UPCC — that was convened on Saturday by state party president, Rita Bahuguna Joshi, Mayawati was blamed for being partial to farmers' woes. She asked the members of the group to organise mass level protest of farmers in their respective districts, followed by divisional level and state-level mass protest of farmers.

"First in the name of Taj Expressway and then in the name of Ganga Expressway, the state government is making huge money by acting as a middleman between farmers and developers. They are acquiring land at a lowest possible price from farmers. Despite giving the lands to the developers at higher rates both the government, as well as the developers, are making huge profit. It is only the poor farmers who are at loss," Joshi said.

The dates of district-level protests will be decided within next two days. "The protest will take place simultaneously all across the sate," Joshi added.

The Congress party wants the land acquisition policy of UP to be reframed on the lines of Haryana government's policy. "It is surprising to find that while the Haryana government is giving Rs 80 lakh per acre as compensation to the farmers, the UP government pays mere Rs 8 lakh per acre for acquiring land very close to Haryana," Joshi said.

She further said that the Haryana government, which is at present ruled by the Congress party, is paying annuity at the rate of Rs 15,000 to Rs 30,000 per annum for the period of 33 years depending upon the type of land. The farmers are also given a portion of a land to do some small business. "In case the land is being used to set up an industry, at least one member of the family is given job in that industry. All these things are missing in UP," she said.

Pointing towards the land acquisition in Mayawati's native village Badalpur, a senior party leader said that none of the villagers were actually informed about the purpose of land acquisition. 'While the land was actually being acquired to build some recreational centre, farmers were thinking that there will be some industry," he said.

Sonia to visit Rae Barelli
Congress president Sonia Gandhi will be visiting her Lok Sabha constituency Rae Barelli on October 14 to lay the foundation stone of the Rail Coach factory in the Lalganj area of the district. She is scheduled to inspect health camps and health facilities provided by the Life-line train, which began on October 3.

Heading: Global meltdown panic echoes in the corridors of IIM-Lucknow - Indian Express
Content:
Not less than 12 hours since assailants shot down a property dealer in Sarojini Nagar, the police on Saturday morning shot dead the main accused, Jogeshwar Prasad alias Fauji, at Bhagwant Kheda village.

Prasad's nephew, Sandeep, who allegedly was an accomplice in the murder of property dealer Devesh Yadav, was also arrested. The police said Prasad was wanted in around 10 different cases, besides four murder cases, including the Friday night murder. Prasad was carrying a bounty of Rs 10,000.

Late Friday night, four motorcycle-borne miscreants fired indiscriminately at Yadav at Kabristan road in Sarojini Nagar. Yadav had sustained five bullet

wounds and later succumbed to his injuries. The victim's family lodged an FIR at Sarojini Nagar police station naming Prasad and Sandeep for the murder.

According to the police, the two accused fled to Kakori after killing Yadav. Police conducted a search in Kakori and spotted Prasad at his cousin's house in Bhagwant Kheda village. In the ensuing encounter, Prasad was shot dead. A six-round revolver was recovered from his possession.

The police said Prasad's enmity with Yadav over some property issue was the reason behind the latter's murder. Prasad was also accused of murdering Yadav's younger brother Jeevendra in 2006.

"Yadav was to appear as a witness in the same case shortly. Since it was almost confirmed that Prasad would get life imprisonment in the case, to prevent him from appearing in the court, Prasad killed Yadav," said Additional Superintendent of Police, East, Harish Kumar.

Heading: Seat-sharing talks will be sorted out with Congress soon: Mulayam - Indian Express
Content:
The students of the country's B-schools are keeping a close watch on the global financial crisis that was triggered by the problems in the US housing mortgage. Their interest, however, doesn't end here for they are aware of the repurcurssions such a meltdown can have on their placements.

When the discussion moves on to the topic of placements, the management students of IIM-Lucknow seem to be speaking with a desperation in their tones.

This year, five major investment banks will not arrive at the gates of the B-school. "We are not expecting global investment banks, which earlier offered exotic job profiles at international locations, to come for recruitment this time," said Sumit Garg, a second-year student of IIM-L specialising in finance.

Debojyoti Chakraborty, who interned at Lehman Brothers, was expecting a pre-placement offer. But with the firm declaring solvency in the US, he is now looking for other options. "I will look for job opportunities in Indian investment banks such as Edelweiss and Kotak," he said.

The future of the Finance subject, which till this year has been the most coveted specialisation at the B-school with 40 to 50 per cent students of IIM-L's final year opting for it, seems to be bleak. "Now many students may switch over to other specialisations," said Vipul, a professor at IIM-L.

Sharat Chander, a first year student at the institute has decided to choose general management or strategy as his specialisation instead of finance, which was his initial choice. "The current financial crisis made me change my mind about specialising in finance as jobs are going to be scarce in the sector," he said.

Though this may affect the graduates in the coming year, they might not suffer as much as their working counterparts, according to professors. "They will be able to flexibly reorient their career paths," Vipul added.

For those who had set their sights on a career in investment banking, the expert opined that the situation would get better with the passage of time.

Heading: Man’s death triggers violence in Howrah - Indian Express
Content: Former BJP councillor Raghubir Kuchhal was shot dead late evening. According to sources, Kucchal was near his medical store in Vijaynagar Ghaziabad when the two motorcyclists shot at him and fled. As the news spread all the BJP party workers and leaders flooded Yashoda Hospital of Ghaziabad. The wife of the murdered ex-councillor, Bimla Kucchal, is the sitting BJP councillor from Vijaynagar. "Kuchhal was dead when brought to the hospital," doctors said.

Heading: Santoshpur Puja committees block road against ‘police highhandedness’ - Indian Express
Content:
The death of a 40-year-old man sparked violence in the Domjur area of Howrah, about 30 kilometres from Kolkata, on Saturday, as residents vandalised and set on fire a number of shops and houses. They clashed with police and even blocked the Howrah-Amta road for more than four hours.

Angry locals were demanding immediate arrest of the people responsible for the death. The police had to resort to lathicharge and fired tear gas shells to bring the situation under control. Two persons were arrested on charges of rioting.

Local MLA and food processing minister Mohanto Chatterjee said the situation is under control. "Those who were agitating should have given police some more time to arrest the criminals. This vandalism was uncalled for," he said. Chatterjee, however, denied that there was any communal tension in the area. On Friday night, during the immersion procession in Chandimandap area of Makardah in Domjur, Pradip Kurari was killed after a brawl ensued.

The police said Kurari was allegedly beaten to death by people from a neighbouring locality. "He died on the spot," a police officer said.

Locals alleged that Kurari, a resident of Kuraripara, was killed by the residents of Malikpara area.

On Saturday morning, residents of Kuraripara blocked the Amta- Howrah Road, demanding the arrest of the culprits. But no sooner the police tried to clear the road blockade, situation flared up.

Irate mob became violent and started ransacking shops in the adjacent market area. Police said that some of the protestors set ablaze five shops.

"The protestors broke into the house of a local who allegedly led the gang that beat up Pradip. They vandalised the house and another adjacent house," the police officer said.

"The Rapid Action Force (RAF) had to be called in and the police had to fire tear gas shells to control the mob," said Neraj Kumar Singh, Superintendent of Police, Howrah. It took the police more than two hour to bring the situation under control.

"The entire episode started off as a clash between two localities but later it took an ugly turn as a section of people tried to give the incident a communal colour," said a police officer of Domjur police station. Incidentally Domjur is known to be volatile as far as law and order is concerned. About a year ago, the area was affected by communal tension. Shops were set on fire and the administration had to impose Section 144 in the area.

Heading: CPM ready for Lok Sabha polls: Yechury - Indian Express
Content:
Commuters in Santoshpur — located on the southern fringes of Kolkata — had a tough time on Saturday after locals and members of Puja committees in the area blocked th road for over four hours.

The committees alleged that police had lathicharged on their members during the immersion procession on Friday night. The police have, however, denied the allegation.

The Santoshpur Avenue Road remained blocked from 10 am to 2 pm, as members of the local puja committees protested. The road blockade was withdrawn after the police intervened.

Members of the puja committee alleged that 12 people, including women and children, were injured in the police lathicharge. According to them, the injured had to be taken to KPC Medical College and Hospital, Jadavpur, for first aid. Some of the committee members also alleged that they were attacked by the members of Viveknagar Jheel Rakhsha Committee.

One of the injured, Saurav Roy, said: "We had gone to Viveknagar Jheel for idol immersion. Suddenly the Jheel Raksha Committee and the local police started to beat up."

"There were no senior officers at the spot. We do not have any idea as to why we were attacked," said Babul Das Gupta, a member of the Santoshpur Sarvojanin Durgotsav.

South 24 Parganas SP Ajoy Ranade, however, said: "There were enough police personnel deployed at the ghat to maintain law and order. There was no lathi-charge at the site."

Heading: Save Nano committee will meet Governor to bring Tatas home; eager to meet Mamata too - Indian Express
Content:
CPM Politburo member Sitaram Yechury has said that his party is ready for the Lok Sabha elections. Yechury, who arrived in Kolkata on Saturday to attend party's central committee meeting, said that discussion will be held on Sunday's meeting for forming the third alternative.

On the issue of Singur, he said the party will get success in rural areas. "We are ready for the polls. The alliance will be formed that will include non-communal and non-Congress parties," Yechury said.

He said that in spite of the Congress party's plan to highlight the Indo-US nuclear deal as a success story, the party will not gain any extra advantage during the polls.

The top leadership of the CPM is scheduled to discuss several crucial issues, including its strategy for the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections during the three-day central committee meeting, party sources said.

The meeting would also finalise a document on the demands for restructuring Centre-State relations.

Senior party sources said the CPM suspects that the UPA government will try to hold the Lok Sabha elections in January or a little later.

Heading: Big B’s birthday celebration turns sombre as fans pray for his health - Indian Express
Content:
The Save Nano Committee set up by farmers and businessmen in Singur has pinned all hopes on Governor Gopal Krishna Gandhi for bringing back the Tatas. A dharna urging the Tatas to come back to Singur began on Saturday.

Members of the committee will meet the Governor on Monday to request him to step in and save the situation. Sadai Koley, secretary of the newly-formed committee, said they had sought an appointment from the Governor a few days ago, to which he has responded.

"The Governor responded to our appeal and agreed to meet us. We will meet him on Monday evening and request him to ensure that the Nano plant stays in Singur. He had initiated a tripartite meeting to address the Singur impasse. We want a similar initiative from him to save the Nano project."

Koley said the committee members are also willing to meet Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee to request the same. "In the interest of the state, it is the duty of all political parties to stop the Tatas from shifting the Nano plant. We hope Banerjee will agree to talk to us," Koley added.

The committee comprising local unemployed youths, contractors, intellectuals and students had organised a rally at Beraberi — the stronghold of Trinamool Congress backed Singur Krishi Jomi Raksha Committee — on Friday and urged people to support their movement to convince Ratan Tata to change his mind.

"We will organise similar rallies at various other places in Singur," Koley said.

The Save Nano Committee has put up a camp at Ratanpur Crossing near gate number one of the Nano plant demanding that the project be constructed at Singur. "It was most unfortunate for all of us that Ratan Tata had decided to shift the project from Singur at a time when almost 90 per cent of the work was complete. We are trying our best to persuade him to return," the agitators said.

Heading: Power cuts imminent as technical problems affect Santaldih station - Indian Express
Content:
With Amitabh Bachchan admitted in Mumbai's Lilavati Hospital on his birthday, it was probably one of the grimmest birthdays not just for the actor but also for the members of his fan club in Kolkata.

Like most years Big B's fans had planned a special tribute for their ideal. His museum, which was established in 2000, was formally inaugurated on Saturday, after a renovation.

Sanjay Patodia, secretary of the fan club, said: "We had plans to celebrate the birthday in a big way and we performed a puja in the morning with a priest conducting the rituals. But then we got the news of his illness and although his secretary said he was not in grave danger we are praying for his recovery."

The celebrations take place in Mumbai every year with the members doing some charity work. This year, however, Kolkata was selected as the venue. The members also fed 250 underprivileged children in the neighbourhood.

"We always gift him a card and a bouquet but he is most pleased when we celebrate his birthday by doing social work. We spoke to him on Friday night to wish him and he expressed his pleasure at our plans. The museum that we have made is a shrine for us and will have various memorabilia of Bachchan," said Amitabh Guha, treasurer of the club.

After learning about his illness the fans are in constant touch with his secretary and his family in Mumbai.

"We have heard that he will be taken for an endoscopy on Saturday night. We are praying to God that things go well," said Guha. The members also paid a visit to Kalighat in the evening to offer a special prayer for his recovery.

Heading: Boy crushed to death, residents vent ire on buses for overspeeding - Indian Express
Content:
The state could face power outages during this festive season. In a major incident, the conveyor belt of Santaldih power station in Purulia broke down on Friday night. At present only 90 MW is being generated by the plant which has a capacity to produce 480 MW. The existing shortfall in power generation in the state is around 700 MW. Though repair work has started, chances are that the plant will be shut down completely. Santaldih thermal power station GM Sajal Ranjan Roy said: "The conveyor belt which feeds coal to the boiler broke down suddenly last night. These units are 40 years old and such things happen."

According to sources, two of the four units of the Santaldih power station were shut down in the last few days for repair works. After the conveyor belt broke down, the remaining two units are being run on oil, which is not possible for a long time. "If the Santaldih power station is shut down the shortfall will exceed 800 MW and the residents will have to bear the brunt of power cuts," said an official of the state power department.

Heading: With licence in hand, Cash & Carry starts upgrading stock - Indian Express
Content:
Hours after a speeding bus crushed a 14-year-old boy, locals stopped two buses morning and smashed its windscreens after they found that the two vehicles were moving at a high speed and trying to overtake each other while crossing a traffic signal at Khanna on Saturday.

The two private buses — of route 230 and 234 —nearly collided while crossing the traffic signal.

"One of the buses nearly knocked down an old man standing at the crossing," said Samir Pal, local pan shop owner at Khanna. The locals chased and managed to stop both the vehicles, he added. Both the drivers were beaten up. Some of the locals pelted stones at the buses and smashed the glasspanes.

The menace of speeding buses has been haunting the city for a long time. Despite loss of lives and promises for reprieve, there is hardly any improvement. It is often alleged that the on duty policemen simply turn a blind eye to rash driving.

At least 21 people drowned to death in April this year in Kestopur in north Kolkata after a private bus fell into a canal while trying to overtake another bus of the same route.

Heading: City Scapes - Indian Express
Content:
After receiving the APMC licence from the West Bengal government, the German wholesale major Metro Cash & Carry has began upgrading its stock. It would start catering to its clients from its outlet on E M Bypass.

Initially, the wholesale giant is targetting large number of hotels, restaurants, caterers and grocery stores. The company will market the 18,000 stock keeping units (SKUs ) from an area of one lakh square feet. Of the 18,000 articles only 8,000 are food products. The company plans to begin its operations in the next six to eight weeks.

"Many people have registered with us for doing business, even before the licence was issued. It is a continuous process and more people will be joining us, as now the licence has been awarded to the company," said a spokesperson of the German firm.

"Our business model does not involve selling to household customers. It is a business-to-business model which will primarily cater to a wide range of clientele. Metro Cash & Carry clients will be provided with a registration card," said a representative of the firm.

Inspite of the delay caused by the political opposition, hotels and restaurants in the city have welcomed the decision to award the licence to the company. "It will be a great advantage to the hotel industry. Earlier, we used to buy our stocks from different vendors. Now we can procure about 80 to 90 percent of our stock from under one roof. Since a company like Metro Cash & Carry will be supplying the products' quality will be also assured," said R S Singh, vice-president, Operations, Kellinworth Hotels.

"This wholesale facility will help the farmers to market their produce in other states and even outside the country," said Sunderban Development Minister Kanti Ganguly, who had been actively supporting the venture.

The Metro Cash & Carry operations will generate employment for about 1,800 people directly. Other than the company, a large number of people will be involved in transport and preservation of the produce, said the minister.

Though the Forward Bloc-controlled State Agriculture and Marketing Board retracted from its earlier stand by withdrawing the minimum purchase limit of Rs 5,000, they said the party's cadres will be monitoring the activities of the German firm to keep a check on whether they are getting into the retail domain.

"We will keep an account of the stocks of the company and see how much they are buying and selling. We will have our representatives at the counters of the wholesale major to monitor and scrutinise the bills," said Naren Chatterjee, chairman of the Board.

Heading: The Ice Age - Indian Express
Content:
Loud & Clear

Big 92.7 FM goes to campuses with 'Sony Ericsson BIG Loud and Famous Fresher Hunt' contest. Conceptualized as a means to capture the excitement in colleges with the entry of new batch of students, the 'Fresher' contest aims to provide a platform to the freshers to showcase their talent. While the first one in IBS, Mohali, was held on September 8, the contest will now go to DAV College, ITFT, Indo Global campus, Chitkara and a few government colleges of the city. The contest will be simultaneously organised in ten cities — Chandigarh, Kanpur, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Trivandrum, Surat, Udaipur, Agra, Vizag and Amritsar. Students from 15 colleges from each city will participate in the contest. BIG Jock will visit colleges and screen participants through various interesting rounds like talent, IQ, Sony Ericsson Loud, louder and loudest, Streax Funky Hairdo contest, BIG talent and Chal cut ley. RJs will also visit the college campuses and conduct the screening on the same along with live links. While the college finalists will get a funky hairdo from Streax, each winner couple per city gets a Sony Ericsson R300 phone.

Between life and death

Virasat theatre group will present its new play "52min60sec" on 13 and 14 September in Punjab Kala Bhawan 7pm onwards.

Written and directed by Asif Ali, who has been awarded Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puruskar by Sangeet Natak Akademi in the field of playwriting, the play is a story of the last one hour of the lives of six young naxalites in hiding to complete an operation. Their mission is successful and they want to celebrate it. However, the next moment they are surrounded by the army. Confusion sets in the hide out. Army commander gives them a time of 59 minutes 60 seconds to surrender and from here the play progresses in its real time.

Enacted by professional actors the play's thrust is on life not on death.

Heading: On a prowl - Indian Express
Content:
Two Indian girls will accompany UK adventurer Felicity Aston on a gritty expedition to the Antarctic

Thirty-year-old UK adventurer Felicity Aston's love for the polar region started eight years ago, when she was studying physics and astronomy at University College London. She was part of a team sent to map the remains of Viking settlements on the Greenland ice sheet. Though unsuccessful then, she vowed to return. "I looked over my shoulder and promised to cross the ice shelf one day," she says, clad in formal trousers and a shirt. Since then, Aston has the distinction of being the only British woman who's spent three years at a stretch on the Antarctic with a British team that was monitoring climate change. Aston also led the first women's team on a 360-mile endurance challenge across Greenland in 2006.

She is in Delhi to announce team members for the Commonwealth Women's Expedition to the South Pole in 2009. "The ice is addictive and once you get used to the wilderness, it's a different experience altogether," she explains. And if braving sub-zero temperatures, blizzards, walking on thin ice sheet in Siberia without a life line and narrowly missing encounters with polar bears was not enough, Aston now wants to undertake an expedition to Antarctica. "The idea was always lurking in my head. After I finished sixth out of 16 teams in the Greenland Race in 2006, I wanted to spread awareness about the polar region in other countries. This trip will clear all doubts about women not being good at endurance races," says Aston. The expedition will last for 40 days and team members will cover 500 miles, climbing almost 12,000 ft from the edge of Antarctica to the South Pole.

A team of eight women, representing different countries from the Commonwealth — Cyprus, Singapore, Brunei Darussalam, Ghana, Jamaica, New Zealand, India and the UK — will participate in this expedition. On Saturday, after an interview and character assessment, Aston named two Indians, Aparna Ray and Reena Kaushal Dharamshaktu, who have been selected for the adventure. Ray, 27, a lawyer by profession, seems enthusiastic and is looking forward to the challenge. "I have been camping and trekking for many years, but my knowledge of the polar region is only through films and pictures," says Ray. Dharamshaktu, a freelance mountaineering instructor, on the other hand, has an advantage as she has undertaken several trips to Ladakh. "I enrolled for this expedition for want of greater adventure. Despite my experience, my knowledge of the polar region is limited. I want to motivate other women to get into this sport," she says. Dharamshaktu is preparing to leave for an expedition to the Pindari glacier, Uttarakhand, next month, as part of training.

The women, though not proficient mountaineers, are willing to test their endurance. "I am looking for mental toughness, not physical attributes. Things will also depend on how well they are able to get along with each other in the harsh climate. Training and experience are things you can work on, but character cannot change," explains Aston. Also, Aston believes that India stands at an advantage since there are many mountaineering enthusiasts in the country. "The participants leave for Scandinavia in June 2009 to train in sub-zero conditions and build endurance. The trip will leave for Antarctica in November 2009 and will reach the South Pole at midnight December 2009," says Aston, who considers crevasses and blizzards as the biggest threat. Look out for the polar girls.

Heading: Man of questions - Indian Express
Content:
Fondly known as 'Pickbrain', Quiz master Giri Balasubramaniam finds Indians take to knowledge easily!

You can make out the lines of disappointment on his face. The under-eye bags, the slight puffiness, the irritability. Seems like Love Story 2050 has pulled Harry Baweja down. While he disagrees with it, defends it with his life, we sit there, 'facing' it. The only good thing that's come out of it is that Harman's going places. "It couldn't get better for Harman. He's signed up with directors like Sanjay Leela Bhansali, Ashutosh Gowatrikar, Anees Bazmi and his second film, Victory which is on cricket will release on January 30, 2009," the proud dad beats about the success of his son, who, but the way, bears uncanny resemblance to Hrithik. "People have asked him that a 1000 times, and he always points to us - 'why don't you ask my parents how they managed it'!" That's right, blame it on the genes. Meanwhile, what actually brings Harry to town is a talent hunt. In collaboration with ITFT - CMES, (Centre for Media and Entertainment Studies) along with the Department of Tourism, UT, the hunt is to build a talent bank for TV serial and film producers. "We are always on the lookout for fresh talent and this platform will further help in networking and promoting cinematic tourism," says Harry, adding that the winners will get free scholarship for a three year degree course in media at CMES. "The idea is to tap and direct talent. It's for people who don't want to be part of reality shows. In this case, we'll be reaching out to those in the interiors and pick them region-wise," Harry feels that there's immense opportunity and money in fields like writing, directing, special effects, radio, animation et al. "These are creatively satisfying jobs and all that's needed is to create awareness."

On the personal front, Baweja shrugs off queries regarding future projects, although there is a news about directing his son in James and Bond, inspired from the famous British spy. "I cannot commit anything...right now, all I'm doing is relaxing. It's holiday time for me and my family," he evades again. Come to think of it, who wouldn't? "We are all dependent on that one Friday...I feel the audience just couldn't connect or relate or understand my film," he talks of the three years and crores put in it, and the defends with fast changing technology all over the world. "In two years, you'll see flying cars in Europe, people in the US can get into a virtual game as a character...there are skyscrapers coming up in Mumbai...I'm sure there'll be a different world in 2050." With a city that's struggling with its population, nonsensical political issues and is waterlogged every time it rains, all we can do is pray for a change! As for Baweja, he's in a risky business, and he agrees that only those who have the courage to make path-breaking films, those who take a gamble survive. "It may or may not work, but the risk has to be taken."

Heading: Sarul, Gurkeerat propel Chandigarh - Indian Express
Content:
For a change we are the ones throwing questions at him and he's doing all the answering! With Giri Balasubramaniam that doesn't happen very often. The quiz master, well-known for his distinctive style and fondly called 'Pickbrain', was in the city to conduct the regional round of the Tata Crucible - The Business Quiz 2008. Into its fifth edition, it's one of the country's most challenging corporate quizzes with much credit to Giri and his team. "Today, quizzing has gone vertical. While at school and college levels it still has a broader base by way of subjects, at the professional stage it's more specific and topical," mentions the quizmaster who also heads Greycaps India Pvt Ltd, the country's third largest quiz company with its headquarters in Bangalore. It's here that they churn out specialized quizzes like IT quizzes, corporate quizzes, quizzes designed for docs et al.

Quizzing has evolved over time, feels the quiz master. For one, it's no longer perceived as a "nerdy" activity to be a part of. "There was a time when a quiz brought in straight fact file questions. Preparing for such quizzes meant mugging it all up. But that's no longer the case," feels Balasubramaniam who finds the big shift now towards contemporary quizzing that's moved away from traditional style. "We now design questions that actually get you to apply your mind and not just fall back on recall information. Even factual questions can be presented in a new way," he mentions. With so many mediums opening up, quizzing is fast becoming a career option as well. "I find that Indians take to knowledge easily. But to be a successful quizmaster, there's more than a good voice and stage presence that you need," he says adding, "It's about doing your homework well. The quizmaster has to know what he's asking. The research has to be thorough."

Speaking of question and answers, his company has pioneered into quizzing in regional languages too. "It all happened thanks to our former President Dr APJ Abdul Kalam. I presented him a book of IT quizzes and he asked me to replicate it in regional languages as well. That's how the ball got rolling," tells Balasubramaniam who is impressed by the talent in the non-metros. "Cities like Jamshedpur, Pune and Chandigarh have bright sparks that do really well. Perhaps it's got to do with the element of sincerity that's still present in the education system here." As for how he managed a name 'Pickbrain', Giri smiles to say, "I ran a newspaper column by that name and was accidentally introduced as that on a function. It just stuck on and I think it's fun with kids and easier to pronounce that Balasubramaniam." You said it.

Heading: Gurbinder swims GC, Hoshiarpur to glory - Indian Express
Content:
Continuing with his scoring spree, opener Sarul Kunwar made a brilliant 84 run for Chandigarh and was involved in a 99 run partnership with Gurkeerat in the first semi-finals of the Katoch Shield Tournament being held at Sector 16 Cricket Stadium on Thursday.

Batting first, Chandigarh team was all out for 273 runs in 94.2 overs. Apart from Sarul and Gurkeerat, Gaurav Gambhir and Uday Kaul were the main contributors with knocks of 43 and 29 runs respectively. For Mohali, Jaskaran Singh claimed four wickets while Gunjit Singh and Varun Khanna bagged two wickets each.

In the second semi-final, Amritsar team was bowled out for a paltry 129 runs in 46 overs. Medium pacer Deepak Bansal and Gagandeep Singh tormented the Amritsar batsmen with their incisive bowling. Deepak Bansal bagged five wickets while Gagandeep scalped three wickets. Mayank Sharma (29) and Bharat Loomba (27) were the only noteworthy batsmen to show some resistance. Content:

Heading: Chandigarh-Ludhiana rail link by year 2010 - Indian Express

NRTS-II beat ERTS-I 48-15 in the pre-lunch session while it overcame NRTS-I by 36-22.

Heading: PU library to remain open 24 X 7 - Indian Express
Content:
Almost a decade after its inception, the Chandigarh-Ludhiana rail link project seems to be on the verge of completion now. The Rs 566-crore project is expected to reduce the distance between the two cities by 46 kilometres and will provide an alternative to the existing railway route between Chandigarh and Ludhiana.

The 112-kilometre project is divided into three phases, of which phase II (Morinda-Sahnewal) is expected to be completed by 2010 and phase III (Sahnewal-Ludhiana) before March 2009. The first phase — Chandigarh-Morinda link — has been functional since 2006.

Land acquisition for the Morinda-Sahnewal link has already been completed. The Northern Railways has acquired around 21 kilometres of land from the state government between Morinda and Khamano. Of the total five stations — Morinda, Khamano, Samrala, Madpur and Sahnewal — three are under construction.

Construction for the 15-kilometre Sahnewal-Ludhiana link is on in full swing. As this section is parallel to the existing rail link, the trains will pass through the only station — Dhandari Kalan.

"Execution of the project does not take much time — the major hurdle is land acquisition, which is the state government's responsibility. Our target is to complete the project by 2010. Electrification of the track will be started after the engineering department finishes the construction of bridges and tracks," said a senior official of the construction wing.

Sources said the rail link will have 50 level crossings, 13 major bridges and 10 minor bridges and 11 stations.

Heading: Heart surgery gives new lease of life to infant - Indian Express
Content:
Come December and the students of Panjab University will have a reason to cheer, as the A C Joshi Library will remain open round-the-clock.

The icing on the cake is that students can issue and return books any time.

An Auto Issue system will be set up to facilitate 24-hour issue and return of books.

The A-I system will require students to punch in their identification proof (the campus ID-card) for issuing a book.

For return, drop boxes will be placed outside the library.

PU authorities said the library would be the first in the country to adopt an upgraded security system — Radio Frequency Identification Technology (RFIT) — to ensure that no book is sneaked off the premises.

Librarian V K Anand told Newsline: "A chip will be inserted in every book, which will store the book's description including author and title. Once the book is issued, the chip will be rendered non-functional. Otherwise, the chip will start beeping if taken out of the premises."

As a part of the RFI technology, the library will have a digital library assistant to help locate books.

"Books kept on the inappropriate shelves can be located in no time at all. Otherwise, it takes us around 45 minutes to rectify the stock," added Anand.

The library houses nearly 7 lakh books.
