"The recessionary trend is slowly becoming a reality with the twin threats of the financial markets crisis and consumer anxiety... crisis has triggered serious liquidity problems, with the money market interest rates shooting up.

"If not addressed with speed and determination, the prolonged liquidity concerns could turn into solvency problems, further jeopardising the stability of the global financial system," Finance Minister P Chidambaram said in his formal statement to the International Monetary and Finance Committee.

His statement was read out in absentia by Reserve Bank of India Governor D Subbarao, as Chidambaram had to cancel his visit to assuage fears at home about the global financial storm hitting the Indian shores.

India said that although the Fund's role in the crisis was so far perceived to be "peripheral," the IMF should gear up to meet the borrowing needs of member countries engulfed by the crisis, which has its origins in defunct mortgages in the US.

"The financial institution (IMF) should have the mending instruments and the financing capacity to address potential borrowing needs," according to Chidambaram.

Admitting that emerging markets economies (EMEs) "are not islands of tranquility and the crisis could be transmitted to them through multiple channels," he felt external corporate and bank borrowing was becoming scarcer and dearer and housing and real estate markets are slowing down. "The current crisis holds important lessons for EMEs which they should factor in as they move forward on financial sector reform," he felt. According to Chidambaram's statement, growth in EMEs would slow to 6.9 per cent in 2008 and further to 6.1 per cent in 2009.

Noting that there were a number of concerns over the attempts to resolve the current crisis, India suggested that IMF should step in to channelise fragmented efforts at different levels for more effective results. Besides, India wanted member countries to be "encouraged to approach the Fund in the incipient stages of a crisis".

Chidambaram's statement further said: "We are not too sure about the full magnitude of the problem. Despite some incipient signs of cooling, inflationary pressures arising out of elevated food and fuel prices have not fully subsided.

"Clearly, these are troubled times for the world economy. Nevertheless, crises do give us an opportunity to quickly take stock of what went wrong and to act."

Heading: GM, Chrysler in merger talks - Indian Express
Content:
President Bush emerged from a meeting with foreign financial officials on Saturday and pledged a global response to the credit crisis that will lead toward a "path of stability and long-term growth."

Bush announced no new strategies to attack the economic woes circling the globe, stressing instead, "We will do what it takes to resolve the crisis and the world's economy will emerge stronger as a result."

The president spoke in the Rose Garden outside the White House, joined there in a show of solidarity not long after daybreak by finance officials from the G-7 — Japan, Germany, Britain, France, Italy and Canada, in addition to the United States. Treasury Secretary Henry Paulson and Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice also attended.

Bush's comments were aimed at avoiding the mistakes that worsened economic conditions during the Great Depression in the 1930s. Then, some nations pursued go-it-alone strategies such as erecting protectionist trade barriers to shield their domestic industries. Those trade barriers ended up only worsening the global downturn.

Heading: BMC springs into action to solve city’s water woes - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Roof collapses in Sakinaka; one killed, three injured - Indian Express
Content:
Days after corporators raised a storm over severe distribution problems in the city's water supply network causing acute scarcity in some pockets, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) last week announced efforts to resolve the problems.

As part of a series of short term goals, the civic body has now promised to fix leaking water pipes in the city.

"Considering that leaking pipes are one of the main causes of water wastage, our first priority is to fix such pipelines in the city," said chief hydraulic engineer, M M Kamble.

Two weeks ago, a water pipeline was punctured at Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar road in Matunga due to construction work in the area. In the process, an estimated damage of Rs 1.5 to 2 lakh was caused.

To top this, some 50,000 to 60,000 million litres a day (MLD) of water was being wasted. As a result, Matunga, Dadar, Parel and Lalbaug were hit by an acute water shortage for most of the last fortnight.

As part of the long term goals, the civic body has reiterated that it will rehabilitate and replace pipelines throughout the city wherever necessary.

"We are planning to relay water pipelines and resize the existing ones. But this will take time and at present we don't know when the work will be completed," said Kamble.

The civic body has recognised the administrative wards of L, R and K (Kurla, Dahisar and Andheri areas) as the worst affected areas as far as water shortage is concerned.

The civic body claims that this is also due to fewer pumping stations in these areas. "We will construct more pumping stations in these areas and increase the pressure points of the existing ones," said Kamble.

Keeping in mind the menace of illegal connections and water mafia in the city, BMC has also decided to come up strongly against illegal connections.

"After surveying the city, we found about 3,000 illegal water connections at Shivaji nagar, Govandi. We have cut these illegal connections," said Kamble.

Heading: Pay for govt loss, ex-housing body members told - Indian Express
Content:
A labourer died and three were injured when the roof of a two-storey structure collapsed at Sakinaka. The building near Ashish Hotel was old and dilapidated. The roof of the structure caved in early on Sunday morning.

Twenty two-year-old Bajrangi Haddha Harijan died on the spot. Nehemko Ramdeo Harijan (21) has been admitted to Sion hospital with serious head injuries while Madaya lochan Khan (22) along with Binju Chinmun Gautam (28) have been admitted to Rajawadi Hospital.

According to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's disaster management cell, the four were sand and brick labourers and were staying at a room in the building.

Heading: Cop’s wife hit in accidental firing - Indian Express
Content:
The former office bearers and members of a co-operative housing society that lords over 101.56 acres of land at Ambernath in Thane have been asked to make good the loss of 4.77 crore caused to the state ex-chequer. Recovery of such a huge amount by the state from members of housing society is unprecedented. The amount that each member, who have been served notice, would have to cough up would be Rs 53 lakh.

"We have dispatched notices to the nine members including office bearers of Sarvodaya Co-Operative Housing Society (CHS) at Ambernath and are awaiting their reply," said Rajesh Lavhekar assistant registrar of co-operative societies department.

It is the government's contention that the state incurred losses of Rs 4.77 crore when the society members authorised transfer of 26 plots of land without the collector's approval during the period 1999 to 2005. In the officially approved transfers, the seller has to pay the state government a certain percentage of the sale proceeds. The state's share in the transfer of plot is 50 per cent of 'unearned income'. The 'unearned income' is the difference in the price brought by the seller to the price that is being sold to the new buyer. Thus for a plot of land that was originally priced at Rs 5000 and now being sold at Rs 1 lakh the unearned income is their difference i.e. Rs 95,000 and the government share at the rate of 50 per cent is Rs 47500.

In 1999-2000 the government had seized the land of Sarvodaya CHS owing to irregularities in the transfer of plots. Two years later in 2002 the government returned the seized land on the condition that the society rectify its irregularities within a period of six months.

After the government directives to rectify the irregularities were ignored by the managing committee of Sarvodaya CHS, the district anti-corruption committee headed by the collector ordered the assistant registrar of the co-operative societies department to submit an inquiry report.

The final report, submitted in March 2008, has recommended the recovery of Rs 4.77 crore from the then members of the managing committee.

The then chairman Shantaram Jadhav said, "There is no irregularity as purported by the assistant registrar. For an inquiry to be conducted there has to be mandate of at least one third of the members. None of these procedures were followed."

He added that in cases of alleged irregularity, the plot transfer has been registered with the stamp duty duly paid. "If the transfer was illegal then it should not have been registered by the registrar's office," said Jadhav.

He added that in several cases builders have developed plots into buildings without the knowledge of the managing committee and disappeared after selling the apartments.

Heading: Life in a metro - Indian Express
Content:
The wife of a police constable was accidentally struck by a bullet fired from close range on Sunday afternoon.

Chaya Kamble (35) is now recuperating in the ICU of Roy Hospital in Chembur, while her husband Tanaji Lakshman Kamble (40), a police constable with the Nehru Nagar police, has been booked for negligence by the Pant Nagar police station.According to Police Inspector (Crime) P Patil, Pantnagar police station Kamble had gone home to his Pant Nagar residence for lunch when the accident occurred.

"Its possible that Kamble's wife might have wanted to see the revolver and while he was showing it to her it may have gone off. We will be investigating the case and only then shall we get a clearer picture," he said.

Chaya was rushed to Roy Hospital in Chembur and has been operated upon.

"She was wheeled in with low blood pressure. The bullet was fired at close range. It had pierced her chest and entered the abdomen and it took a three-hour operation to extricate it. We handed over the bullet to the police," said Dr Roy Patankar who performed the surgery.

According to officials at the Nehru Nagar police station, Kamble has spent over a year at the police station and has been in the police force for over 16 years.

Heading: Gem of an auction? - Indian Express
Content:
In the devised play 60 Seconds Deep, five theatre personalities explore various components of urban life

A N 80-minute play is 60 Seconds Deep. Or may be more, when it serves the quintessential urban panorama. With Mumbai as muse, this devised play strings together various threads of the city as the spotlight remains firmly on its quirks, mood swings, changing images and madness.

To begin with, Jaimini Pathak had Prithvi Theatre booking for four days (getting dates is becoming rarer than getting parking space near it) next week. However, with no electrifying script in sight and the mind abuzz with images of Mumbai, he roped in four theatre actors—Sheila Govindaraj, Nayantara Roy, Mandar Gokhale and Atul Mongia. They all came with different takes on the city. And that kicked off marathon brainstorming sessions two months ago.

By the end of three such weeks, the group had explored several themes related to urban life. And it was time to write down the impressions. The task went to Roy, who is responsible for the bound script of 60 Seconds Deep. "Nearly 90 per cent of what we had discussed and agreed upon, have made it to the script," says Pathak.

"It's the imageries of urban life and abundance of it in Mumbai that made me think of devised theatre. That's when I got four more on board, all of them with varied take on the city," says Pathak, taking a break from the rehearsal. The play opens at Prithvi Theatre on October 16 and will run till October 19.

Devised theatre has made a number of theatre groups from the UK and the US shift focus from the text-based works. The last century witnessed the emergence of devised theatre based on images and symbols in many parts of the western world, particularly Eastern Europe. The imagery-rich 60 Seconds Deep seems to have taken a leaf from them. Mumbai has, in the recent past, seen devised plays like Hamlet, Hair and Numbers in the Dark.

The Working Title's newest work is also a collage of different theatre forms. "We have tried to present different threads in different formats. The play is wacky and irreverent, but not inaccessible to the common audience," says Roy. "We have explored themes like love, traffic, sexuality, music, culture, media and entertainment, and given our taken on them," says Mongia, who is only a year-old in Mumbai.

However, the brainstorming sessions have not been as serious as they sound, assure the actors. "On the days we couldn't come up with ideas, games took up our time," says Mongia. That, says Roy, has helped them bond better. It has also come handy in understanding their personalities. As a result, she has managed to blend the quirks of Govindaraj, Gokhale, Mongia and hers, into the play. Asif Ali Baig's lyrics and music too have helped some images, like food, find expression.

Heading: Once upon a time - Indian Express
Content:
At 42.02 carats, it is the world's largest Forevermark yellow diamond, estimated between Rs 2.7 crore and Rs 3.2 crore— one best friend for a man or a woman. But when the un-mounted gemstone came under the hammer at the recent Saffronart Fine Jewels auction, it failed to invite a bid that touched the reserve price. The fate was shared by 74 of 130 lots that went on sale, and the closing figure stood at Rs 6.3 crore, far from the estimated Rs 22-28 crore.

But that did not deter the spirit of Minal Vazirani, co-founder of the online auction house. "Keeping the current global economic conditions in mind, we did well," she said, still beaming at having organised what is arguably India's first public auction of fine jewels and watches on October 7 and 8.

With only international auction houses to look for guidance, Vazirani had formed an in-house team of experts that scouted precious jewels from the world over. Apart from the diamond, there were a natural-pearl necklace with a seven-strand cascade that invited the highest bid of Rs 1 crore, a diamond necklace that sold for Rs 79.8 lakh and a diamond sarpech that went for Rs 49.8 lakh. "The auction comprised jewellery made over the past 100 years," says Vazirani.

Saffronart's results might not have dazzled, but in his Bangalore office Maher Dadha, CMD of the auction house Bid & Hammer, is busy examining the provenance of vintage jewellery. It will be part of the auction that will take place in January 2009. Unlike Vazirani, Dadha will bring to the auction, jewellery that is a minimum of 50 years old and will tap sources that have remained outside the radar of international auctioneers that are bound by trade regulations that restrict the export of heritage jewellery from India.

"There is a lot of demand in India and it will not be difficult to find buyers," says Dadha.

Mumbai-based Ma Passion, meanwhile, hopes to revive the craft of gemstone carving with its October 22 auction. Curated by Nisha Jamwal, this will comprise, among others, emerald Ganesha, Krishna and Radha in blue sapphire and crystal Buddha under the Bodhi tree carved by craftsmen from Rajasthan.

Even as the country wakes up to hammer coming down on jewels, foreign shores will as usual be glitzy. At its Geneva auction next month, Sotheby's will have enough Indian jewels, while later this month Christie's will bring under the hammer, in Dubai, an early 20th century rose-cut diamond sarpech, estimated at $50,000-70,000, and two India-influenced Cartier jewels —a pendant estimated at $200,000-300,000 and a 1940s clip brooch priced at $13,000-18,000.

Heading: Country of gods - Indian Express
Content:
Danish Husain and Mahmood Farooqui are back in Mumbai with Dastan Goi, the lost art of storytelling in Urdu

In a city where the inability to use the Hindi in its pure form has given rise to a publicly acknowledged Bambaiyya dialect, chaste Urdu is but a distant dream. But the duo of Danish Husain and Mahmood Farooqui is determined to raise Mumbai from its slumber of indifference towards this prized language.

On October 19, Husain and Farooqui, after a year's gap, yet again bring Dastan Goi—the lost art of storytelling in Urdu—to Mumbai's Bhavan's Cultural Centre at Andheri.

Dastan Goi is the art of storytelling with roots in medieval Iran. According to the tradition, the narrators, also known as dastan-gohs, would recite fantasy tales of fearless warrior kings around camp fires, in coffee houses and palaces. The stories narrated through Dastan goi usually revolve around the ordeals of these kings and their encounters with the enemy.

"The traditional art spoke about demons, magicians and djinns. Though that's magnificent in itself, we have adapted Dastan goi to present times and the stories that we can relate to," says Husain. The duo has planned two performances, The Talking Birds and Partition Dastans on the Multiple Tragedies of 1947. While the first is a romance epic and an adaptation of a famous tale, Talisme Hoshruba (literally meaning 'magical word that blows your senses away'), the latter, as the name suggests, speaks about the tragedies of the partition.

Husain explains that the storyteller, through the text and the performance, live every emotion and tragedy of the characters of the tale. "We are just the narrators, yet one can feel everything the character does, through us, "making it sound like a beautifully bound string of pearls".

Not surprisingly, Husain and Farooqui are the only living dastan-gohs, the last one alive was in 1928. Based out of Delhi, the duo travels extensively to metropolitan cities for these performances, and have even been to Lahore and Karachi in Pakistan with their stories. "The response was fabulous as the country is more familiar with the language," explains the artiste.

The duo last performed in Mumbai at the Kala Ghoda Festival in February 2007. However, they will not be participating in the ongoing festival. About their forthcoming event in the city, Husain says they're excited and the audience's knowledge regarding the art has definitely improved over their last few visits but is still limited to the theatrical circles. "But by the time our event is over, we'll have improved everyone's Urdu in Mumbai," he laughs.

Heading: Open play - Indian Express
Content:
A Brazilian film festival teams up the novel with the predictable

A spate of Brazilian cinema in pop-festivals of recent years has painted a somewhat one-sided picture of the country's society. Though it's true that cities like Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo have some the worst recorded crime rates in the world, films like City of God, Elite squad and City of Men depict the lives of the poor as grim and violent and qualities like tenderness, grace and calm seem like qualities that only pervade the lives of the rich and the secure.

Brazil's cinematic tradition boasts of an indigenous counterpart to the new waves of European cinema in the '50s and '60s. Cinema Nuevo, a 1960's movement spearheaded by the late Glauber Rocha was deeply political and critical of the military dictatorship that held the country at the time. This quality cinema remained till a little more than the next decade and then virtually disappeared, to resurge again a decade and half later.

The NCPA, in collaboration with the consulate of Brazil will stage a festival of some the country's acclaimed films between October 13 and 17. The festival will open with Cidade de Deus (City of God) which has reached almost cult status with its stylised and bloody depiction of the favelas (Rio slums) with its gun-totting, coke-snorting youth that groove to the rhythms of samba and funk.

But the films that follow are the ones that sound like the treat. They are a mix of tender stories about women and children and part-fantasy tales. Domesticas (Maids, 2001) is a woman-centric film that highlights the socio-economic disparities in Brazilian society. Casamentos de Louise (Louise's Wedding, 2001) is a biting satire about Brazilian society, class divides and corruption. Central do Brasil (1998) by critically acclaimed director Walter Salles, is a touching film about a relationship that develops between a nine-year-old boy and a woman. Villas Lobos (2000) is a biopic about the prodigious Brazilian composer Heitor Villas Lobos and traces his rise. Auto da Compadecida (The dog's will, 2000) is a fantasy tale that was a box-office hit in Brazil. The closing film Dois Filhos de Francisco (Francisco's Two Sons, 2005) is the true story of two brothers — Brazil's leading country music duo, Zezé di Camargo and Luciano—and their father's constant struggle to see them succeed.

A criticism railed against the recent cult of Brazilian cinema has also been almost non-existent role of women in daily life. This selection of films hopes to strike a different chord with their depiction of women, romance, music and a little bit of magic.

Heading: Garden of delight - Indian Express
Content:
Gallery loyalty is changing as artists swap galleries and display works across the globe

It is admirable when an artist today can actually stick with the gallery that nurtured him or her when they were just starting out. Someone like TV Santosh, who does not even give his work out for group shows and only displays with Guild Art Gallery when there's much demand for his work by other art dealers," says Farah Siddique, who recently launched her own gallery, Farah Siddique Fine Art Centre, with a selection of budding artists. "I hope that my artists remain loyal to me," she adds with a laugh.

Recently one has seen big names like Atul Dodiya and Jitish Kallat, who were nurtured by Chemould Art Gallery, showing in other big spaces like Bodhi Art Gallery and other galleries in Seoul or Berlin.

"The loyalty to partners on projects is a two-way unwritten code and is central to the ecosystem of the art world at large. Given the bandwidth of my practice with simultaneous projects in Seoul, Sydney, Berlin and New York, it's necessary that galleries representing me work in a spirit of symbiosis," says Kallat.

With the globalisation of art and its widening circumference, the politics of exhibiting is going through a change. Kallat and Dodiya are of the opinion that galleries in India are adapting to being seen on par with their Western counterparts-the current prices that Indian art fetches makes it possible. "Hence my gallery in Mumbai, Chemould Prescott Road, can interact with my Berlin Gallery Arndt + Partner or my Korean-Chinese gallery Arario for instance," says Kallat.

"Actually the idea of showcasing in many galleries is a privilege that a few 'golden' artists enjoy. Over time though, the hierarchy of things will change. Right now artists are at the top of the pyramid when it comes to taking decisions but I foresee toppling since the clients are limited," says Chemould's Shireen Gandhy who takes the switching galleries in her stride as an inevitability of market forces.

An artist like Hema Upadhyay is clear that she would not showcase her solo in Mumbai with galleries other than Chemould, instead she collaborates only with galleries in Europe. Riyas Komu now follows a similar mantra though he is known to have built relationships with Sakshi, Guild and Bodhi Art Gallery.

"It all depends on your personal equation on how you represent yourself to the galleries. My relationships with galleries are rather emotional-I still work with Sakshi since I started my career with them. They supported me for large-scale installations," says Komu who is showing with Sakshi in September 2009.

"Bodhi gave me a space to showcase when I was still adapting to the new environs of Sakshi, which had moved from their ideal Lower Parel gallery. Now I have made it a point to have my other solo with Bodhi Berlin and not have it in Mumbai," says the prolific Komu who also showcases photographic works at the Guild.

That way everyone is kept happy.

Heading: What is a totem? - Indian Express
Content:
A Ramachandran, a reticent painter from the old school, has a big solo

His colourful narrative of paintings have decorated the living rooms of homes and sat on auction podiums where they fetched handsome prices. Now, the veteran from Kerala is showing a large body of works that include large oils and three-dimensional sculptural forms that reflect his concerns of line and detailing.

"I had moved from urban reality to embrace a traditional style, when a tribal group in Rajasthan with their vibrant ethos gripped my imagination," says the artist who once taught in Jamia Milia Islamia on traditional murals in Kerala.

He fused his knowledge of the murals with his fascination of the tribes and came up with a unique blend of art that is distinctly his own.

His work is often allegorical and the densely vegetative lotus pond is one of his favourite metaphors for the matrix of life. Beautiful and decorative, this ecosystem gives birth to hybrid creatures, a goat with a woman's head, a winged seductress or a newborn babe wrapped in the folds of a lotus-leaves. Often we see the artist rendering a mocking self portrait of himself as an owl. "I use Indian mythology but it is important for me to re-contextualise them which is why I often include a self-portrait," says the artist who also has executed a series of individual portraits of village belles facing the viewer in a frontal and inquisitive manner, as if they were curious about the world outside the canvas.

"When talking about the art of the post Independence period in India, Ramachandran's art works became much acclaimed for their traditional style in rendering a figurative narrative but with a language speaking about the contemporary," says art critic Ela Pal.

Ramachandran's obvious delight in observing men and women in their natural settings often result in curious fantasies. The artist's imagination converts fragmented moments into drawings contoured by powerful swiping lines resembling unruly motions of wind or sometimes restrains of any solid natural form. His mastery over narrating ephemeral yet engaging moments of observation into short-lived story lines turns his works into visual delights.

The show will be on till October 14 at Jehangir Art Gallery

Heading: Culture vulture - Indian Express
Content:
Some would argue that modern-day totems exist in the modern-day art and to some extent that may be true, however the content would have changed drastically and the votive nature of the totem has been transformed to modern concerns.

The original totemic art originated in the Pacific Coast northwest from Alaska and British Columbia. Native Indians carved wooden totems, imbued them with a spiritual symbolism and have been protected by the dwindling tribes who live on the coast. The monumental totems of the Haida and Tlingit in the Totem Bight State Historical Park in Alaska, and the intricate artwork of the Kwakuitl, Salish, and Bella Coola are worth mentioning. The significance of totems is that their verticality lends them a status that is both intimidating and sublime. Historian Eddie Malin (1986) has proposed a theory of totem pole development. He argues that the poles served the purpose of house posts, funerary containers, and memorial markers into symbols of clan and family wealth and prestige. In popular culture, totems have also been associated with witchery and the black arts.

The carvings on totems are highly symbolic but they have also been adapted to bags, T-shirts for tourists and souvenirs. Unfortunately very few of the original poles remain because they were made of wood and decayed easily in the rainforest. The custom of carving these poles may pre-date the existing ones that date back to the 1880s, since there are many accounts by European travelers. Post-Impressionist painter Paul Gauguin who set up an artist's residency on the islands of Tahiti was also influenced by totemic art and it reflects in his art time and again. One lyrical depiction of this influence is his painting of a girl lying on a yellow blanket being watched over by a spirit-a totem that has glowing eyes and presence that is neither benign nor aggressive.

(Demystify art, e-mail georgina.maddox@expressindia.com)

Heading: MIG takes off after three years - Indian Express
Content:
Film mania
Shamiana, the film club that started at Mocha and has moved to Jazz by the Bay, under the guidance of Cyrus Dastur, is on a roll. After a successful screenings of short films at Pune the club returns to Mumbai with a new section of cutting edge music videos by shot filmmakers and along with a package humorous, quirky short films from Switzerland, Canada, Mexico and India. Entry to the event is an affordable Rs 100.
At Not just Jazz by the Bay, Marine Drive, October 15, 6.45 onwards

On paper
BIG names, quality works but yet it's affordable? That is the beauty of works on paper, it makes good art affordable to young collectors and allows even those earning in the medium-income group art that is within a budget. Now Hacienda presents a group show with Anjolie Ela Menon, Shibu Natesan, Rekha Rodwittiya, Paritosh Sen and an unusually figurative work by Jyoti Basu. Drop in, even if it's just for a gander.
At Hacienda Gallery, Kala Ghoda, October 13-23

New and improved
THE suburbs seem to be looking up, what with another gallery opening and showcasing art that goes beyond the popular camels and village belles that is usually characteristic of suburbia. Bina Aziz and Zarine Khan, present their new gallery Tradition Art, which launches with a block-buster group show titled Kaleidoscope, featuring 64 artists, from Jatin Das and Jehangir Jani to Gurucharan Singh and Papri Bose. This vast range of art is a something for everyone kind of exhibition and it caters to tastes across a diverse group of collectors and viewers.
At Tradition Art, Sanjay Plaza, Juhu Post Office, till October 28

Dream on
BASED on a novel by Shri Gyan Chaturvedi, Baramasi is all about dreams, expectations, disappointments and failures. The play, directed by Dhanendra Kawade, travels through the 60s rural India. The play revolves around the Dubey family-Amma (a widow), Gucchhan (a firm believer of God), Chuttan (a hardcore Dharmendra fan), Lallan (aspiring dacoit), Chandu (aspiring doctor) and Binno (over the hill but still dreaming of marriage). The most important member of the family is Mamaji (a retired railway employee), whose sudden demise gives the play an expected twist. Amma's only hope for a better financial condition is her youngest son Chandu. But after achieving his goal, Chandu leaves the family. The play with its twists and turns represents the problems of a rural middle-class family.

Heading: Central Rly thrash Pifa Youngstars - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai skipper Wasim Jaffer speaks about his new responsibilities and the season ahead

It isn't really clear why the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) decided to drop Amol Muzumdar as captain of the Ranji team. However, their decision to replace him at the helm with Wasim Jaffer should augur equally well for the side that'll be desperate to get back this season with a bang. For his seniority and the credibility of being a Test opener, Jaffer commands respect within the team and, over the decade, has been a force to reckon with.

In a chat with Sportsline, he spoke of the newly awarded captaincy, Mumbai's preparations and whether he already has a roadmap for success.

Excerpts

Was it a surprise when they name you as captain?
Not really, I knew it was coming. I have led the West Zone side is Deodhar and was also the captain of the Irani Trophy team. Leading Mumbai is always an honor and a tough task, I'm happy to get the job.

You have been always looked upon as one of Mumbai's most prolific run-getter. How easy will youngsters find in approaching you?
If you ask the players you'll realize how easy it is to talk to me and how approachable I am. Be it an Under-17, Under-19 or an Under-22 player, I' always there. I don't think there'll be any issues.

Any plans in place already?
Not really. If you ask any captain or team member what are your plans for future then there's one simple answer always to give: Everybody just want to win and we'll be preparing to do the same. Frankly, we're looking forward to a good and healthy domestic season, and of course winning back the Ranji Trophy.

Do you fear your non-aggressive nature will make players little complacent on the field?
Who says I'm not aggressive? I'm an aggressive person but the point is I don't really show it on the field. I try to keep it myself. We are all professionals and we all know what our task and role is. I think if a good chat can get my work done then there is no need of panicking. It's all about sending across your message clearly to the player.

Mumbai does have a good mix of youngsters and those with experience
Of course, we do have experience. There's Ajit Agarkar, Ramesh Powar, Amol Muzumdar, Nilesh Kulkarni and now with Sairaj Bahutule coming in, we have solid line up. On the other hand we have youngsters like Murtuza Hussain, Dhaval Kulkarni, Rohit Sharma, Ajinkya Rahane and Sahil Kukreja. We have a good side and we are hopeful of doing well this season.

Are you concerned about any injuries?
It's hard to talk about injuries, especially when nothing is the individual's hands. No player wants to get injured. If you see half of the current pace attack, they're either recovering from their injuries or are under rehabilitation. Ajit recently had a hernia operation while Murtuza and Avishkar Salvi too are recovering. But hope these players are perfectly fit when Ranji begins. There's still a month left.

How do you motivate players like Ajinkya Rahane or Sahil Kukreja who are fighting for the same slot like you in the national side?
Every player is competing with each other here and competition is a never ending process. As a player I know what I have to do so do Ajinkya and Sahil. We all are professionals. Every player wants to play for his country and that is what we are always hopeful about. There are ups and downs in cricket but a player needs to keep going.

Heading: Phenomenale signals arrival on Classic scene - Indian Express
Content:
If getting thrashed 4-1 by Central Railway wasn't bad enough, Pifa Colaba Youngstars's (Pifa CYS) performance during their MFL Elite Division League encounter at the RCF ground in Chembur on Sunday also seemed to leave a bad taste.

As early as the 19th minute of the game, Satish Keer (Pifa CYS) and Douzy Godinho (CR) got into a scuffle and both were given the marching orders by referee Kumaran. From the resultant free-kick, Clifford Garret scored a goal for Pifa Colaba.

Seemingly incensed by this shocker, the experienced railway players blasted home three goals in quick succession to take the wind out of the young Pifa CYS forward line.

Aziz Qureshi scored the first goal from the top of the box in the 33rd minute, followed by Krishna Naidu from 25 yards in the 37th minute. Maverick Kasif Jamal, who had laid off passes for the first two goals, then received one from Karim on the right flank, slipped the ball onto his stronger left foot and fired a pile-driver from 18 yards that nearly burst through the net.

As the railmen took it easy thereafter, under humid conditions, the Pifa youngsters tried their best to get back into the game but their efforts were thwarted by the reliable Railway defence.

In the 51st minute, defender Nilesh Patidan let fly his elbow at a CR forward and he was duly punished with a yellow card. Karim Sheikh, who came in as a substitute in the first half, rounded off the goal tally by scoring through a zero angle shot from the right flank in the 73rd minute.

Central Railway now have seven points from three games and look well on their way to make it to the Super 7. Pifa Colaba Youngstars on the other hand have just one point from three games.

Heading: Making No Bones About It - Indian Express
Content:
The National School of Combat Art teaches women to fight back, using karate, kick-boxing and Eskrima, a popular martial arts form from the Philippines

As a child, Sanya Modak was shy, meek and submissive never daring to look into your eyes as she spoke. Today, the 20-year-old is a transformed young woman, not only taking in the confidently but also quite ready to respond with a well-aimed kick or a punch if you mess with her.

A resident of a sprawling slum in Bandra, Sanya's life changed when the National School of Combat Art (NSCA) visited the Anjuman-e-Islam school where she studied, and offered the girls classes in martial arts. For many others in the school too, this was a ticket to a new and improved self, a confidence makeover.

NSCA is an institute teaching martial arts to young kids, especially girls from underprivileged sections. Significantly, most of its patrons are from the Muslim community.

Completing 25 years this year, the institute is run by a feisty 42-year-old, Radhika Sheikh. "Women cutting across all barriers of caste and community are a vulnerable lot. But, after the riots, many innocent Muslim women were harassed. They became unnecessary victims. My late husband Arif Sheikh and I were irked by this, we wanted to do something for these young women," says Radhika.

They started their first branch in Nagpada. After advertising in Urdu newspapers, the duo tied up with Anjuman-e-Islam schools dotting the city and soon, their movement started flourishing.Today, the institute has branches all across the country from Mizoram to Kerala to Bangalore.

"The institute is actually my late husband's idea. He himself was an accomplished martial arts trainer. He was deeply disturbed to find women going into a shell stemming from the fear of riots," says Radhika. "Initially, we had a tough time convincing parents to send their girls. But later they saw that the classes are held in the safe grounds of schools and conducted by women instructors, so their inhibitions dulled. More and more school principals from Anjuman-e-Islam schools started inviting us."

The institute charges a nominal sum of Rs 10 per month per student and teaches various aspects of martial arts, from karate and kick-boxing to stick-fighting and punching. Radhika says the art is collectively called Eskrima Kali Arnis, a popular martial arts system that has its origins in the Philippines. "Mere karate is not enough; we need to teach girls how to react in any unguarded situation. Also, they need to be taught how everyday articles like books, a pen or a hairbrush can be used to protect themselves, Eskrima does that," says Radhika.

Several of Radhika's students have gone on to become instructors grooming younger batches of girls. "Learning self-defence boosts your confidence immensely. This is especially true for girls coming from slum pockets who are as it is a deprived lot and hence have less confidence. Also, today Mumbai is no longer safe for women. Self-defence is the only solution," says Sanya.

She herself joined NSCA in her fifth grade and thanks the institute for helping her to get rid of her meekness. "Once, when I was in Class VII, a guy would regularly stalk me. It would become a pain to get out in the morning and see him following me. One day when the opportunity struck, I kicked him in the groin. That was the end of the episode. It taught me I don't have to take any nuisance from anybody," she says.

Sanya today juggles her college and works as a trainer and counselor at the institute.

"We do face some reluctance among parents. But thankfully today the problem is reducing, more and more people are realizing the importance of self-defence," she adds.

The NSCA has also tied up with several corporate houses and call centers to train female employees. "With gender violence rising in the city, more and more corporate houses and call centers are waking up to the need to train their female employees. We are only too happy," smiles Radhika, as she gears up for another round of punches, kicks and stick-fighting.

Heading: Sound Sense - Indian Express
Content:
Arthritis Day saw former patients walk and dance, to drive home the message that complete recovery is possible

Mumbai awoke on a chilly Sunday of 1991 to what could have been the lowest temperature in this city in my 60 years here, around 11 degrees Celsius. And it was as if a host of health problem were knocking at my doorstep, along with arthrithis," says Agnes D'souza, recalling the day she first experienced acute pain in her limbs. Now 77 years old, Agnes later discovered she was suffering from chronic arthritis. "I was not able to move, leave alone performing my daily chores. I carried on with this problem for a good 14 years, and it was only in 2004 that I underwent a surgery."

Agnes was one among several patients who've successfully fought off arthritis who gathered for a "walkathon" at Bandra early on Sunday morning, to mark World Arthritis Day.

While about 1,000 former arthritis patients participated in the walkathon, Powai's Olympia Building hosted a unique dance competition where scores of middle-aged patients and senior citizens participated, showing it's possible to age gracefully. Organized by the Dr L H Hiranandani Hospital, the dance competition ¿ Joints in Motion ¿ was a chance to assert that people with arthritis need not lead painful, restricted lives, according to Dr Sujit Chatterjee, CEO of Hiranandani Hospital.

Several group as well as individual dance numbers were presented, with dancer-actor Sudha Chandran, having herself overcome a major setback after losing a limb, cheering the participants on.

Orthopaedic, joint replacement and hip resurfacing surgeon Dr Sanjeev Jain said the objective was to reaffirm that people with arthritis can dance, or carry on with normal activities after receiving proper medical treatment and guidance. "Many in the middle-age group and above seem to complain about chronic joint pains. The causes of such joint pains are usually osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. Sadly, they assume that such aches are part of aging and do not visit a doctor for treatment. Upon diagnosis, well-guided treatment options in advancing orthopedics guarantee great improvement in the quality of living of the elderly," he said.

Agnes, meanwhile, says there are tremendous misconceptions prevailing in India about the disease. "People feel undergoing knee operation will paralyse them for ever." For Agnes, who underwent the operation on both her knees, nothing could have been a better decision. "While I was troubled for over a decade, today even at 77, I am fit and able to take care of my errands," she says.

Heading: Family in debt carries out suicide pact - Indian Express
Content:
These two management graduates are striking out to promote new Indian alternative music, offering infrastructure for new artistes

If contemporary Indian music only remainds you of regular fare coughed up by Bollywood or some forgettable albums with repetitive dance movements and beats, then this duo wants you to lend them your ears. The fact that commercial Bollywood fare is the most popular does not deter Nihar Manwatkar (25) and Viraj Sawant (26) from choosing the non-commercial space as their source of daily bread. The duo ¿ both management graduates ¿ are convinced about alternative Indian music and have invested their early days in promoting such music.

After completing their business diplomas from a city management institute, Nihar and Viraj got together and arranged for capital to set up a jam room to help upcoming bands to record their music, since most of these musicians could not afford recording studios in the city. This led them to establish their venture which they called 'anecho'. "I managed a job with a financial firm after completing my studies but realised that this is what I wanted to do," said Nihar. Thus, after establishing their jam room at Andheri in February last year, the duo launched into their cause — promoting alternative Indian music.

"At first it's a bit difficult for people to understand what we're doing. They take us for just another event management firm, but what we're actually trying to do is partner with alternative Indian sounds," said Viraj. "At any point of time throughout the day, we have aspiring musicians who are practicing and recording their music. And all we charge them is Rs 150 an hour," he adds.

While Nihar, a musician himself, was part of a rock band in Pune since early college days, Viraj is the man who deals with the company's finances and strategies. "I do not have much knowledge about music but love listening to good music," Viraj says.

While the duo has hosted many musicians by ways of organizing live performances and acts, in August last year they were approached by a major portal for a partnership. "They required content and we had a lot of alternative music as well as videos on offer for them," said Nihar.

According to Nihar, to sum up their efforts in a single sentence, they are formalising and growing with an industry that's still in its early stages. "By introducing new artists and helping them with infrastructure is to create future market for the company as well in the alternative space," he says.

Overall, according to the two, it's the passion to promote good music that, above all, has helped them reach where they are. "I really had no clue about business management but had to do it because my family insisted on it but even as I finished management, I realized that I was not interested is such stuff and wanted to pursue a career with music at its centre," says Nihar. For Viraj, it's the challenge to create an enterprise of his own that keeps him going. The recent high was receiving support from none other than Sergymour Stein, the Warner Brothers' Music head honcho credited with bringing out Madonna's first album in 1981. "We had him here with us for a week's time in India and he has promised us to help us promote alternative Indian music internationally," Nihar gushes.

Heading: Weary of bomb hoaxes, railway cops ask for call tracing system - Indian Express
Content:
Man and wife drink poison; son and daughter found hanging after signing suicide letter

A financial crisis and debt prompted four members of a middle class family in suburban Mumbai to kill themselves on Friday. When the bodies of A K Nair (65), wife Shyamala (60), son Sudhir (46) and daughter Suchitra (47) were discovered on Sunday afternoon, policemen also found a suicide note that said they were "frustrated".

While investigators said a financial crisis was a key possibility, there was also speculation that the drastic move may have been prompted by the current slump in the markets.

Officials of the Kasturba Marg police said that the family of four appear to have taken the step on October 10, which was Dussehra. The bodies were discovered on Sunday after residents complained of a foul smell from the flat that had been rented to the Nairs and the owner of the flat was then called in to open the door with a spare key.

The family of four had been residing in the seventh floor flat of Ekta Woods building at Raheja Estate, Borivali (East) from February this year. "The bodies of the daughter and son were found hanging in the main hall, while the parents, it seems, had consumed posion. Their bodies were found in sleeping position in the bedroom," said zonal Deputy Commissioner of Police Ajit Patil.

Policemen spent a considerable amount of time removing the bodies from the flat. While the bodies of Sudhir and Suchitra were brought out first, those of the ageing parents could not be removed till much later at night, as they were heavily bloated and decomposed. The bodies were later sent to the Bhagwati Hospital for a post mortem.

Police said the suicide note had been signed by the daughter and the son, both unmarried. It mentioned that the family has no relatives. "We have no future. We have nobody to claim our bodies. We request the authorities to dispose them of as they see fit," the suicide note read.

According to the police, Suchitra had been planning to start an enterprise in her hometown. "She was holding a high post with Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited and had taken Voluntary Retirement from Service. She was looking at the possibility of starting a business in Trivandrum," said Senior Police Inspector P R Suryavanshi.

Patil said that investigations would continue on the cause for the suicide. Asked if there was indication of a serious financial crisis in the family, he said: "We cannot confirm it at present but are looking at the possibility."

Neighbours said the Nair family was always aloof and never spoke to anyone. "We hardly had any contact with the family. They didn't speak to anyone. There was no way to even actually know whether they stayed in the flat or not," said a neighbour.

Heading: Is Bigg Boss an indecent show? Lonavala police probe complaint - Indian Express
Content:
Close on the heels of the tough talking done by the Railway Protection Force (RPF) regarding hoax callers, the Government Railway Police has now said they hope to seek the Railways' assistance in tracing such callers.

With more than 40 hoax calls received by various railway police stations since January this year, Mumbai Railway Police commissioner A K Sharma has written to both the Central Railway and the Western Railway, asking them to install caller identification system for all telephones in key railway offices, railway stations and railway police stations of both the RPF and the GRP across the city.

"We get plenty of calls alerting us about bombs or explosives being kept in trains or on platforms and they all turn out to be hoax calls. This is mischief on the part of the caller as he or she either wants to play a prank or is running late to catch a long distance train," said Sharma. Most of the hoax calls were traced to public telephones or cellphones, with the caller usually offering a fake name and address for himself. However, some four or five callers were traced in recent months and a case was also registered against one caller.

"It becomes problematic for us to trace the caller since he calls up randomly and informs the railway stations or important railway establishments. Apart from the control rooms, all important offices do not have caller identification systems installed, which makes it difficult to trace the caller," added Sharma.

According to Sharma, some 15,000 man hours were wasted due to hoax calls since January. The hoax calls not only spread panic but also cause delays to long distance trains. Last month, the RPF's chief security commissioner B S Sidhu had submitted a proposal to the rail ministry seeking that hoax calls be treated on a par with 'terror activities'. The proposal is currently pending with the Centre for consideration.

"We have received the letter from the railway police and we are working on it. Currently, some seven to eight railway stations have caller identification system installed, but we plan to install it in other suburban stations as well. The telephone exchanges covering stations beyond Kalyan are currently not offering the caller identification facility. We have written to the telephone exchange to get this problem sorted out," said S Sharma, additional Divisional Railway Manager (CR). "We are working on it too," added S S Gupta, chief spokesperson for WR.

Heading: Big B stable, recovering well - Indian Express
Content:
Following a complaint of alleged obscenity on reality television show Bigg Boss, the Lonavala police on Sunday registered a First Information Report against three inmates of the "house". The FIR was registered after the Lonavala police viewed footage of the show, telecast daily on Colors.

Based on a complaint made by the Mumbai Youth Congress Committee (MYCC) alleging that the show "bred vulgarity, indecency and indecent representation of women", the Andheri police had registered an FIR against some of the participants of the show, the production house Endemol and Colors. However as the set where the show is recorded is located in Karjat, the case was being transferred to the Lonavala police.

Two Andheri police officers arrived at the Lonavala police station on Sunday afternoon with the case papers. Lonavala cops also reportedly visited the show's sets.

"We have been briefed by the Andheri police and filed an FIR against three of the show's participants — Rahul Mahajan, Payal Rohatgi and Sambhavana Seth, who have been accused of behaving in an obscene manner, under Sections 294/34 of the Indian Penal Code. Endemol and Colors have also been charged with telecasting the footage," said Senior Police Inspector of Lonavala S Darekar.

Representatives of the channel remained unavailable for comment despite repeated phone calls.

MYCC President Sunil Ahire and other party members had visited the Andheri police station on October 4 demanding that the police take action against the show's participants, producers, directors and the channel. However the police had firmly refused to take any step without first viewing the contested footage. "We had expressed a general protest. It was after the police saw the scenes that they themselves registered a case against the participants who were indulging in these acts," said Ahire.

"We viewed the footage and found that there are some scenes featuring Mahajan, Rohatgi, Seth and Raja Chowdhary which were obscene as the complainant had alleged. While we registered the case, as the location of the show is in Lonavala we will be transferring the case to the police there along with all clips of the scenes which were obscene. While they will be handling the investigation, we will assist them if needed," said P P Suryavanshi, Senior Police Inspector of Andheri.

Such scenes include Rohatgi and Mahajan shown together in a swimming pool, a massage in progress and a dance by Chowdhary and Seth.

"The Andheri police have given us a couple of CDs while the show has completed 62 episodes. We will call the producers and directors and channel tomorrow asking them to give us the CDs of all the controversial episodes. The evidence will also have to be presented to the court to draw up an arrest warrant. While Rohatgi and Seth will have to be called back as they have left the show, we won't hesitate to arrest Mahajan from the house if the accusations against him are found true," said S Darekar, Senior Police Inspector, Lonavla. He added Section 294 is a cognizable but bailable offence.

Congress MP and former Bigg Boss contestant Sanjay Nirupam congratulated the MYCC on their protest. Nirupam, who claimed that he had refused to be a part of the wild card round because he disapproved of the 'vulgarity and obscenity' said: "I congratulate the MYCC have not remained quiet on the indecency and I am glad that the law has taken its course. The show is surely not for family viewing and also flaunts national regulations of public viewing."

Heading: Later this week, city to join global hand-scrubbing movement - Indian Express
Content:
A day after Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan was admitted to Lilavati Hospital, doctors treating him said the superstar is "stable" and "responding to medication". While they refused to divulge the precise nature of his medical condition, doctors said he could be discharged in a couple of days if he continued to show positive signs.

Bachchan was admitted to the hospital on his 66th birthday after he complained of acute pain in the abdomen.

"He has had a restful night and the tests do not show any abnormality," said Dr Narendra Trivedi, vice-president of the hospital, in an official press statement issued early Sunday morning.

"The tests do not suggest any abnormality. Under the circumstances, medicines have worked. He has responded well to our line of treatment and will be discharged in a few days," he said.

On Saturday, sources said the actor was suffering from sub-acute intestinal obstruction (partial blockage of gastrointestinal tract) and also incisional hernia. On Sunday, the hospital maintained that Bachchan was suffering with "abdominal pain".

Thousands of Bachchan's fans, in the meantime, prayed and sent wishes for his speedy recovery. One group of 30 to 35, mostly Samajwadi Party activists, even held a rally outside the hospital on Sunday, to wish him a speedy recovery.

Bachchan was in the midst of his 66th birthday celebrations at his bungalow Pratiksha in Juhu when he was rushed to the Nanavati Hospital at Vile Parle on Saturday afternoon after complaining of abdominal pain and breathlessness. He was then shifted to Bandra's Lilavati Hospital where he continues to be under observation. He is being treated in Suite number 1101 on the 11th floor of the hospital.

His wife Jaya, daughter Shweta Nanda, son Abhishek and daughter-in-law Aishwarya Rai were all at the hospital for most of Sunday. Among the visitors on Sundya were close family friends Reliance ADAG head Anil Ambani and Samajwadi Party general secretary Amar Singh, Priya Dutt, Tinu Anand and Ram Gopal Verma.

Heading: Sarnaik surprises pundits, refrains from joining Sena at Dussehra rally - Indian Express
Content:
A modest school somewhere in Mumbai's outskirts is home to a roomful of children who rush out of their classroom to find somebody waiting to share their lunch dabbas — 'Master Blaster' Sachin Tendulkar, who not only admonishes them for not washing their hands before lunch, but also goes on to show them the right technique to washing, with soap. This 60-second television spot that's on air on Doordarshan's Sahyadri channel from Sunday will soon be translated into 13 other languages in the run up to the first ever 'Global Hand Washing Day' on October 15.

Tendulkar will also be on posters and banners as teachers across the country participate in the campaign, launched in the international Year of Sanitation. All government schools in Maharashtra and all Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) schools in Mumbai will be participating too — 32,000 schools in all. "We have already issued notices to all schools to observe the global hand washing day," said Sheila Tiwari, deputy director of education, Mumbai region.

Teachers from each of these schools have also undergone special training in sanitation and hygiene education. "The discourse for the day will be as per the guidelines, hand washing training, followed by the oath-taking, and a hand washing drill before the special mid day meal," said Anuradha Nair, a UNICEF official in Mumbai. Also planned are NSS camps to promote school health and sanitation and rallies by schoolchildren in smaller towns and villages.

Joint Municipal Commissioner Chandrashekhar Rokde said the BMC had already procured posters from both the Centre and the state governments. "We will put these up at every BMC school, in the eating area as well as near the toilets." He said all schools are equipped with washbasin but not soap. "We can certainly provide soap, it does not cost much," Rokde said.

"Children are catalysts of change. Ideally situated at the intersection of the home, school and community, children can be powerful agents of behavioral change. Schools can be important centres to educate children on health and hygiene issues, if proper water and sanitation infrastructure is made available," said Gopinath Menon, state chief of the UNICEF.

Globally, South Asia has the worst sanitation indicators and six of eight countries in the region are not on schedule for meeting the sanitation targets of the Millennium Development Goals, one of them being India.

Washing hands with soap prevents the transmission of disease and helps reduce diarrhoea and respiratory infections, as well as skin, eye and worm infections. A recent study suggests that washing hands with soap can reduce diarrhoeal diseases by over 40 per cent, and respiratory infections by 30 per cent, according to Menon. "Diarrhoea and respiratory infections are the number one cause for child deaths in India," said Menon.

"The idea is to make it a habit to wash hands at least after defecating, before and after meals and after sneezing. Also hand washing is a part of the massive campaign on sanitation," said Nair.

Across the world
* In Afghanistan, with the highest child mortality rate in the region, the government is backing hand-washing competitions and television talk shows
* In Bangladesh, some 1,00,000 playgrounds (more than 16 million children) will be buzzing with songs about cakes of soap
* In Pakistan, the famous animated figure of Commander Safeguard and even newscasters will join organizations including soap manufacturers and media groups to endorse hand washing
* Sri Lanka will popularise correct hand-washing techniques in clinics, hospitals and tea plantations
* In Nepal the new government will be actively engaged in hand washing events; and mobile phone companies will send out mass text messages reminding the Nepalese to get out the soap
* In Bhutan, animated videos will help spread the message that clean hands make strong bodies

Heading: Survey reveals dismal state of public's knowledge on facilities in Ulhasnagar - Indian Express
Content:
'I've only been suspended from the NCP and continue to be a member; I don't intend to quit now; maybe in a month or so I'll make a move'

Thane municipal corporator and suspended Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) leader Pratap Sarnaik surprised speculators and political pundits by not joining the Shiv Sena during the party's Dussehra rally at Shivaji Park. Sarnaik was suspended from the NCP last month.

"I've only been suspended from the party. But I still continue to hold the party membership," he told Newsline. "As of now, I don't have any intention to quit my party. Maybe in a month or so, I'll be making a move," he added.

Sarnaik, who has been an elected representative to the civic body since 1997, was suspended from the NCP on September 6 after criticising NCP Thane city unit chief Jeetendra Avhad over the appointment of Hanmant Jagdale as leader of the opposition in the civic body.

There was speculation about Saranaik's entry into the Shiv Sena after party's Executive President Uddhav Thackeray's visit to his Navaratri pandal at Vartak Nagar. However, Sarnaik hinted that he had no desire to quit the NCP but only wanted to embarrass the party leader by openly mingling with Sena members while continuing to be in the party.

Sarnaik cited the example of Mumbai MLA Bala Nangaonkar, who despite being elected on a Sena ticket has been supporting the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS). "Nandgoakar cannot be dismissed, though he espouses the cause of the MNS. He still continues to obey the party whip," Sarnaik pointed out.

According to some political sources, the dilemma faced by Sarnaik is that if he volunteers to join any other party, it will pave the way for his disqualification as a corporator. "It's the whip that makes the difference and the party may continue to claim him as its own corporator even though Sarnaik decides to join another party. The party would make a clear case of rebellion, if Sarnaik defies the party whip and cast his vote in favour of any other party. If he is ousted from the party, its whip would automatically collapse giving him the liberty to make his next political move while continuing to be a corporator. A seasoned corporator, Sarnaik has ambitions to contest the next Legislative Assembly elections. However, as the polls are still a year away, he wants to keep his cards close to his chest," the sources said.

NCP Vice-President Madan Bafna said that Sarnaik continues to remain under suspension and there is no change in his status.

First rose to fame with Dahi Handi
Pratap Sarnaik was first elected to the Thane Municipal Corporation on a Congress ticket in 1997. He later joined the Nationalist Congress Party. He rose to prominence with his Gokulasthami (Dahi Handi) celebrations.
The record of a nine-tier pyramid was made at the Dahi Handi organised by him this year. He was also in the news for gifting a diamond studded mobile phone to Ajit Pawar.
This mobile phone was auctioned by the Siddhivinayak Temple Trust.

Heading: Gaurav anchors GNPS win - Indian Express
Content:
At least 23 per cent of Ulhasnagar's population dumps their garbage out on the streets and open spaces, about 46 per cent residents are disposing of wastewater in unauthorized spaces — these and many such interesting facts have been revealed by a survey carried out in the city on public utilities.

Conducted by the Ulhasnagar Municipal Corporation in collaboration with Smt. Chandibai Himmatmal Mansukhani (CHM) College, the survey covered 30,000 families in span of two days.

According to the survey, the drainage system of at least 34 per cent of residences in Ulhasnagar is not connected to the municipal drainage system and only 45 per cent is connected to the septic tank.

On the health front, the survey said that residents' understanding of prevention is not very common with at least 40 families showing ignorance on the preventive measure on monsoon-related diseases and communicable diseases.

The report, prepared by the students of CHM College who carried out the survey, recommends the UMC to introspect why 45 per cent families either has no knowledge on the existence of civic hospitals or are not using the services of these hospitals.

Municipal Commissioner Samir Unhale assured that the effort of the students would not go waste as the civic body would set-up a committee of elected representatives and civic officials for considering the recommendations of the report. "This survey could be a role model for other civic bodies to emulate as it provides the public perception on the civic services," said Unhale.

Principal of CHM College Dinesh Panjwani said: "This report has provided us an insight into the ground realities in Ulhasnagar, some of which are very encouraging and some are very challenging. If taken in the right spirit the corporation can use this report for strengthening public utilities. Also, our college can develop more meaningful community welfare projects on adult education, school dropouts and civic responsibilities of the citizens."

Appreciating the unique collaboration, vice-chancellor of Mumbai university, Dr Vijay Khole said that the survey of 30000 families by 3000 students in two days was a record feat that may vie for a Guinness record. The use of students in surveys has not been exploited and there is tremendous scope for determining the quality of civic services."

Ulhasnagar is estimated to have one lakh families and this survey having reached 30 per cent of the families makes the results more than acceptable indicator of the citizen's feedback.

Heading: Parminder bowls Sigma XI towards victory - Indian Express
Content:
Buoyed by a fine half-century by Gaurav Sharma (75), Guru Nanak Public School, Sector 36 score an emphatic 76-run win over APJ Academy, Kharar in a league match of the Inter-Academy Cricket Championship for Under-14 being conducted by Desh Prem Azad Cricket Academey on Sunday.

GNPS Academy batted first and scored 188 for 8 in allotted 30 overs. Gaurav Sharma was the top scorer for GNPS playing a fine knock of 75 runs which was studded with nine boundaries and he was ably assisted by Gaurav who played a solid knock of 34 runs. Arpit Singh contributed 25 runs.

For APJ Academy, Vardhman claimed two wickets while giving away 24 runs while Sahil claimed two wickets for 26 runs. Sarthak claimed two wickets giving away 40 runs.

In reply, APJ Academy could manage a total of 114 for 9 in the stipulated 30 overs. Kapil was the top scorer for APJ Academy playing a knock of 45 runs while Pukhraj made 24.

For GNPS, Vaibhav was the pick of the bowlers claiming three wickets for 17 runs while Saurav claimed two wickets for 12 runs.

Brief scores:

GNPS : 188 for 8 in 30 overs (Gaurav Sharma 75, Gaurav 34, Arpit Singh 25, Vardhaman 2 for 24, Sahil 2 for 26, Sarthak 2 for 40); APJ Kharar: 114 for 9 in 30 overs ( Kapil 45, Pukhraj 24, Sarthak 12, Vaibhav 3 for 17, Saurav 2 for 13, Harry 1 for 6, Arjit 1 for 3, Arpit 1 for 20).

Heading: NPS cagers enter final - Indian Express
Content:
A fine bowling performance by Parminder (4 for 16) enabled Sigma XI defeat Airtel XI by 36 runs in the ongoing Second MG Cup League Cricket Tournament, being organised by the Chandigarh Sports Club here at DAV Senior Secondary School, Sector 8 on Sunday.

Batting first after winning the toss, Sigma XI had a disappointing start as the openers were back in the pavilion within two overs at a score of 10 runs. Sandeep Mehta steadied the ship for his team and made 32 valuable runs for his team and helped it to get to a score of 139 runs for the loss of 8 wickets in 25 overs. Manpreet and Rajesh instilled a terror in the batsmen with their lethal bowling and a great fielding by their team-mates. They shared six wickets between them giving away just 40 runs in the process.

In reply, Airtel XI never seemed in the fray as their batsmen were giving away their wickets from the beginning of the innings. Parminder was the pick of the bowlers as he picked up four valuable wickets for the team and was pretty economical giving away only 16 runs. Manpreet was the highest run getter for his team as he made 37 runs. In the end

Airtel XI were bundled out for 103 runs in 19.4 overs.

In the second match of the day, INSCOL XI bowlers ripped through the bating line up of Citi Financial to hand their team a 39 run win.

Batting first, INSCOL could manage only 112 runs for the loss of eight wickets in 25 overs, as the batsmen were not comfortable at the crease and were under pressure as the fielders did not allow any ball to pass through. Mithun showed some finesse and chipped in with 40 runs for his team. Ashok Kumar was the pick of the bowlers as he picked up 2 wickets for 13 runs.

In reply, Citi Financial had a bad start and the batsmen were throwing away their wickets form the word go. Only Amit Sharma crossed 20-run mark and Deepak and Loksh were the other two batsmen who got to double figures. Ramesh was the wrecker in chief as he picked up 4 wickets for 17 runs.

Brief scores:

Sigma XI : 139 for 8 in 25 overs. (Sandeep Mehta 32, Anoop 21, Manpreet 3 for 25, Rajesh 3 for 15, Alok 2 for 27); Airtel XI : 103 all out in 19.4 overs. (Manpreet 37, Vinay Bhardwaj 27, Parminder 4 for 16, Sukhwinder 3 for 6);

INSCOL XI : 112 for 8 in 25 overs. (Mithun 40, Rajesh 21, Ashok Kumar 2 for 13, Vikas 2 for 23); Citi Financial: 73 all out in 16.2 overs. (Amit Sharma 21, Deepak 12, Ramesh 4 for 17, Ravi 3 for 27).

Heading: Neeraj fashions Fortis win - Indian Express
Content:
On the occasion of World Arthritis Day, a joints replacement and arthritis cure camp was held at SPS Apollo Hospital on Sunday. As many as 150 patients participated in the joints check-up camp.

The camp was held to make the patients aware of options of joint replacement therapy and get their questions answered on managing the pain of osteoporosis and rheumatoid arthritis, said Dr Harpreet Singh Gill, Orthopedician and Joints Replacement Surgeon, during the inaugural lecture.

Dr Rahul Bhan , another renowned orthopedician and joints replacement surgeon, said that this year, the theme for World Arthritis Day was 'Think Positive'. This theme acknowledges that the challenges associated with arthritis/rheumatism could also affect you emotionally, but that there were a number of positive things you could do to help you feel better and get more from your life.

Newer knee joint implants have better quality and they last longer. They are so designed that a patient can even sit cross-legged. Surgical techniques have also undergone a revolution with minimally invasive surgery being the order of the day. As female's bony structure is different from males, hence specially designed knee implants are used for them.

Dr Rahul Bhan informed that some latest advancements in joint replacement surgery were the minimally-invasive surgery where the size of incision was half the size of conventional incision, which is more cosmetic.

Heading: City DAV colleges shine in state wrestling - Indian Express
Content:
A Blazing knock of 81 runs off just 61 balls by Neeraj Rana enabled Fortis Healthcare XI to defeat United Sports Club by 91 runs in the ongoing fifth Godrej Defender Cup organised by the Chandigarh Sports Club on Sunday.

Electing to bat first, Fortis Healthcare lost one of the openers at the team's total score at 22. Thereafter, Neeraj came to bat and played some brilliant shots all over the ground. His innings included four boundaries and three towering sixes. The team did well to score

161 runs for the loss of eight wickets in the allotted 25 overs. Vinod emerged as the most successful bowler with two wickets for 28 runs.

Chasing the target, United Sports were bowled out for a paltry 70 runs in 15.3 overs. Vindo Sharma was the only batsman to reach the double figures. Sukhwinder and Harman bagged three wickets each.

Meanwhile, in the second match of the day, Godrej CC humbled HDFC Bank XI by six wickets. While batting first, HDFC put up 160 runs on the board.

Vipin Chauhan's contributed 46 runs to the team's total score. Gurinder Saini chipped in with a useful knock of 38 runs. Inderjeet picked two crucial wickets for the Godrej CC team.

In reply, Godrej CC openers gave a good start to the team. Umesh Kaira made 45 runs while Kulwinder Aromy made a brilliant 41 runs. Vipin Chauhan also shone with the ball as he picked up two wickets for the team.

Brief scores:
