Heading: 64 sites to go under hammer on Oct 23 - Indian Express
Content:
"It is a myth that men are more susceptible to heart diseases. Women are at a higher risk of contracting cardiovascular diseases," said Dr J P S Sawhney, consultant cardiologist, Sri Ganga Ram Hospital. He was speaking at the Continued Medical Education (CME) 2008, held at Hotel Shivalikview today.

Talking about the sensitivity that surrounds heart diseases, Dr Sawhney said that women fear cancer more than cardio-vascular diseases (CVD), which is why not many women take symptoms like chest pain seriously.

"CVD is the biggest cause of death among women in the US. The trend is equally alarming in developing nations, with India taking the lead. The way our lifestyle has altered has a lot to do with the increase in the number of women falling prey to CVD," he said. He cautioned that post-menopause, the risk of acquiring CAD and CVD increases manifold.

"Women at the age of child-bearing do not come under the danger zone as they have hormonal protection; once they enter menopause, they become prone to CVD. The possibility of pre-menopausal women suffering from CVD increases four times if they smoke," said Dr G S Kalra, Director, Cardiology, Fortis Hospital.

The symptoms related to CVD among women, feel the doctors, are too few. "While the warning signs are too many among men, the symptoms in women are a few and subtle. Women experience pain in the shoulder and jaw, sweating and nausea, which should not be ignored," said Dr Rajneesh Malhotra, senior consultant cardiac surgeon at Indrapastha Apollo Hospital.

Elaborating on factors leading to CVD in women, Dr Sawhney said that sedentary lifestyle is largely to be blamed. "There is a lack of activity among women, which often leads to obesity. Apart from this, smoking also adds to the risk. Hypertension, which increases steeply after menopause, diabetes and stress are other vital factors," said Dr Sawhney.

While 50 per cent of risk factors are genetic, 80 per cent is acquired through habits that one forms, feel doctors. "We need to bring about changes in our eating habits. Consumption of desi ghee, red meats and alcohol should be in moderate quantity. One should eat more of fresh vegetables and fruits. All dairy products need to have good cholesterol, which should be greater than 40 mg/dL in men and 50 mg/dL in women," Dr Malhotra added.

Heading: With spiralling commercial rentals, small fish relocate to other sectors - Indian Express
Content:
Reserve price calculated by enhancing the last auction's average price by 5%: Bid for one-kanal plot kept at Rs 2.65 cr

After a year, the Chandigarh Administration is all set to hold another auction of the residential and commercial sites in the city. While the tentative reserve price for a residential plot is expected to fetch Rs 53,000 per square yard; the reserve price for a commercial site is being pegged at Rs 3.05 lakh per square yard.

The auction for 64 sites — 35 residential and 29 commercial-will be held at Hotel Shivalikview on October 23.

The commercial sites include five shop-cum-offices in Sector 32-D and one shop-cum-flat in Sector 7-C, besides booths in Sectors 7, 24, 29, 37, 40 and 44.

Going by the tentative figures, the reserve price for a four-marla residential plot (100 square yards) will be around Rs 53 lakh. This is the smallest plot-size category among the 35 residential sites to be put up for auction.

The tentative reserve price for a 7.5 marla plot (187.5 square yards) is expected to be Rs 99.37 lakh. A 10-marla plot (250 square yards) will cost around Rs 1.32 crore. For a 14-marla plot (350 square yards), a buyer will have to shell out Rs 1.85 crore. A one- kanal plot (500 square yards) will cost Rs 2.65 crore. The tentative reserve price for a two-kanal plot (1,000 square yards) will be a whopping Rs 5.3 crore.

The last auction of residential and commercial property was held in December 2007, after a gap of three years. While the reserve price for residential plots in the last auction was around Rs 30,000 per square yard, for the commercial plots, the figure was Rs 1.35 lakh per square yard. The auction saw an average of Rs 50,000 per square yard for residential plots and Rs 2.9 lakh per square yard for commercial sites.

Calculating the forthcoming auction's reserve price on the formula of "enhancing the reserve price by 5 per cent more than the last auction's average price of total auctioned sites", the UT Finance Department has already given tentative figures of the reserve price to the UT Administrator for his approval. The approval is expected in the coming week.

In the small category, four four-marla plots will be auctioned in Sector 42-B; two five-marla plots in Sector 38-D and nine one-kanal plots in Sector 32-D; Sector 38-C; Sector 40-B, 44-A and 46-A. There are only two two-kanal plots in Sector 33-B that will be put up for auction. Six 14-marla plots in Sector 37-A and 40-B will also be put up on auction apart from ten 10-marla plots in Sectors 37 and 40.

"The file with the tentative reserve prices has been sent to the Administrator for his nod. The enhancement is definitely there, but it is subject to the prevailing market rates and the average of the last auction," said a senior UT Administration official.

Reserve price doubles in four years

* While the UT Estate Office had auctioned the residential sites in 2004 at an average selling price of Rs 25,719 per square yard, this time the tentative reserve price is expected to be more than Rs 53,000 per square yard.

* In the commercial-site segment, the reserve price in 2004 auction was Rs 1.17 lakh per square yard. The forthcoming auction on October 23 is expected to have a tentative reserve price of Rs 3.05 lakh per square yard.

Terms and conditions

* The interested bidder will have to deposit an earnest money of Rs 2 lakh in cash or by means of demand draft to be eligible for participating in the auction

* 25 per cent of the bid accepted by the auctioning officer will be paid at the fall of hammer through a demand draft; failing which the earnest money (Rs 2 lakh) would be forfeited

Heading: In Panchkula, authorities have ‘no information’ on Right to Information - Indian Express
Content:
With the owners of commercial properties in Sectors 8 and 9 on Madhya Marg demanding exorbitant rents, the number of vacant sites in these sectors has gone up. High rentals have led to existing medium and small establishments like restaurants and consumer goods shops to move to other lesser attractive spaces, making it affordable only to big companies.

"The benchmark for rentals has increased manifold over the years. Rentals have increased by almost 100 percent in the past one year. Five years ago, the rent for a showroom in Sector 8 on the Madhya Marg was around Rs 3 lakh. Today, it has shot up to more than Rs 16 lakh. The upcoming auction will further boost the rentals considerably," said Mangat Rai Baboota, a real estate consultant.

The rent of an 8000-square feet showroom, if divided floor wise, comes out to be Rs 12 lakh for the ground floor, between Rs 3 lakh and Rs 4 lakh for basement and first floor. According to the existing trend, multinational companies take the complete showroom on rent rather than independent floors.

The same rentals exist in Sector-17 main market. According to sources, recently a showroom rented out by a popular sweet shop in Sector 17 to a clothing chain is fetching Rs 16 lakh a month.

With rentals spiralling northward, the percentage of vacant commercial spaces has also amplified.

"At present, the availability of vacant commercial spaces in these sectors is 15 per cent, which otherwise could have been an excellent source of income to the landlord and tenant," says R P Malhotra, general secretary, Property Owner Welfare Association, Chandigarh.

The rent in other sectors like 7, 26 and 35 is almost half the rates at Sectors 8, 9 and 17. This is forcing small and medium enterprises to relocate to cheaper areas or inner markets of these sectors.

Heading: 15 tie the nuptial knot at mass marriage - Indian Express
Content:
Ridiculing the Right to Information (RTI) Act, the Haryana government offices in Panchkula are misinforming the public. While a notice, posted at various offices, claims that Rs 2 per page will be charged for any information under the RTI Act, the applicants are made to shell out Rs 10 per page.

The officials, unaware of the amount being charged, prefer to remain tightlipped even when quizzed about the basic rules of applying through the RTI Act.

"If you want to file an RTI with the department, we will first have to check the rules. While we are not aware of the amount that is to be charged, the notice board affixed outside the office would give you complete details on the Act and the required payment," said an official of the District Public Relations office, Panchkula.

The official added that the RTI application would be accepted only after having a word with the senior officials, as most of them are unaware of the rules.

For senior BJP leader Gyan Chand Gupta, the RTI Act is being ridiculed at by the Haryana offices. "On seeing the details put up on the notice board, I went ahead filing an RTI with the ADC department asking for the complete 'Below poverty line' (BPL) list of urban and rural areas of Panchkula.

While initially it took the department four days to accept my RTI application, I was made to run from one official to another to deposit the fee of Rs 50, as no official of the department was ready to even accept the application," said Gupta.

The BJP leader added, "Worst came when we were told that the department was not even aware of who was the State Public Information Officer (SPIO) for their department," said Gupta.

In yet another case, while Gupta applied for an RTI from the Haryana Public relation department asking for some information, he was asked to deposit Rs 40,000.

"As the amount was high, I requested the department to supply the information in a CD for which only Rs 50 is charged, but I was told that the department had no CD available. So the only option with me was to deposit the amount if at all I wanted the information," added Gupta. He said that while all the other states charge Rs 2 per page, Haryana has been charging exorbitantly, thereby, discouraging the very concept of the RTI.

In another case, when an RTI was filed in the Haryana Public Relations department by our Newsline reporter, seeking information on the various programs having been conducted by the Haryana Kala Parishad, the parishad directly went ahead asking for a payment of Rs 15,000 from the applicant, jumping all the rules and regulations of the RTI Act.

According to the RTI rules, the assessed amount is to be communicated to the applicant through the SPIO or the Assistant SPIO and not any third incumbent.

Talking to Newsline, Meenakshi Anand, head of the Haryana Information Commission said, "Rs 10 per page is being charged from the applicants. If any department has displayed wrong information, action would be taken against it.

As far as the rates are concerned, we have till date received no complaints claiming that they are exorbitant."

She also added that training is imparted from time to time to the various SPIOs and ASPIOs.

"There have been several penalties levied against officials who fail to comply with the RTI rules. It is always through the SPIOs that the RTI information has to be communicated to the applicants," added Anand.

Heading: After nine years, farmer to be compensated for poor quality seeds - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Dalit Chetna Manch on Sunday solemnised the marriages of 15 couples belonging to poor families. The ceremony took place at Ramgarhia Bhawan in Phase 3B2 in Mohali.

Heading: Kharar civic body chief to be elected today - Indian Express
Content:
As you sow, so shall you reap, goes the old saying. But it took nine years and a trying time running from pillar to post for a Mukstar-based agriculturist to finally be awarded with compensation for the 'defective seeds' he sowed way back in 1999.

Alleging his entire crop was destroyed and he suffered huge losses, the farmer had moved the district consumer forum, Mukstar then. After being first rejected by the district forum, his appeal was finally heard by the Punjab Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in 2004 and the seed manufacturer has been asked to compensate Rs 69,000 for the costs of the seeds and his agricultural income now. The manufacturer is also entitled to pay the farmer litigation costs of Rs 10,000.

Paramjit Singh, a resident of village Bhulerian in district Mukstar had purchased 40 kilograms of paddy seeds at a cost of Rs 560 from Pagia Enterprises in Mallout in April 1999. After sowing the seeds, he spent a huge amount in various inputs like fertilisers, insecticides and pesticides.

Alleging that the plants that grew were of varying sizes and varieties which resulted in huge losses for him, he moved the district forum in Muktsar claiming compensation of Rs 1.5 lakh for mental tension, losses and costs incurred.

In the reply, Pagia Enterprises stated that the said seeds were duly certified by the UP government. It said the seeds were analysed from the Seed Analyst Laboratory, Ludhiana, and were found as per specifications. The complaint was then dismissed in 2000.

Undeterred by the order, the agriculturist appealed to the State Commission where his appeal was accepted and the district forum was directed to decide the case afresh. In 2005, the district forum directed Pagia Enterprises and Kissan Beej Bhandar to pay joint compensation of Rs 1.8 lakh to the agriculturist.

The seed manufacturers further appealed to the Punjab Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

On the basis of a report by the Agriculture Development Officer, the commission found that the plants of paddy were not uniform in height or growth. "Some plants were high while others were of medium height and others were of dwarf size. While the roots of some plants were red, those of others were green in colour, depicting inferior and mixed quality of seeds," the report said.

President, Punjab State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, S N Aggarwal, ruled that the remedy lies in compensation to be paid to the farmer for defective seeds. The commission, however, found that the seeds were sown in five acres of land and not twelve acres as alleged by the farmer. The verdict also ruled that no separate compensation is required for mental tension and harassment.

Heading: Insurance firm to pay up for not issuing policy on time - Indian Express
Content:
The Kharar Municipal Council (MC) will elect its president and two vice-presidents at a special meeting of the MC on Monday.

Rajeev Kumar Gupta, Kharar Sub-Divisional Magistrate, who was appointed as convener by Mohali Deputy Commissioner Rahul Bhandari, has issued a notice to all the 15 newly elected councillors, for holding the first meeting to administer the oath of allegiance and conduct the election for the same.

With this, the Administrator's rule at the Kharar MC, which was in place since March, when the five-year term of the previous civic body ended, will also come to an end. New councillors were elected during the general elections held on September 14, and the presidential election was delayed due to a litigation filed in the High Court, which was disposed recently to pave way for holding the same.

With the much-awaited presidential election now less than 24 hours away, the lobbying for the top posts has reached a flashpoint.

The opposition Congress, which has only two councillors besides Kharar MLA Balbir Sidhu, who as an ex-officio member, has a voting right in the MC, and has started hobnobbing with the rival Akalis and independents to capture the top post. Punjab Cooperation Minister Captain Kanwaljit Singh, who had worked to ensure the clean sweep of the ruling SAD-BJP combine in the MC elections by winning 10 of the total 15 seats, meanwhile, is confident of the ruling alliance taking over the reigns.

A group of at least nine councillors are required to elect the president.

Sources said that a group of five councillors has gone underground on the eve of election, while Balbir Sidhu, was busy holding meetings with a senior Akali leader, believed to be the arch-rival of Captain Kanwaljit, and an Independent MLA, to split the SAD-BJP combine.

They further said that the five councillors elected on the symbol of the 'Rising Sun' of the SAD-BJP combine, are in touch with the anti-Captain Kanwaljit group, which enjoys the support of at least two independent and two Congress councillors besides Sidhu, to reach a consensus on the name of the presidential candidate. They added that Sidhu, a rebel Akali leader and an independent MLA, have reached a consensus to topple Captain Kanwaljit's choice for the presidential candidate.

They said the anti-Captain Kanwaljit group is considering the name of an independent and a councillor from the SAD-BJP, for the top post as Sidhu has reportedly given his unconditional consent to nominate anybody, who is against Captain Kanwaljit's choice.

Officer shifted

The state government shifted Kharar MC Executive Officer Sunil Kumar Gulati and posted Raj Kumar Mittal in his place. Mittal was earlier posted on same post at the Zirakpur MC.

Heading: Sukhbir promises 1 lakh houses for EWS within a year - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed an insurance company to compensate a senior citizen who was not issued insurance policies for months after making payments for the same.

A resident of Sector 11, Panchkula, Wing Commander (Retd) RC Bedi moved the consumer forum alleging that he and his family suffered mental harassment after Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance Company Limited failed to issue policies to them. He had made the payment against a cheque of Rs 7.5 lakh for three proposal forms of life insurance, treatment and hospitalisation exigencies. After waiting for days on end without any response, Bedi finally decided to cancel the proposals.

The UT consumer forum directed the insurance company to pay Rs 30,000 as compensation along with Rs 5,500 as costs of litigation. The firm had refunded Bedi's amount with interest earlier.

Heading: All India Conference of Intellectuals held - Indian Express
Content:
"The Punjab Government will build one lakh houses for the economically weaker sections (EWS) in various parts of the state within a year. Also, before giving approval to any integrated township on an area of 100 acres or more and with an investment beyond Rs 100 crore, the government will make sure that 10 per cent is reserved for the EWS," said Sukhbir Singh Badal, President, Shiromani Akali Dal, at the inaugural function of JTPL Townships Pvt Ltd in Mohali today. He said the government will spend Rs 2,000 crore on the development of Mohali, especially on infrastructure. "The land for the expressway between Mohali and Baddi will be acquired by December 2008," he said.

The township is spread over an area of 85 acres of prime land, of which, the first 70 acres has already been approved by the government. An IT, ITES space and a hotel will also be developed within the township. The rate of the plots will be Rs 14,000 per square yard and Rs 25-30 lakh for the apartments. The company plans to spend around Rs 450 crore in the next three to four years. The time frame for completion of the project is four years.

Heading: Private schools have no seats for EWS students - Indian Express
Content:
"Education is the key to human progress, life and peace and we should not lose sight of that," said Dr GVG Krishnamurty, while speaking at the annual celebrations of the All India Conference of Intellectuals, held at SD College, on Sunday.

"The present generation does not know how to respect elders. We must not forget our culture in our quest to be westernised," he said.

Dr AR Kidwai, Governor, Haryana, was the chief guest on the occasion. Educationists and academicians from Punjab and Haryana were conferred the Haryana Ratna and Punjab Ratna awards by Dr Kidwai. Dr Ashok Chitkara of the Chitkara Group, Professor RK Kohli, Department of Botany, Panjab University, were among those honoured with the Punjab Ratna. The awardees for the Haryana Ratna included Dr KC Bhardwaj, Vice-Chancellor, Chaudhary Devi Lal University, Sirsa, Anjali Marriya, Principal, CL DAV School, Panchkula.

Heading: ‘Medical tourism to soon become one of India’s greatest revenue generators’ - Indian Express
Content:
Many private schools in the city have failed to follow the directions issued by the Education department, which has made it mandatory for all schools to admit a minimum of 15 per cent students from the economically weaker sections (EWS) of the society. While the Department says they have taken note of this, schools are violating the norms unchecked.

According to the data procured from the Education Department, out of the 57 schools assessed by the Department for the norm as in June 2008, only eight schools have admitted 15 per cent of their total strength from the economically weaker sections of the society.

Schools including Chandigarh Baptist, Dutt Vishesh, St. Anne's, Paragon Convent are among the few schools that have more than the required percentage of students from the economically weaker sections. While Chandigarh Baptist has 23.5 per cent, Dutt Vishesh has 19 and St. Anne's has 27.6 per cent students studying under the EWS.

On the other hand, of the 560 students studying in Strawberry Field School, only 0.7 per cent belong to the EWS. St. Soldier School, too, has an equally alarming figure of only seven students out of the total 1189 studying under the EWS scheme.

The Education department had issued instructions to all the private schools in the city to follow these norms as an effort to provide quality education to students from poor families. Many schools, however, have not followed the norms. While most erring principals refused to come on record, others said they will admit the required number from the next session onwards. "This process takes time. We are working on it and have not denied admission to anyone belonging to a poor family. But they are not willing to come forward," said a principal requesting anonymity.

Among the other schools that have not admitted students from the EWS are Bhartiya Vidya Bhawan, Sector 27 (4.36 per cent), DAV Public School, Sector 8 (2.03 per cent) and Ryan International School (0.5 per cent).

Commenting on the issue, Samwartak Singh, Director Public Instructions (Schools), said the department has taken serious note of the schools that have not followed the rules. "It is a serious matter. Education is the right of every child irrespective of his economic status. We will make sure that they are not denied their right," he said.

Heading: ‘Spare your time to save the country’ - Indian Express
Content:
"India is fast emerging as the hub of medical tourism. With most hospitals in the country offering the best medical facilities, medical tourism will soon become one of the greatest revenue generators," said Dr Rajneesh Malhotra, senior consultant cardiac surgeon, Indraprastha Apollo Hospital. He was speaking at the Continued Medical Education (CME) 2008 at Hotel Shivalik View on Sunday.

India has seen a significant rise in the number of tourists coming for treatment in the past decade and the number is expected to increase steeply in the coming years. "If we operated upon 6,000 patients in a year, 10 per cent were foreigners... we see a rise in these figures. Patients are coming not only from neighbouring countries but also from developed nations like the US and UK," said Dr Malhotra.

He attributed the reason for India being the preferred destination for medical tourism to many factors. "Leading private hospitals in the country are offering world-class facilities to patients. With state-of-the-art hospitals to world-renowned doctors, tourists are getting everything they require. Indian hospitals have excellent workforce, infrastructure too is similar to international standards," he said.

"Cost is one of the prime reasons that people from abroad are flying down to India for their treatment. While medical facilities are very expensive in foreign countries, the cost here is one-tenth. One can get a bypass surgery done for 6,000 US $ in India and the same costs 40-50,000 US $ there," Dr. Malhotra stated. He added that most patients come for cosmetic and cardiac surgery and dental operations. "Of late, joint replacement is also picking up as it is very cheap in India, priced around Rs 2 lakh," Dr Malhotra said.

The doctor feels that the concept of medical tourism should not remain limited to private hospitals. "Government medical institutions too should participate in this. Though they need to work a lot on improving their standards, but it is not impossible," he said.

Heading: Cyber Crime Cell arrest one for extortion over web - Indian Express
Content:
'The Territorial Army is a voluntary part-time civilian force. It gives civilians an opportunity to receive military training and also provides the country with a reserve force that can assist the Indian Army'

He won the finals of the 1983 cricket World Cup at Lords and made India proud by captaining a weak Indian squad with good leadership qualities. The same person — Kapil Dev — has set the standard for celebrities in various walks of life by joining the Territorial Army (TA) as a Lieutenant Colonel.

Not far behind is Punjab's Finance Minister Manpreet Singh Badal, who even after being one of the busiest persons in the state, decided to join the Territorial Army.

When the two icons don the Army uniform, it will be a big morale booster for the defence personnel and aspiring youngsters who want to join the same. We are already facing a shortage of officers in the Army and there is a dire need to inspire the youth to opt for the Armed forces. And I believe the two have done a commendable job.

It is certainly a slap on the face of those celebrities and politicians who only talk about patriotism. But when it comes to leading from the front, they vanish from the scene.

The celebrities including film stars, sportsmen and politicians should learn that instead of promoting hair gels and shampoos, they should lead by example and this can be done by enrolling themselves into the Army. It is the need of the hour and a noble way to fill the increasing gap of officers in the Army.

The Territorial Army is a voluntary part-time civilian force that has a role to play in the defence of the country.

It gives the civilians an opportunity to receive military training and also provides the country with a reserve force that can assist the regular Army during operations, whenever required.

Territorial soldiers undergo military training in their spare time either as part of a formed local unit or as specialists in a professional field.

Territorial Army members have a minimum commitment to serve 27 training days per annum, with specialists only required to serve 19 days that normally includes a two-week annual camp. The celebrities can easily spare this small amount of time to serve the country.

Since its inception in October, 1949, the Territorial Army has rendered valuable service, both in times of war and during internal disturbances. One should feel proud in being a member of the Territorial Army.

Heading: Former home secretary acquitted - Indian Express
Content:
Cyber Crime Investigation Cell of the Chandigarh Police today arrested one Puja Negi, for involvement in an "extortion through the Web" racket.

Police said one of the accused, posing as Shelly, met and chatted with complainant Manjit Singh (name changed) of Chandigarh online on October 1 this year. During the conversation, the complainant disclosed personal information, which the accused later used to blackmail the victim over the phone, saying she would disclose their relationship to his parents if he did not fulfill her demands.

"The complainant parted with valuables like his mobile phone, a Play Station 3, a webcam, a wrist watch, sunglasses and recharge coupons worth Rs 4,500. Another of the accused collected the items from the complainant.

Police said the accused demanded another mobile phone and more recharge coupons from the victim and asked him to wait with the items near Airtel Mobile Buzz, Zullu in Sector 17-E. The victim then reported the matter to the Cyber Crime Investigation Cell, who arrested the accused from the designated spot. The girl, is a resident of Sector 39, Chandigarh.

Heading: Cn & heard - Indian Express
Content:
Former UT Home Secretary, NK Jain, was acquitted of corruption charges in an eight-year-old case by the CBI court on Saturday. The co-accused in the case, Ex-Superintendent of the UT secretariat, KB Goel, however, was convicted of corruption charges.

The court of special CBI judge Jagdeep Jain, found Goel guilty of replacing the answer sheets of a clerk recruitment examination. The quantum of Goel's sentence will be pronounced on Monday.

The case dates back to April, 2000 when the CBI had registered a case against Jain and Goel under the Prevention of Corruption Act for misuse of official powers and acceptance of illegal gratification. A Haryana-cadre IAS officer, NK Jain, was booked when Goel in his confessional statement said he resorted to unlawful means at the behest of the former home secretary.

Baljit Singh, an employee of the State Transport Authority, had complained to the CBI that Goel had allegedly demanded a hefty amount to allow him to remain on the same post.

Facing charges of forgery, Goel was also accused in a case involving the recruitment of clerks in the Home department, in which, he allegedly changed the answer sheets of a few candidates.

Sources said in order to prove allegations, the CBI produced more than 20 witnesses before the court but a majority of them turned hostile.

The prosecution reportedly also claimed that among many other allegations levelled against the two officials, the Vigilance department had received an anonymous complaint accusing the two of demanding bribe from a private company, which wanted to make smart cards.

It was also alleged that in connivance with KB Goel, NK Jain, took bribes for the transfer and reinstatement of various officials and recruitment of clerks.

Heading: INLD back in NDA-fold - Indian Express
Content:
The wise men had predicted that things would be turned on its head in Kalyug. While they meant it metaphorically, here is a literal and visual exhibition of that. See the picture above which shows Ravan with nine heads. The ten pates of the legendary king of Lanka were a symbol of the immense wisdom he possessed, but it looks like that the Ravan of Kalyug is one head less wiser than Ravan of yore!

Anything for you Mam!

The better half of one of the Deputy Inspector General of Punjab was recently 'accosted' by a traffic policeman for violation of a rule. The cop on duty showed amazing alacrity in issuing a challan to the lady who was on the wheel of her personal Maruti Zen. It was when the receipt was handed to the lady that she revealed her identity. The cop was mortified but couldn't do much about it because the receipt had already been issued. So, he took the receipt back along with the licence, went and deposited the 'fine' himself and then personally delivered the licence back at madam's home. Bravo!

Traffic awareness drive

The traffic cops do not reserve their congeniality only for the wives of the top shots. Consider the case of a violator who was caught while talking on a mobile phone. The only relevant documents which he was able to produce were the challan chits of previous violations, which happened to be for the same offence i.e. talking on phone while driving. Our concerned constable advised the repeated offender to buy a handsfree phone set. He also gave the shop address from where the driver could buy it at a reasonable price. Thanks Mr Cop but isn't talking even on hand-free phone while driving unlawful too ?

Prince of Kolkata versus Prince of Chandigarh

Sourav Ganguly's announcement to retire from Test cricket after the ongoing India- Australia series has fuelled hopes of the city residents that Chandigarh's lad Yuvraj Singh could be the heir to Ganguly's spot in the Test team. Unfortunately, this looks highly improbable as of now. While no one doubts Yuvraj's talent but his records in Test cricket are hardly encouraging. In fact, he has been criticised for not making the most of the chances that have come his way. With the likes of Rohit Sharma and Badrinath also staking promising claims to Ganguly's place, the Prince (Yuvraj) of Chandigarh will have to work extremely hard to replace the Prince of Kolkata.

Friends forever

The bonhomie between the new Home Secretary and the Finance Secretary is too conspicuous to be missed. The pictures of the two hugging each other like long lost friends were splashed across the papers the day the Home Secretary joined. During a recent book release also the two behaved in a similar manner with the HS specially inviting FS to join the function and declaring that the two would do everything together. Here's hoping that the bond lasts forever!

The name still rings a bell!

The former DPI(S) S K Setia has left his impressions in the Education department in such a way that even after so many days of his discharge, the school principals are still receiving the orders under his name detailing their duties for his innovative plans. Thanks to the inexhaustible proposals mooted by him during his tenure.

Show me the money!

Haryana Chief Minister's announcement that his state would be the first to implement the provisions of the Sixth Pay Commission, gladdened the hearts of state government employees. They started conjuring images of higher salaries and what they planned to do with it. Their hopes that the announcement was likely to made in the festive season has now received set back with the state government not making any formal announcement to this effect. The employees are wondering if they will actually get to see the promised monies or not.

Heading: State BJP to toe the line - Indian Express
Content:
To contest LS polls with BJP; no precondition, says Chautala

The Indian National Lok Dal today rejoined the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance and announced that it will contest the coming Lok Sabha elections in Haryana in collaboration with the BJP. INLD, the principal opposition party in Haryana, had snapped ties with NDA in February 2004.

Announcing the tie-up here, BJP national president Rajnath Singh, senior BJP leader L K Advani and INLD supremo Om Prakash Chautala said the main objective of the alliance was to push the Congress-led UPA out of power.

The two parties did not mention about the number of seats each will contest in Haryana. "The alliance is not based on preconditions ... in 1998 too I had extended support to Atal Bihari Vajpayee without any conditions attached," said Chautala.

To a poser on the future of the alliance, Rajnath Singh said, "INLD is an uncompromising, anti-Congress force ... the alliance will ensure that Congress is voted out of power." Chautala claimed that Congress has vitiated the political atmosphere of the country. "We will together cleanse the atmosphere," he added.

Rajnath claimed that the INLD rejoining the NDA was only the beginning. "I had said months ago that the number (of allies) will increase," he said.

No representative of any of the NDA constituents were present at the press conference at the BJP headquarters. Om Prakash Chautala claimed his aim was to ensure that the NDA becomes "as strong as it was in 1998."

A joint statement issued by the two parties said INLD and BJP would organise a variety of campaigns to highlight the "anti-kisan (farmer), anti-people and corrupt record of Congress." To a poser on BJP's stand on two-party system, L K Advani said "multiplicity of parties" was a must for Indian democracy. "It was the BJP which created bipolar polity in the country by uniting parties against the monopoly of Congress," he added.

Advani claimed that with NDA and UPA having been in power, the voters will find it easier this time to make a choice. "We had fought terror, worked for the benefit of the common man and even antagonised the US by conducting a nuclear test ... under the UPA regime, the biggest problem is inflation," he said.

When Rajnath was asked about BJP's state unit launching campaign against "corrupt INLD leaders," he replied that when "parties are united under an alliance, they have their individual agenda ... no court decision has come out against anyone so far."

During the last Lok Sabha elections, Congress had won nine out of ten seats in Haryana, while the BJP had managed to bag one. BJP has negligible presence in Haryana with the Congress and INLD occupying most of the seats in the state Assembly. Chautala's sharing platform with SAD and JD(U) chiefs Parkash Singh Badal and Sharad Yadav, both major constituents of NDA, at a rally in Bhiwani recently had given clear indications of a tie-up.

Heading: Wakf invites applications for vocational courses - Indian Express
Content:
After the announcement of an alliance with their bitter foes, the Indian National (INLD), by the central leadership, state BJP leaders have been forced to eat their own words. Having suffered, what they term, insults and humiliations at the hands of the INLD after the two came to power in the Haryana Assembly elections in the year 2000, the BJP had decided to sever relations with its alliance partner in 2004.

The state BJP leaders had since vowed never to have an alliance with the INLD. Till the last moment, they insisted against the alliance, but political compulsions reportedly forced the BJP high command to go ahead with the pact, sources say.

As for the INLD, it has now become part of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) again, following another shot at forming a Third Front.

Though seat-sharing between the BJP and the INLD is still to be finalised, sources say the BJP is likely to contest six seats and the INLD four. The INLD would, in all likelihood, be given the Bhiwani, Hisar, Sirsa and Kurukshetra seats. However,sources in the INLD said they would insist for at least five seats.

Meanwhile, the BJP is planning to sound the poll bugle with a state-level rally at Sonepat on October 31, to be attended by senior leader Lal Krishna Advani.

Incidentally, one section of the BJP had also advocated a pact with the newly-formed Haryana Janhit Congress (HJC BL) of Kuldeep Bishnoi, but the idea did not click with the top brass.

After their break up in the year 2004, the BJP and the INLD fought the last Lok Sabha and Assembly elections on their own. While the BJP managed to win just one seat in the Lok Sabha, the INLD drew a blank. But in the assembly elections that followed the next year, INLD managed to win nine seats, while the BJP had to be content with just two, compared to the six it had won in the previous assembly polls.

Reacting to the alliance with the INLD, Atam Prakash Manchanada, president, Haryana BJP, who had opposed such an alliance earlier, said they will abide by the wishes of the party High Command. "Ours is a cadre-based party. We will definitely do well in the Lok Sabha polls,'' he said.

Kishan Chand Sangwan, BJP's lone MP in the state from Sonepat, said the party leaders had expressed their views on the alliance to the high command, but now that the decision was made, the two partners would certainly benefit from the move in their fight against their common enemy, the Congress. Senior BJP leader Gyan Chand Gupta also welcomed the alliance.

Ashok Arora, INLD Haryana president, too welcomed the alliance, saying it was to the benefit of both the parties, as had been proved in the 2000 Lok Sabha and assembly elections in the state as well.

Reacting to the development, Kuldeep Bishnoi, president of the HJC (BL), said the alliance would benefit his party as majority of the BJP leaders and party workers hated Chautala. "All the disgruntled elements in the BJP and other parties would now rush to the HJC," he claimed.

Heading: Centre constitutes power reforms steering committee - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana Wakf Board has invited applications from Haryana-resident Muslim students for admission to six-month computer education and beautician training courses.

A spokesman of the board said that the minimum qualification for computer education course is 10+2 and for beautician course is class 10.

The annual income of the parents of the candidates applying for the course should not exceed Rs one lakh. The last date for applying for the course is October 30.

The board has also invited applications from doctors for empanelment in the board for providing basic health facilities to the poor, particularly in the areas of Mewat, Palwal, Faridabad, Panipat, Yamunanagar and Panchkula.

Applications have also been invited from companise and individuals interested in imparting training in computer education and beautician courses.

Heading: Three killed in road accident - Indian Express
Content:
The Union Ministry of Power has constituted a steering committee for implementation of the Accelerated Power Development and Reforms Programme (APDRP) under the 11th five-year plan. The committee would be headed by Union Power Secretary Anil Razdan.

A spokesman of the Haryana Power Utilities said here today that Haryana would have a strong representation in the steering committee as the state's financial commissioner and principal secretary (power), Ashok Lavasa, has been appointed as a member of the committee for one year.

The committee would approve the guidelines for operationalisation of various components of the scheme, including the approval of the charges to be paid to the nodal agency; it would sanction projects, including modification of revision of estimates and monitor and review the implementation of the scheme.

It would also sanction activities to be taken up by the ministry under part C of the scheme, appoint agencies for verification and validation of base-line data systems and approve conversion of loan into grant.

The spokesman said that the Power Finance Corporation would be the nodal agency for the programme, and would provide manpower, material and other logistic support to the committee for smooth implementation of the programme.

Heading: Transmission losses down by 12 pc in six months - Indian Express
Content: Three persons were killed after their bike collided with a tractor near Kheri Chopta here on the Hisar-Jind road, police said on Sunday. The accident occurred last night when the bike collided with a tractor coming in the opposite direction, police said. While one person died on the spot, others succumbed on the way to hospital. Two were identified as Suresh from Rajasthan and Jaghir of village Sisia Bolan here. The another is yet to be identified. A case has been registered against the tractor's driver, who is absconding.

Heading: Pay commission to be implemented soon: FM - Indian Express
Content:
The Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN) has claimed that its transmission losses have gone down by 12 per cent in the last six months.

Officials said the nigam has achieved considerable reduction in aggregate transmission and commercial (AT and C) losses.

The losses have gone down to 25.52 per cent and 33.23 per cent, respectively, in 2007-08 against 39.42 per cent and 42.65 per cent during the financial year 2001-02. Nigam officials claim they would bring down the losses to 16 per cent by the end of the current financial year.

Besides, revenue collection has also been increased by over nine per cent in the past six years; from about 92.4 per cent in 2001-02 to over 101 per cent in 2007-08 in the area which falls under the DHBVN and from 89.19 per cent in 2001-02 to 99.96 per cent in the area under the purview of UHBVN.

A senior official said it is the result of replacement of faulty and mechanical metres with new electronic meters and segregation power in a proper way from low-tension wire system to high-tension wire system.

Adequate transformation capacity in the distribution system is another important step taken by the distribution corporations.

Heading: The Road Marshals - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana Finance Minister Birender Singh today said that the recommendations of the Sixth Pay Commission were being reviewed by a four-member committee headed by the Chief Secretary and those of for pensioners by a three-member committee.

Following their reports, the recommendations of the sixth pay commission would be implemented in the state, he said. He asserted that the recommendations of the sixth pay commission would be implemented in Haryana either by Diwali or by the end of the year.

Birender Singh, who was addressing a press conference at village Gorakhpur of Fatehabad district, said that Haryana had received an investment of Rs 40,000 crore and an investment proposals to the tune of Rs 27,000 crore were in pipeline. Now the depression, which is a global phenomena, had affected the process of investment resulting in slowing down of investment process.

With regard to the alliance between the INLD and BJP, he said that people would not support these parties, as they had not forgotten their misdeeds.

Heading: Taking Stock - Indian Express
Content:
Smitten by the thrill of the game, these 'officials' make sure its a safe 'Raid'

It's the sport of the raw and the real. Real roads, real machines, real danger, and driving all over them - real heroes. It's time, yet again, for the Raid-de-Himalaya, and before the machines could get menacing, here are the men who have been on the road for a good eight months now, traversing the length and breadth of the route, checking, re-checking the cavities and crevices, loose-ends and loopholes and filling them up with their timely intervention. These are the safety-hands behind the scenes, the officials or the marshals of what people call the most dangerous rallies of our times. They have braved weather and criticism, they've tried and tested the raid route, stood under the naked cold sky waiting for cars to take a safe pause. And they go about all this silently. "Real heroes don't boast. They simply do it and move on," says Vijay Parmar, the man behind the Raid, and President of Himalayan Motorsports Association. As the Raid takes off at Shimla on October 2, we try to scrape and understand their grilling routine, and what brings these men back on the road trip every year despite all the hurdles and challenges.

Working relentlessly to make sure that everything falls into place, Vijay Parmar, the man behind the success of the Raid feels, it's better said than done. "Organising Raid is one helluva of a job. The preparation for the event begins six to seven months in advance. Right from deciding the route, getting permissions, checking accommodation, safety checks, everything is taken care of by the officials," he adds. Manjeev Bhalla, the only Indian to navigate a European rally champion, believes that marshals are the real fighters at the Raid. "We have to handle emergency situations without panicking," the man's on guard all the time. Associated with the difficult feat for four years now, Bhalinder Sangha, proprietor Sangha Motors', enthusiasm never diminishes. "As a rallyist, I've tasted blood, and the rally will always be my passion!" he grins.

"Officiating Raid is not a simple job, it involves a lot of physical and mental stress," reflects Nikhil Jaspal, an OEM supplier with Punjab Tractors and founder - 'Team Chandigarh'. "We have to brave difficult weather conditions, stand 24/7 under the cold winter sky, but it's so much a part of our lives!" Who said standing on the road throughout the day, without a breather was a cakewalk? "It's not a nine to five job, it's a 24 deal," quips Nikhil, telling us about the gruelling schedule that includes getting up in the middle of the night to preparing for the day and be at round-the-clock vigil.

This time round, about 800 officials are on their feet for the event, and most of them have given their profession a break. Says Gulpreet Aulakh, co-founder 'Team Chandigarh' and a businessman running a credit appraisal agency in North India, "the 'very tiring schedule' is nothing because there is thrill and fun too. We get to see new places which otherwise we would have never even thought of visiting. There is a temple in Kunzum Pass where it is believed that you have to travel around it for a safe journey and good health, so we never miss that one!"

These are people driven by passion and adrenaline rush. Ask what it takes to be a official and they shoot, passion and patience. Remarks Kishie Singh, one of the officals, "Patience is the key word at Raid. An official has to wait till the last car crosses the route. Sometimes we have to go in search of a car that gets off the radar, and sometimes we have to get up in the middle of the night in case of an emergency." As for Manjeev Bhalla, you have to bitten by the adventure bug. "There is no way you wouldn't be on the fag end of the road, waiting to hear the engine grrring from a distance." When it comes to passion, stakes don't matter.

Heading: Second list of ‘irregular’ appointments released - Indian Express
Content:
Director Shona Urvashi mints sense out of sensex

At the risk of causing a severe bout of indigestion to the opposite sex, we'd like to quote, and agree with fillmaker Shona Urvashi when she states 'women are smart'. "Take an ordinary housewife, the way she runs a house on a strict budget and manages to save and invest. Women know how to do business and they can be savvy with the sensex," Shona, who turned 'bullish' with her latest film, Saas, Bahu Aur Sensex, takes 'stock' of the situation and shares that it's no rocket science. "It became more clear when I got down to research women as investors and came across amazing examples, most of them housewives...in fact, there was one in Chandigarh I talked to, one Anu Rai, who tracks the market on a regular basis," for Shona, the idea of getting a nation's favourite characters, saas and bahu, and hitting a high on the sensex with these unlikely players was simply irresistible. "C'mon, what can be more typical? The obsession with them is finally justified," she chuckles, the film being her second after Masumeh (they are sisters) and Zulfi Syed's Chupke Se.

In a country where women are still treated as second class citizens, Shona's tried to tweak the laws of physics in her favour and give the audience, especially the women, something to feel great about. For starters, she has the adorable Farooque Sheikh as the women-hating stockbroker and Kirron as the vivacious on-the-move housewife. "I'm trying to capture a silent revolution where women are more than just bhenjis and bhabhijis," she feels that a lot of under confidence among women is due to negative perceptions men enforce on them. "We should take pride in whatever we do, after all women make up half of the planet," she shrugs off the 'niche subject' adage and exclaims - "move over men, we need our space!" Had she not had her baby girl, Shona, who comes from a family that's given us masterpieces like Hero Hiralal, Chashmebaddoor, Jalwa and Khatta Meetha, would've directed Jaane Tu Ya Jaane Na. But that was then, now is the time for raging bulls and bear hugs, which reminds us of the spat with Tanushree Dutta. "Bollywood has this thing of blowing up the teeniest of issues. It was something real small and people do it just to attract attention and be different," she reasons.

She's a trained Bharatnatyam dancer, a sharp photographer, great writer (in days when Maharashtra Herald had only men reporters), and fine actor. "All in one, it's being a director," Shona's sticking to her choice of profession, and yes, making everyone see green with her investments. "Of course, I'm hooked," she chirps. Lookout for her next: "a romantic commercial blockbuster script." Till then, lets 'stock' and 'share'.

Heading: Tough days ahead for Ahluwalia; bail plea to come up today - Indian Express
Content:
Shimla police arrested 40 protesting teachers, who had returned for dharna outside the Secretariat after having released on the bail. Yesterday, more than 70 striking teachers were arrested, but later released on bail.

Meanwhile, the government released the second list of the irregular appointments ordered by the earlier government.

A spokesman of Education Department said,"Numerous irregularities have been found in the appointments such as ignoring qualification and merit."

The inquiry revealed the candidates were appointed without following proper procedure, violating of rules.

The spokesman said the government received 134 complaints from Rohru area of which 63 candidates were recommended for discontinuation of service.

The details of other irregular appointments were also released.

Heading: Dhumal plans cabinet expansion - Indian Express
Content:
Expecting his bail application tomorrow, Subhash Ahluwalia may find state's Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau acting tough.

Sources in the Vigilance Bureau said a proper custodial interrogation is required to verify several sensitive details of his alleged dispropotionate assets.

Two bank lockers at Panchkula, belonging to Ahluawalia and his wife that were surrendered within three months, could provide vital clues about his movable property.

"The lockers were operated frequently but were suddenly surrendered," a senior Vigilance official told The Indian Express. The Vigilance team grilled Ahluwalia for two hours at the IGMC hospital's private ward, where he has been admitted.

"Unless Ahluwalia provides full details of the sources of the assets, the

Vigilance will continue interrogation,"he added. Another issue which has come to the notice of the Vigilance is that his property has been grossly undervalued.

His flat in Gurgaon has been valued at Rs 11.75 lakh which, the Vigilance officials say, is 40 per cent of its actual value. A plot at Ropar is valued at Rs 5.75 lakh, another plot at Kaithu in Shimla is valued at Rs 5.15 lakh. Two other properties at Panchkula and Rampur are also undervalued. " We will seek further remand tomorrow and will apprise the court with full facts," he said.

Ahluwalia was arrested last week but was admitted to the hospital. The court had given four days remand which will end tomorrow. Meanwhile, his request for bail is pending for hearing. Ahluwalia's wife, who is also a senior government servant, is also under the vigilance scanner.

Heading: Celebrations end on a bitter note - Indian Express
Content:
Representation from Mandi on the cards

Ahead of party's preparations on completion of its one-year rule, Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal is weighing the option for cabinet expansion to fill-up two existing vacancies—-one these from Mandi district.

If the plan materialise, Dhumal may invite Jairam Thakur, who is also the state president and not keen to contest the upcoming Lok Sabha poll. He also plans to consolidate BJP's position in Mandi district, where Congress is using the row over opening new medical college in the private sector to capitalise on the simmering anti-BJP sentiments.

Two other names going around include former minister and MLA Roop Singh Thakur and Maheshwar Singh, a former MP and senior party leader. Mandi has only one cabinet minister-Gulab Singh Thakur, out of the six MLAs elected in December 2007 elections. According to sources poor representation of the district is already causing discontentment in the party cadres.

The other contender for the cabinet could be from Una district- which is part of Hamirpur Parliamentary constituency. The district has not yet got any representation in the government.

According to sources, Dhumal wants to give Congress a serious challenge in Mandi, instead of his home district Hamirpur.

His close aides said it was PCC president Kaul Singh Thakur's political "coup"in Hamirpur that provocated Dhumal.

Thakur tried to jolt the BJP by luring Narinder Thakur to Congress, to field him against Anurag Thakur, Dhumal's son and BJP's candidate for next Lok Sabha election from Hamirpur. "Everyone is free to chose his political future. If Congress is happy with new entry, BJP wishes it good luck. This development has not affected our position in the district," Chief Minister said, reacting for the first time on Narinder Thakur's exit.

Now Dhumal plans to take his battle across the district's boundaries. With an eye on the Lok sabha polls, Dhumal has announced two medical colleges for Mandi. An international airport, which is expected to cost nearly Rs 750 crore and IIT campus are other plans on the cards.

Heading: Himachal confidential - Indian Express
Content:
The two-day Gurta Gaddi Divas, organised by local Guru Singh Sabha to celebrate 300 years of the Guru Granth Sahib, ended on a bitter note here today.

Shankaracharya of Kanchi Kamkoti Peeth Jayendra Saraswati along with Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal, former chief minister Virbhadra Singh, PCC president Kaul Singh and other social figures attended the function.

Kartar Singh Takkar,member of Gurdwara Prabandhak Committee, Paonta Sahib, raised objection about Shankaracharya's seat. Dhumal snubbed Takkar and said Shankaracharya,who had come from Tamil Nadu to attend the function, enjoys a very high position in the Hindu religion. "You should respect other religions and avoid such comments and hurts the feelings of others," Dhumal said.

Chief Minister did not appreciate Takkar raising certain issues relating to development of Paonta Sahib and said the government was aware of its role. "One should know, where to raise such issues," he added.

Speaking to mediapersons Shankaracharya said was overwhelmed by the treatment and honour given by the sikh leaders.

Heading: The Great kidney bazaar - Indian Express
Content:
Who next?

The ruling BJP suffered a blow when Narender Thakur shifted to the Congress. But the Congress had to cut short the celebrations as state's Vigilance Bureau arrested Virbhadra Singh's close aide Subash Ahluwalia, a serving IAS officer. Former chief minister's blue-eyed boy B.R. Rahi, former chairman HP Board of School Education was the next victim after government cleared his criminal prosecution. The Congressmen are left guessing who would be next in the line of fire.

Well-prepared

The PTA teachers who are protesting against government's decision to hold an inquiry into their irregular appointments had come prepared to face the wreath. It is learnt that since they knew the situation could go out of hand, men wore two-three jeans to reduce the impact of the cane blows. However, the real victims were the women who had to suffer the most.

Birds of a feather

Bureaucrats, who were close associates of Subash Ahluwalia, did not know how to react after he was arrested by the Vigilance Bureau. IAS lobby, police officers switched off their cell phones and refused to take calls from the media.

Champions in olive

The 11th Koti golf tournament saw town's golf enthusiasts, from IAS, IPS, Army, in full action at Naldehra on Saturday. When Army lifted the trophy, one team member said, "One should not expect us to defeat the Army. Be it fighting enemies on the border or a golf match, they are the champions."

Heading: Authorisation committee - Indian Express
Content:
Amritsar hits the headlines whenever a kidney racket is exposed. Top doctors have allegedly worked in connivance with the bureaucrat-politician lobby to make the city a hub of organ trade.DHARMENDRA RATAULthrows light on the shady alleys that were exposed in the past, but are still swathed in darkness

The recent controversy over donation of a kidney to a bureaucrat, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Tarn Taran Kirpal Singh ,has again conjured up the same demons that haunted Amritsar in 2003.

A poor youth, Sunny, alleged that he was promised a government job and monetary help in lieu of his kidney to the officer. Sunny, who earlier said that he was ready to part with his vital organ for the PCS officer out of "love and affection" for him, later not only backtracked, but also spilled the beans, much to the agony of Kirpal Singh, who is fighting for life at a private hospital in Mohali.

Amritsar seems to have become synonymous with kidney scams. In 2003, a multi-crore racket involving about 480 illegal human organ transplants was unearthed here. Doctors and middlemen, with active involvement of bureaucrats, were running the racket.

At that time, the present Amritsar SSP Kunwar Vijay Partap Singh had brought the well-heeled and powerful to book. The case is now pending in three separate fast-track local courts here. However, the lawyers and police officials are skeptical about the case reaching a logical conclusion, as many witnesses have turned hostile. But the fact that is more worrisome is that illegal trade of human organs continues unabated in the city and this case has not proved to be a deterrent for the traders.

"Had there been proper investigations and sincerity to punish the accused, things would have been different. The high and mighty take advantage of legal anomalies, besides a lot of money is involved in the racket," says Justice Ajit Singh Bains (retd), who heads the Punjab Human Rights Organisation (PHRO) that had carried out its own probes into the human organ sale scandal.

However, legal experts dealing with the high-profile case feel that verdict, whenever it's delivered, would be historic and exemplary in the judicial history. A mammoth 178 witnesses are to be questioned in courts, which has already sentenced at least six persons to three to four years of imprisonment.

However, Bains says all these convicts are mostly mediators and donors and are out of the jail as they had already served their sentences during the trial.

"The big fish, including Dr P K Sareen and other top city doctors, are still facing serious charges," he adds.

"Some witnesses have turned hostile. But that is not going to affect the case, which is all set to reach the logical conclusion. The process of recording statements of a large number of witnesses is on," says Additional District Attorney (ADA) RK Salwan.

SSP Kunwar Vijay Partap Singh, who as an SP City-I had unearthed the racket five years ago, echoes Salwan's views, "Some witnesses have gone missing and some turned hostile. But we are always ready to help legal authorities in tracing missing persons. I will not comment further as the case is sub-judice."

Commenting on the legal lacunae, Salwan says the accused, mostly doctors and donors, had also sought to include recipients of kidneys in the accused list, but their applications were turned down by various courts, citing legal provisions. "There might be some delays due to such pleas, but the case is heading towards a logical conclusion," says another lawyer dealing the case.

Brief case-2003

Top city doctors were pocketing lakhs of rupees, throwing legal norms to winds, by luring the poor, illiterate and needy to donate kidney to influential and rich in exchange for jobs. Various doctors, bureaucrats, lawyers and political leaders were involved in the case. The operations were conducted at Kakkar Hospital situated in the heart of city, where Dr Sareen was employed. The other doctors whose names popped up in the scandal included Dr O P Aggarwal and Dr Jagdeesh Gargi, who were booked and arrested under the Human Organ Transplantation Act. They were accused of not routing transplantation cases through the authorisation committee. Dr Gargi was then head of the Forensic Sciences Department. The kidney scam had shaken the very foundations of the doctor-patient relationship.

Donor's tale

One Sukshil Arya dangled the bait of a good job and brought Sikandar Ali, who lived in a Delhi labour camp, to Amritsar. Ali, however landed at Kakkar Hospital, where his kidney was removed and given to Arya in exchange for a pretty penny.

After running from pillar to post, Ali got a case registered at Lahori Gate police station in Delhi in 2003, in which he disclosed how the doctors at Kakkar Hospital removed his kidney, leaving him with various ailments that ruined his life. His case is pending in the Delhi's Tis Hazari Courts, while the accused are out on bail and no charges were framed, "as the doctors are in public service". Ali now keeps unwell, and with no means of income, he cannot even arrange a two-square meal for his family.

Sonia's death failed to move anyone

Last year, death of three-year-old Sonia Dubey, whose kidney was removed without the consent of her parents allegedly by former principal of Amritsar Government Medical College JPK Shergil, brought more shame to the Holy City.

Though Dr Shergil was absolved of all charges, Sonia's parents demanded an impartial investigation. Her father, Shridhar Dubey, staged a series of protests and sought registration of a murder case.

However, his pleas fell on deaf ears and the crestfallen father quietly left for his home in Shidhaua village in Gonda district of Uttar Pradesh. After Dr Shergil was reinstated, she said it was an attempt by her rivals to defame her.

GURGAON LINKS

In 2007, when the Gurgaon kidney scandal came to light, Amritsar-based middlemen and doctors again brought the city to limelight. It was alleged that had the investigations in the 2003 kidney scandal been in the right direction, the Gurgaon case would have been exposed years before. Various names of the middlemen that popped up in this scandal had also figured in the 2003 racket. It was found that after getting bails from the local court, the accused had been playing a major role in the Gurgaon racket. A middleman, Vicky Bhatia, who was the kingpin in Amritsar kidney racket, was found boasting of conducting operations in other parts of the country. Later, a Ludhiana-based teacher, Prof Kiran Kapoor, also gave a written complaint to SSP Kunwar Vijay Partap Singh, saying that Dr P K Sareen was conducting operations in Delhi and Ranchi. Prof Kiran's allegations were investigated, but the police authorities never made the final report public.

KNOCK ON COURT'S DOORS

Irked over the "improper investigations" by the SIT into the kidney scandal, the PHRO has filed a writ petition in the Punjab and Haryana High Court. "The SIT did not investigate operations conducted outside Amritsar properly. The middlemen, after fleeing from the Holy City, following a police crackdown, started working outside the state, and made good use of their experience in the illegal trade," says Justice Ajit Singh Bains (retd) in the plea. PHRO principal investigator Sarbjit Singh Verka says, "The SIT failed to nab the judicial officers, political leaders, lawyers and other influential persons. The middlemen, who were freed, and the doctors, who are on bail or released, were found involved in other such rackets elsewhere. There is no end to the organ transplant business."

Heading: Legalising donation - Indian Express
Content:
Every time a kidney scandal shakes the state, the body that comes under the scanner is the authorisation committee. Earlier, the committee comprised doctors, heads of the Forensic Department, surgeons and principal of the local Government Medical College. After the 2003 kidney scandal, the committee was re-constituted with the Deputy Commissioner as its head and the SSP and the Civil Surgeon as members. But despite this, it failed to reform the process of clearing the kidney donation and the glaring example is the recent clearance Kirpal Singh's case. Tarn Taran DC Khushi Ram was holding the additional charge of Amritsar DC-- as K S Pannu was on leave for his foreign tour-- when a hurriedly-called meeting of the committee cleared the case for donation.

When the episode came to light, Pannu was back and the first decision he took after assuming office was canceling the authorisation committee's sanction.

This case leaves many questions unanswered. In Kirpal's case, police had given its report, the committee had said that it was convinced that the process did not involve money and the donor agreed to give away his vital organ out of "love and affection". However, later, this proved wrong, and no action was taken against the committee.

Heading: MLA local area fund doubled - Indian Express
Content:
A slew of controversies has triggered a debate in the medical and legal fraternity regarding rationalising and legalising the organs transplantation. Experts feel that the trade should be legitimised by formulating a legal framework to buy and sell organs. Advocate V P S Bhatia says that a minimum amount should be fixed for taking organ for transplantation, but it will require legislation changes.

Those in favour this argument also says that every individual has the right to sell his organs. But those against the argument say that India has a huge population of poor, and a legal support would give rise to large-scale selling of organs, giving rise to more tragic stories. There is also an argument that no country has so far legalised the trade. "The authorisation committee should be more transparent in its working. But, legalising transplantation is the only answer," says right activists Sarbjit Singh Verka.

Civil Surgeon Lehmber Singh says, "The Human Organs Transplant Act, 1994, bans organ trading. I want more debate on the issue and if there is a consensus then we should rationalise transplantation by bringing changes in the law."

Heading: NCM: Review cases against blacklisted NRIs - Indian Express
Content:
In election mode, Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal today announced an additional Rs 2 crore for the development of every assembly constituency.

With this announcement, every MLA would get Rs 4 crore for local area development. Of the additional Rs 2 crore announced today, a sum of Rs 1 crore would be utilised for improvement of education and infrastructure.

"While the DCs would be asked to prepare lists of infrastructure required in various schools, the government will ensure that every school has a teacher," the CM said.

The CM was speaking at a function held to mark the laying of foundation stone of the Rs 123-crore ambitious revamp project of Patiala feeder and Kotla branch at the local Desh Bhagat School grounds in Babanpur village, near here.

By doubling the local area fund, the CM also tried to brush aside the allegations of meting out special treatment to Malwa. "There is no bias towards Malwa and we would like every part of the state to develop." Rejecting the Congress' demand for a White Paper on alleged discrimination meted out to Majha and Doaba, Badal said equal opportunity was being provided to every part of the state. He also listed out examples of various projects initiated in Majha and Doaba. Earlier, Badal said he would again meet the Union Agriculture Minister and Prime Minister for ensuring a bonus of Rs 200 per quintal of paddy.

Badal said the revamping of first Patiala feeder and Kotla branch would benefit four lakh farmers of Sangrur, Mansa, Bathinda, Ludhiana, Barnala and Patiala districts. He said with the completion of strengthening and brick-lining of the canal by March 2009, additional 68,624 hectares would get water for irrigation. Irrigation minister Janmeja Singh Sekhon said, "Apart from canals, the government has chalked out a plan for repairing drains and distributaries."

Sangrur MP SS Dhindsa, former and present Dhuri MLAs Gaganjit Singh Barnala and Iqbal Singh Jhunda, respectively, also spoke on the occasion.

Heading: AISAD chief: move on to unite splinter Akali groups - Indian Express
Content:
Emphasising the need to connect non-resident Indian (NRI) Sikhs-- who were blacklisted for supporting extremist groups in the eighties during terrorism in Punjab-- with the mainstream of the country, the National Commission for Minorities (NCM) has asked for a review of the cases lodged against them.

The commission adopted the report submitted by NCM member Harcharan Singh Josh last month and has sent it to the Central government for further action.

Josh submitted the recommendations after a visit to London in August. The commission member had gone there to participate in India's Independence Day celebration organised by Southwark Hindu Centre of London. The commission has noted that some of the Sikh migrants, after Operation Bluestar and anti-Sikh riots in 1984, joined the terrorist camps, where they were exploited and used against the Indian government.

The government of India had put names of such persons in the blacklist due to which they are unable to get Indian visa and passports. "Now they have realised their fault and want to come back to India in the main stream," the commission said.

Heading: PAU-201 variety will also be bought - Indian Express
Content:
The All India Shiromani Akali Dal (AISAD) chief Jaswant Singh Mann today said that concerted efforts were on to re-unite various splinter Akali factions in the state to "expose" the ruling SAD-BJP government.

He said CM Parkash Singh Badal's regime was marked by bad governance and incompetence, where development had come to a standstill. Mann, while talking to mediapersons along with his party office-bearers, including Bharpur Singh Balbir, Manjit Singh and RS Dhillon, said in the coming parliamentary elections, they would come on a single platform to pose a challenge to the SAD- BJP.

He said his party was open to an alliance with the Congress. He said the SAD (1920), headed by Ravi Inder Singh, SAD (Amritsar) of Simranjit Singh Mann, and SAD (Panch Pardhani) of Daljit Singh Bittu should join hands.

Asserting that the Congress was not anti-Sikh, he said Badal had first time become MLA on a Congress' ticket in 1957. Expressing concerns over rising attacks on minorities, Mann said they would organise a minority conclave in Chandigarh on November 1, in which representatives from Muslim, Sikh and Christian communities would participate. He said the recent attacks on churches in Orissa and Karnataka and rape of nun were shocking.

He also said, "Dakhani Sikhs (converted Sikhs living around Nanded in Maharashtra), Nanak panthis living in Madhya Pradesh and Bihari Sikhs were part of the Sikh community, but no one has ever thought of looking after them. We will bring out a Sikh mission, wherein they would be given prominent representation."

He said the population of these Sikhs was three crore in the country and they could have an influence in 104 parliamentary seats, out of the total 545 in the country.

Heading: Sikh women raise concern over low sex ratio - Indian Express
Content:
The much-in-news paddy variety, PAU-201, developed by Punjab Agricultural University, would finally be procured from Monday.

The paddy was not being picked up earlier as it was brownish in colour, which led to doubts over its quality. Punjab Mandi Board chairman Ajmer Singh Lakhowal said, "To dispel all doubts, the state government has announced that this variety will also be picked up."

The variety was promoted by PAU and the Department of Agriculture after the state decided to delay the sowing of paddy in Punjab, as the variety matures faster than other varieties. As per B S Sidhu, Director, Agriculture, "Of the total 26.6 lakh hectare under paddy, one-fifth had this variety."

The variety is more popular in the south-western districts of Punjab and is widely grown in the CM's home district, Muktsar.

Dr N S Malhi, Director, Extension Education, PAU, said, "The university is convinced with the quality of PAU-201 and its traits were recently demonstrated to representatives of the Rice Millers' Association, FCI and Markfed."

"The president of Rice Millers' Association, Tarsem Singh Saini, has made it clear that millers will purchase this variety," he added. Dr Malhi advised the farmers to contact the district administration concerned in case of any problems during procurement.

Meanwhile, the problem of excessive moisture content in paddy this season continues to dog the farmers.

Distress sale of paddy in Amritsar, Gurdaspur and Batala districts has also been reported, where farmers are being paid Rs 30 to 40 less than the MSP. This money is being charged by commission agents for drying the crop. Lakhowal also admitted to instances of distress sale being brought to his notice, which, he claimed, were settled on the spot."

Principal Secretary to CM D S Guru, who is currently on a tour of state mandis, said he has directed all agencies to pick up paddy and pay the farmers within 48 hours. He assured, "FCI has promised to procure 10 per cent of the crop. The state will not tolerate any diversion from the promise."

Heading: Industry should be based on state’s natural resources: Kalia - Indian Express
Content:
Expressing concern over the low sex ratio in Punjab, Sikh women intellectuals, at a seminar held here, urged the government to strictly implement the PNDT Act.

The seminar, which was presided over by Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Gurbachan Singh, was organised by Global United Sikh Women's Organisation.

Dr Paim Rajput, a researcher on women's issues, said India falls in the category of countries ranking lowest in terms of sex ratio in Asia Pacific, while Punjab had the most abysmal sex ratio in the country.

Gurbachan Singh said the women were responsible for the crimes committed against them, and they need to summon courage and be more vocal about the abuse.

Sikh scholar Dr Mohinder Kaur Gill attributed the practice of female foeticide to zamindari system, which was still in vogue.

Education Minister Upinderjit Kaur and SGPC member Kiranjot Kaur also spoke at the seminar, which was organised in collaboration with Chief Khalsa Diwan, SGPC, Gurmat Training Camp, Kendri Sri Guru Singh Sabha and Naad Pargaas Sri Amritsar.

Heading: Lord Swraj Paul awarded ‘Punjab Ratan’ in London - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Industries Minister Manoranjan Kalia today said that the Union Government should make a blueprint to identify natural potential of the states to develop industries as per the availability of resources. Answering a media query, Kalia, who was in Bathinda today for a function, said the natural resource-specific industry was the answer to check disparity between different states. He said Punjab could do well with agro-based industry.

Talking about seat-sharing arrangement of the BJP with the SAD (B) in the coming parliamentary elections, Kalia said the Akalis would contest from 10 seats and his party from three.

Heading: Demand for blood increases as dengue tightens grip - Indian Express
Content:
NRI industrialist Lord Swraj Paul has been conferred the prestigious 'Punjab Ratan' (Jewel of Punjab) award in recognition of his achievements in fields like business, politics and public service.

Lord Paul, chairman of the 1.5-billion-pound Caparo Group, was awarded by the World Punjabi Organisation, European Division, last night. The trophy was presented to the 77-year-old industrialist and parliamentarian by Lord Navnit Dholakia, Deputy leader of the Liberal Democrats in the House of Lords at a glittering ceremony at the Park Lane Hotel in Piccadilly, Central London.

"I am overwhelmed to receive this. It is a surprise. It is also a proud moment when you are being honoured by your community. There is nothing better.
