I am truly grateful to all of you for giving me this honour," an emotional Lord Paul, best known for his one-million-pound donation to save the London Zoo in 1993, said while receiving the trophy.

Besides his wife Lady Aruna Paul, his brother Jit Paul, an educationist who had specially come from India, was present on the occasion. About the current global economic turmoil, Lord Paul, British Ambassador for Overseas Business and chairman of Westminster and Wolverhampton Universities, said, "It is an unprecedented crisis and nobody knows how to deal with it. Fortunately, we have a Prime Minister (Gordon Brown) who has the longest experience of having been a successful Chancellor for 10 years and respected by all world leaders. He is working full-time because it is an international problem requiring global solution. We are fortunate that in this, all three political parties (in Britain) support him."

Bollywood legend Dev Anand was the recipient of the maiden award last year for his contributions in the field of art and entertainment. Reading the citation, R S Baxi, president of the World Punjabi Organisation, European Division, said, "Winner of this year's award is a very special person, who became one of the first Asians to lead as captain of industry, having founded his company in 1968, followed by growth achieved through development of several greenfield start-up projects and a series of acquisitions and turning around existing businesses."

Lord Dholakia said, "I hold him in high esteem for the remarkable contribution he is making to the society." Shailesh Vara, chairman of the Conservative Friends of India, said, "Lord Paul is well known not only in Britain and India but in the whole world."

Lord Paul was awarded the 'Padma Bhushan' by the government of India in 1983.

On the occasion, Baxi presented a cheque for 2,500 pounds to Susan Price, acting Vice-Chancellor of the University of East London, for promoting the WPO scholarship for education of students from India. Two MSc students, Rupinder Kaur and Sarbit Singh ,benefited from the scholarship scheme. Three more students would benefit from the scholarship in 2008-09, Baxi said.

He also launched a campaign to raise environmental awareness both in India and the UK, called 'Plant a Tree, Save the Planet'. Under the campaign, WPO European Division will plant 2,000 saplings in the forests of Punjab at the launch of the International Punjabi Conference scheduled to be held in New Delhi for two days from January 3, 2009.

Among those present on the occasion included Judge Mota Singh; Madhav Chandra, Minister (Political) in the High Commission of India; Kartar Lalvani, founder chairman of Vitabiotics, the biggest vitamin producing company in Britain, and Raj Loomba, founder chairman of the Loomba Trust, a charity promoting the education of children of widows in India.

Heading: SC asks Ludhiana civic body to reconstruct razed marriage hall - Indian Express
Content:
With the official count of confirmed dengue cases going up to 690 in the district and nearly 70 patients being admitted in different city hospitals everyday, the blood requirement has increased manifold.

The Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH) has admitted the largest number of patients so far, with the total count crossing the 800 mark. The number of suspected cases in the district, recognised by the Health Department, is pegged at 240 so far. The total number of dengue patients, including those from the district, has already climbed up to 1200.

In the wake of the rising platelet-needs, owing to the increasing dengue cases, a city-based NGO Salaam Zindagi Foundation, on Sunday, offered to hold an emergency blood donation camp for dengue patients at the request of the Dayanand Medical College and Hospital. The NGO holds blood donation camps every month for thalassamic children.

"The situation now is more serious than the one we faced in 2006. This time the requirement of blood platelets has increased considerably and therefore I requested the NGO to hold the camp in the blood bank of the hospital itself so that we can meet the increasing demand," said Dr Amarjit Kaur, Head of the department of transfusion medicine at DMCH.

Manjit Saini, president of Salaam Zindagi Foundation, said: "Some patients of dengue have been facing extreme conditions and require blood platelets immediately. So we decided to hold this camp with support from Sidh Baba Balak Nath Mandir trust, Prem Nagar, Ghumar Mandi and Bhartiya Social Welfare Society."

The requirement of RDP (Random Donor Platelet) at the DMCH is normally just 30-40 units per day. But over the last few weeks, the demand has shot up to 120-150 units of RDP per day, said Dr Amarjit Kaur.

On the other hand, while only 5-6 units of SDP (Single Donor Platelet) is required at the hospital everyday, the rising dengue cases have increased the demand to 25-30 units per day.

Understanding the gravity of the situation, the chief minister has also directed the Health Department to provide free treatment to dengue patients at the government hospitals.

The platelet-dengue relation

A healthy person has blood platelet count ranging from 1.5 to 4 lakh. A person suffering from dengue may, however, lose it up to as low as 20,000 which may result in death. The patient then requires to be given platelets either through Single Donor Platelet (SDP) or Random Donor Platelet (RDP). In case, bleeding occurs through urine, gums or nose, the patient needs additional platelets, even if the platelet level is 50,000 to 60,000.

In SDP, only the platelets are transferred to the needy patient from a donor with the same blood group while the rest of the blood is again returned to the donor in a 90-minute long process. In RDP, the entire blood is used from which platelets are taken for transfusion to the dengue patient.

Heading: Land registry scam: Krishan Gopal not ‘cooperating’, says SP - Indian Express
Content:
The cost of reconstruction will be recovered from the salaries of officials responsible for demolition

A civic agency in Punjab has landed in trouble for demolishing a marriage hall despite restrictions imposed by a court. The Supreme Court now has held its action "arbitrary" and directed it to reconstruct the hall.

The cost of reconstruction will be recovered from the salaries of officials responsible for the illegal demolition.

A Bench, comprising Justices S B Sinha and Aftab Alam said the Ludhiana Municipal Corporation authorities had arbitrarily demolished the hall, located on Link Road, after issuing vague notices, despite the fact that the original owner Hira Devi had died and an injunction restraining the demolition was pending in the court.

The apex court said the authorities were wrong in claiming that the third notice issued by them in 2001 was final, as Hira Devi had died in 1998.

After initially issuing two notices to Hira Devi, the authorities issued the third notice in her name in 2001, even though she had died and the property was in the possession of her grandson Inderjit Singh.

As per the law, the authorities were supposed to issue fresh notices to Inderjit Singh, which they did not do; instead they demolished the structure despite a court restraining them from doing so.

Inderjit Singh filed an appeal in the High Court, which held the demolition illegal and directed the civic authorities to reconstruct the marriage hall and recover the cost of the construction from the salaries of officials responsible for the illegal demolition.

Aggrieved by the High Court's order, the Ludhiana municipality filed a special leave petition in the apex court. The apex court, however, concurred with the findings of the High Court and said the municipal authorities should have issued a comprehensive notice explaining in detail the extent of the alleged illegal construction and also informed the district court, which had passed an injunction against the demolition.

"The said notices were also found to be absolutely vague. They did not contain the description of the property in question. Indisputably, they were issued in the name of a dead person. The appellant, furthermore, acted arbitrarily insofar as it demolished the structures, despite pendency of the suit. We would assume that the order of injunction was granted for a limited period, but it is expected of a statutory corporation to thereupon to inform the court about it," the apex court said while dismissing the appeal.

Heading: SSP’s son was mastermind: cops - Indian Express
Content:
Even after Gopal Krishan, the clerk alleged to be the main man behind the multi-crore land deal scam, joined investigations on Saturday, the Vigilance Bureau (VB) has reportedly made little headway in the interrogations.

After being on the run for nearly 22 days, Krishan joined the investigations a day after he received anticipatory bail from the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

A police party led by Superintendent of Police (Vigilance) Ravcharan Singh Brar questioned Gopal and also opened the four almirahs, that had been sealed during the September 19 raid, the keys of which were with Krishan.

SP Brar said, "Krishan is not co-operating with us at all. We know he is hiding a lot of facts. He had the keys to these almirahs all these days and thus, he may have destroyed or hidden several evidences."

The SP added, "Some registries, as old as 2005, which were not given to the owners who failed to pay the bribes, were also found. We have also recovered some unused stamp papers and other documents indicating the names of those from whom the money was to be taken."

Brar further added, "While Krishan will be asked to come for questioning again, we have many other leads to find, like the people involved in the transfer of money. We are working on other leads and will be able to crack the entire nexus very soon."

Interestingly during the period for which Krishan was absconding, he was reportedly "on leave" as per the revenue department for which he works. Talking on the Krishan's bail, a senior VB official added, "The court asked us to submit a reply on October 24 and we are still to submit it. We will contest his bail in the HC on October 24 as we need him for interrogation."

The scam

Arvind Kumar, tehsildar (West) allegedly had demanded Rs 10,000 from one Baljit Singh for making a power of attorney. In a raid conducted on September 19, the VB arrested Kumar and registered cases against two clerks — Parminder Singh and Gopal Kishan — and a constable, Harjinder Singh

The police party, later, also raided the tehsildar's house in Jallandhar and recovered two unlicensed rifles, Rs 1.69 lakh, 643 gm gold, 47 bottles of scotch and several other official documents. Separate cases for stocking scotch and possessing rifles illegally were registered with the Division number 4 police station, Jallandhar. The VB also found 19 registries of properties, including the office copy and the owner copy.

Heading: Festive season spells traffic woes for shoppers in the city - Indian Express
Content:
The son of Shiv Kumar, Senior Superintendent of Police (Vigilance), Patiala, had masterminded and stage-managed the diamond robbery that took place near Phillaur on Thursday, said the police today while claiming to have cracked the diamond robbery case.

Mohit Kumar Sharma, a 26-year-old Bishop Cotton pass out, was arrested on Saturday with gunman Harbans Lal.

The duo has been sent to two days' police custody with the Phillaur police till October 15.

According to the police, Mohit had planned and executed the entire act with the assistance of seven others that included two security guards from the Indian Reserved Battalion (IRB).

The other six accomplices, including a security guard, Amandeep Bittu, are, however, still at large.

Talking about the case Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) R S Sohal said, "The needle of suspicion had always pointed towards Mohit for he was the person who knew that Shah was carrying such expensive stones.

We also found that the taxi too had been hired for Shah by Mohit. The case was, therefore, crystal clear."

The DSP added, "After his arrest, Mohit disclosed that he hid the diamonds in his room and we recovered them."

Mohit and Shah were known to each other as the two had been reportedly trading for quite some time, said the police.

"Till now, the 400 gm of diamonds that we have recovered are worth Rs 4 crore. The value, however, could be higher," added Sohal.

The diamond merchant, Bhupesh Shah, was looted of diamonds worth Rs 1.5 crore by some unidentified people when he was on his way from Ludhiana to Amritsar in a taxi hired from the city.

The merchant had come from Mumbai for a business transaction and was staying in a hotel on the Ferozepur Road here.

However, when they neared Phillaur, the taxi driver stopped to relieve himself.

Bhupesh Shah is said to have restrained him to stop there as he saw few men standing suspiciously but the driver stopped the car nevertheless.

As the driver went out, four people attacked him with sharp-edged weapons.

They fled from the scene after injuring him along with the taxi driver in the same car.

Heading: PU diamond jubilee youth & heritage fest kicks off - Indian Express
Content:
Traffic jams are a common problem during festivals. This year too, is no different and markets across the city are witnessing a heavy rush of vehicles leading to frequent jams.

The main reason behind this is encroachment on roadsides, and vehicles parked in violation of the rules.

The worst hit are the daily commuters. Subhash Sheel, an employee with a company says, "There is utter chaos in Chaura Bazar, which I have to cross to reach office. Moving freely on the road, however, is an uphill task. People hardly care about traffic rules. These days, it takes me almost double the time, to cross the market in the evening."

Despite, one-way traffic rule at the Ghumar-Mandi, people from both sides cross this area, which results in huge jams.

Surinder Dhir, a city resident says: "Shoppers park their vehicles without paying any heed to the traffic rules. They do not think about inconveniencing their fellow commuters."

The scene at the other markets of the city like Model Town, Jawahar Nagar Camp, Field Ganj and Kareem Pura, too is the same.

Gurdeep Singh DSP (Traffic) says: "Traffic personnel were deployed for VIP duty since the last two days. We will regularise the flow of traffic within a week. A meeting will also be held and routes will be diverted accordingly."

Heading: Mystery surrounds Jaswinder Bhalla mom-in-law’s death - Indian Express
Content:
Panjab University Diamond Jubilee Youth and Heritage Festival, Zone B, commenced with great gusto and aplomb at Guru Nanak Girls College, Model Town, today.

As many as 11 colleges are participating in various competitions spread over the next four days. The Youth and Heritage Festival was inaugurated by the chief guests, H.S. Mattewal, Advocate General, Punjab and Dr S.M. Kant, Director, Panjab University Youth Services, who lighted the lamp and delivered inspirational addresses. Kant announced that inter-zonal youth festival, the final competition of the youth festival for all the 12 zones, will be held at Guru Nanak College, Doraha.

Speaking on the sidelines of the festival, he also announed that the university will hold North India Inter university youth festival at the university campus in which participants from 63 universities are expected to take part.

Principal of GNGC Dr Charanjit Mahal extended a warm reception to the chief guests and other dignitaries including the Principals and staff of the participating colleges. She also welcomed all the participants and special invitees and extended her best wishes to all participating teams. Gurbir Singh, President, Guru Nanak Education Trust, also in his address to the audience spoke on the importance of such Youth and Heritage Festivals which help in the overall development of a balanced personality.

The results of various heritage and cultural competitions organized on the first day of the festival are as follows;

Winner of Ladies Traditional & Ritualistic Songs of Punjab was MTSM College, while 'Still Life Drawing' competition was won by Jaspreet Kaur from Guru Nanak Girls College. Master Tara Singh Memorial College for Women bagged the first prize in 'Vaar/Kali'. The competition of 'Folk Dance Sammi' was won by Guru Nanak Girls College. In 'Knitting', Gaganpreet Kaur of MTSM College, in 'On the Spot Painting', Sophia of Govt. College for Women, in Rangoli, Sonam Vijin of AS College, Khanna, in Clay Modeling, Balpreet Kaur from Guru Nanak Girls College, in Creative Writing (Story Writing), Neeraj from DD Jain College and in Essay Writing Nisha from Ramgariha Girls College bagged the first prize.

Heading: Gurta Gaddi Diwas Yatra organised - Indian Express
Content:
Amrit (70), mother in law of noted satirist Jaswinder Bhalla, today died under mysterious circumstances by drowing in the Sidhwan canal. While her family members suspect foul play behind her death, police believe that she had committed suicide.

According to sources. Amrit Kaur had left her Shastri Nagar situated house this morning for attending a function at the gurdwara of Model Town Extension. But when she did not come back till afternoon, her family started searching for her.

At about 4.30 pm, the body of an old woman was found from the Sidhwan canal near the bridge on the Pakhowal road. Later, this body was found to be of Amrit Kaur. Her body was identified by her family members.

Talking to the mediapersons, her family members suspected a foul play behind her death. They suspected that she might have been killed by someone for her jewellary as her gold chain and a purse were missing.

On the other hand, the Sarabha Nagar SHO Devinder Kumar said that their investigations did not point towards any foul play.

He said that except her gold chain, all her other gold jewellary was intact. He said that the body had been sent to the Civil Hospital for post-mortem. The SHO said that inquest proceedings under section 174 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC) have been initiated in this connection.

Heading: KCW principal receives Punjab Ratan award - Indian Express
Content:
To commemorate the 300 years of "Guruta Gaddi Diwas" of Sri Guru Granth Sahib, a "paidal march" was organised here on Sunday. The march started from Gurdwara Dukh Niwaran and passed through Jagraon bridge, Vishawkarma chowk, Campa Cola chowk, Aatam park, Dugri road, Model Town, Sarabha Nagar, Ferozpur road, Ghumar Mandi before reaching again at Gurudwara Dukh Niwaran Sahib.

The march was led by Shri Guru Granth Sahib in a well-decorated palaki. A large number of devotees, who recited shabads, participated in the march along with religious leaders of different organisations.

Many organisations and societies organised stalls of eatables for the devotees participating in "paidal march". The city gurudwaras were decked up on the occasion even as a number of people also decorated their homes with colourful lights. At many places, commuters faced problems because of the traffic jams and reached their destinations late. "Today, it was sangat darshan and paidal march which created traffic jams at many places," said a principal.

Heading: Woman commits jumps before train along with two kids - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Varinder Kaur Thind, principal, Khalsa College for Women, Civil Lines, was awarded the prestigious "Punjab Ratan Award 2008" here yesterday for her contribution to the field of education and social development.The award, which is given by the all-India conference of Intellectuals was bestowed on her by the Haryana Governor, Dr A.R. Kidwai at a function held at GGDSD College, Chandigarh.

This year, a total of 10 Punjab Ratans and seven Haryana Ratans have been awarded by this body. The Punjab/ Haryana Ratan award, which is given by the organisation every year is an attempt to honour and motivate people who have put in efforts to do their bit for the society in fields like education, medicine, social work , agriculture etc.

Thind, who is a PH.D in zoology and has been working as the principal of Khalsa College for Women for the last six years said she has strived to provide quality education to the modern youth alongwith instilling in them the moral and religious values.

Heading: PAU sexual harassment case dominates PAUTA elections - Indian Express
Content:
A woman committed suicide along with her two minor children by jumping before a train on Saturday evening. While her daughter died on the spot, she succumbed to her injuries on the way to the hospital and her son died at the DMC hospital.

The deceased have been identified as Pooja Singla, her son Mohit Singla (9) and her daughter Madhvi Singla (7). They were residents of Jagraon. They jumped before the Delhi-Amritsar superfast train, near the bridge on the Buddha nullah near Salem Tabri.

According to sources in the Government Railway Police (GRP), it has yet not been established what provoked the woman to take this extereme step.

Heading: Shobha Yatra taken out - Indian Express
Content:
While this issue does not appear in black and white, yet the sexual harassment case at the Punjab Agricultural University is dominating the PAU Teachers' Association elections too. PAUTA, it may be mentioned, goes to polls on October 21.

Thus while for the ruling regime a long list of achievements and for the opposing group, a long list of failures are not the only points to woo the voters. In this case the so-called moral and ethical stands on this issue too have become scoring points.

And the same is evident from the fact that a senior faculty member of the university and others like him do not shirk from announcing, "If we are elected to power, we will openly stand behind DSW Dr Brar, against whom this complaint is filed."

Also noteworthy here is that both the ruling and opposing factions over the previous weeks had met vice-chancellor Dr Manjit Singh Kang, which they claim was just to, "to press upon Dr Kang to conduct an enquiry at the earliest and fairly."

So while on the face of it, both the groups in fray for the polls may seem poles apart as far as their election manifestos are concerned, yet they seem to stand unanimous on this use. Not only in meeting vice-chancellor for the 'sexual harassment complaint' but even in issuing 'politically correct' statements.

Meanwhile, Dr M.L. Sharma, the contestent for the post of president, against Dr M.S. Mahal, president of the ruling executive, commented, "We do not know anything about the facts in the case so it would be inappropriate to comment."

Even Dr Mahal's group had plastered various notices around the campus stating their non-affiliation with the two parties involved in case, after the news reports stated that faculty members are trying to harness support for the accused."We have made our stand clear. Enquiry should be conducted in a fair manner and we do not have anybody to favour," said Mahal.

Heading: On the right note - Indian Express
Content:
Ten new designers focus solely on accessories at the Delhi Fashion Week

As the city gears up for the clash of the fashion weeks, the Delhi Fashion Week and the Wills India Fashion Week that start barely a day apart, fashion watchers can be sure of one thing; to see more holistic work since the fallout of the FDCI has opened the platform to many new young designers, eager to showcase their work, some of it startling in its originality.

For the first time since the inception of Indian fashion, accessories, crucial elements in fashion will not be neglected. Ten accessory designers are showing for the first time at Delhi Fashion Week beginning on Tuesday. Bags, scarves, shawls, wrap dresses, jewellery stalls, even blankets dot the venue, Emporio Mall in Vasant Kunj. The look is defined by etching Kalidasa's poetry on silver, weaving sequins in hand weaves of Bengal and using Moroccan designs on a Cashmere shawl. "We received an overwhelming demand from buyers who attended the fashion week last time. Most of the designers showing here are currently exporters," says Geetanjali Kashyap of Fashion Foundation of India. Bangalore-based jewellery designer Deepti Sudhindra who has been in the circuit for nine years has found her niche by etching Henry David Thoreau's poetry on to silver, transforming a ubiquitous coconut shells into delicate beads, pendants and necklaces and contemporising the 200-year-old filigree craft of Karimnagar artists of Andhra Pradesh. "I take a coconut shells and embellish it with silver," explains Sudhindra, 32, who will be showcasing eight different collections. "My look is contemporary but the design element is essentially Indian," says Sudhindra who works on a commission basis.

Turning scarves, shawls and wraps into a heritage label is Kolkata based designer Bappaditya Biswas, 36, who founded Bai Lou in 2002. Closely working with weavers of Bengal, Biswas uses Jamdani and double cloth weaving techniques. "We don't believe in embellishments on top of the fabric. Everything is woven in and comes out as a finished product," says Biswas who works with 350 weavers. His collection has stoles in malta silk with geometrical patterns, scarves in a blend of silk and wool in an oyster pink and aqua blue. "Wearing scarves is a recent trend in India and the hand weaving craft of Bengal has got a boost," says Biswas.

But it is Nepal based fashion designer Yasmine Rana who has given the jaded crafts industry in the neighbouring country a lift, by incorporating traditional Nepalese designs into luxurious loungewear. Rana, of French origin, has been in the field for 25 years. Her collection—lounge wear, chic jackets in shining blue and jade green, cashmere shawls and blankets have a bourgeoisie elegance. "My designs are classy, multi-cultural and bold. I pick-up ideas from my travels, use local designs and natural material," she emphasises.

Among others, Peachy Bawa of Basta will show a range of leather bags, Delhi-based Shilu Kumar of Pashma will exhibit a collection of scarves and Jyotika Jhalani of the label Janavi will show a trendy line of beach garments, hand bags and high end wraps in silk and chiffon.

Heading: Folk Tales - Indian Express
Content:
After the success of his solo Lambi Judaai, Pakistani singer Kamran Ahmed is optimistic about his first album, Judaai, releasing soon

Song writer, composer and singer Kamran Ahmed never imagined that Lambi Judaai of the Emraan Hashmi starrer Jannat that he actually wrote for his parents would turn out to become one of the most downloaded love tracks of all time. "My parents live in Pakistan. And I have been staying away from them in Dubai, since 2001, meeting only occasionally. This song brought back memories of time spent with them. I am glad people understood how I felt," says Ahmed, 26. Fresh from the success of his first single, Pakistani artiste Ahmed, is performing in India for the first time at Elevate, Noida. Ahmed is thankful to Bollywood for putting him in the spotlight. "It is an honour that Bhatt saab (Mukesh Bhatt) selected my song as one of the tracks for his movie. It has really turned the tide in my favour and I am getting offers from music directors. Even though the song did fairly well in Canada, USA and the UK, nothing compared to the success I received from Bollywood. Appealing to an Indian audience is always much easier," reasons this self taught singer.

His song however, was slightly tweaked to suit the movie, explains Ahmed. "The initial composition did not have a female voice. But in the movie a female voice adds a dynamic undertone with the aalaps. Even the arrangement of the lyrics and timing of the various instruments was slightly customized. Bhatt saab told me, 'one should hear the song and get the feeling of being lonely in a crowd'." Other singers from Pakistan in the past have complained of being robbed of the credit of creating the music but Ahmed says his first outing in Bollywood has been more than satisfactory. Now Ahmed is busy wrapping up his first album, Judaai, which releases early next year, comprising eight soulful rock ballads. "There is a soft rock track Gin Gin I am excited about. Its video has been shot in Pakistan and will air in a few weeks time. The album maintains my signature sound, fusion of the electric guitar and vocals and has my hit song Lambi Judaai as well," says Ahmed. If given a chance he would love to collaborate with AR Rahman for an album. "I admire his passion for music. Singing with him would be an honour, but first I would like to finish my album," says the self taught singer who picked up the electric guitar at 14, and counts Pakistani band Junoon as among his favourites. No one hit wonder, this.

Heading: Style File - Indian Express
Content:
In a new book, Arpana Caur pays tribute to folk art from the world over

"This is the Tithi bird. It has been cursed to live in fear of the sun," states artist Arpana Caur, as she looks at an ink and acrylic on canvas by Gond artist Rajendra Singh Shyam. She swiftly moves to the other side of the room to show us Jangarh Singh Shyam's bull with fine red dots painted on a black background on paper. The two works from her collection of folk art seem rather dissimilar, but the artist traces common elements as she points out that Rajendra was a disciple of Jangarh. She has been carefully studying every work in her Folk Art Museum for a long time, but during the last year the research has been more in-depth as she dedicated pages to each of them in the book titled The Magic Makers that will be released next month.

"With this we hope to reach people who may not be able to visit the museum. The aim is to popularise folk art," says Caur, as she sifts through the 300-page publication that has been neatly classified into different categories, in tandem with the display at the folk art museum. If the Midnapore patua portraying incidents from Ramayan finds place in the section on 'Folk Painting', then ceramic pots from Cambodia and Turkish teapots are under 'Images from Abroad'. Details about scrolls with tantric motifs are discussed by author PC Jain in a chapter on 'Tantra' and 'Sculptures' has several beaten metal artifacts from Bastar. "The classification puts the information in a streamlined manner," smiles Caur.

Amid the 500-odd objects of Folk art, Caur's canvases too find place in the publication in an article written by John H Bowles that narrates her collaboration with Mithila-based artist Sat Narayan Pandey for a show titled 'Between Dualities' that took place in 1997. While this had the duo work together on artwork, later Caur used motifs of folk art in several of her canvases. For instance, in 'Tears for Hiroshima' she paints godana motifs with the ruined Genbaku Dome to depict destruction caused by the bombing and 'Rites of Time' has Warli trees circling the canvas.

More contemporary themes, meanwhile, find place in work by folk artists. If Amrita Das portrays Tsunami in Sri Lanka in Mithal patterns, Bapi Chitrakar paints the Gujarat earthquake on a Bengali scroll and Gond artist Durga Bai has the Bhopal gas tragedy in an ink drawing.

As Caur checks the final proof of the book, also lined up are annual exhibitions on folk art. The beginning will be made with an exhibition on Bengal folk art featuring Roma Chatterji's collection that will take place on October 25 and up next are a series of curatorial shows that will feature work from Caur's museum. "Folk artists need to get their due," notes Caur. The book she says, has more tales related to folk art, bringing together the traditional and modern.

Heading: At RML, injured fight to keep spirits high - Indian Express
Content:
Elections to the students union in Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) will be held on November 3, the Election Committee said on Monday.

The JNUSU Election Committee issued a notification to this effect.

"Councillors to different schools and two student representatives to Gender Sensitisation Committee Against Sexual Harassment (GSCASH) will also be elected on the same date," Chairperson of Election Committee Sarada Prasanna Das said.

The Election Committee issued the notification after consultations with representatives of different student organisations and independent candidates.

"Nominations will be received on October 16 and 17 and they can be withdrawn on October 19. Final list of candidates will be displayed the next day," said Prasanna.

The Presidential debate will be held on November one. Elections will take place on November three while results will be declared on November 5.

Earlier, the outgoing JNUSU was dissolved and it handed over charge to 28-member Election Committee, which comprises student representatives from different schools.

The Election Committee is responsible for conducting free and fair elections in JNU and it has to hand over the charge to the new union within 28 days of taking over from outgoing one, according to the JNUSU constitution.

Heading: Divert drain, we don’t want Delhi’s pollution: UP - Indian Express
Content:
A month after serial bomb blasts rocked Delhi on September 13, Newsline revisited the Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, where a majority of blast victims were rushed to on that "Black Saturday".

The hospital received 69 patients after the blasts, of which 10 were declared dead on arrival. At present, nine patients are still recuperating at the hospital, many still waiting to be operated upon.

Puneet Wasan (24), admitted in the orthopaedics ward, broke his thighbone, which then twisted backwards. An 80-kg weight has been hanging from his injured leg for the last one month, which the doctors say is to straighten his bone. "The doctors are still waiting for the broken bone to straighten, after which they will operate upon my leg and put an iron rod," Puneet says, trying to keep his spirits high.

He had gone to Gaffar Market to get his mobile phone repaired when the blasts ripped through the area. This happy-go-lucky youngster finds lying on a hospital bed for a month quite "boring". But he loves to crack jokes and keeps other patients around him amused.

"My husband died when Puneet was very young. My other son is still studying. Puneet has been taking care of the family," says Pooja Rani, Puneet's mother. "I am really tired now. I have been at the hospital all through the month and don't really know when the doctors are going to operate upon Puneet," she adds.

Zahid (26), another patient in the same ward, was also at Gaffar Market to get his phone repaired. A college dropout, Zahid had a 3-inch by 2-inch metal piece in his leg, weighing around 50 grams. "I am feeling better now. I want to go home," he says.

Shakil Ahmed (32), a resident of Ghaziabad, was on his way home when he was caught in the blast at Barakhamba Road. "I was standing just one metre away from where the blast took place. Its impact was such that I was thrown to the middle of the road," Ahmed says, showing copies of newspapers that carried photographs of him lying on the road in a pool of blood. A driver by profession, Ahmed doesn't know what he will do after getting discharged from the hospital. "I don't think I will ever be able to drive again. My left leg was badly injured and I can still feel splinters in my arms and legs," he says.

Rama Nadibatt (48) is also recuperating from a broken arm in the same ward. He lost his daughters in the same blast, while wife Krishna (44), also in hospital, miraculously defied death.

His younger daughter, 17-year-old Pooja, was declared dead on arrival at Lady Hardinge Medical College on September 13. Elder daughter Santosh (22) died at the hospital on October 10.

Even as Rama tries to reconcile with the loss of his daughters, Krishna hasn't been informed about their deaths due to her critical condition. "I don't know why this has happened to us. My daughters never harmed anyone," he says.

Nisha Manral (19) was discharged from the hospital after first aid,

only to realise there was a pellet in her shoulder, after she felt a shooting pain there. Nisha was brought back to the hospital and operated upon twice.

She was sitting in CP's Central Park with her friend Babita when the blast occurred. Babita died on the spot. "She was my best friend and I used to share everything with her. I still can't believe what happened that day. It is impossible for me to sleep now or even close my eyes: all I see is Babita's face," Nisha says.

Twenty two-year-old Surendra, who was discharged from the ICU last week, complains that he lost his mobile phone and a gold ring at the hospital. "My brother arrived after I was taken for operation. The nurse had taken my phone and gold ring, saying it would be returned later. I still haven't got my stuff back."

Monetary help for slain cop's family from Salim Khan
EXPRESS NEWS SERVICE
MUMBAI, OCTOBER 12


FILM actor Salman Khan's father, veteran writer Salim Khan has sent a cheque for Rs 1 lakh to the family of slain Delhi Police inspector Mohan Chand Sharma, who lost his life in the Batla House encounter with suspected terrorists in September.
In an interview to a Mumbai daily, Khan said he gave his personal money which he had kept aside from his writings for regional dailies.
"Those who indulge in terrorism in the name of Islam cannot be Muslims. The Quran doesn't recognise such acts. Agar jung ho toh bekusuron, baccho, budho aur auraton ko marna gunaah hai. Islam propagates spreading peace, living in harmony and forgiving people. What we witness today is the acts of cowards," he told the daily.
Khan, who in partnership with Javed Akhtar had written the screenplay for several successful films in the '70s, has always shared a personal relationship with the police force. His father had retired as the DIG of Indore. The police force also served as an integral background for some of Salim-Javed's most celebrated works like Zanjeer, Sholay and Deewar.

Heading: 2 more deaths on Delhi-Gurgaon Expressway - Indian Express
Content:
SHAHDARA DRAIN: Joint panel to look into feasibility; officials say demand 'unreasonable', difficult to implement

The Uttar Pradesh government has told Delhi that it does not want its Shahdara drain to flow into Noida. A delegation of senior officials from the UP government, including the chief executive officer (CEO) of Noida, was in the Capital last week to hold a meeting with Delhi government officials to push for diverting the drain. The official reason cited by the officials was that they "do not want Delhi's pollution to enter UP".

"We had a meeting with the CEO and senior officials from the UP Irrigation and Flood Control. They have demanded that the Shahdara drain should not flow through Noida and instead be diverted along the Hindon directly into the Yamuna. Delhi and UP have now set up a joint committee to look into the feasibility of the proposal. The committee is also to consult the Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee, for technical feasibility of implementing the proposal," said Delhi Chief Secretary Rakesh Mehta.

The committee comprises the deputy CEO of Noida Authority, Delhi Jal Board Chief Engineer V S Thind, officials from both the UP and the Delhi irrigation and flood control departments and senior officials from the Noida Authority.

Officials in the Delhi government said the demand made by the Uttar Pradesh government might not be technically feasible.

"The flow of the drain and the topography of the area are such that it may not be possible to divert the drain. In any case, this will be an extremely expensive proposition. The diversion cost aside, once the drain is diverted, there is likely to be a water accumulation of two metres or higher on the Delhi side, which will need to be pumped out at a very high cost. But UP is so keen to have the drain diverted that they have offered to bear this cost," said a senior official.

If the proposal is sanctioned, Delhi will have to divert six kilometres — the Delhi-Noida stretch — of the drain. The drain flows though Sectors 12 to 14 in Noida, according to the officials.

The Delhi government had proposed to UP that it would treat the drain water and release only clean, unpolluted water, but the neighbouring state turned it down.

"There are plans to clean the drain water as part of our interceptor canal sewerage system — in which Najafgarh and Shahdara are the first two drains targeted. We will in any case start releasing clean water into Noida soon, but the UP authorities just don't want the drain to run through the state at all. The direction of the flow is natural and has been there for the last 100 years. It will be, therefore, very difficult to divert the flow. The cost will be phenomenal. This is unreasonable. We feel the UP government wants to cover up the drain and auction off the land, with land prices being optimum right now," said a senior DJB official.

Even if the diversion is done, both the governments will require clearance from environment bodies and the Water Commission. Shahdara drain is one of Delhi's six major drains, including Najafgarh, Maharani Bagh, Sarita Vihar, Barapulla and the Sen Nursing Home drain, which together account for 90 per cent of the Yamuna's flow and 80 per cent of its pollution.

Heading: Bank account ‘hacked’, Noida firm poorer by Rs 1.86 crore - Indian Express
Content:
Two persons lost their lives on the Delhi-Gurgaon Expressway near Rajiv Chowk when a speeding vehicle, reportedly a call centre cab, rammed them as they were trying to cross the road.

Residents of Sikhopur, the mother-daughter duo—Seema (30) and Priya (9)—had gone to a medical store in Rajnagar. As they were crossing the Expressway, the car hit them, killing them on the spot.

Police have, however, not confirmed the make of the vehicle and have registered a case of rash and negligent driving against an unknown person.

The deaths are yet another reminder of the promises made by the highway authorities of building foot overbridges for the convenience of pedestrians.

This is not the first time lives were lost on the Expressway since it was opened in December 2007, all due to lack of overbridges or subways, which has resulted in people risking their lives to get to the other side. The Expressway is also without proper pedestrian crossings.

NHAI officials had last year promised to build five foot overbridges, ensuring pedestrian safety on the stretch between Udyog Vihar to Hero Honda Chowk.

The assurance came after protests from residents of neighbouring villages who had threatened to block the Expressway if the authorities did not listen to their demands.

The plan, however, missed its deadline in July this year. The project was then transferred to the Haryana PWD, after the NHAI cited failure to procure land from villages for construction work.

Haryana PWD Secretary K K Jalan said: "The project was handed over to us in a meeting in July this year. We have undertaken work on two overbridges near Udyog Vihar and IFFCO Chowk. We are floating tenders for two more and plans for a fifth one will also fall in place once we procure land for it."

Talking about security measures, Jalan said: "The security aspect is not in our purview and has to be maintained by the NHAI. Since the task of building the foot overbridges was handed over to us, we have been prompt in our job."

According to sources, however, the construction of the two overbridges, at an estimated cost of approximately Rs 2 crore each, is running behind schedule.

Heading: Placement cell at JNU aims to find research-based jobs for students - Indian Express
Content:
A Noida company has lost over Rs 1.86 crore to an Internet hacker since the last week of September. The manager of the company found the amount missing from the firm's bank account after he returned from a foreign trip.

Pawan Aggarwal, the manager of PPS International Private Limited, an international electronic automotive goods supplier for the Indian Railways, found that the money had been siphoned off to various bank accounts across the country.

According to the FIR lodged in Sector 20, the first transaction took place on September 29, in which Rs 21,51,500 were transferred to a Mumbai branch of the Punjab National Bank (PNB). The money was transferred to the account of M/s A1 Channel Logistics Private Limited. "The company withdrew around Rs 16 lakh the same day and made a demand draft of Rs 4 lakh," said a senior police officer.

"Three more transactions took place on September 29 — of Rs 20 lakh, Rs 21 lakh and Rs 4 lakh. The total amount was transferred to the PNB account of one N Venketeshwaran in Coimbatore. Of the Rs 45 lakh, Rs 15 lakh was further transferred to a Standard Chartered branch in Mumbai and the remaining Rs 30 lakh was sent to an ICICI Bank branch in Mumbai the very same day," reads the FIR.

The last transaction took place on October 1, in which around Rs 81 lakh was transferred to the PNB account of M/s Minrani Exports and Imports in its Goa branch. "From there, around 75 lakh was transferred to the ICICI account of M/s Asiatic State Developer Pvt. Ltd. on October 6. Asiatic withdrew Rs 70,000 in cash. The remaining Rs 5 lakh from the account of Minrani was then transferred to an SBI account of Adarsh Enterprises Mysore," said a senior police officer.

Noida SP (City) Ashok Tripathi said the transactions took place through Internet banking over a period of almost a week. "Between September 29 and October 1, the company lost Rs 1, 86,52,500. The money was transferred through several transactions to various bank accounts located in other parts of the country," he added. A complaint has been registered at the Sector 20 police station.

Police sources said they suspected an Internet hacker to be behind the transactions. "We are also checking on the involvement of bank employee, if any," said Tripathi, adding that teams had been sent to Mumbai, Goa and Coimbatore.

Heading: Public forum for independent probe in Jamia encounter by apex court judge - Indian Express
Content:
At Jawaharlal Nehru University, well-known for its late-night debates, anti-US marches, firebrand Lefties and the Ganga dhaba, the focus now seems to be on getting jobs for its students. But again, jobs with a difference.

People behind the newly created placement cell say they have decided to "look beyond BPOs and MNCs" and focus on providing research-based jobs to university students.

The issue has gained ground after JNU, which has traditionally wanted to maintain its stature as the ground for researchers, academics and central services aspirants, recently set up a placement cell in the campus. The university is trying to address this question by striking a balance between placement and research.

Professor Anand Kumar of the Centre for the Study of Social Systems, who is a member of the committee appointed to put the placement and counselling cell in place, points out: "While a need has been felt to orient the students to gain practical experience, our attempt will be to minimise the commercial aspect of placement, by looking at job avenues other than BPOs and MNCs. The primary focus is not to push students towards the job market, but to encourage them and also provide them with alternatives in research."

Both the JNU authorities and the student bodies on the campus say the objective of the placement cell is to promote research opportunities and career counselling, along with job placements.

Highlighting the importance of counselling, Mobeen Alam, joint secretary of the JNU Students' Union says: "Since every centre has its own nature, their requirements in terms of placement may vary."

The first session of career orientation is to be organised before the end of the current semester in December. A committee set up for the purpose has decided to launch a website to update and follow up on research opportunities by giving students access to experts in various fields. The cell hopes to rope in the alumni from various fields to expand its resource base.

In a meeting of the committee this week, it was decided that the placement cell would focus on adopting a "student-centric", and not "employer-centric", approach. The Student Faculty Committee in each centre of the university will be the hub of placement and career guidance activities.

The implementation of the activities is to be decentralised with each school and centre looking after its needs and requirements.

In the Schools of Social Sciences, Life Sciences and International Studies, the focus is on advanced studies and the need to look at the alternatives. "These can be research organisations like the Indian Institute of Science, Centre for Studies of Developing Societies among others, in addition to various centres run by international organisations like the United Nations," said Kumar. One of these is the Molecular Biology Research Centre near JNU. The options include teaching and working with NGOs and media organisations, among others, according to Professor Kumar.

In certain schools, however, much of the decision-making in this regard has been left to them. The School of Computer Systems has had an active placement cell since the early 1990s, with students getting close to 100 per cent placement in MNCs like IBM, Mackenzie and domestic IT majors like TCS and Wipro. "With starting salaries ranging from Rs 3.5 to 9 lakh (per annum), the students seem to be happy," says Dr D K Lobial, faculty in-charge of the school's placement cell.

Placement activities have been going on in the School of Language, Literature and Culture Studies for the last three to four years. "Languages like French, Spanish, Arabic, and Portuguese and Italian to a lesser extent, are much in demand," says Professor Rizwanur Rahman, faculty in-charge of the placement cell.

Heading: Over Rs 1 lakh compensation to injured in bullock cart accident - Indian Express
Content:
At a public meeting organised at Jamia Nagar, to discuss the police encounter at Batla House, around a dozen neighbours, eyewitnesses and relatives of either the deceased or the accused said although the problem of terrorism needs serious attention, one cannot subscribe to what they called "an alternate reign of terror perpetrated by certain sections of the authority."

The forum that organised the meeting called Jan Sunwai was supported by the Jamia Teachers' Solidarity Group on the Batla House encounter on Sunday in the ground opposite Khalilullah Masjid, Batla House, in Jamia Nagar.

Family members raised questions regarding the condition in which the bodies of Atif Ameen and Mohd Sajid were received and why and how they were not allowed to bury their kin in the Okhla

graveyard.

The jury of the Jan Sunwai included activists like Swami Agnivesh, John Dayal, Harsh Mander, Tripta Wahi, Tanika Sarkar, Vijay Singh and Nirmalangshu Mukherji.

Others, including writer Arundhati Roy, activist Kavita Srivastava, lawyer Prashant Bhushan, Kavita Krishnan, some members of Jamia Millia Islamia, Delhi University, JNU teaching faculty and students attended the programme to listen to the eyewitness accounts of the encounter.

Several questions, which were termed "discrepancies" in the police accounts were highlighted and Manisha Sethi from the Jamia Teachers' Solidarity Group read out its study of the same.

"Believe it or not, as evidence in support of their (the police's) claim that the boys living in L-18 were terrorists, the police presents a bucket, adhesive tape and a bag. The bucket was used to keep bombs (but was presumably empty at the time of 'seizure'); the adhesive tape was used to seal the explosives; and finally the bag was used to carry the bombs (but again presumably empty when the police 'recovered' it). "Let it be noted that legal requirements were flouted with regard to seizures. The police are required to prepare a seizure list of all items recovered from the site, which should be attested by two public witnesses not connected with the police. Given that a huge crowd had gathered at the site, surely, the police could have sought the assistance of members of the public. And why does L-18 continue to remain sealed?" the report questions.

The report presented by Manisha Sethi also questioned why the postmortem reports of Inspector Sharma, Atif and Sajid were not being made public.

"Our doubts remain. Our questions unanswered. Only a time-bound, independent inquiry under the sitting judge of the Supreme Court can bring out the truth," said Sethi. The jury members would meet early next week to finalise their 'verdict' on the encounter.

"The Jamia Teachers' Solidarity Group demands a time-bound, independent inquiry under the sitting judge of the Supreme Court and in the present situation of the ongoing media trial of the accused, concerted action is required," said Anuradha Ghosh, member of the Jamia Teachers' Solidarity Group. No member of the Delhi Police was present at

the meeting.

Heading: L-G to appoint a retired Lt Gen as security officer for Games 2010 projects - Indian Express
Content:
If you thought that low speed vehicles can avert mishaps at all times, think again. A year after their bullock cart was hit by a tempo, two men have been awarded over Rs one lakh in compensation by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT).

Hitching a ride on a bullock cart proved costly for 23-year-old Rohit Kumar after a tempo hit his not-so-common mode of transport and he had to spend almost a week in hospital. Rohit suffered a fracture in his right leg and was unable to work for at least a couple of months.

On September 16 last year, Rohit and his friend Deepak, after getting tired of waiting for a bus near Patel Nagar, decided to take a "lift" on a bullock cart, with little idea that a ride on even a slow-moving vehicle like a bullock cart could be fraught with danger.

A carrier tempo hit the cart from the rear. The passengers fell off the vehicle due to the impact and were dragged by the tempo for a certain distance. '

The two were then rushed to the Lady Hardinge Hospital where they were subsequently treated.

A month later, the duo filed claim petitions before a MACT, complaining the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving by the tempo driver in an attempt to overtake the bullock cart.

Their petitions asked for compensation on account of joint liability on the part of the driver, the owner and the insurance company with which the tempo was insured.

A year later, the tribunal has finally accorded reprieve to Rohit and directed the parties to bear medical and other expenses incurred by him due to accident.

The MACT judge at the Tis Hazari courts has awarded a compensation of Rs 1.08 lakh along with an interest of 7.5 per cent to Rohit, directing the National Insurance Co Ltd to make the payment within a month.

Deepak, who was also injured in the mishap, has been awarded a compensation of Rs 10,000 for his medical expenses.

Heading: Man falls to death in Gurgaon - Indian Express
Content:
In the aftermath of the recent bomb blasts in the Capital, the Lieutenant Governor has decided to appoint a retired lieutenant general from the Indian Army to function as a security advisor for all projects related to the Commonwealth Games, to be held in 2010. According to highly-placed sources in the Delhi Development Authority, chaired by the L-G, the decision came after a "general security" guideline was issued by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs. "The Home Ministry issued general guidelines to us regarding security for Commonwealth Games projects. After a series of internal meetings, as well as meetings with the Delhi Police, the L-G decided to appoint a security advisor," said a senior official.

The L-G's office too confirmed the decision. "No one has been appointed as yet but plans are underway to do so," said Ranjan Mukherjee, officer on special duty to the L-G. Sources have confirmed that the search is on for a suitable candidate.

According to officials, the security advisor will work closely with the DDA to ensure that all security arrangements are in place for the Commonwealth Games projects, not only during the games but also during construction.

"There were fears from certain quarters that projects under construction, particularly the Games Village, were not being adequately monitored. While that is not true, it has been decided that security has to be of the utmost importance. Hence, this appointment of a dedicated security advisor will go a long way in addressing such fears," an official said.

There are already stringent methods in place for all personnel and labourers involved in all the projects. No one is permitted to enter the premises without proper identification and there are CCTVs in place to monitor all the projects.

"Perhaps, one fear that everyone had was that a security breach today could prove disastrous three years from now. Therefore, it was suggested that appointing a security advisor is important," a senior member in the DDA said. Meanwhile, DDA officials have been meeting with the Delhi Police regularly to ensure that all possible security measures are in place.

"The Delhi Police have been extremely co-operative and have assisted us at every step along the way. You must understand that the appointment of a security advisor is not because it was felt that security is light at the moment but only because it will help strengthen it even more," an official closely involved with the Commonwealth Games projects said.

Heading: 24-year-old woman commits suicide - Indian Express
Content:
The body of a 27-year-old man was found in the parking area of Hero Apartment on Saturday night in Sector-56 here. According to Gurgaon Police, it could be an accidental fall from his ninth floor room. However, they are still investigating possibilities.

The incident came to light around 10 pm on Saturday when the security guard saw the body of Devdutt Sharma in a pool of blood near the parking area of the building. He rushed to ask the owners if anyone had fallen from the house, said the police. When the owner checked Devdutt's room, it was locked from inside but no one answered the door.

It is then that they realised Devdutt had fallen off. Initially, the police thought it to be a case of suicide but after preliminary investigations, the police say it could be just an accident.

Sharma is a native of Shimla and had moved into the apartment in may this year.

Heading: Delhi underground - Indian Express
Content:
A 24-year-old woman reportedly committed suicide by hanging from the ceiling in RK Puram area of South district on Sunday. According to the police, the incident came to light when her brother-in-law found her hanging in her room. Nutan Mishra alias Baby who got married to one Amod Mishra used to live at the RK Puram residence along with Amod's elder brother.

"While Amod used to stay with his wife on the first floor, his elder brother stayed on the ground floor," a senior police officer said. Nutan got married to Amod in February and according to his brother, both were leading a peaceful life.

The police, however, are waiting for Nutan's parents to come to Delhi from Bihar before taking further steps.

Heading: On eve of Sonia visit to Rae Bareli, Maya scraps land allotment - Indian Express
Content:
The battle for GK
Congress stalwarts Kiran Walia and Health Minister Yogananad Shastri were in a fix after the BJP's V K Malhotra declared he would fight the upcoming Assembly polls from Greater Kailash. Walia fought the last Assembly elections from this constituency, while Shastri has been eyeing GK for these elections ever since substantial parts of his own constituency, Malviya Nagar, were shifted to GK following delimitation. Both Shastri and Walia don't know whether they want to contest the polls against Malhotra. They have been keeping their cards close to the chest and have been heavily lobbying for a "winnable" seat.

Faceless foe
Next month's Assembly elections are likely to be the most unusual polls Delhi has seen in recent times. For one, the BJP will be going to the ballot against a faceless Congress CM. While for all practical purposes Sheila Dikshit will unofficially be seen as the main rival candidate, sources in the Congress say that even if the party wins, it is "highly unlikely" the Congress high command will give her a third term. So, who is likely to be the Congress' chief ministerial candidate in her place? Even Congress insiders don't have a clue on how the high command will decide at last minute. The most likely candidate, according to poll experts, would have been Minister of State for Urban Development Ajay Maken. He has held important folios such as transport and power as a minister under the Dikshit government, before defeating Jagmohan in parliamentary elections. It is, however, now being said the high command isn't keen on Maken taking charge of Delhi. Maken himself is keeping an unusually low profile. Despite being on the election committee, he has barely been seen, as opposed to the municipal elections, when along with then DPCC president Ram Babu Sharma, Maken was the most visible face in Delhi politics.

All pomp, no show
In a rather extravagant gesture, Mayor Arti Mehra chose nothing less than the Taj Mansingh Hotel to host an annual gathering of mayors from across the country, spending, by one estimate, up to a whopping Rs 35 lakh of taxpayer money. The All India Mayor's Conference, held on October 6 and 7, was to be an elaborate affair to begin with. But the meet quickly turned out to be a damp squib, thanks to a thin turnout. Metros and megacities like Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bangalore, Baroda and Lucknow were not represented at all. Instead, the conference was attended only by the mayors of Faridabad, Kanpur and other small cities, leaving Mehra miffed. Sources in the Municipal Corporation of Delhi revealed that attendance at the conference was so low that Mehra had to call corporation staffers to fill up seats, instead of carrying out their duties, on both days.

Going the distance
It has been over a month since the district court at Dwarka was inaugurated, to ease the burden of existing courts and help speed up the disposal of cases. Its distance from the rest of the city, however, seems to be posing a big problem for some. So much so that when a prosecution counsel was contacted recently for details after controversial "godman" Chandraswami, facing 10 FERA violation cases, was acquitted by a Delhi court, he seemed to be at a loss. "The court is so far away, you can't expect me to go all the way, especially at the time of festivities," he said.

Fence sitters
It seems the Delhi Police is so keen on continuing the battle over respective jurisdictions that it, perhaps, doesn't even care if this means endangering lives in the process. Last week, during Durga Puja immersions in the Sonia Vihar Pushta area, nine people, who had gone to the river as part of the celebrations, were washed away by the strong Yamuna current. The Loni (UP) police were called in first for rescue operations. After engaging a few fishermen for the recovery of bodies, the UP cops called in the SDM, as they were not sure whether the area was in their jurisdiction. The SDM, upon assessment of the area, declared it was within the jurisdiction of the Delhi Police. Precious time was lost, as the Delhi Police arrived at the spot only at 5.15 pm and called in the MCD and Fire department. Lives could have been saved if the two police forces had coordinated on quickly tracing those missing.

Thank you for smoking
Even as most students and teachers in JNU insist the ban on smoking in public places won't deter them from smoking on campus, as cigarettes and tea are what the JNU academia lives on, a few bravehearts have taken it upon themselves to make the campus smoke-free. Even as anti-smoking posters depicting danger signs (skulls) have been pasted all over campus, it is a known fact that many "skulls" are still smoking everywhere on campus. Unlike Delhi University, the JNU administration does not appear to be well equipped to deal with a ban on smoking in public places. Comrades continue to debate issues and non-issues alike over multiple rounds of cigarettes and tea, in dhabas all through the night and day.

It's all about democracy
JNU elects representative councillors for all its schools, and they present an annual report on what they have accomplished during their tenure. In the general body meetings of various schools, councillors, mainly from the ultra left AISA and CPM-backed SFI, have been getting a drubbing and have seen their annual reports being defeated. The meetings are an open forum, where all students of the school concerned are eligible to vote. The defeat, say members of AISA — which won the last students' union elections and many councillor positions — is primarily down to most students being away from campus on account of Durga Puja vacations. Besides, they insist this is not a "real" defeat. The councillors managed 35 per cent of the votes, with the opposition united against them. In a democracy, an AISA member said, that is more than enough to win. NSUI activists, on the other hand, said the AISA's "conclusive defeat" was down to the lack of redress of issues like shortage of hostels on campus. The JNU Students' Union elections are due in the first week of November.

Heading: Farmers say rail coach factory land has nothing to do with them - Indian Express
Content:
Two days before UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi was to perform bhoomi pujan for a rail coach factory in her constituency Rae Bareli, the Mayawati government on Sunday cancelled the allotment of nearly 190 hectares that it had made for the project just three month ago, saying it wanted to prevent a "Singur-like situation" in Uttar Pradesh. The UP decision, Railways sources said, was a setback since they would now need to look for more contiguous land to set up the factory.

"The chief administrative officer of the project received a communication from the Rae Bareli district authorities stating that the entire process of handing over 189 hectares of land to the Railways stands cancelled," a top Northern Railway official told The Indian Express.

Railway Ministry officials said land totalling 542 hectares was needed to set up the Rail Coach Factory for the manufacture of 1,000 passenger coaches every year. There were three categories: 281 hectares of private land, 72 hectares of gram sabha land and 189 hectares of government land. While the private and gram sabha owned land had already been earmarked and notified under the Railway (Amendment) Act, 2008, which empowers Railways to acquire land for special railway projects, only the compensation aspect remained. Rae Bareli Deputy Commissioner Santosh Kumar Srivastava denied any political consideration was behind the decision to cancel the land allotted to Railways.

"When we gave them over 450 acres in May, the understanding was that the Railways would buy the remaining 750-odd acres from the villagers first and then begin work on the project.

However, villagers complained that without doing so, the Railways were going ahead with the bhoomi poojan on October 14. This went against what had been agreed to. This is why we took the step," Srivastava said.

"The decision has been taken to save the state from a Singur-like situation as the farmers had threatened to commit suicide if the land was given for the rail coach factory. A law and order situation would have confronted us," Srivastava said.

The state Congress angrily, calling the cancellation " a mindless act of a whimsical chief minister".

"We will have a rally and the Congress president will be here on the appointed day (October 14)," Ashok Singh, one of the four Congress MLAs in Rae Bareli, told The Indian Express.

UPCC president Rita Bahuguna said, " This is a mindless act of a whimsical chief minister. This project was to create employment for close to 10,000 people here."

"While Chief Minister Mayawati has acquired hundreds of acres of land in and around Noida and Greater Noida and erected her own statues in the state, she chose to sabotage one of the biggest investment opportunities. We will fight this decision tooth and nail," she added.

Heading: With uncertain future, villagers may resort to bloodbath: govt - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the state government claimed that farmers of the area do not want the rail coach factory in Lalganj, Rae Bareli, the scene at Ground Zero said a different story.

Minutes after the news of the state government taking back land from the Railways reached the area, residents came to the streets and blocked roads leading to Lucknow to protest against the decision. According to them, the land has nothing to do with farmers, as there is no cultivation work going on.

"It was acquired by the Gram Sabha in 1982 and is mostly barren land," said Usma Devi, Gram Pradhan of Dhekauli village, which comes under the Aihar Gram Sabha. "Not a single inch of the land belongs to any farmer," she claimed, shocked at the news that the state government has attributed its decision to protests from the locals. In fact, the rail coach factory project has been a good omen for the area, so much so that "people are ready to give their private land, if the need arose", said Mohd Ameen, a member of Bannamau Gram Sabha.

Lekhpal M B Yadav confirmed that so far, only the Gram Samaj land has been transferred to the Railways. Since the Railways need more land, besides the Gram Sabha land, about 110 farmers have been sent notices for land acquisition. Till date, there have been no protests from any farmer.

"Everybody has happily given their consent," said Ram Gopal Gupta, a member of the Gram Sabha. Avinindra Pandey, a BSP worker, whose land has also been earmarked, added: "I was waiting to give up my land as it has been lying useless for years." Other villagers like Ganga Sewak Vajpayee, Jai Prakash Shukla, Mohd Ghani, Putti Lal, Ganga Vajpayee have also received notices and are willing to give up their land. At the site where bhoomi pujan was to be performed by UPA Chairperson Sonia Gandhi, labourers engaged in preparations refused to leave the site. "We are hoping for a solution," said K M Mishra, a contractor.

Heading: LDA plans to reserve site for political rallies - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to justify its decision to take back the 189.25 hectare land of the gram sabha from the Railways in Rae Bareli, the UP government has said that the villagers were "agitated" as they felt that an additional 700 acre of land would be acquired for the rail coach factory that would make them landless and leave their children with no employment opportunity.

In a statement released, the government quoted the district magistrate of Rae Bareli, as saying: "This would create incidents of self-immolation and bloodbath which would be dangerous for law and order situation."

The government said the district magistrate, in a report sent on October 10, had stated that the villagers were angry over the transfer of land to the Railways "because they have lost their hope of getting pattas on the vacant gram sabha land."

The villagers "thought that the state government was working against the interests of the poor, especially a majority of Scheduled Castes, backward and poor people belonging to upper castes, by providing land to the industries instead of landless labourers," the statement stated.

It further stated that for 30 years, the gram sabha land remained with the central government's agriculture farm "but no beneficial action had been taken regarding this, and now the land, instead of being allotted to the poor people of SC/ST, was being transferred for such a purpose, which had nothing to do with the improvement of their condition."

The government said that for all these reasons the state government cancelled the process for acquiring land, ordered the return of the land to the gram sabha and also ordered refund of the money deposited by the Railways. It added that the government has asked the district magistrate to find land elsewhere for "such an important project."

'Rail coach factory will generate employment for 10,000 people'
The proposed rail coach factory (RCF) in Lalganj area of Rae Bareli, is expected to provide direct and indirect employment to more than 10,000 people and lead to development of ancillaries in the area, railway sources said. The project when completed would be third in the country after the Chennai RCF in Tamil Nadu and Kapurthala RCF in Punjab.
"It is one of our ambitious projects and it would convert the area into an industrial hub like Jagdishpur," said Chahatey Ram, Divisional Railway Manager of the Nothern Railway.
The railways had appointed D A Ananda as the Chief Administrative Officer of the rail coach factory, Rae Bareli, a few months ago.
The plant, planned to come up over 476 hectare of land, will have a capacity to manufacture 1,500 coaches per annum. The project is expected to cost around Rs 1,000 crore in the first phase, with provision for expansion later.
It was to be built on the public-private partnership model and the railways have already floated global tenders.
Originally, the plant was scheduled to begin production in 2007, but the land acquisition process delayed it. Officials said they were hoping to complete it by 2012, but now it looks uncertain.

Heading: UP tells Delhi: Divert drain, we don’t want your pollution - Indian Express
Content:
The Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) Board will take up a proposal on Monday to reserve Ramabai Ambedkar Rally Sthal for political rallies. For this, the LDA will charge a fee of Rs 50,000 for per day from the political party that will hold rally at the site.

The rally sthal, a multi-crore project of the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) government, is under construction on 51-acre area at Bijnore Road since last one year. The BSP has already organised two rallies at the site — on October 9, 2007 and August 9.

The state government had decided to develop the rally sthal keeping in view the need to hold rallies and meetings at a site which is outside the city. Besides the construction of boundary wall, gates, a permanent stage and two Swiss cottages for VIPs, statues of Bhimrao Ambedkar and Ramabai Ambedkar have also been erected at the sthal.

At the meeting, the LDA Board will also take up a proposal to construct a police post on the Gomti embankment for security of adjacent Ambedkar Memorial in Gomti Nagar. On September 23, the LDA had stopped construction work after the High Court had expressed its dissatisfaction over the closure of the road. It had also asked the development agency to reconsider its plan. But from the last two days, construction work resumed on the site.

LDA Vice-Chairman Mukesh Kumar Meshram, however, said: "Construction of police chowki is almost complete. The High Court had asked the LDA only to reconsider the idea of developing that police barrack at that site. Whether the barrack will stay at that site or not, that will be decided by LDA Board." A PIL in the regard was filed by Gomti Nagar Jankalyan Mahasamiti and its next hearing is scheduled for October 14.

The Board will also take up a proposal about Kanshiram Sanskritik Sthal to be developed on 80-acre area, adjacent to Kargil Smriti Upwan at Bijnore Road. Sanskritik Sthal will be used for organising cultural programmes like the Lucknow Festival. This year, Ravan Dahan was organised at the site.

Heading: UPTU to woo engg students for other streams than IT - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh government has asked Delhi administration that it does not want its Shahadra drain to flow into Noida.

A delegation of senior officials from the UP government, including the chief executive officer of Noida Authority, was in the Capital last week to hold a meeting with Delhi government officials to push for diverting the drain. The official reason cited by the officials was that they "do not want Delhi's pollution to enter UP".

"We had a meeting with the CEO and senior officials from the UP Irrigation and Flood Control. They have demanded that the Shahadra drain should not flow through Noida and be instead diverted along the Hindon directly into the Yamuna. Delhi and UP have now set up a joint committee to look into the feasibility of the proposal. The committee will also to consult the Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee, for technical feasibility of implementing the proposal," said Delhi Chief Secretary Rakesh Mehta.

Officials in the Delhi government said the demand made by the UP government might not be technically feasible. "The flow of the drain and the topography of the area are such that it may not be possible to divert the drain. In any case, this will be an extremely expensive proposition. The diversion cost aside, once the drain is diverted, water is likely to accumulate to the height of two metres or more on the Delhi side, which will need to be pumped out at a very high cost. But UP is so keen to have the drain diverted that they have offered to bear this cost," said a senior official. If the proposal is sanctioned, Delhi will have to divert six kilometres — the Delhi-Noida stretch — of the drain.

"There are plans to clean the drain water as part of our interceptor canal sewerage system — in which Najafgarh and Shahdara are the first two drains targeted. We will in any case start releasing clean water into Noida soon, but the UP authorities just don't want the drain to run through the state at all," said a senior DJB official.

Heading: VHP men ransack shops of minority community - Indian Express
Content:
As the world tries to come to grips with the current financial crisis, over one lakh students of information technology (IT) in Uttar Pradesh now face an uncertain future.

Though experts believe that the situation will soon ease, the engineering institutions and students are already looking for other opportunities.

A case in this regard is the Uttar Pradesh Technical University (UPTU). The university is mulling over an idea to encourage students to take up other engineering streams from the new academic session.

UPTU Vice-Chancellor Professor Prem Vrat was delivering a speech on "Information Technology Enabled Engineering Education: Opportunities and Challenges," organised by Computer Society of India, Lucknow Chapter on Sunday.

The university plans to project the idea of a balanced engineering education. In order to achieve its goal, UPTU will organise workshops and guidance programmes before the admission counseling to make students aware of the prevailing market conditions and job requirements in the various engineering streams.

Vrat maintained that if a student of civil or mechanical engineering has some knowledge about IT, he could be eligible for global employment.

"The information and guidance bureau of the university will organise the programmes," said Vrat.

He added that the recent meltdown in the market has hugely affected the IT sector. "Several IT companies have postponed the joining of students they had recruited from campuses in the beginning of the year," he said.

Heading: UP backward panel for abolition of creamy layer - Indian Express
Content:
Members of Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) ransacked, pelted stones on a few shops belonging to the minority community during Ram Baraat — a religious procession to celebrate Lord Ram's victory over Lanka — on Saturday night in Faizabad city. They also tried to put the shops on fire.

The VHP leaders accused the Muslims of keeping a piece of flesh in the way of the Ram Baraat.
