When the procession reached Fatehganj, members of the minority community stopped the Baraat and also made provocative remarks, they alleged. A group of around 100 people moved towards the Muslim-dominated Chowk area and started pelting stones on shops and houses.

Later, District Magistrate Anil Garg and Senior Superintendent of Police R K S Rathore met leaders of both the communities to take stock of the situation.

According to SSP Rathore, a few anti-social elements were trying to disturb peace in the area. "We have photographed the mob that had indulged in stone pelting and ransacking. We will take action against them after the festival is over," Rathore added.

A police officer said the place where the VHP activists allegedly found a piece of flesh was near a meat market, and often dogs pick up discarded meat from the shops. Circle Officer Rajesh Pandey said: "The Muslims fully co-operated with us to get the festival concluded peacefully."

Raj Kumar Arya, a local VHP leader, however, said: "Planting of flesh on the route was pre-planned. The local administration, instead of taking action against the accused, tried to end the issue in the name of communal harmony. But we will not remain silent."

Heading: Ganga loses its fresh water fish to marine species - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Centre has decided to raise the income criterion for the creamy layer of Other Backward Class to Rs 4.5 lakh so that more people could benefit from the reservation quota, the Uttar Pradesh State Backward Classes Commission has urged the state government to abolish the creamy layer, citing that it creates division.

In a letter to the state government, the chairman of the commission, Parasnath Maurya, wrote that all the OBC should be treated alike. He has asked the state government to take up the matter with the Centre.

He has also stated that there should be a separate quota for the OBCs in proportion to their population.

Principal Secretary (Backward Classes Welfare) Chandraprakash said the government is yet to take any decision on the matter. "The recommendations need to be approved by the Cabinet before we send them to the Centre," he said.

The letter, dated October 7, says that all backward classes are "facing exploitation" and therefore, they should be treated alike. It states the concept of creamy layer was "unconstitutional" because it finds no mention in the Constitution.

Maurya also questions the 27 per cent reservation for OBC in UP where its population is 54 per cent. He said that the reservation should be in proportion to the population as followed in several states like Madhya Pradesh and Uttarakhand.

When told that the concept of creamy layer had been prescribed by the Supreme Court, which has also stated that reservation cannot exceed 50 per cent, Maurya said he had given his views to the state government and it was for them to decide what needs to be done.

Heading: Lucknownama - Indian Express
Content:
The eco system of Ganga is changing so is the characteristics of the revered river's water, according to scientists. In a shocking finding, the scientists have observed that various species of fishes which helped in keeping the river water clean are facing extinction. In its place, numerous marine species are thriving in the river.

Marine species like Sea Bass, Rostellascaris, Xenentodon Cancilla, Clarius Gariepinus or Thai Magur have been found in the fresh water of Ganga in Allahabad and its surrounding districts.

Known to flourish in salty seawater (32 ppt water), these marine species have been found thriving in the freshwater of Ganga and Yamuna.

These parasites live on the food of the indigenous fish like sewage water and other pollutants and water insects. Since, these species grow very fast they have outnumbered the indigenous fish species like Clarius Batrachus (Magur) and Heteropneustes (Singhi) — the most eco-friendly fish that helps in removing a lot of filth from Ganga water. While Magur has vanished from Ganga and Yamuna, Singhi is on the verge of extinction.

Dr Sandeep K Malhotra from the Department of Zoology, Allahabad University, while terming it a serious threat to human lives, said: "The comfortable stay of marine species in Ganga is a cause of worry as they pollute the river water, besides posing serous threat to human lives through bacteria like Pseudomonas and Escherichia Coli that cause intestinal infection to people who consume fish."

He added that faecal matter of these species causes water pollution.

The branch of Parasitology in Allahabad University which has a memorandum of understanding with National Institute of Oceanography, Goa, has made a study on the new phenomenon and has concluded that immediate measures should be initiated to check the inflow marine species in the river.

Heading: Maya's Muslim meet planned 'in desperation' - Indian Express
Content:
In a significant recommendation, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) on Sunday recommended that undertrials be allowed to vote in elections.

The Commission, which celebrated its 15th Foundation Day on Sunday, has also recommended that the maximum period of detention of a person should not be more than six months. It has also asked the Government to ratify the Convention against Torture by amending the Indian Penal Code.

These and many other key recommendations were made at the culmination of a two-day international workshop on detention organised by the Commission here.

"An undertrial in custody or who is not on bail can contest an election but does not have the right to vote. The provision of right to vote should be ensured to the undertrials. It will have a positive impact on bringing out changes in the attitudes of the undertrials and the people," the recommendation said.

If this is done, the NHRC feels, it would impart a sense of dignity among undertrials and they would also be considered part of the society.

On the issue of preventive detention, the participants in the workshop said, it could not be for an "unlimited period" and that there was a need to reduce the maximum period of detention to two to six months and also have mechanism of periodic review.

"The difference between preventive and punitive detention must be clearly understood. Preventive detention is aimed at preventing the possibility of an activity by a person which may be detrimental to public order or national security. Preventive detention is an anathema to the rule of law but is a necessary evil. There is need to sensitise the authority that it should be resorted to as an exception in rare cases. Preventive detention is not to substitute the normal procedure established by law," the participants concluded.

They also said in case the detenue is found unlawfully detained, there should be adequate provision for interim relief and compensation.

The Commission also suggested that speedy trials could be the way out to deal with the issue of growing population of undertrials languishing in jails.

It said establishment of more courts and filling the vacant posts in judiciary as well as taking steps to expedite the process of recording evidence of the police officers and medical practitioners who are witnesses in certain cases could go a long way in tackling this problem.

Heading: Tribal stripped, beaten up by Surendranagar cops - Indian Express
Content:
The Bahujan Samaj Party's plan to hold a national convention on the "Problems of Muslim Community in India: Its Causes and Solution" in Lucknow on Monday has not gone down well with some Muslim clerics.

The convention will be held a day before Muslim clerics from all over the country will meet at Delhi's Jama Masjid to discuss the issue of terrorism.

Shahi Imam of Jama Masjid Ahamed Bukhari, who is organising the Delhi gathering, however, claimed Chief Minister Mayawati had hurriedly planned the convention "in desperation". According to him, Mayawati decided to hold the convention after getting to know of the Delhi meet, for which invitations had been sent out in September.

Bukhari said he had invited clerics from across the country, including Lucknow, Aligarh, Bulandshahr, Deoband, Varanasi and Azamgarh.

The common invitees at the two functions include the chairman of All India Muslim Personal Law Board (AIMPLB) Maulana Rabe Hasni Nadwi, Naib Imam of Lucknow's Aishbagh Eidgah and AIMPLB's member Khalid Rashid Farangi Mahali, prominent Shia cleric Kalbe Jawad and the head of Darul-Ulm-Warsia Maulana Iqbal Quadari. Maulana Nadwi may not be able to attend either because of his illness. BSP national general secretary Satish Chandra Mishra had called on him on Saturday and requested him to send his representative at the party's convention.

Common invitee like Rashid Farangi Mahali, however, is not ready to link the two functions. "While BSP's convention is siyasi (political), the meet that Bukhari has organised is an attempt to unite the Muslim community members. Thus, I plan to participate in both the functions. At present, Mayawati needs the Muslim community. We hope she will take steps for the betterment of the Muslim community after our discussion," he said.

Maulana Iqbal Quadari, who is associated with the Darul-Ulm-Warsia, said BSP convention has been organised "in haste". "Today, Public Works Department Minister Naseemuddin invited me to attend the convention. I have requested him to provide grants to 400 madarsas," he said. He will also attend both the meets. Sources in the BSP said all the party MLAs will be present at the convention. "We expect participation of about 4,000 people," said a source.

Heading: DCB busts terror module having links with Indian Mujahideen, LeT - Indian Express
Content:
The pride of Uniform and upper caste makes a lethal combination. This manifested one of its ugliest forms in the feudal hinterland of Gujarat on October 8 when two policemen from the Darbar community brutalised a tribal man at Nanikati village in Limdi taluka of Surendranagar district in full public view.

The policemen stripped Kana Gesapara (40) in the village panchayat office, beat him up and then pushed a stick wrapped in petrol soaked cloth up his rectum and put it in his mouth later.

Not satisfied with this, the policemen then took the semi naked man to the village temple, where they beat him up again and made him wear a ghaghra. Later, they forced him to walk in that dress carrying his pants and shoes on his head till the panchayat office, where they made him dance as well.

According to Kalpesh Sapra, a villager, the police had come to look for Gesapara following a complaint by the latter's wife against him in the police station.

Gesapara said: "On the evening of October 7, I was sleeping in my house when the peon from the panchayat office came to call me. As I followed him, Beat Head Constable Janaksinh Rana and Constable Indu Rana, both from the Darbar community from the nearby Bhalgamda village, accosted me on the way." He added: "They grabbed me by my collar and dragged me to the panchayat office and stripped me there. Later, they pulled me out of the panchayat room and beat me up in full public view."

He added: "Then they forced me to bend down before the doors of panchayat room where they pulled out a stick, wrapped it with petrol soaked cloth and pushed it up my rectum, before putting the stick in my mouth."

He further said: "Then they took me to the Ramji Temple in the village and made me lie down and hit me on the buttocks with sticks. Later, they made me wear a ghaghra and walk through the village to the panchayat office, where they made me dance."

He said finally the two policemen took him to the Panitola police station where they kept him overnight with his hands tied. "The next morning they took me to the court. En-route they gave me a bath at the Bhavani Hotel, which is also owned by another Darbar community person, to clean my blood stains," he said.

While the police refused to admit an FIR due to alleged political pressure, a private complaint has been filed with the Limdi Court.

"We moved a private complaint before the judge in this matter, even before we moved the bail application for Gesapara," said VK Rathod, the victim's lawyer.

He added: "The judge has asked for a medical report and he (Gesapara) has been examined in the Surendranagar Civil Hospital." He said the medical reports have shown injury marks and the matter has now been forwarded to the District Judge for further action.

Meanwhile, Gesapara and the villagers allege that there has been significant political pressure on the doctors, whom they visited for Gesapara's treatment.

"Starting from the Limdi Civil Hospital to Surendranagar Civil Hospital, everywhere we have been refused treatment as Kiritsinh Rana has been creating pressure on the doctors. It still pains and there is no one to even treat me," said Gesapara.

Balji Dargaiya, a member of Nanikati Panchayat said: "There is tremendous terror of the police in the area as they frequently beat up people like this. They did all this to Gesapara in full public view, but the police refused to register an FIR as they fear to act against the minister's men. (It is mentionable that Gujarat's Minister of Forest and Environment Kiritsinh Rana belongs to Bhalgamda and is a member of the Darbar community).

He added that some days ago a man in Ranagadh village narrowly escaped death due to police beating.

Political patronage to the police, particularly to the ones belonging to the Darbar community, was evident when a sub-inspector of the Panesara police station switched off his mobile phone after the Newsline tried to get in touch with him a couple of times on Sunday evening.

Surendranagar Superintendent Ashok Kumar, however, denied any political pressure and said that he has already received an application in this regard.

"I have already asked a DSP to inquire into the matter and submit a report to me in a week's time," said Kumar, adding that strict action will be taken if evidence is found against the accused policemen.

Kiritsinh Rana gave a clean chit to the police by saying that "nothing of this sort has happened" and that the villagers went to the police station to lodge a false FIR.

"If there was anything substantial, they could have come to me and I would have sorted it out. But let me tell you, nothing of this sort happened," he said.

He added that the area is his own constituency and he is very much aware of the develop-ments there.

But Sapra added: "I am an eye-witness to the entire episode and I will testify about this in the court of law if required."

Heading: Transfer of probe officers galore in Sohrabuddin case - Indian Express
Content:
Intelligence official says it is just the tip of an iceberg as number of such 'sleeper cells' active in the state would be very high

During the investigation of the July 26 blasts, the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) has busted a terror module having links with organisations like the Indian Mujahideen (IM) and Laskhar-e-Toiba (LeT). It has arrested a number of its members from the city and other parts of the country.

Interestingly, the local members of the module do not share any links with another terror module, which was busted by the Gujarat Anti-Terror Squad (ATS) in 2006 with the help of Delhi Police's Special Cell. Both the modules, however, comprised members of the banned Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI).

In May 2006, the ATS had arrested four local youths, allegedly SIMI members, on charges of waging a war against the nation. Earlier, two of them, Muhammed Ali Chhipa and Firoze Ghaswala, were arrested by the Special Cell of the Delhi Police along with 4 kg RDX in the National Capital. The other two were Sheikh Umar Farooq Mohammed Nuruddin and Vakil Ahmed Mohammed Saiyed from Ahmedabad.

The police had then said that the accused were members of the sleeper cell of the LeT in the city and were planning terror strikes at some religious and commercial places in Gujarat. According to the police, all the members of the recent busted module were also members of SIMI.

Additional Director General of Police, Intelligence, P P Pandey said the present instance indicates the fact that the module is just the tip of an iceberg. According to him, the number of such 'sleeper cells' active in the state would be very high and its existence would be known only to its controllers across the border, most probably in Pakistan.

Pandey said: "The sleeper cells generally work in isolation and its existence would be known only to its controller who will engage people in various jobs based on their expertise. Sometimes, in a sleeper cell, the members of the same cell would not know each other." He added, "It could be possible that the controller of the 2006 module and the present one is the same person located across the border."

Pandey said that generally, the members of a sleeper cell work as a local support to carry out a terror activity and they get active only when the need arises.

"In such a scenario, it is very difficult to figure out the cell. And even if one cell gets busted, existence of the other ones will not be known to the police as only its controller would be knowing about it," he added.

According to the police, members of sleeper cells are inducted by different means like holding meetings during some pilgrimage or during an individual's tour to a hostile country by initially providing them minor jobs.

Heading: Mistaken identity: Farmers bring home two leopard cubs thinking them to be kittens - Indian Express
Content:
Investigation officer Inspector P B Jadeja has been shifted to the Ahmedabad Police Commissionerate

Ten officers of the Gujarat Police have been arrested in connection with the Sohrabuddin Sheikh fake encounter case. Surprisingly, an equal number of CID (Crime) officers investigating the case have so far been shunted, it has been learnt.

The latest name in the transfer list is that of Inspector P B Jadeja. He has been transferred to the Ahmedabad Police Commissionerate. Jadeja, who was given his transfer order on September 29, joined his new office on Friday. However, he is yet to get a posting in the city.

Abrupt transfer of the officers involved in the probe is not new. The investigation, which was initially being supervised by Inspector General of Police Geetha Johri, was suddenly handed over to her deputy Rajnish Rai in March 2007.

A 'firebrand' Rai, who got the IPS trio of D G Vanzara, Rajkumar Pandian and suspended Rajasthan SP Dinesh MN arrested within a month of taking over the case, was shunted in the first week of May 2007. This came a day after he moved an application before the then Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, K J Upadhyay, seeking permission to conduct narco-analysis test on the three. A few hours later, Johri was told that she was back in the case, and has been heading the investigation since then.

Among investigators, Inspector V L Solanki was transferred to the Economic Offence Wing of the CID (Crime) before his retirement. Inspector R H Hadia, who replaced Solanki, also could not continue with the probe and was transferred to Surat city in March this year. Hadia's senior, Deputy Superintendent of Police G B Padheria, who was supervising the probe, was transferred to the Police Research Cell (PRC) of the CID (Crime).

Before Hadia, Inspectors Y A Sheikh, T K Patel and O B Sharma were transferred to Civil Defence, Patan and Rajkot city respectively. IPS officer Raju Bhargav, who was assisting Johri in the case, was transferred to Mehsana in September 2007. Apart from Johri, the only investigator in the case now is Inspector D H Trivedi, who was transferred to the CID (crime) from Anand in April this year. The 10 policemen who are presently lodged in the Sabarmati Central Jail in connection with the case are suspended IPS officers Vanzara and Pandian; suspended DySPs N K Amin and M L Parmar; suspended Inspectors N H Dabhi and V A Rathod; suspended Sub-Inspectors Balkrishn Chaube and N V Chauhan; and suspended Constables Santram Sharma and Ajay Parmar.

While all the police top brass refused to comment on the issue, Home Minister Amit Shah said he was not inclined to discuss the matter.

Heading: Young at 70: Lonely hearts seek partners at Swayamwar - Indian Express
Content:
Two farmers, who went out as usual to till their maize field on Friday afternoon in Laved Vasahat of Sankheda taluka, found two kittens lying abandoned. Filled with sympathy and hoping to keep them as pets, the brothers took them home.

But they were shocked when their elder brother told them that they had brought home leopard cubs just about two or three days old — one male and another female.

While ploughing, they noticed the two furry little ones in the middle of the maize field. "They were too small to be left alone, so we brought them home," said brothers Kanji Dungrabhil and Urasiya Dungrabhil.

Kevji, who is the sarpanch of Laved Vasahat, told Newsline: "My younger brothers were feeding them milk when we I told them that they were not kittens, but the young ones of some wild animal."

Worried what to do with the leopard cubs, the family contacted local heads to find a solution to their problem. Forester P B Baria reached Kevji's residence. "I made a small bamboo basket, weighed both the cubs and put them in a basket. Three more foresters and a beat guard went and sent the cubs back to their habitat on Saturday night. We were instructed to keep a watch on the cubs from a safe distance of 250-300 metres. It was a moonlit night and soon we saw a wild animal nearing the bamboo basket, uncovering it, and taking the young cubs away. It was a relief to see them go," said Baria.

Nayan Desai, Deputy Conservator of Forest, Social Forestry, Vadodara, said it was good and timely thinking on part of the Dungrabhil families to inform the authorities about the cubs. "They could have caused a lot of trouble for the village that has more than 1,000 people. The mother leopard may have crossed the threshold and ventured into the village in search of her young ones, posing a threat to the villagers."

The Jambughoda Sanctuary lies very close to human habitat in Sankheda district. Leopards have entered the village in the past, but this might be the first time that they have enjoyed the hospitality of the people.

Heading: Cong files RTI application to get details of Nano deal - Indian Express
Content:
Autumn romance may not be unheard of, but what about beginning a live-in relationship after crossing the sixties and seventies? If what five senior women, all coincidentally from south India, preferred in their applications for partners to the Vina Mulya Amulya Seva (VMAS) is any indication, then this might be an emerging but less known paradigm.

VMAS had arranged a platform on Sunday in the city for lonely hearts of the older generation to find spouses, which several senior citizens from places as far away as Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and even the US, besides all across Gujarat, attempted to put to best use. Clad in the best attire, the old suitors flocked to the Swayamwar venue at the Town Hall as part of the All India Senior Citizens Marriage Mela.

The well-suited and booted men, with excitement and anticipation more than obvious on their old faces, could hardly wait to see the beautifully dressed and equally old women. The prospective candidates were introduced one at a time on stage where they looked up each other and made a note of their favourite choices, so as to meet the chosen ones for a special one-hour personal chat session after the programme.

The males had a tougher task though. About 500 men turned up at the event, compared to only 80 women who sashayed up the stage for them. Over 800 aged applicants had applied to VMAS, seeking spouses.

Incidentally, VMAS has successfully fixed the marriages of 22 such couples this year alone.

Sixty-year-old Ghanshyam, one of the old couples who married through VMAS, said: "My new wife had three sons but she was living alone as they never took care of her. We met through this organisation and were married. Re-marriage is not wrong. Women should open up more as they are the ones who face severe problems when they lose their husbands."

Old age is often associated with loneliness, health complications and depression, especially for women who are

widowed or divorced. Re-marriage still being a taboo, women just do not open up. "Being a divorcee I know it is a little difficult for women to be accepted in society, which is why not all women come forward for initiatives like this." "I chose this method as I found it more reliable than the marriage portals. But women should come out of a closed mindset and get set to start afresh. After all, at this age we only want companionship and security," said Rekha (45), a divorcee.

Those who believe marriages are for the young and oldies cannot enjoy marriages may find disagreement in Kanti Bhatt, an author and a columnist. "Even at the age of 77, I can enjoy sex. So oldies who think there is no life after 50 should correct themselves."

The bubbly spirits of the old men and women at the event was the actual show stealer. The grandpas and grandmas showed no hesitation to try and choose new partners and begin life anew. Many were divorcees and widows, and were looking ahead with a lot of hope.

Indu Shah (70), who flew from the US hoping to find his lady love, said there is nothing like a 'desi' partner. "There are many beautiful women in the US. I have enjoyed a lot in life. But I want an ordinary woman from Gujarat who can take care of me," he said.

Babu Chawda, a delegate, who is also a social activist, said: "I am a 79-year-old widower and I live alone. I want a companion who can love me. What is wrong in getting married at this age? I am not really that old!"

Heading: Delegation to Pak for fishermen’s release - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress has sought details of the deal signed between the Gujarat government and the Tata Motors for the Nano car project under the Right to Information (RTI) Act.

In an application to the Industries Commissioner, the party has sought details of the

incentives given to the Tata Motors, party spokesperson Arjun Modhvadia said.

Meanwhile, CPI (M)'s Gujarat unit on Sunday said it will not oppose any development projects, including Nano plant, in the state. The party, however, demanded the Modi government to make public the agreement it has reached with the Tatas.

Heading: Inadequate rainfall behind compulsory holiday: GUVNL - Indian Express
Content:
Islamabad had sent New Delhi an invitation to send a representation to resolve the issue

The recent round of friendly talks between Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari has raised a ray of hope among the fishermen community in the state.

Islamabad had recently sent an invitation to New Delhi to send a representation of fishermen to Pakistan to resolve, among other issues, the boats owned by Indian fishermen, now in possession of Pakistan, detained in the last five years.

Now the eight member team of fishermen leaders from Saurashtra are going on a visit of Pakistan on October 12.

Islamabad has not released the 378 boats and 487 Indian fishermen captured by the Pakistan Maritime Security Agency (PMSA) in the last five years. The fishermen community had made a hue and cry over the issue, but to no avail. "After almost five years, the Pakistani authorities moved a step ahead in the peace process by inviting a representation of the fishermen community. With orders from the Centre, the state government has now formed an eight-member team to hold talks with the Pakistani authorities," said Veljibhai Masani, a fisherman leader from Mangrol and vice-president of the Akhil Gujarat Machimar Mahamandal.

The eight-member team will be led by Veljibhai Masani. Other members include Bhagubhai Solanki of Jafarbad, Kishorbhai Kuhada of Veraval, Kishan Gosai of Mangrol, Sunil Gohel, Bharat Modi and Premji Modi of Porbandar and Fisheries Department official Mahendra Chaudhary. The delegation will leave Mumbai for Karachi on October 12 and is likely to return on October 22.

Veljibhai told Newsline that Pakistani authorities had informed their Indian counterparts to send a representation before October 30 to check and survey the condition of the 378 boats, failing which they will auction the vessels.

It was following this that the Gujarat government formed the eight-member team and processed the visa and other formalities, said Veljibhai, adding that they have been in touch with the fishing community leaders in Pakistan to sort out the issues.

"We will meet the Pakistani authorities and the Karachi Fishermen Co-Operative Society leaders and discuss for a permanent solution to the issue. We will survey the condition of the boats, but we don't think they will be sea-worthy. In the last five years, three cyclones have struck the Pakistan coast and the boats must be nothing more than wreckages now. The recently captured boats can be taken back though. But we will definitely see if the old boats can be brought back with little repair," he said.

He further said that the Indian fishermen have been booked by the PMSA for illegally fishing in Pakistani waters and they are not involved in any anti-social or anti-national activity.

He said: "We will meet our 487 fishermen brothers lodged in Pakistani jails and request the authorities there to provide them with medical treatment or other help as required."

Incidentally, the fishermen leaders of both countries have decided to extend help to their community members lodged in each other's jails and approach the two governments for the same. Veljibhai added that if the representation successfully brings back the boats, then this will be the first time in five years that Pakistan will be releasing crafts captured by it.

Heading: Ambaji pilgrims pledge before goddess to fight female foeticide - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited (GUVNL) has cited inadequate rainfall as the reason for imposing a compulsory holiday on industries across Gujarat from October 6. The fact, however, remains that the state owned power company is facing a daily deficit of over 1000 MW, thanks to the non-functioning of its various power units following technical snag.

The GUVNL has twice imposed power cuts on industries since August. The company has again imposed a forced holiday on the industrial sector as power demand, according to GUVNL, has gone up in the agriculture sector following inadequate rainfall.

But the power generation and consumption figures tell a different story altogether. Interestingly, when GUVNL had imposed a two-day power cut on industrial sector in the months of August and September, 25 per cent of the total 8,000 MW generation in the state was consumed in farm sector, which was 8 per cent less than the power supplied in the month of May and almost equal to the figure for the months of June and July.

According to GUVNL officials, power consumption has gone up by 1,500 MW due to inadequate rainfall. At present, the power demand is to the tune of 9500 MW, as against the total power generation of nearly 8000 MW.

Power demand as on October 10 was 8272 MW and the generation was 7703 MW. The deficit due to non-functioning of 7 units was to the tune of 1405 MW, which was half of the actual deficit. This means that if all the units had been in order on October 10, there would have been surplus power generation.

Wanakbori power station unit-1, which has a capacity of 210 MW, has not been functioning since September 17 due to some technical snag. Similarly, Wanakbori power station unit-II, which has the same capacity, went out of order on October 9. Unit number VI at the same power plant also stopped functioning on October 9. Moreover, unit –1 at Ukai power station has been out of order since September 15.

GUVNL director (technical) P H Rana refused to comment on the issue. The State Industries Minister Saurabh Patel was not available for comment.

Heading: Gujarat awaits 11th Five-Year Plan to improve sports infrastructure - Indian Express
Content:
A total of five lakh 'Sankalp Patras' signed to save the girl child and curb sex discrimination

Pilgrims at the famous Ambaji temple in Banaskantha district found a new way to check the dwindling female sex ratio in the state - 'Sankalp Patras'. The Ambaji Temple Committee members made the devotees sign the 'Sankalp Patras' to curb sex discrimination and female foeticide, along with a pledge to save the girl child. A total of five lakh 'Sankalp Patras' were signed.

R.J Patel, District Collector of Banaskantha and Chairman of the Ambaji Temple Committee, said: "Out of the 25 lakh pilgrims who visited Ambaji Temple, a total of 5 lakh devotees signed the Sankalp Patras in a span of 5 days between September 11 and 15."

He added: "While the idea has been implemented for the first time at any religious place, the chances of its success are quite high as people have willingly taken a pledge before the goddess and are most likely to abide by it. In fact, we did not have to make too many efforts to persuade the devotees. All we had to do was to put up notice boards along with the Sankalp Patras."

The Ambaji Development Authority also plans to implement the same method to make devotees pledge for saving the girl child by making the Sanklap Patras available in the soon-to-be developed replicas of the 51 Shaktipeeths at the Gabbar mountain.

Patel said: "We have plans to extend the experiment to other religious destinations in the area as well. This is for the first time that such an experiment has been undertaken at a religious place in the state. However, with the active participation of future devotees, the awareness campaign is bound to be effective."

Heading: Sabarmati Jail inmates ransack jail dispensary - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat government had set aside an amount of Rs 2,000 lakh for several sports and youth development schemes in the 10th Five-Year Plan (2002-2007). However, it has been able to achieve only about 30 per cent of its goal till now.

"We knew that despite spending so much money we would not be able to get the appropriate result, as there is huge scarcity of coaches in the state. At present, there are 58 coaches appointed by SAG in the state. This is only 25 per cent of the required number of coaches," said Ajay Desai, senior coach of Sports Authority of Gujarat (SAG), Anand district.

He said: "In the 10th Five-Year Plan, an Integrated Scheme of Youth Welfare was proposed and the aim was to organise seminars and leadership camps throughout the state to create awareness about burning issues such as population control, communal harmony and so on. But how can we create awareness without enough coaches and physical instructors?"

C I Chunara, also a senior coach in Kheda district, said: "We have to follow orders of higher authorities. But we don't find their plans efficient despite crores of rupees being spent on the schemes."

He added: "There was a proposal to find talent in tribal areas of the state. Lakhs of rupees were proposed to be spent on the scheme. But SAG follows a very slow procedure and we do not know when we will be able to get good sportspersons in large number."

A senior official of SAG, Gandhinagar, feels that the schemes introduced in the 10th Five-Year Plan were not up to the mark.

"If they continue to follow the same path, then God only knows if the state will be able to improve the level of sports activities," he said.

"Around 70 per cent of the talent hunt camps organised every year fail because of some reason or the other. But, I believe, we will be able to work efficiently with a new director general for SAG," said V S Solanki, senior coach of SAG, Surat.

"The state still lacks proper infrastructure for the development of sports activities and developing new sports talents. How can we function without improving sports complexes, grounds and equipment? Let's hope that we try to recover the failure of the 10th Five-Year Plan in the 11th Five-Year Plan," said G P Gothi, senior coach of SAG, Patan.

Heading: Modi likely to discuss terrorism at NIC meet in Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
In the third major incident reported from the Sabarmati Central Jail in Ahmedabad in the last two days, three inmates created a ruckus inside the jail dispensary on Saturday night and attacked an orderly after having an altercation with the dispensary staff over the delay in medical treatment.

Following the incident, the Sabarmati police registered an FIR against the three accused. Further investigations into the case are on. Two of the three accused have been identified as Mohammed Yunus Abdul Rahim and Usmangani. Dr L N Somani, doctor of the jail dispensary, lodged a complaint in this regard.

According to the police, the three had gone to the jail dispensary to get some medical treatment. But when the dispensary staff got delayed in providing them medical treatment, the three got enraged and started abusing the staff. Following a brief altercation, the three beat up the nursing orderly of the dispensary.

Sabarmati Inspector K M Joshi said: "The three created a ruckus in the dispensary after a delay in their medical treatment. They beat up the orderly and ransacked the dispensary. We have registered a case against the accused and will arrest them after completing some formalities."

On Friday, a prisoner at the jail, Prakash Barot, was attacked with a knife, allegedly by eight other convicts. Barot, who sustained injuries on his eye, is currently under medical treatment.

In another incident, two inmates — Mukund Tanna (52) and his brother-in-law Paresh Kariya (36) — were attacked with a sharp-edged weapon, allegedly by fellow convict Mahipatsinh Jhala. The incident took place in the canteen around 5.30 pm.

Heading: Soaring textbook prices push students to leave school - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Narendra Modi is likely to raise the issue of terrorism at the National Integration Council's (NIC) meeting called by the Prime Minister in New Delhi on Monday, though the same has been reportedly removed from the agenda.

Sources close to Modi said on Sunday that since NIC usually takes up the contentious issues of country's security and integrity, the chief minister might raise the issue of terrorism during the deliberations at the Monday meeting, which is to be attended by the chief ministers of all states.

Modi had already suggested to the UPA government at the Centre to chalk out a strategy to curb terrorist activities and also strengthen the Intelligence apparatus, sources said, especially in the wake of July 26 serial blasts in Ahmedabad and the recovery of live bombs in Surat.

"It is in this context that our chief minister may raise the issue of terrorism at the NIC meet on Monday. He has already written to the Prime Minister in protest against the topic of terrorism being removed from the agenda of NIC's meeting at the eleventh hour. He has also faxed a copy of the protest letter to all the chief ministers," sources said.

At the NIC meet, Modi will also speak about the various measures his government has initiated to remove economic imbalance in Gujarat. Besides other things, economic imbalance is one of the main topics on the Council's agenda. On this front, he will apprise the participants of the three multi-crore schemes the Gujarat government has launched in the state for the socio-economic uplift of tribals, the fishing community and the urban poor, a senior official said.

Heading: ‘Nano land transfer a publicity stunt’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat State Board of School Textbooks (GSBSTB) has increased the cost of textbooks for Classes VII, VIII, IX and X by 150-200 per cent in the last three years. However, this price-hike has affected lakhs of students, both from urban as well as rural areas. Moreover, the state government has not provided any financial aid to the students for purchasing the textbooks.

Seema Patel (name changed), from Vastarpur village, Ahmedabad, said: "I have three kids. Two of them are in Class VIII and one is in Class X. My husband and I are labourers in a factory and our financial condition is not good as of now. Moreover, due to the price-hike in the textbooks we might ask our two kids to leave school."

Mohan Modwadia, principal of Aksar Vidhya Mandir told Newsline, "Several Class VII students have left school due to the price-hike in textbooks. The GSBSTB has increased the price of Class VII textbooks by 150 per cent this year."

Dushyant Shukla, principal, Vishwas Bharti School, Thaltej, Ahmedabad, said that the state government keeps on increasing the price of the textbooks without thinking that parents of almost 60 per cent of students will not be able to afford them.

Hitesh Patel, principal, Shajanad Vidyalaya, Ahmedabad, said: "There is no doubt that the GSBSTB is upgrading the syllabus of Classes VII, VIII, IX and X. The price-hike in the textbooks is bound to happen because of inflation and cost of printing. But the least they can do is start giving textbooks at concession to students who cannot afford to buy them."

The GSBSTB officials were unavailable for comment.

Heading: Solid waste management to get a facelift in Vadodara - Indian Express
Content:
Shankersinh Vaghela accuses Modi of taking credit for schemes launched by the Centre

Union Textiles Minister Shankersinh Vaghela on Sunday termed the Gujarat government's move to give land to the Tata Motors for the Nano car plant as a publicity stunt ahead of the general elections.

Inaugurating a Woollen Expo in Godhra, Vaghela accused the state government of often taking credit of the schemes launched by the Centre.

"Nano is just a hogwash to lure people to vote for the BJP in the Lok Sabha elections… on many occasions, (Narendra) Modi has taken credit of the schemes launched by the Union Government," he said while referring to the Jyotigram Yojana.

Vaghela did not miss out on the opportunity to highlight the Centre's achievements and said that the Manmohan Singh-led UPA government has also signed several important pacts, including the nuclear deal with the US.

He assured the wool producers of the state that his ministry is working on the insurance for cattle rearers. "Your cattle are your assets. Keep them safe. Don't let the wolves feast on them," said Vaghela.

Interestingly, the minister did not say anything about the first report of the Nanavati-Mehta Committee, which gave a clean chit to the Chief Minister in the post-Godhra riots.

A large section of sheep rearers from Kutch attended the Expo held at Newra High School Ground. Vaghela felicitated around six local taluka sarpanchs from Santrampur, Godhra and Lunawada for their contribution to the cotton farming.

Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas Dinsha Patel and Dabhoi MLA Siddharth Patel accompanied Vaghela at the event.

Heading: MSU to host five-day NCERT workshop - Indian Express
Content:
Faced with laxity in the solid waste collection process, the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) has decided to provide city residents with new personal waste bins to facilitate door-to-door garbage collection.

VMC officials said they have been receiving complaints from residents for over-flooding waste containers. They have now taken up the new measures to ensure proper waste collection, the officials added.

Sailesh Naik, executive engineer, VMC, said: "Most residents ask us to carry out the waste collection drive at a particular time of the day, which is not possible. With the new personal waste bins, residents as well as collectors can work with ease."

In the initial stage, the VMC plans to install 100 litre bins at each residence.

"The ongoing collection is not being monitored properly by the ward offices and most of the collectors miss out on smaller societies in their route of collection," said Naik.

He further informed that the ward offices have been given a new notification on the monitoring and registration of collection and disposal of the waste at the landfill site.

"The routes have been specified and the points of collection have been reduced from 650 to 240, so that the collectors can cater to all the spots. The decreased collection spots will be coupled up with increased door-to-door collection, so as to make solid waste collection an uninterrupted process," Naik added.

Heading: Govt’s art promotion claims fall flat as Pithora painter awaits bill clearance - Indian Express
Content:
M S University's Faculty of Education and Psychology will host a five-day workshop on monitoring systems to enhance elementary education in the states under the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) from Monday. In the zonal workshop, the department will play host to educational fraternity from four states — Gujarat, Rajasthan, Orissa and Uttarakhand.

Admitting to the deteriorating quality of school education, the NCERT has taken up a new project to understand the loopholes in the system and introduce stronger monitoring systems.

With this aim, the NCERT has organised the event titled 'Regional Workshop for Strengthening Monitoring Mechanisms in the States for Enhancing Quality in Elementary Education'.

M S University Vice-Chancellor Ramesh Goyal will inaugurate the workshop. The NCERT has organised five such workshops in various zones across the country.

R C Patel, the convener of the workshop and a member of the Faculty of Education and Psychology, said, "The deteriorating quality of elementary education is not an unknown fact. But the whole primary education is spread over the national, state, district and even the taluka level. The basic aim of this workshop is to monitor the loopholes in the system from every region of the country and prepare guidelines for better administration."

Around 48 people, 12 participants from each state, will take part in the workshop. The participants include school teachers, members from the State Council of Primary Education (SCPE), District Institute of Education and Training (DIET), District Resource Centre (DRC) coordinators, Clustered Resource Centre (CRC) coordinators and Block Resource Centre (BRC) coordinators. The workshop will be headed by Prof K K Vashistha, Head of the Elementary Education Department, NCERT.

"The coordinators have inspected all the schools at the taluka and district levels. They will discuss their observations on the teaching and learning module, the difficulties faced by the teachers and the students during their visit to the schools," said Patel.

"After identifying various issues from all the states, the NCERT will prepare a guideline to strengthen the teaching module," he added

Heading: Former BJP Anand councillor stabbed to death - Indian Express
Content:
For 28-year-old Kanti Rathwa, a Pithora painter from Vankadia village near Halol, the promotion of folk art by state agencies is a farce. For the last two years, he has been running from pillar to post to clear his payment for banners and frescoes prepared for the District Panchayat in November 2006 when former President A PJ Abdul Kalam visited the Pavagadh-Champaner site.

It was during Kalam's visit when the historic place was declared a world heritage site. At that time, Rathwa along with 11 others from his small self-help group Jai Babadev Swa Sahay Juth, catering to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) adivasis, prepared banners and frescoes.

He had submitted a bill of Rs 23, 532, which included material and transportation cost. But the Zila Panchayat paid him only Rs 4,966 in July 2008. Since then, he has been shuttling between various offices of Godhra and Halol in Panchmahals district to clear his bill.

Halol Taluka Development Officer N Gamit, however, said that the bill of Rs 23,532 was not correct. "I was not posted here when the bills were sent to the Taluka office. But the artistes from Jai Babadev Swa Sahay Juth have been paid what was necessary," said Gamit while admitting that the delay was unfortunate.

Rathwa, on the other hand, said the delay was never a problem. "They said it (the event) was aimed at the promotion of the dying tribal culture. While the District Administration passed my bill, the Taluka officers kept on refusing the money. Now, by paying Rs 4,966, what sort of tribal art promotion are they talking about?" asked Rathwa.

He said that on May 31, 2007, the Panchmahals District Development Administration in a letter (No. GVA/SGSY/VC/512) to the Taluka Development Office asked it to pay Rs 23, 532 under the Rashtriya Shram Vikas Yojna for 12 banners of size 6 by 3 feet each.

On September 5 this year, Rathwa filed an application under the Right to Information (RTI) Act to the Halol Taluka Development Officer, seeking information as to why he was paid only

Rs 4,966 after two years and on what basis the Taluka officials gave the sum. "It has been over a month and they are yet to provide me with any information," said Rathwa.

This was not the first time that he had filed an RTI application. On February 21, 2008, he had filed an application about his earlier payments made by the local administration for his frescoes in the Halol Rest House. Then, he was asked to submit blank bills on the letterhead of the Jai Babadev Swa Sahay Juth trust.

"I wanted to know what happened to those bills, though they paid me Rs 6,000 once and Rs 9,000 for the frescoes I made," said Rathwa, showing the copies of the reply in which the district administration said the information of the bills are secret (RTI no TP/IRD/RT/VC/631).

Rathwa's Pithora paintings adorn the walls of at least five government buildings, including Taluka Panchayat Office in Lunawada, Halol Taluka Office, Godhra District Panchayat Office and Pavagadh Temple Trust in Macchi.

Rathwa learnt the Pithora art from his ancestors. However, to make his ends meet, he works as a part-time electrician, catering to a family of five. Similarly, the 11 others who are part of his group have changed their professions and work as daily wage earners or farmers.

"I would have carried on with the Pithora art but there is no incentive for all these things," said Rathwa.

Heading: ‘Harmonising Indian accounting standards with IFRS needs amendments in law’ - Indian Express
Content:
Former BJP Councillor Mehmood Beg was stabbed to death in the heart of Anand town near the Anand Railway Station on Saturday evening.

According to a complaint lodged with the Anand Town police station, Beg and his brother Naseeruddin were stabbed by six people following a deadlock between them and the accused.

Beg was going back to his residence along with his brother when the six attacked their car. The accused stabbed the former councillor at six places and fled from the spot even before Naseeruddin could raise an alarm, said Anand town Inspector G N Rao.

He said: "Naseeruddin has also been stabbed at one place and has received serious injuries. He is undergoing treatment at a private hospital in Vijaynagar."

The six, who have been named in the complaint filed by Naseeruddin are Idris Shiekh, Salim Ghachi, Asif alias Manal Vohra, Younus Vohra, Ibrahim Gharyali and Yakub Vohra.

Rao said the accused are known bootleggers in the area. "The matter is under investigation. We are waiting for Naseeruddin to recover," he said, adding that Beg had previously complained to the police about the six.

Heading: One killed, another injured after ST bus hits motorcycle - Indian Express
Content:
M S university (MSU) on Sunday had a slew of experts and industrialists discussing how to face the challenges before harmonising the Indian Accounting Standards with the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

Every country, according to the experts, has different accounting standards to suit its business set up. They said matching the Indian accounting standards with the IFRS will also mean amendments in the Indian laws.

"From April 1, 2011, all the countries have declared to harmonise with the IFRS accounting system. However, this will mean change in various economic policies as well as laws," said Sirish Kulkarni, a lecturer from MSU Commerce faculty.

Experts were of the view that on the face of it, Charted Accountants (CAs) should first be well versed about the Indian accounting standards, saying that only the CAs in the multinational companies are adept in both the IFRS and Indian accounting standards.

A participant said, "The language of IFRS is very technical. CAs should be preparing themselves with IFRS polices before chalking out plans to follow it." "There are certain economic rules and regulations of India which match with other countries. The country should be first adopting the economic policies of these countries before taking up the IFRS," he added.

Over 235 participants, including academicians, CAs, industrialist as well as people from public and private sectors, attended the day-long discourse presented by the University Grants Commission at the IG Patel Seminar Hall.

Heading: First impression - Indian Express
Content:
One person was killed and another seriously injured in a road accident on NH-14 near Jagana village in Palanpur (rural) on Sunday morning. The accident took place when a Palanpur-Maloshana ST bus hit a motorcycle while taking a turn on the road.

Sardarbhai Chamar died on the spot after he was crushed under the rear wheel of the bus. The injured, Valjibhai Charma, who was driving the bike, sustained serious injuries on the head and leg and is presently undergoing treatment at the Civil Hospital, Palanpur.

The two worked as construction labourers and were on their way to work when the bus hit them.

Meanwhile, the unidentified driver of the ST bus (GJ18V1078) fled from the spot and is yet to be arrested. The bus, however, has been brought to the police station.

Sub-Inspector Somabhai Patel, who is investigating the case, said: "The ST team visited the spot and brought the bus to the police station. The bus driver is yet to be identified. However, they will declare the name of the driver tomorrow."

Heading: Mission beautiful Kashmir - Indian Express
Content:
Funny girl

After winning hearts in the reality show Zara Nachke Dikha, Delnaz Paul, one of the most popular comic actors on Indian television is making an entry in Paani Puri's October 11 episode as Sumeet Raghavan's character, Vikas Puri's childhood friend, Sapna. Her entry will lead to a love triangle. She is doing a running cameo wherein she'll keep making appearances on the show. Talking about her character, Delnaz says, "For the first time, I will be doing a love triangle. I am playing a Punjabi girl who is full of life." Delnaaz, for whom comedy comes naturally, is coming back to what she does best - tickling the funny bone.

Twists of fate

After sharing sizzling chemistry with her co-host Karan Singh Grover in reality show Zara Nachke Dikha, pretty and petite Shweta Gulati has joined as a new intern on the show Dill Mill Gayee. Shweta will be playing Dr Nikita who goes on to become best bud with Riddhima. Nikita actually enters the hospital when Dr Armaan is away at a conference. When the two bump into each other after his return, it is revealed that Armaan and Nikita happen to be friends from college days. Obviously audiences are looking forward to see sparks fly once again.

Heading: The dial help - Indian Express
Content:
Borderless World Foundation's photography workshop has not just brought out the hidden talent in the children orphaned by violence in Kashmir, but also taught them to view their land through different eyes

Pune would soon witness the beauty of Kashmir through children's eye, who have suffered militant attacks that plagues Kashmir since Independence.

After participating in the All India Photography competition, Borderless World Foundation (BWF) that looks after orphaned Kashmiri girls plans to put up an exhibition of photographs taken by them, in Pune. A workshop for the same has been organised by BWF in Kashmir.

"This is the same place where I was walking around with my camera covered hidden under a hand towel. And today, girls are going around all over the place with six SLR cameras in their hands photographing everything that is coming in their way," recalls Nitin Upadhey, programme coordinator, Basera-e-Tabassum (BET), a project in Kupwara district of Kashmir, under BWF.

Girls of BET are gearing up to participate in an all India photography exhibition. Adhik kadam, chairman, BWF, says that though Nitin Upadhey has been conducting a photography workshop for the girls so that so that they could send selected entries, but actual motive is to give another opportunity to these kids to explore their creativity and love their surroundings. We selected six girls who had a liking for photography.

The BWF is running orphanages, under the name of BET, for Kashmir girls, who suffered during militant attacks. Altogether there are 83 girls in the orphanage.

"Photography is being promoted here as an art form and the undercurrent message is to make people realise the beauty in their surrounding and love it. Competition, being incentive-oriented, gives a clear goal to the participants and makes it more interesting. However, the idea is to allow freedom of expression and know the heart behind the art," says Kadam.

He has brought six cameras, which were given to the girls and a day of free photography session was done. "I was amazed to see the result. It was very evident from the photographs that despite all fear and danger, Kashmiri girls know that they live in a beautiful place.

One of the staff members however was afraid that the session may appear too heavy as for the girls the details seemed a little "too technical". However, the observation was proved completely wrong as the girls on the first day of their workshop gave an outstanding performance concentrating on the minutest of details," says Upadhaye, adding, "The sincerity with which they completed the first day of the workshop was very encouraging and motivating and certainly has given us bigger dreams for the future of these girls."

Six girls -- Ishrat, Sunita, Afroza, Nuzhat, Rabia Shaista -- are participating in an All India Photography Competition.

The photography contest is being organised on a national level and entries are invited from all over the country. The contest has been divided between two categories – nature and human in action—and is contested by the girls in the age group pf 12 years to 18 years.

"It is great to see girls appreciating their own environment as this is the foundation of love for their land, observes Kadam, who is right now in Kashmir.

"Despite all violence and suffering, these girls and their art depicts beauty and hope, and this is appreciable. This gives us immense happiness and a sense of satisfaction that our initiative not only gives a platform to the art but also mends the heart of children of Kashmir," adds Upadhye.

Upadhey informs that an exhibition of the photographs would be put in Pune soon and the children would be here in the city to see the reactions to their work.

Heading: Target set - Indian Express
Content:
The only animal welfare directory of the city is in its third edition now; the 76-page directory will help ailing animals head to the right places for their treatment

Often ignored by the onlookers is the braying of a helpless donkey with its legs tied with a rope and so is ignored the plight of any ailing animal treading the streets, striving to cope with its pain in a mute way with helpless eyes pleading for mercy from the people passing by. Even though the pain of these voiceless creatures evoke sympathy, the fact remains that the one sympathising with them does not really know whom to contact to help them.

Trying to find a solution for this very problem the Business Development Bureau's social response wing,, The BDB Foundation came up with the concept of animal welfare directory in the year 2003, which the foundation printed and distributed for free to individuals to make them aware about institutions and organisations dedicated to animal welfare. In order to improve on the accessibility factor the foundation went online with the directory in the year 2006.

Updating the directory and getting in loop seven other organisations and also three more individuals dedicated to animal welfare, the third edition of the directory was released this Saturday. The one- of- its -kind animal directory of the city can now boast of having almost every animal welfare organisation in in the city listed down on its pages. "That is what we aimed at when we came up with the first edition of the directory. If you will see we are trying to bring the animal lovers under one roof so that it prompts them to come together to take any action. We are signalling them to come together by making the information about them accessible to all," shares S V Krishnan, founder, BDB foundation.

Proving to be the perfect vantage point, providing the view of the current scenario of animal welfare in the city the directory also has helped many animal lovers get rid of the guilt of not helping a stray in need. "As a mother I can say my kids are my first priority and when I see an ailing animal I can't just neglect my one duty to perform another but with the numbers in the directory I can at least be sure of the fact that I have called for help and the animal will get its proper treatment now," shares Divya Seth who launched the third edition of the directory in the city.

The 76 page directory is the storehouse of numbers of veterinary doctors to animal shelters. "People often want to help the animals but they really don't know what to do as they too have their own priorities and can't go out of the way to help animals but the sympathy is certainly there. So we wanted to guide these people to the right places so that they can help the animals in need. Coming up with the directory was one option," elaborates Krishnan,

Apart from the numbers of the vetenary doctors and animal shelters, the directory under the section activists stores the addresses and numbers of more than 20 activists to which the people can refer to if they come across any animal being ill-treated by its owner. "Donkeys are the worst sufferers. Especially in Pune one can often come across donkeys being ill-treated. Go to dhobi ghat and the sight in itself is repulsive. You can't stand it," shares Krishnan.

With its treasure trove of more than a hundred numbers and addresses of animal welfare organisations and also individuals working for animal welfare, the directory will continue leading Puneites in to helping the voiceless creatures of the city. for the years to come.

Voicing the voiceless the evening of the launch of the third edition of the only animal welfare directory of the city voiced the problems of the voiceless loud and clear. The seminar Diwali Dhamaka Without A Phataka organised by the BDB foundation saw a healthy discussion amongst animal lovers and city's veterinary doctors Pradnya Dhokrikar and Milind Hatekar. The seminar raised issues of the stray animal being traumatised by the sound and the smoke filling the atmosphere during Diwali. Also the fact that unlike pet animals the stray animals have to fight their problems on their own was brought to notice. Thus concluding that the plight of the stray is much more that the pet animals. In the seminar that also had Divya Shah, a Peta activist as one of the speakers the animal lovers pledged to have Diwali sans firecrackers every year. On the occasion also animal welfare NGO's in Pune were felicitated.

Heading: Mercy. Games open without a hitch - Indian Express
Content:
With two silver and one bronze medal at the Maharashtra State Shooting championship, city youngster Shehzad Mirza has his eyes set on the Commonwealth Games 2010

If it is about focusing, 25-year-old Shehzad Mirza has hit the bull's eye- and that too a number of times. In fact, recently Mirza won two silver and one bronze medal at the Maharashtra State Shooting Championship, held at Worli sea phase in Mumbai between September 30 and October 6.

According to an excited Mirza, "I won one silver medal in Standard pistol category, another silver in Centre fire pistol and one bronze in Rapid fire category. The prerequisite of this competition was that only the qualifiers for pre-nationals could participate. This made the competition even tougher. But I am happy that this was a fruitful competition for me."

Having won two gold medals at the pre-nationals in 2005, silver at the open nationals in 2006 and bronze at the open nationals in 2007, Mirza's decision to take up shooting as a full time profession was not accidental. "My father has a licensed trigger and it was because of him I developed interest in shooting. I joined the Pune District Rifle Association in 2004. My initial teacher was Gani Shaikh but after that I have received great help from Arjun Award winner Ashok Pandit and his son Ronak Pandit. I also won district championships before targetting the state and national level competitions," adds he.

Mirza feels that after the performances by Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore and Abhinav Bindra, the way people look at shooting as a sport has changed. "People take it more seriously now! In fact you will be surprised to know that the Commonwealth Youth Games have one of the best ranges in the entire continent," adds he. Commenting on the nature of shooting as a sport Mirza says, "Contrary to the commonly perceived notion that shooting is about focus, I would like to comment that shooting is a neuromuscular game. It is about the coordination between one's body and mind. In fact other than the regular shooting practice that I do at home, I also spend a lot of time doing Yoga, exercise and Pranayam."

With Ashok Pandit and Jaspal Rana as his idols, Mirza now has his eyes set on the open nationals scheduled to take place in December this year and the Commonwealth Games taking place in Delhi in 2010. "All my colleagues and friends blame me for not celebrating my success. But I feel that more than enjoyment, the winning moments are about looking ahead and targeting the competitions in the future and to start working towards them. I want to take the competitions to come as stepping-stones and target the 2012 London Olympics."

A part of his profession, it seems that targeting has become a habit for this young shooter. And knowing the champion that he is, no target seems unachievable!

Heading: One seat, one party, three leaders in hunt - Indian Express
Content:
City's biggest show weathers rain threat and controversies, Kalmadi says Pune now on international map

The dozen controversies that had threatened to ruin Pune's biggest show disappeared, at least for the time being, at a spectacular start to the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) at the Balewadi Sports Complex on Sunday.

The delay in infrastructure development at the sports village and the city were forgotten as an Indian Air Force show, a laser show and cultural events each went without a hitch. A drizzle at the start of the ceremony had raised fears of the event being jinxed, but the rain, like the controversies, disappeared at just the right time.

President Pratibha Patil declared open the third CYG, the largest so far due with 71 countries. Various Union ministers, Chief Minister Vilassao Deshmukh and state ministers attended the ceremony.

Union Agriculture Minister Sharad Pawar was absent though his nephew and Guardian Minister Ajit Pawar was present.

Organising committee chairman Suresh Kalmadi, preside7nt of Indian Olympic Association, sought to showcase the city as one of the fastest developing cities of the country that is making a mark internationally in the IT, automobile and animation industries.

Kalmadi, who is the city MP, thanked Puneites and political parties for making the event a success. "The CYG will put the city on the international map. The event cannot be made successful by a single person or a party and I thank all political parties in the city for the cooperation," Kalmadi said with special reference to Sharad Pawar, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and several Union and state ministers.

"The interntational event has contributed a lot in raising world class infrastructure for the city," he said. He felt the CYG had set the stage for a great Commonwealth Games in Delhi.

The Indian Air Force enacted a show with Sarang helicopters and Akashganga paratroopers while Army Service Core did a motorcycle show. Hema Malini presented Ganesh Vandana and Shreya Ghoshal a welcome act. The stadium echoed with chants of Ganpati Bappa Morya as Hema Malini's troupe performed a Ganesh aarti.

The ceremony was marked by a programme depicting Marathi culture: an audiovisual presentation of grand Maratha, a dhol and lezim performance, a carnival procession of Janta Raja, Peshwa, Lavani by Urmila Matondkar and a dance by actor Saif Ali Khan.

Earlier, contingents marched in to a thundering welcome from the audience. It was the smaller countries that won hearts with their traditional attire and dance sequences. The largest contingents were those of India, Australia, England and Canada.

The highlight of the function was the felicititation of Indian players led by ace shooter Abhinav Bindra who had led the country's best ever performance in the recent Olympic Games in Beijing. Indian sportspersons Anjali Bhagwat, Dhanraj Pillai, Jitendra Kumar and others carried the baton relay. Badminton ace Saina Nehwal took the oath on behalf of the participants.

Representing the atheletes, Bindra said the CYG would promote sports among Indian youths.

A colourful firecracker display brought an end to the function.

Heading: Some terror funds straight into bank, some via hawala - Indian Express
Content:
Young turk, former MP and civic leader want to contest for BJP

Much before the announcement of schedule for the Lok Sabha elections, the BJP unit in the city is split over who the party candidate for the Pune seat would be, with three names already in the ring.

The root of the bickering within the city BJP unit is the differences at the state level, with one faction led by BJP state chief Nitin Gadkari and the other by BJP national secretary Gopinath Munde.

Anil Shirole, a staunch supporter of Munde, is optimistic of getting the party ticket with the blessings of his mentor's close aides. "I have been given favourable signals from senior party leaders and have already started my preparations," says Shirole, a former BJP city unit chief.

Vikas Mathkari, leader of the opposition in the Pune Municipal Corporation, and Anna Joshi, a former MP, are also said to be eyeing the party ticket. But the multiple claims have not dampened Shirole's spirit.

"It is obvious there will be many claimants in a democracy. It is up to the party to decide," says Shirole.

Mathkari does not comment on the other contenders but says there cannot be a better candidate than him. He uses statistics to justify his claim, which he has also cited before top leaders. "The average age of a voter in the city is 34 and I am the young face of the party, with a lot of experience. I have access to the youth, being a professor," says Mathkari.

Of his experience, he says he has been leading past campaigns for the party in the Lok Sabha polls and working at the grassroots.

As for the third contender, Anna Joshi is banking on his past Lok Sabha victory. "I am the perfect candidate to take on the Congress candidate in the Lok Sabha polls with my past experience of defeating Congress candidate Vithalrao Gadgil in 1991," he says. He cites strong support from alliance partner Shiv Sena as another advantage if he is given the ticket to contest.

Joshi is working on reviving his support base in the city.

Party leaders admit the present situation could create confusion among voters and therefore it was necessary to address the issue.

Heading: Health diet in CBSE textbooks right from Class I - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai police say that the Indian Mujahideen men arrested from Pune received funds from the Gulf countries, deposited into their Indian bank accounts, and also through hawala and other illegal channels. Some of these transactions were made in Pune, though the police refused to specify if any of the money from the Gulf had been deposited into Pune bank accounts.

The police said the suspects received Rs 26 lakh from Gulf countries and probably a lot more through the illegal channels. Joint Commissioner of Police (crime branch) Rakesh Maria confirmed the amount deposited in banks. "Since 2006 a total of Rs 26 lakh was sent from Gulf countries to accounts held by the suspects in nationalised banks. The IM members used the money to fund their operations," he said.

The crime branch has already frozen the suspects' savings bank accounts but refused to say if any of these accounts was in Pune.

On other funding channels, Additional Commissioner of Police (Mumbai crime) Deven Bharati said, "We have some clues about transactions in Pune. They were receiving funds through hawala and other channels." Police sources said software executive Mansoor Asghar Ali Peerbhoy and one of his accomplices, Salman Kadar Sheikh, had received Rs 70,000 each in cash from wanted terrorist Riyaz Bhatkal. The money went into a training course in hacking in May 2007.

Riyaz's brother Iqbal was also providing money and material to the "media wing" operatives. The Mumbai crime branch has formed a special team to probe the funding channels. Police have scanned the suspects' mobile phone lists and will check if any of the people listed was involved in the funding.

Hawala transactions are not new to the city. Two men wanted for the 2006 train blasts had Pune links and got funds through their hawala connections, the police said. Rizwan Daware was born in Pune while the other suspect, Mumbai-based Rahil Shaikh, used to live here. "Both were part of a big hawala racket," said police inspector Peter Lobo of the Pune ATS unit.

However, it has not yet been established if the hawala transactions in the city involve terrorists, said Assistant Commissioner of Police Sangramsinh Nishandar. "So far we have no inputs about any illegal money transfer racket used by the SIMI or IM members. The rackets we busted were used mostly by traders and businessmen," said ACP Nishandar.

Heading: Traffic headache on highway in PCMC limits eases - Indian Express
Content:
Health is set to become an independent school subject. The National Council of Education Research and Training (NCERT) has approved Health and Physical Education as part of the curriculum.

The subject will be compulsory for Classes I to X and optional for Class XI and Class XII, said Dr Mohan Deshpande of Pune, who was part of the team that framed the curriculum.

He said the subject would be introduced in CBSE schools, public schools and Navodaya Vidyalayas within a year.

The subject will cover a wide range of topics like hygiene and sanitation, the human body, food and nutrition, common ailments and epidemics, health services, indigenous healers, health and consumerism, health rights, and reproductive health.

"The subject will be helpful for students who plan to study medicine, pharmacy courses and biotechnology," Deshpande said.

Another team from the NCERT will start working on the textbooks in November. "We are also planning to have a dedicated team of artists to do the illustrations for these textbooks to make them attractive and informative, keeping students of rural areas in mind," said Deshpande.

Evaluation for the subject will be different from that for other subjects. "Unlike the conventional method of evaluation, we are working on introducing a system where exams will be held every month," Deshpande said.

The subject will be taught initially in English, but the textbooks will later be translated into Hindi and regional languages.

The team that framed the curriculum included Professor Rama Baru of Centre for Social Medicine and Community Health at Jawaharlal Nehru University; Professor J L Pande, Director of Education Centre of Social Medicine with NCERT, Dr Saroj Yadav, also from NCERT; Ramesh Pal, professor with Laxmibai National Institute of Physical Education in Gwalior, and Dr Balasubramanian, a rural health worker in Mysore.

The team has recommended that the NCERT begin training teachers for this subject, simultaneously with other trainers.

Heading: ‘Pune could become research centre of excellence’ - Indian Express
Content:
RS 300 CRORE PROJECT n Two more grade separators opened, major portion of the highway concretised, Army wall on way out

Citizens from Kothrud, Kondhwa, Wanavdi, Bibvewadi, Pune Camp, Koregaon Park, Khadki, Vadgaonsheri and Yerawada can look forward to a smooth and hassle-free drive on the 11-kilometre stretch Pune-Mumbai highway within the limits of the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation. That is because on Saturday, on the eve of the Commonwealth Youth Games, the PCMC inaugurated its much-talked about concretised surface of the highway stretch and two grade separators.

With the inauguration of the Chinchwad and Akurdi grade separators and the concretised road surface at Kasarwadi and Nigdi, the Pune-Mumbai highway stretch on PCMC terrain sports a complete new look though there is some more work yet to be completed. The new highway has 10 lanes, five subways, three grade separators. The Pimpri grade separator was opened in 2006 and concretised surfaces in Nigdi, Chinchwad, Pimpri, Nashik Phata, Kasarwadi and Phugewadi. Now only the nearly two kilometre work in Dapodi area remains. "We will demolish the Army wall phase-wise and construct new compound wall 19 metres away from the present location," said PCMC city engineer Eknath Ugile, who has played a key role in the highway widening process.

The highway work, which began four years back during the Dilip Band regime has cost the PCMC Rs 300 crore. It was Band who took the initiative in road widening process soon after he took over as the municipal commissioner. Despite severe opposition from shopkeepers and local politicians, Band first demolished the shops in Chinchwad station areas and then hammered down shops, hotels, offices, located at Akurdi, Pimpri, Kasarwadi, Dapodi, Phugewadi. First, the Pimpri grade separator and Pimpri to Nashik Phata concretisation work were taken up and then work in Chinchwad, Akurdi, Kasarwadi and Nigdi began. During this time, the PCMC administration was also dragged to the court by civic activists.

Saturday's inauguration of the road work has come as a big relief for motorists and two-wheeler riders, who were getting caught in traffic snarls in PCMC limits almost every day. Especially from 4 pm to 9 pm, the daily traffic chaos remained at its peak with traffic police struggling to keep the vehicles moving. The Kasarwadi-Nashik Phata stretch has been the worse with both PCMC administration and traffic police having no clue as to restore sanity. "From yesterday, the traffic chaos has completely disappeared," exults Dushyant Nahata whose shop is located on the highway. Nahata had bore the brunt of the road widening process. "First, our shop, which was the oldest one on the highway was demolished and then the slow pace of work affected business at our new shop," he said.
